papers.title: ArtKit: Motion-Driven Re-Segmentation and Link Re-Generation for Articulated Objects from RGB-D Video
papers.abstract: An RGB-D camera that films an object being moved, often from one viewpoint, sees one side of it and how its parts move. We present ArtKit, which takes such a video as input to create an articulated model with complete parts, a kinematic tree, and typed joints. Our central idea is generating the hidden geometry and verifying it against what the camera sees. A generative part prior proposes complete, part-decomposed geometry based on the first frame. Point tracks, grouped into rigid trajectories, split and merge the generated parts into links. We then fit revolute and prismatic joints, with a visibility-aware energy ensuring that the articulated model explains the depth observed across the video. A rule checks against the video to choose between synchronous group fits and per-frame chain fits, so that one pipeline serves a diverse range of articulated objects, such as household items and robotic hands. Finally, we regenerate each link of the chosen fit as one part and keep it wherever it agrees better with the observations. We evaluate on Articulate-100 and on HArt, a new benchmark of 60 PartNet-Mobility objects and 8 robotic hands and grippers rendered as RGB-D videos with ground-truth parts and joints. ArtKit reduces the axis and part motion errors of the strongest baseline by more than half on the objects, as well as the axis error on the hands. ArtKit also runs on real recordings and generated videos.

authors.name: Vivian Yu
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ArtLang-4D: Articulation-Aware Dynamic Language Fields from Monocular Videos
papers.abstract: Language that describes an articulated object is often about its state: the drawer pulled out the furthest, the door opened halfway, push the drawer all the way in. Existing 3D language fields attach one feature to each point and cannot tell these descriptions apart, and 4D language fields condition on video time, which has no kinematic meaning and cannot be set by a user. We present ArtLang-4D, which reconstructs an articulated object from a single monocular RGB-D video and equips it with a dynamic language field indexed by articulation time t, the normalized state of its joints, instead of video time. The geometry is a canonical triangle field whose triangles follow typed screw joints, discovered from the video without any joint initialization. The language field is supervised by a t-tagged caption bank that describes each part with comparative state phrases in a whitened open-vocabulary text space. A free-form query is answered by maximizing part relevance jointly over parts and states, which returns both the part and the articulation state it describes; a command is then executed by moving only that part along its recovered joint. On the 100 objects of Articulate-100, ArtLang-4D recovers more accurate joints and part geometry than reconstruction and articulation baselines, retrieves the queried state far more reliably than a state-agnostic language field, and executes language commands with lower motion error.

papers.title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
papers.abstract: AI systems are increasingly capable of producing machine-checked Lean proofs of advanced mathematical results. Real mathematical formalization, however, is not isolated theorem proving: it requires building the definitions and intermediate lemmas that connect a result to a formal library. Existing evaluations often provide isolated theorem statements in settings where much of this supporting theory is already available in Mathlib. We introduce AutoformBench, a benchmark of 341 Lean 4 formalization tasks drawn from 24 advanced mathematical sources. Lean-experienced mathematicians formalized and audited each target statement, leaving the corresponding Lean proof to the evaluated agent. Each problem is embedded in a broader mathematical development: agents receive the informal proof but must translate it into Lean while constructing the missing definitions, intermediate lemmas, and supporting infrastructure. We compare the performance of frontier models on these problems. We find a largely shared difficulty frontier: success depends less on mathematical domain than on models' ability to construct missing formal infrastructure. Data and code at https://github.com/facebookresearch/autoformbench

authors.name: Fabian Gloeckle
authors.institution: École nationale des ponts et chaussées

authors.name: Amaury Hayat
authors.institution: École nationale des ponts et chaussées

authors.name: Julia Kempe
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: FERRETS: A Scalable Symbolic Transform for Time Series Classification
papers.abstract: Dictionary methods for time series build bags of symbolic words from subsequences, but the accurate ones scale poorly. Against other families of methods, their accuracy no longer pays for their cost. We present FERRETS, a label-free dictionary transform built on WEASEL~2. It keys windows of random length and dilation into exact eight-bit words, adds a level word of each window's mean and spread, and on multivariate data adds cross-channel words. We compare it with leading classifiers, deep networks and foundation models included, on the UCR, Multiverse and MONSTER archives. FERRETS is the fastest of the eleven methods timed on UCR under a ten-thread budget. Of the ten others, only MultiRocket-Hydra is significantly more accurate, taking 24.7 times as long. FERRETS is not significantly different from WEASEL~2, the most accurate earlier dictionary method, which takes 125 times as long, and is significantly ahead of the other dictionary methods. On the Multiverse core, it is not significantly different in accuracy from HIVE-COTE~2 and MultiRocket-Hydra, though behind both on UCR. It is also significantly more accurate than five frozen foundation models on UCR's published split. On the MONSTER problems both complete, MiniRocket takes 3.7 times as long to fit as the streaming FERRETS classifier, which is significantly more accurate.

papers.title: Statistical analysis of crossing beam speckle fields
papers.abstract: Building on the statistical analysis of single beam speckles, this paper develops a statistical description of speckle fields formed by crossing laser beams. A formal definition of individual speckles and their domains allows us to quantify the effective size and abundance of speckles. For two crossing beams, the effective speckle size is derived from the local curvature of the intensity field, and the expected speckle abundance is found asymptotically with the Kac-Rice formula. Monte Carlo simulations of speckle abundance show excellent agreement with the theoretical abundance formula. The two beam speckle analysis is then applied to a symmetric quad beam configuration motivated by polarization smoothing and demonstrates that increasing the separation between beams reduces expected stimulated Brillouin scattering reflectivity from saturated speckles. The statistical model is then extended to an arbitrary number of beams using a coordinate free formulation to obtain the spectral density of laser driven electron density fluctuations.

authors.name: Ian D. Min-Roberts
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Multi-Party Authorization of Maintenance Prescriptions on a Permissioned Blockchain
papers.abstract: In industrial prescriptive maintenance, an equipment supplier's model may recommend an intervention that a plant schedules, a contractor executes, and a quality or safety function approves. A shared ledger records who submitted the prescription, yet cannot check whether the agreed model and decision rule produced it. We require permissioned-blockchain endorsers to verify a succinct proof of that calculation before releasing a work order. On a four-organization Hyperledger Fabric testbed using a public engine benchmark, this stopped all nine contested or mis-operated prescriptions, whereas hash checks accepted four that either raised simulated maintenance cost or reintroduced late failures.

authors.name: Ebru Turanoglu Bekar
authors.institution: Institut National des Sciences Appliquées de Lyon

papers.title: The type I conjecture for locally compact groups acting on trees
papers.abstract: We prove that a closed group of automorphisms acting minimally on a locally finite tree and two-transitively on its boundary is uniformly admissible, hence of type I. This solves Nebbia's conjecture in a strong form. Together with the work of Caprace, Kalantar and Monod, this shows that for every closed nonamenable subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(T)$ acting minimally on a locally finite tree $T$, $G$ is of type I if and only if the action on $\partial T$ is two-transitive. The key ingredient is the following operator algebraic result: if the projections of two atomic von Neumann algebras $A_1, A_2$ have integer traces, then every amenable amalgamated free product $A_1 \ast_B A_2$ with $B$ atomic is of type I.

papers.title: Magnetically Guided Sequential Multi-Filler Alignment Enables Anisotropic Heat Pathways in Stretchable Composites for Soft Electronics
papers.abstract: Stretchable, skin-conformal electronics demand thermal interface materials that combine high through-plane heat transport with mechanical softness and lateral electrical insulation. In particle-filled composites, these requirements are typically antagonistic. Heat transport is governed not only by the intrinsic thermal conductivity of the fillers but, more critically, by thermal resistance at the interparticle interface. As the interparticle distance is reduced by increasing the particle content, mechanical reinforcement and in-plane electrical conductivity become unavoidable. The existing particle alignment processing strategies result in inefficient uncoupling of multifunctionality. Here, we present a hierarchical two-step process strategy to induce strong conductivity anisotropy in a soft composite. First, an align-before-blend process forms a scaffold of magnetically aligned nickel (Ni) microparticles in air before polymer infiltration. The absence of the viscous elastomer matrix during the particle alignment facilitates handling large amounts of particles, which assemble into highly ordered and densely packed vertical heat-conduction pathways. Second, a liquid metal (LM)/Ni mixture is infiltrated into the aligned scaffold to bridge interparticle gaps, minimizing interparticle thermal resistance. The composite reaches 7.5 W/(m K) through-plane thermal conductivity with lateral electrical conductivity below $10^{-12}$ S/m and ultrasoft mechanical compliance (approximately 160 kPa), enabling coupling layers in thermoelectric generators and finger-mounted heat-spreading pads for wearable technologies.

papers.title: Collaborative Language Models for Semantic IoT Data Processing: Validation through Zero-Shot Human Activity Recognition
papers.abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) systems generate low-level sensor observations that are not directly suitable for process analysis and must first be transformed into semantically meaningful events. This paper investigates collaborative language models as a zero-shot semantic abstraction layer for converting such observations into higher-level event and activity labels. We propose a five-stage workflow comprising semantic mapping, semantic aggregation, temporal and contextual aggregation, specialized reasoning, and final event abstraction. The resulting labels and contextual information can subsequently be represented as event records for downstream Process Mining (PM) tasks. The approach is evaluated through Human Activity Recognition on the CASAS Aruba smart home dataset using eleven workflow configurations. The experiments show that collaboration alone does not guarantee improved performance: general-purpose auxiliary SLMs can degrade recognition, whereas assigning complementary specialist roles leads to better results and allows a smaller final classifier to retain much of the performance of a larger model. The selected workflow achieves a macro F1 of 0.643 in the 1.5-day comparison and 0.567 (weighted F1 0.680) in a one-week evaluation. Although trained ML approaches remain more accurate on this dataset, the results demonstrate a different design point: modular semantic event abstraction using off-the-shelf models without task-specific parameter fine-tuning. The findings indicate that the structure of LM collaboration and task decomposition is more important than simply increasing the number of participating models.

papers.title: Functional Factor Graphs and the Functional Sum-Product Algorithm
papers.abstract: We propose a generalization of factor graphs and the sum-product algorithm (SPA), widely used in the estimation of data, channel state information and sensing parameters, to unknowns that are functions, such as waveforms, time-varying channels and continuous-aperture array currents, which must otherwise be sampled first. In order to mitigate the challenge that functions have no probability density functions (PDFs), the proposed scheme measures densities relative to the prior of each function, not to the flat reference implicit in every PDF. Messages then become likelihood ratios, and the factor-node rule an average over the priors, still exact on trees. For Gaussian models, the proposed functional SPA (FSPA) is Gaussian belief propagation (GaBP) with kernels in place of matrices and a grid-independent convergence condition, whereas scalar GaBP on grid samples provably slows down under refinement, as information hops from sample to sample. Simulations in a multi-user detection setting confirms the latter, and shows that sampling first can also fail for smooth priors.

papers.title: Learning from Natural Images Untangles Number Sense
papers.abstract: Numerical cognition is a simple yet fundamental ability that remains challenging for modern vision-language models. Meanwhile, number sense is already present in numerically na\"ive animals, suggesting that it can emerge without explicit numerical learning. Deep neural networks provide a related observation, with numerosity-selective units appearing after training on unrelated natural-image tasks and even before any training. However, these findings leave unresolved whether visual learning contributes beyond the spontaneous emergence of numerical selectivity. Human development provides a clue, as children become better at making judgments in which numerosity and proportion conflict. Here, we introduce a geometric framework to trace how representations of these two quantities change across learning. Although untrained and pretrained networks exhibited similar unit-level numerosity selectivity and basic comparison performance, natural-image pretraining increased the angle between numerosity and proportion subspaces while reducing their overlap, supporting more robust readout under conflict. Direct manipulation of these geometric properties further demonstrated their functional contributions to decoding accuracy and functional independence. Importantly, conventional supervised pretraining was not essential for quantity separation, which also emerged through self-supervised learning without category labels and synthetic-image training without natural-image exposure. Together, our findings suggest that structured visual learning can refine spontaneously emerging number sense into robust and functionally independent quantity representations without explicit numerical training.

authors.name: Hyeonsu Lee
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: D\'ej\`aVu: Plurality Consensus by First Repetition
papers.abstract:
We analyze D\'ej\`aVu, a simple protocol for plurality consensus: in each synchronous round, each agent samples one uniformly random agent and adopts the first opinion it observes twice, resetting its memory after every adoption. The rule requires neither frequency counters nor knowledge of the population size or the number of opinions. It relies only on repetition detection, an ability documented in single neurons and reflected in the mere-exposure effect.
  For a population of $n$ agents with $k$ initial opinions, let $M_0$ be the initial count of the plurality opinion (so $n/M_0 \le k$) and $\Delta_0$ its bias, the difference between $M_0$ and the count of the second most popular opinion. We prove that, whenever $\Delta_0 = \Omega(\sqrt{M_0 \log n})$, D\'ej\`aVu reaches consensus on the initial plurality opinion within $O(\sqrt{n/M_0} \log(e M_0 / \Delta_0) + \log\log n)$ rounds with high probability. Moreover, we show that, for the same bias regime, D\'ej\`aVu is asymptotically never slower than the $h$-majority protocol, collecting its $h$ samples one per round, for every fixed choice of $h$, even one chosen optimally for the initial configuration. There are also initial configurations for which D\'ej\`aVu is asymptotically faster for every $h$.
  The opinion counts alone do not determine the dynamics: each adoption depends on a hidden memory filled over many rounds while the population changed, and agents with older (hence fuller) memories tend to reset sooner, so an advantage held mostly by them can be lost. The few rigorous convergence results we are aware of for such dynamics concern only two opinions. We derive the exact law of the memories given the history of opinions and resets, and track how the plurality opinion's advantage is distributed across memory ages, giving more weight to recently reset agents as they are less likely to reset again soon.

authors.name: George Giakkoupis
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: NASA's Pandora SmallSat Mission: Gaussian Processes for Simulated Stellar Heterogeneity Corrections under Imperfect Stellar Models
papers.abstract: Stellar contamination is the primary bottleneck limiting robust atmospheric characterization of exoplanets orbiting active K- and M-dwarfs with James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) transmission spectroscopy. Launched in January 2026, NASA's Pandora SmallSat mission addresses this challenge through long-term, simultaneous visible photometry and near-infrared spectroscopy of planet-hosting stars, providing the data to disentangle planetary and stellar signals. However, conventional stellar-contamination corrections rely on stellar atmosphere models, making them vulnerable to model inaccuracies that can impede accurate inferences. Here, we investigate how Pandora data can be used to mitigate stellar contamination without an accurate host star model. We present a Gaussian-process-aided stellar retrieval framework that learns wavelength-dependent deviations from current stellar model grids. We propagate stellar contamination factors directly from the stellar retrieval into the planetary atmospheric retrievals, allowing the atmospheric inference to marginalize over stellar-contamination uncertainty without relying on a biased stellar model. Tests using simulated Pandora observations with realistic stellar model mismatch show that this framework consistently improves the recovery of disk-integrated stellar spectra. For a WASP-69 b-like system, this approach can reduce model-driven biases in inferred atmospheric properties, though degeneracies among stellar and atmospheric parameters can leave residual biases. This flexible, data-driven framework is a promising approach toward accurate stellar-contamination corrections and more robust atmospheric inference even when host-star model grids are inaccurate.

authors.name: Suman Saha
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

authors.name: Rae Holcomb
authors.institution: The University of Texas at San Antonio Health Science Center

papers.title: Schwinger-Dyson recursion, Gr\"obner elimination and graph combinatorics
papers.abstract:
Schwinger-Dyson equations are a cornerstone of quantum field theory (QFT). Derived using integration by parts, they capture relations between correlators of different orders, forming an open, infinite-dimensional system. In zero-dimensional QFTs with polynomial actions, which is just a physical interpretation for multivariate Gaussian integrals with polynomial insertions, conventional Gr\"obner elimination can be used to express all higher-order correlators (moments) in terms of a fixed basis set. One consequence is a closed finite-dimensional system of differential equations for the coupling dependence of these `master' correlators.
  An important application of zero-dimensional QFTs is in counting discrete geometric structures (as in simplicial approaches to quantum gravity). For the problem of counting labelled regular graphs, applying this Schwinger-Dyson closure results in a computational breakthrough relative to the existing state-of-the-art: for 9- and 10-regular graphs on $n$ vertices, a finite-depth, finite-width recursive formulation is obtained, making it possible to compute the total graph counts in $O(n)$ arithmetic operations.

papers.title: Quantifying combined rate- and noise-induced transitions in a multiscale system
papers.abstract: Excitations in multiscale dynamical systems produce persistent but impermanent excursions away from a quiescent state. A novel mechanism for inducing excitations, through a combination of rate-dependent parametric and stochastic forcing, is discussed using the FitzHugh-Nagumo model as an example. In the absence of noise, a quasithreshold separating the state space between supercritical and subcritical behaviour is defined with respect to slow manifolds associated with the metastable excited state. This is formulated in an autonomous system framework, which can be obtained via a compactification of time. Techniques from singular perturbation theory elucidate how canard trajectories shape the geometric structure of the quasithreshold as the system's pullback attractor moves through it. The probability with which weakly stochastically driven sample paths travel through the quasithreshold and undertake (i) solely noise-induced and (ii) combined rate- and noise-induced excitations is estimated numerically for each of the corresponding forcing scenarios, using the adaptive multilevel splitting algorithm. The probability of weak stochastic forcing preventing a rate-induced excitation, which occurs deterministically, is likewise estimated. This quantifies the different rates at which the probability of each transition scenario scales exponentially with the noise strength, in accordance with sample path large deviation principles. It is revealed that a combination of (deterministically subcritical) parametric and stochastic forcing is exponentially more likely to induce excitations than stochastic forcing alone, which is attributed to the pullback attractor and quasithreshold converging towards one another.

papers.title: Score-based Black-box Attack via Adversarial Condition Guided Diffusion Model
papers.abstract: Generative models enable unrestricted adversarial attacks that aim to fool classifiers while preserving the natural appearance and semantics of the original image. However, existing diffusion-based black-box attacks largely rely on transferability from surrogates, making their effectiveness sensitive to differences between surrogate and victim. Improving transferability can also distort semantic content and degrade image quality. Moreover, retaining the original prompt to preserve fidelity leaves the diffusion model's conditional prior underused for adversarial guidance. We address these limitations by adapting score-based black-box attacks to reverse diffusion, using the victim's output probabilities to guide latent updates without accessing its gradients. We further introduce adaptive-target guidance, which uses the victim's current runner-up class as an adversarial condition to steer denoising towards the decision boundary. Because such guidance can introduce unwanted semantic changes, we also propose target-search guidance, which searches for a small perturbation of the original condition embedding using a score-based attack. This achieves comparable attack effectiveness with better image quality than runner-up guidance. Experiments on the ImageNet-Compatible dataset show that our framework outperforms transfer-based baselines in both attack effectiveness and image quality.

authors.name: Xingyu Zhao
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Fixed-level profiles and fluctuations in age-dependent recursive trees
papers.abstract: How many vertices of a growing recursive tree lie at a prescribed distance from the root? We compare two linear attachment rules. When an arriving vertex chooses a parent with probability proportional to its label, each fixed level eventually stops growing. We determine the limiting covariance kernel and the probability that a level will change again after time $n$. Writing $L_\infty(h)$ for its final size, we show that $2^{-h}L_\infty(h)$ converges in mean square as $h$ tends to infinity to a random variable with mean $1$ and variance $1/3$. Consequently the limiting variance of the level size is asymptotic to $4^h/3$. When parents are chosen with probability proportional to their age, each fixed level grows. Its centered fluctuations have a joint Gaussian limit whose covariance constants come from repeated logarithmic integration of attachment noise at the root. An exact finite-size calculation illustrates the difference between the limiting and finite-size variances.

authors.name: Jerzy Szymanski
authors.institution: Kazimierz Pułaski University of Technology and Humanities in Radom

papers.title: Shower Shapes and Data-Driven Simulation Studies using a Highly Granular Crystal ECAL
papers.abstract: Electron shower shapes were measured using standard shower profile models for events observed with a highly granular crystal electromagnetic calorimeter prototype, with data taken from a 2025 test beam at the CERN Proton Synchrotron T9 beamline. The shower maximum, longitudinal shape parameter, and lateral variance were found to be well approximated by log-normal distributions. From these distributions, properties of the absorber were measured to be in agreement with existing literature. Energy-dependent correlations were observed between all parameters and most strongly between the shower maximum and the shower shape parameter. The distributions of energy and event-by-event pairwise log ratios of energy fractions in individual active volumes of the calorimeter conditional on the shower shape were found to be consistent with shifted and scaled Gamma and Fisher's-z distributions, respectively. Generative methods were developed to simulate the logarithm of shower shape variables using Gaussian copulas. Copula sampling for shower shape parameters was found to produce superior modeling of heavy tails observed for the shower maximum and longitudinal shape parameter distributions when compared to direct sampling from a correlated multivariate normal distribution. A copula method was also devised to sample full shower events conditional on the shower shape parameters by exploiting the observation that the vector of energy fractions follows a logistic Log-Gamma distribution, the joint relation implied by the observed Fisher's-z form of the pairwise log-ratios. The generative model was evaluated using standard manifold and classifier metrics and was found to approach the data-versus-data ceiling. The fastest generation time was found to be around 30 {\mu}s per particle shower.

papers.title: Localizing spectra and pseudospectra of a class of unbounded operators on Hilbert space
papers.abstract: We use a localization technique to bound and approximate the spectrum and the pseudospectra of a certain class of possibly non-normal, generally unbounded but closed operators on $L^2(X)$, where $X$ is either a) a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group $G$, not necessarily Abelian, with identity, a proper metric, and a left Haar measure or it is b) a uniformly discrete subset of $G$ with the counting measure. We treat the discrete and continuous cases b) and a) simultaneously. Our results yield computable subsets and supersets of the pseudospectra of $H$ that converge to the corresponding pseudospectrum in Attouch-Wets distance as the size parameter $L$ in our localization procedure goes to infinity. We illustrate our findings with unbounded band operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$ and with Schr\"odinger operators with $L^\infty_{\rm loc}$ potentials acting on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$.

papers.title: Exact sequences of regular LF-spaces
papers.abstract: We show that the category of regular LF-spaces has all kernels but, unlike the category of regular LB-spaces, does not have all cokernels. Its topological exact structure, maximal exact structure and maximal deflation-exact structure form a strictly increasing chain of proper subclasses of the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs. To the best of the authors' knowledge, regular LF-spaces in particular provide the first natural example of a category that has all kernels but is not preabelian and whose maximal deflation-exact structure is neither two-sided exact nor equal to the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs.

papers.title: Low-degree hardness rules out eigenvalue tests but not eigenvector tests
papers.abstract:
We study what low-degree hardness implies for spectral tests, with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE) as the null distribution. We show that, once a fixed amount of Gaussian noise is added, it rules out every test based on eigenvalues, but not tests based on eigenvectors. For eigenvalues, if the low-degree advantage vanishes at logarithmic degree, then the joint law of the noisy eigenvalues converges to that of the GOE in total variation. For eigenvectors, we construct planted distributions with vanishing low-degree advantage whose eigenvalues follow the GOE law exactly at every noise level, yet whose noisy eigenvectors still distinguish them from the GOE. A single eigenvector can suffice. After a small amount of noise, a polynomial-time test that uses only the span of a fixed fraction of the top eigenvectors also succeeds, even when the low-degree advantage vanishes at a prescribed polylogarithmic degree.
  To prove the eigenvalue result, we split the noise into three increments. The first uses the low-degree assumption to establish eigenvalue rigidity. The second couples the two spectra through Dyson Brownian motion and applies homogenization to obtain a transport estimate. The third uses Gaussian smoothing to convert this estimate into closeness in total variation.

papers.title: On the Orthogonal Group of Quadratic Modules
papers.abstract:
We classify the conjugacy classes of isometries in the orthogonal group of regular quadratic modules over Artinian local rings with finite residue fields, provided that the characteristic is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry. (More generally, the same classification holds over Henselian local rings with finite residue fields, such as the ring of $p$-adic integers.) The main idea is to lift results over finite fields to local rings by using the Henselian property.
  By applying these results to the residue class rings $\mathbb{Z}/(p^l)$, we also obtain a classification of the conjugacy classes of isometries of discriminant forms, under the condition that the order of the discriminant form is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry.

papers.title: RIFT for the O4 era: operating points, calibration marginalization, and cross-code validation
papers.abstract: The Rapid Iterative FiTting (RIFT) parameter inference algorithm provides a simulation-based-inference approach to efficient, highly-parallelized parameter inference for GW sources. In this paper, we describe improvements deployed during preparations for and analysis of O4 observations (versions 0.0.17.3--0.0.18.0) that broaden RIFT's reach for single-event inference with contemporary instruments. We provide additional options to increase compatibility and comparability with other codes, notably including (a) enhancing RIFT's capabilities for calibration marginalization; (b) managing our likelihood's internal, output, and time-interpolated representation; (c) introducing new coordinates for (transverse) spin and eccentric mean anomaly, enabling more robust inference of parameters with subtle and complex correlations to others, and (d) revised operating point choices better suited to the loudest, clearest signals. We identify and reconcile the most substantial sources of head-to-head likelihood differences between RIFT and other production inference codes, and describe automated waveform symmetry checks that detect upstream model regressions before they bias inference. Using the previously-reported RIFT/asimov interface for reproducible settings consistent with past work, we demonstrate these capabilities end to end.

papers.title: A Head-Level Investigative Study of Self-Supervised Backbones for Synthetic Speech Detection
papers.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) speech backbones are the standard frontend for synthetic-speech detection, and layer-wise probing has established which layers carry the most signal. But analysis stops there: which of a layer's twelve attention heads compute the spoof decision is unknown. We present the first head-level study of two frozen backbones, WavLM-base and Wav2Vec2-base, on ASVspoof 5. Per-head ablation shows that only a few heads carry the decision while others actively oppose it; removing those heads lowers equal error rate (EER) with no retraining, by 13% relative in WavLM and 22% in Wav2Vec2. We also find a probe-free signature: spoofed speech draws more focused attention than genuine speech, and this gap alone separates the two almost as well as the full representation, peaking at each backbone's most discriminative layer. Finally, attack identity is decodable from every head, yet heads differ in what they do, not in what they know.

papers.title: DeltaRAE: Derivative Tokenization for Long Video Generation
papers.abstract: Latent video generators are trained on clips of a few seconds, and much of this limit lies in their tokenizers, which spend as many tokens on a static frame as on a moving one and need future frames that do not exist during generation. We introduce DeltaRAE, a causal representation autoencoder for video. Its derivative tokenization encodes periodic anchor frames in full and all remaining frames with a few tokens each, and its causal encoder and decoder read a frozen pretrained image encoder. On UCF-101 and Kinetics-600, a standard diffusion transformer trained on DeltaRAE latents is competitive with state-of-the-art video tokenizers. DeltaRAE halves the tokenizer GFLOPs on 16-frame clips relative to keeping the same number of patch tokens for every frame, and it represents a minute of video with 18.8x fewer tokens. The tokenizer trains end to end on one-minute videos, and in video prediction a generator on its latents produces a full minute of video. The same generator collapses within 15 seconds in most videos when the tokenizer has the same token budget but no pretrained encoder.

authors.name: Chengzhi Mao
authors.institution: Rutgers Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

authors.name: Yong Cheng
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Di Jiang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Exploring the Design Factors of Pixel-space Diffusion
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce EiT by exploring the key design factors of pixel-space diffusion from three perspectives: model architecture, representation, and frequency domain. Inspired by Denoising Autoencoders (DAE) which perform denoising through a bottleneck, we construct a U-shaped pixel diffusion transformer that performs explicit compression along the channel dimension. In terms of representation, we find that both pixel and latent diffusion transformers exhibit a three-stage representation dynamics across layers and timesteps: denoising/local feature expansion, basis lift-up, and posterior projection. Moreover, earlier denoising and a longer basis lift-up stage are associated with better generation, which EiT naturally achieves through its channel bottleneck and increased network depth. From the frequency perspective, we establish the equivalence between pixel-space and frequency-space diffusion when keeping the network operating in pixel space. On ImageNet $256\times256$ and $512\times512$, EiT consistently outperforms JiT (Just image Transformers) in generation quality. Specifically, our EiT achieves better FID than JiT: 1.61 vs. 1.85 at $256\times256$, and 1.73 vs. 1.99 at $512\times512$. Remarkably, EiT can be seamlessly applied to video pixel diffusion by simply extending the patch size to temporal dimension and outperforms video latent diffusion in FVD evaluated on Kinetics-600 (resolution 256), under comparable total network parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/forever208/EiT

papers.title: Over a Half-decade Study of Crab Giant Pulses Observed with I-LOFAR
papers.abstract: This work details the analysis of 1,048,138 single pulses from the Crab pulsar detected with the Irish LOFAR station over a 6-year observation campaign spanning 154 epochs and 347.9 hours at 110-190 MHz. Of the detections in the sample 550,445 are giant pulses (GPs, with S/N $\geq$ 10), making it the largest analysed sample to date. The power law indices for the S/N, flux density and fluence distributions range from 3.0-3.4 for the main pulse population and 3.3-3.5 for the inter-pulse population. A subset of 5,474 GPs (with S/N $\geq$ 100) were used to model scattering across the observing band to investigate the entanglement of dispersion measure (DM) and scattering. It was found that DM and scattering have a strong correlation coefficient of 0.70-0.71 across the entire campaign. Removing the long-term trend using a running median windowed at 125-190 days lowers the correlation to 0.48-0.50 respectively. The implications of these DM and scattering observations from the perspective of both the Crab Nebula's structure and the solar wind are discussed, including a rise in DM from August to October 2024 indicating AU-scale density variation consistent with fine substructure within Rayleigh-Taylor shaped filamentary ejecta.

authors.name: Aaron Golden
authors.institution: Ollscoil na Gaillimhe – University of Galway

papers.title: Same Tokenizer, Better Tokens: Choosing Image Tokens by MAP Inference
papers.abstract:
Discrete visual tokens encode images for reconstruction and serve as training targets for autoregressive image generators. Vector-quantized tokenizers typically assign each encoder feature its nearest code independently. The decoder uses these codes jointly, so a sequence of individually nearest codes can reconstruct an image less faithfully than an alternative assignment. A local model of the reconstruction loss yields a closest-vector problem with a decoder-dependent target and metric. Reconstruction-only search improves PSNR across the frozen tokenizers we test. Different code sequences can achieve similar reconstruction quality, leaving room to favour more predictable ones.
  We introduce RecaP (Reconstruction and Predictability), which selects codes for a frozen tokenizer by balancing how faithfully they reconstruct the image with how likely their sequence is under a pretrained autoregressive prior. On ImageNet, LlamaGen GPT-B trained on RecaP tokens achieves lower early-checkpoint FID against training images than GPT-B trained on nearest-neighbour tokens. The difference is smaller against held-out images. On an ImageNet subset, the prior improves generation at comparable reconstruction FID. Our code is available at: https://github.com/gmum/recap

papers.title: The Equational Theory of Rational String-to-String Functions
papers.abstract: We give a sound and complete equational axiomatisation of the rational string-to-string functions, which can be seen as a transducer counterpart of the classical axiomatisations of regular languages by Salomaa [JACM'66], Krob [TCS'91], Bloom and \'Esik [MSCS'93], and Kozen [IC'94]. The axioms are stated over a compositional, algebraic syntax for rational functions, namely the rational fragment of the syntax for regular functions introduced by Boja\'nczyk, Daviaud and Krishna [LICS'18]. The axiomatisation is finitary, as it consists of finitely many uniform families of axioms, each parameterised by the types involved. It is also purely equational: it consists only of equations, with no implication rules.

papers.title: A Real-Time Low-Cost Platform for Non-Contact Respiratory Rate Monitoring: A Comparative Evaluation of RGB Optical Flow and Time-of-Flight Depth Sensing
papers.abstract: Respiratory rate (RR) is one of the earliest indicators of clinical deterioration, which makes its continuous measurement clinically valuable. In routine practice, however, RR is monitored almost exclusively with contact-based sensors, which require skin attachment, may alter natural breathing, and are poorly tolerated by vulnerable groups such as newborns and elderly patients. Non-contact sensing removes these constraints, with RGB video and depth imaging among its most accessible modalities. In this work, we present a low-cost, real-time platform based on a single multimodal sensor that provides both RGB and time-of-flight (ToF) data streams, implemented on a Raspberry Pi 5 edge device. The system integrates three RGB optical-flow pipelines, namely Farneb\"ack, Horn--Schunck, and Lucas--Kanade, together with a depth-based pipeline incorporating region-of-interest stabilization and distance-derived signal extraction, enabling the two modalities to be evaluated independently under the same experimental protocol. The proposed approach was evaluated on twelve healthy volunteers following a controlled protocol, including normal breathing, hyperventilation, and breath-holding, using a piezoresistive respiratory belt as a reference. RGB-based methods achieved lower RR estimation errors, with Lucas--Kanade attaining the lowest median MAE (3.83 BPM), whereas the ToF-based pipeline, although less accurate for RR estimation (median MAE 6.24 BPM), reached a higher apnea detection sensitivity (0.66 vs 0.51-0.55). These findings highlight the complementary strengths of both modalities and support their integration into unified low-cost platforms.

papers.title: Electronic topological modes in hexagonal NbSi$_{2}$ with a double helix
papers.abstract: Chiral systems can host nontrivial topological states, including characteristic edge modes and Fermi arcs. Here, we investigate the electronic properties of hexagonal NbSi$_2$ with chiral symmetry using first-principles calculations for both bulk and slab geometries. We find that spin--orbit coupling (SOC) is relatively weak. Notably, the topological edge state originates from structural chirality rather than the SOC. From the Berry curvature analysis, we confirm the existence of Weyl points, some of which carry a Chern number of $\pm 2$. Furthermore, we demonstrate the existence of chiral edge modes with extended Fermi arcs around high-symmetry points. Finally, we investigate the real-space localization using spatially resolved and site-dependent density of states (DOS). We demonstrate that the surface states can be exclusively associated with the chiral Si chains.

authors.name: Issam Mahraj
authors.institution: Institute of Nuclear Physics, Polish Academy of Sciences

authors.name: Andrzej Ptok
authors.institution: Institute of Nuclear Physics, Polish Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Online Prediction System for Proactive Autoscaling
papers.abstract: We present an online learning system for short-term time series forecasting that enables proactive autoscaling in large-scale distributed systems. Unlike traditional forecasting methods that focus on modeling seasonality and long-term trends, the system targets high-accuracy, low-latency predictions for immediate future intervals for dynamic resource management in internet-scale infrastructures. The system employs a two-stage architecture: a seasonality decomposition stage followed by a residual correction stage using lightweight linear models with engineered features. By retraining models on-the-fly for every prediction cycle, the online prediction system continuously adapts to changing demand patterns without requiring persistent model storage or feature drift monitoring. Deployed across many heterogeneous services, the system processes over 900K predictions per hour; in an offline evaluation on production traffic, its STL-based configuration reduces prediction error (MAPE) by 18.6\% relative to the previous production model. In production, the system has saved an estimated 118K servers daily.

authors.name: Sumit Mohanty
authors.institution: Institute for Atomic and Molecular Physics

papers.title: Where Does the Asymmetry Enter? Staging a Fairness Audit Across a Fused Multimodal Moderation Pipeline
papers.abstract: Almost every short-video upload now passes through a classifier that fuses video, speech, and on-screen text into one decision about whether it may be seen. It moderates every language community on the platform at once, and fairness across them is judged, if at all, from one accuracy score. That score is compatible with error falling almost entirely on one language group. An audit that goes looking reads the model's decisions, the last stage of a long pipeline and the one whose test has the fewest items. We ask where in a fused pipeline a subgroup asymmetry can be detected at all: in what the classifier may read, in what its branches encode, or in what it decides. We answer this with a post-hoc audit of a published TikTok classifier, holding all three stages to one significance standard using only its logged decisions, labels, and pre-fusion features, with source language as the subgroup axis. The asymmetry is significant at the stage deciding what the model may read, and again in what the text branch encodes. At the earlier stage, a language-blind cap admits less of a Vietnamese clip than an English one, for reasons of segmentation, not verbosity. The asymmetry is undetectable at the decision, where the smallest subgroup leaves twelve items to test. An audit reading only decisions looks where its evidence is thinnest; the same test staged upstream recovers a disparity the decision-level view returns as noise.

papers.title: A Large Envelope Can Explain Super-Puffs
papers.abstract: Super-puffs are a class of exoplanets with extremely low bulk densities, having masses of a few to tens of Earth masses but radii comparable to that of Jupiter. Observations suggest that these inflated radii can persist for Gyr timescales, even for planets receiving relatively low stellar irradiation. The physical mechanisms responsible for maintaining such large radii, however, remain poorly understood. Here, we model the thermal evolution of super-puffs with substantial H/He envelopes using a one-dimensional planetary structure and cooling model. We follow the coupled cooling and contraction of the planetary interior and H/He envelope while self-consistently calculating the planet's hydrostatic and radiative--convective structure. We find that planets with H/He envelope mass fractions of approximately $40-60\%$ can retain Jupiter-like radii over Gyr timescales, provided that they begin with sufficiently hot interiors. Massive H/He envelopes substantially delay planetary contraction through two effects: (1) strong thermal blanketing, which slows the cooling of the underlying rocky core, and (2) Kelvin--Helmholtz luminosity generated by the cooling and contraction of the envelope itself, which helps maintain its high entropy and inflated radius. Our results suggest that super-puffs may represent a distinct class of planets that accreted large quantities of nebular gas during formation without undergoing runaway gas accretion.

papers.title: Orthogonal inference for machine learning forecasts
papers.abstract: Forecast comparisons inform investment and other economic decisions, but machine learning forecasts can be trained under objectives that differ from the relevant losses. Estimation error can then create spurious evidence of predictive superiority, even with out-of-sample evaluation. We establish feasible inference for differences in population evaluation risks in this setting. Building on locally robust estimation, we construct scores that preserve the risk target and remove first-order estimation sensitivity. Under geometric beta-mixing, moment conditions and simultaneous learning bounds, we establish Gaussian limits and consistent long-run covariance estimation for overlapping chronological training windows, allowing refitting at every evaluation date. Uniform extensions provide confidence coverage over classes of data-generating processes; Wald inference requires nondegenerate corrected-score covariance. For sparse linear forecasts and neural probability forecasts, we give explicit corrections and simultaneous learning bounds. Simulations with lasso and neural forecasts show substantial reductions in size distortion that bootstrapping uncorrected scores does not reproduce.

papers.title: Greedy Decoding Hides Good Plans: Sample-and-Verify Planning for Vision-Language Driving Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly adopted for end-to-end driving planning, yet their performance is typically evaluated based on a single greedily decoded trajectory. However, greedy decoding may overlook better trajectories within the model's output distribution. Experiments on WOD-E2E and NAVSIM reveal a consistent performance gap between greedily decoded trajectories and the best sampled candidates, showing that planning errors can arise from trajectory selection, rather than trajectory generation alone. On WOD-E2E, when the ego vehicle should start moving, the model often assigns probability to different possible start times, causing greedy decoding to repeatedly favor waiting and produce a stationary plan even though moving trajectories are available. Motivated by these findings, we propose Sample-and-Verify (SaV), which keeps the VLM planner frozen and samples multiple candidate trajectories. A lightweight verifier is trained from ground-truth futures to estimate the relative quality of these candidates. It uses trajectory kinematics, candidate-set agreement and likelihood, and ego-motion features to select the final trajectory. On WOD-E2E, SaV reduces ADE and FDE by approximately 15% across three VLM planners on the validation set. Changes in RFS are smaller: two planners show slight decreases on val-456, while Alpamayo-1.5 improves from 7.74 to 7.81 RFS on the official test set as ADE@5s decreases by 11%. On NAVSIM, SaV reduces ADE@4s by 10-24% across three VLM planners, while PDMS changes are less consistent. These results show that trajectory selection can substantially improve displacement accuracy without additional planner training. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/hzxbzp/sample-and-verify.

papers.title: Fine-Grained Ego-Vehicle Action Recognition from Driving Video
papers.abstract: Fine-grained ego-vehicle action recognition turns large-scale driving video into structured, searchable driving scenarios, providing a foundation for discovering critical maneuvers and systematically developing and evaluating autonomous driving models. However, large-scale driving videos often lack explicit ego-action labels, and existing datasets vary in action definitions, annotation granularity, and available supervision. We introduce EgoManeuver, a unified benchmark of 16 lateral and 6 longitudinal actions constructed from seven public driving datasets. Our multi-source labeling system leverages existing annotations and complementary evidence available in each source dataset, including vehicle signals, ego poses, HD-map topology, and captions, to assign labels under a unified fine-grained action taxonomy. We further standardize temporal action boundaries across datasets and validate the resulting labels through kinematic consistency checks and targeted human review. The resulting benchmark contains 86.6K segments spanning 190.8 h across 26 countries and provides a long-tail-aware evaluation protocol. We also introduce DenseEgo, a video-based baseline that combines spatially aware representations with dense per-step action supervision. On the EgoManeuver, DenseEgo achieves 82.7 lateral and 83.5 longitudinal mAP, outperforming the strongest existing video model by 1.5 and 5.0 points, respectively. Finally, we demonstrate one way to integrate DenseEgo with a language-model agent for retrieving driving videos that match user-specified actions and scenarios. All code, datasets, and model weights will be publicly released.

papers.title: k-Nearest Neighbors estimation of the drift of an ergodic diffusion process under Osgood regularity
papers.abstract: The k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) algorithm is a widely used machine learning method with well-established theoretical guarantees for consistent estimation in multivariate settings and functional time series analysis. In the context of nonparametric estimation of the coefficients of ergodic diffusion processes, however, its use has so far been mainly illustrated through numerical experiments. The main contribution of this paper is to establish theoretical consistency results for drift kNN estimators over both compact and non-compact intervals, under relatively weak regularity conditions on the coefficients of the underlying ergodic diffusion process. The theoretical results are completed with numerical illustrations.

authors.name: Eddy Michel Ella-Mintsa
authors.institution: Laboratoire d’Analyse et de Mathématiques Appliquées

papers.title: Decoder-as-a-Probe: Verbalizing and Steering Visual Representations in LVLMs
papers.abstract: It is commonly accepted that high-level concepts are represented linearly in the representation space of large neural networks. For Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs), finding those interpretable directions in visual representations is important for interpretability. To find them, the classical approach is to train a linear classifier on the representations, but it needs a large amount of labels and only recovers what can be read from the representations, not what the model actually uses. In this paper we start from the following insight: The LLM Decoder of an LVLM is also a classifier whose classes are the possible next tokens. So we use its first-order Taylor expansion as a linear classifier. Hence, we introduce Decoder-as-a-Probe (DaP), which significantly outperforms classical probing and steering baselines especially when training data is sparse. (1) It verbalizes what an LVLM perceives in a given image. (2) It can surgically change the perception of the LVLM about specific attributes (e.g. change only the color, the clothes worn or the action done). Due to its simplicity and data efficiency, we believe DaP can serve as a plug-and-play tool for LVLM research, such as interpretability, hallucination mitigation or instruction tuning.

papers.title: Rethinking Sequential Locate-Then-Edit: Optimality and Stability
papers.abstract: The Locate-Then-Edit framework enables efficient knowledge updates in large language models without requiring full retraining. Recent research has increasingly focused on sequential editing, where knowledge arrives continuously and the model is updated incrementally. However, existing sequential methods commonly suffer from catastrophic forgetting and model collapse after only a few hundred edits. In contrast, batch editing - which jointly optimizes all edits and yields the optimal solution under a specified editing objective - can support tens of thousands of edits with high edit efficacy while preserving the model's general capabilities, resulting in a substantial performance gap between the two editing paradigms. In this paper, we demonstrate that this gap can be closed via a batch-equivalent sequential editing approach. Moreover, we investigate the underlying mechanism of model degradation in existing sequential methods by analyzing the convergence behavior of weight perturbations as edits accumulate. Our analysis reveals that current methods typically exhibit linear or logarithmic growth in perturbation, whereas the proposed batch-equivalent method achieves time-invariant growth, thereby theoretically guaranteeing long-term stability and preserving the integrity of pretrained knowledge throughout massive-scale sequential editing.

papers.title: Riding the Wave: Sim-to-Real Humanoid Control on Elastic Terrain
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots on deformable elastic terrains face a surface whose position and motion are coupled in space and time: deflection and rebound persist between contacts, and load at one foothold alters the support at others, so training must capture how each contact changes the support that follows. We present RIPPLE (Robust Interaction via Proprioceptive Policies on Large-deformation Elastic terrain), a simulation-to-real learning framework for humanoid control on such terrains. RIPPLE integrates ElasticMembrane, a pretensioned mass-spring mesh that models spatially coupled deflection, energy storage, and rebound, together with deformable contact into MJLab for GPU-parallel policy learning. Staged training then transfers rigid-ground skills to balance and jumping on these terrains using only proprioception, without vision or force sensing. Deployed zero-shot, the policies enable a MagicBot Z1 humanoid to balance, jump consecutively, and enter a trampoline from a rigid platform. In simulation, ElasticMembrane training holds standing success of at least 98.7% (mean over three seeds) on ElasticMembrane, IndependentSprings, and BouncyPlate under 0.3 m/s perturbations, whereas rigid-ground or contact-compliance training transfers poorly to the first two. A fixed policy tolerates stiffness from 0.35 to 2.8 times the training value, beds up to 7 m wide, and seven further simulated support scenarios, so transfer needs no calibration to the trampoline's stiffness. We plan to release the code soon. The interactive browser demo, videos, and scene configurations are available on the project page: https://fly-pigTH.github.io/wave_rider/

authors.name: Bozhao Wang
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Certify What You Plant: Shortcut-Free Proof Depth in Logical Reasoning Data
papers.abstract: Procedurally generated logic problems are used to both evaluate and train reasoning in language models. Their difficulty is usually set by planting a proof, that is, by sampling a proof of the desired depth and stating its premises as the problem. However, a planted proof is only one possible proof. A problem can also have shorter proofs, or several unrelated ones, and its stated depth then overstates what solving it requires. We measure what a problem actually requires, relative to a stated set of inference rules. For each problem, we compute the steps every proof must make, the shortest proof, the number of minimal proofs and the indispensable premises, and export certificates that an independent checker verifies. Audits of eight datasets find depth that is forced (ProofWriter, Blocksworld), problems labelled depth 5 that require about two specific rule applications (FLDx2), and answers that need no particular step (ZebraLogic). We then construct problems whose every proof has a requested structure, using a catalog of shortcuts proved once per rule set. Every constructed problem is checked in full and comes with its own certificate. In training, the best data mixes depths and problem types. At equal size, such mixtures of certified problem types, including model-checking problems that forward generation does not produce, transfer better than FLDx2-style derivation data for Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 8B.
