papers.title: Co-amenability and local reflexivity of $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A\subset B$ be a unital inclusion of $C^*$-algebras. We prove that local reflexivity passes from $A$ to $B$ if the inclusion $A^{**}\subset B^{**}$ is co-amenable. It follows that local reflexivity is preserved by minimal tensor products with exact $C^*$-algebras, by inductive limits over directed sets, and by reduced crossed products by discrete amenable groups. We also prove that reduced free products with respect to states with faithful GNS representations preserve local reflexivity and that every locally reflexive $C^*$-algebra embeds into a simple locally reflexive $C^*$-algebra. These results answer Questions~(b), (c), (d), (f) and~(h) in Kirchberg's 2011 list.

papers.title: The Detour Is the Danger: Preserving Security During LLM Agent Recovery
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on external tools and reusable Skills to execute complex workflows, autonomously replanning when operations fail. However, such recovery may preserve task functionality while silently discarding the security protections required by the original workflow. In this paper, we investigate workflow security downgrade, a failure-induced security threat in which agents execute sensitive operations without satisfying their original protection requirements. Unlike prompt injection, this threat exploits autonomous recovery decisions triggered by execution failures, without modifying instructions or tool definitions. We systematically evaluate this behavior through fault injection in an executable MCP/Skill environment spanning seven LLMs, twelve task templates, and three security-sensitive domains. To address this threat, we propose ARGUS, an obligation-preserving recovery framework that combines resource-bound security evidence, isolated recovery-plan validation, and execution-time enforcement. In a separate 864-run evaluation, ARGUS prevents all observed protection-loss events under enforcement, while recovery assistance yields model-dependent improvements in protected task completion over blocking alone. Our findings demonstrate that secure agent recovery requires preserving security obligations across workflow changes, rather than merely restoring task functionality.

papers.title: PICE: Prototype-Informed Conditional Model Evolution Toward Self-Evolving Medical Image Recognition
papers.abstract: Medical image classifiers in clinical practice must continually evolve to accommodate emerging disease categories while maintaining reliable classification of existing conditions. This is challenging because privacy and data-sharing restrictions limit access to historical patient data, while assigning dedicated capacity to each new diagnostic task causes linear model growth. Effective evolution requires preserving prior disease knowledge without retaining historical images while expanding model capacity only when necessary. To this end, we propose PICE, a Prototype-Informed Conditional Model Evolution framework organized around what to preserve, when evolution is needed, and how that evolution is realized. PICE preserves prior disease knowledge in a prototype-statistical memory. For each incoming task, it assesses compatibility with historical references reconstructed from memory, reusing the closest adapter when compatibility is sufficient and instantiating a new one when evolution is required. PICE then realizes evolution by updating the memory and recalibrating the unified classifier with Gaussian pseudo features, thereby integrating new knowledge into the cumulative diagnostic space. During inference, memory-derived similarities guide task-agnostic adapter selection and fusion, enabling prediction over all learned disease categories. Experiments on Skin8, Kvasir-V2, and Path16 demonstrate the effectiveness of PICE across diverse clinical scenarios. On Skin8, PICE achieves a 7.60\% improvement in accuracy over the SOTA method on new tasks, while maintaining 71.10\% accuracy on previous tasks. It also reduces additional learnable parameters by 18.51\%. These results indicate that PICE improves classification while balancing knowledge retention, adaptation, and parameter growth, supporting continual model evolution as new diagnostic categories emerge without access to historical images.

papers.title: Welfare-Enhancing Mechanism Design for Agent Ecosystems
papers.abstract: The emerging Agentic Web forms a multi-agent ecosystem: a decentralized service market where the user agent selects which content agents to query from their submitted profiles, before seeing any documents. Profiles therefore become a new target of optimization. Existing Generative Engine Optimization studies how a single supplier rewrites documents the engine can already retrieve, to improve their citation. In the Agentic Web, multiple content agents optimize profiles to compete for limited opportunities to deliver documents. To study this repeated interaction, we build WildRegistry, a simulation framework and benchmark based on a real agentic-search request stream, and model it as a dynamic game under private monitoring. Long-horizon experiments show that this competition lowers website-selection quality and settles at a harmful stable point, which our empirical criterion identifies as an approximate rewriting equilibrium. We therefore design a welfare-enhancing mechanism, DEC (Delivery-Evidence Credit), a platform-side policy that uses recorded delivery outcomes to reallocate later opportunities and reduce information asymmetry. DEC improves this endpoint, raising website-selection quality while preserving most of providers' exposure gains, for a Welfare Gain of +2.01 points and a healthier long-horizon outcome. More broadly, our findings highlight the importance of mechanism design in agent ecosystems: turning recorded delivery outcomes into evidence that endogenously shapes later user-agent selection and content-agent adaptation can steer long-horizon adaptation toward delivered capabilities.

papers.title: Multi-Modal Causal Disentanglement for Multi-Domain Sequential Audio Recommendation
papers.abstract: Modern music platforms expose users to heterogeneous audio content domains such as songs, playlists, and podcasts. Multi-domain sequential recommendation (MDSR) seeks to exploit such cross-domain behavior, yet two obstacles persist in practice. First, joint optimization across heterogeneous domains is prone to negative transfer, with high-traffic domains dominating the shared parameter space and suppressing weaker domains. Second, conventional ID-based collaborative signals fail to bridge domains that are semantically related but exhibit little behavioral overlap. This paper presents CAMAR, a multi-modal causal disentanglement framework for multi-domain audio recommendation. From a causal perspective, user behavior is modeled as the joint outcome of a domain-invariant preference and domain-specific preferences. Guided by this view, CAMAR factorizes user representations into domain-invariant and domain-specific components and enforces domain adversarial invariance together with orthogonality, restricting cross-domain interaction to the invariant subspace and suppressing harmful transfer paths. To strengthen cross-domain semantic coupling, CAMAR derives trainable semantic-ID embeddings from pre-trained text, vision, and audio features through residual quantization, yielding an end-to-end multi-modal adaptation tailored to recommendation. A transfer network imputes user representations for inactive domains, mitigating cross-domain cold start. Experiments on both public and industrial datasets demonstrate consistent gains over strong baselines. In online A/B tests on NetEase Cloud Music, one of China's largest music streaming platforms, CAMAR delivers consistent gains across all three domains in their main traffic scenarios, validating its effectiveness in multi-domain audio recommendation at scale.

authors.name: Qiang Xiao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Dongjing Wang
authors.institution: PLA Rocket Force University of Engineering

papers.title: How Much Effort Does an AI Code Reviewer Need? Evidence from Claude 5.5 Models on Plausible-but-Wrong Patches
papers.abstract: AI coding agents write code faster than people can review it, so teams add AI reviewers. Reasoning models let such a reviewer trade cost for diligence through an effort setting. We asked how much effort a reviewer needs to catch plausible-but-wrong patches, which pass a benchmark's tests but fail stronger ones. Claude Opus 5.5 (preregistered), Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 (exploratory) each reviewed the same 90 agent-written Django patches from SWE-bench Verified at low, medium and high effort. By strengthened SWE-ABS tests, 55 patches were wrong and 35 correct. In every model, high effort accepted fewer wrong patches than low (false success .45 against .67 for Opus, .49 against .65 for Sonnet, .51 against .78 for Haiku), a supported difference for Opus and Haiku. For Opus, medium was non-inferior to high within 15 percentage points (difference .018, 95% CI [-.065, .108]) and cost 20% less, short of the preregistered 30%. For Sonnet and Haiku, medium cost 39% and 51% less than high but was not shown non-inferior. Opus at medium or high agreed best with the labels; Haiku at high cost about 8% as much per review as Opus at medium, accuracy difference unresolved. Exploratory coding showed that most rejections named the tested defect and that effort added such rejections. No setting is a strong gate: each accepted at least 45% of wrong patches. For 32 of the 55 wrong patches the issue may not require what the failing test checks; without them, neither accuracy hypothesis holds for any model.

papers.title: CariesBench: A Hierarchical Multi-view Benchmark for Dental Caries Screening and Diagnostic Reasoning from 3D Intraoral Scans
papers.abstract: Dental caries assessment is a structured clinical process requiring lesion localization, identification of the affected tooth and surface, and severity grading rather than simple image-level recognition. 3D intraoral scans (IOS) preserve detailed dental geometry and surface morphology and support standardized rendering from complementary viewpoints, enabling fine-grained visual assessment while introducing a distinct need for anatomically grounded multi-view reasoning. Despite recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and dental vision-language benchmarks, existing evaluations do not jointly assess hierarchical arch-to-tooth-to-surface reasoning, cross-view evidence integration, and surface-level caries assessment. To address this gap, we introduce CariesBench, a hierarchical benchmark constructed from 5,932 3D IOS, comprising 85,455 standardized multi-view renderings and 133,994 clinically grounded visual question answering instances with expert quality control. CariesBench comprises three complementary task families: Arch-level Clinical Screening (ACS), Tooth-level Diagnostic Reasoning (TDR), and Structured Clinical Decision-Making (SCD). Using the CariesBench training set, we further fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct to obtain IntraoralGPT. Extensive evaluation of 24 representative baseline MLLMs reveals a substantial benchmark-level performance disparity between arch-level screening and tooth-level diagnostic reasoning, with higher accuracy on ACS than on TDR. CariesBench-specific supervision substantially improves the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct baseline, increasing the 19-task macro-average clinical accuracy from 52.7% to 69.5% and TDR Overall from 34.4% to 44.7%.

authors.name: Shinan Zhang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Learning Temporal Stabilization for Double-Talk-Robust Delay Estimation in Acoustic Echo Cancellation
papers.abstract: Acoustic echo cancellation (AEC) depends on accurate time-delay estimation (TDE): the adaptive canceller converges only after the bulk delay between the far-end reference and the microphone is compensated. GCC-PHAT remains the standard TDE front-end and, in our stress tests, wins or ties against a fully learned estimator under interference, low SNR, strong reverberation, loudspeaker nonlinearity, and noisy references. Its principal failure mode is short-window sustained double-talk, where near-end speech creates spurious correlation peaks that classical smoothing and confidence gating cannot reliably suppress. We therefore retain GCC-PHAT as a fixed, non-learnable backbone and learn only a 13.2K-parameter causal 2-D CNN stabilizer over the time--lag correlogram. The stabilizer exploits a simple temporal distinction: true delays form persistent ridges, whereas double-talk artifacts appear as transient spikes. Across synthetic and real AEC-Challenge echo paths, it reduces MAE and gross-outlier rates by approximately $3$--$5\x$ over tuned classical estimators and the WebRTC AEC3 matched filter. A faithful AEC3-style downstream testbed further shows that these delay gains translate into lower echo-leak rates and faster post-jump ERLE recovery in time-varying regimes, closing much of the gap to the oracle-delay ceiling. An optional coarse-to-fine pre-alignment stage extends the same residual stabilizer to stable 100--400\,ms bulk delays without retraining, while keeping the learned component focused on short-window double-talk robustness.

papers.title: $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM: Efficient Hierarchical Memory Across Modalities and Timescales for World-Action Models
papers.abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires historical context, yet retaining extensive visual histories incurs growing storage and retrieval costs, while aggressive compression risks losing fine-grained information needed for subsequent decisions. Moreover, executed action histories capture intermediate behaviors that sparse visual observations may miss. Preserving this complementary context efficiently calls for modality-specific memory mechanisms that balance recent detail with long-term retention. To this end, we introduce $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM, a world-action model equipped with hierarchical visual and interaction memories. $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM preserves recent visual observations in dense short-term memory while consolidating entries evicted from this window into fixed-size associative long-term memory through gated delta updates. Within the same short- and long-term hierarchy, interaction memory encodes executed action prefixes into compact temporal representations, complementing visual observations with behavioral context. These complementary memories are integrated into world-action modeling through layer-wise retrieval, enabling memory-augmented action generation with a bounded online memory footprint independent of episode length. On the memory-dependent simulation benchmarks MIKASA-Robo and RMBench, $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM achieves +53.2% and +61.2% absolute improvements in average success rates over Fast-WAM, respectively. These gains extend to real-world manipulation, where $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM achieves a +29.3% absolute improvement over LingBot-VA in average success across three tasks. These results suggest that $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM offers a promising approach to efficient memory-augmented world-action modeling.

authors.name: Yueqi Hu
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

authors.name: Yin Zhang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme II: multi-frequency radiation transport
papers.abstract: Conventional discrete ordinate methods are widely used for thermal radiative transfer, but their fixed number of angular degrees of freedom (DoFs) incurs unnecessary computational cost near equilibrium. We therefore develop a nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme (NCUGKS) for multi-frequency radiation transport. The scheme preserves the mul tiscale capability of UGKS through interface evolution that couples transport and collision. Radiation intensity is expanded in an orthonormal basis of the discrete angular space. The expansion coefficients serve as angular DoFs, with their number adapted independently to local nonequilibrium in each cell, frequency group, and quadrant. At each time step, the coefficients to be evolved are selected using the exponentially decayed contribution from the previous step and the requirements of interface transport. The selected coefficients are advanced by the finite volume scheme and corrected to match the macroscopic radiation energy before higher-degree coefficients are discarded according to the prescribed relative tail tolerance. Therefore, in the optically thick limit, the resulting representation retains only one angular DoF per quadrant. Numerical tests spanning different optical regimes show close agreement with reference solutions, validating its accuracy. Furthermore, in terms of memory and computational efficiency, the proposed method reduces memory by factors from 21.7 to 154.0 and achieves speedups from 24.87 to 257.9 compared with the original discrete ordinate UGKS. NCUGKS thus provides the ability to accurately simulate multiscale ra diative transfer with reduced memory and computational costs. The proposed approach also offers a framework for adapting angular degrees of freedom in other discrete ordinate methods.

papers.title: A sparse bilinear form with mean oscillations
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish an oscillatory sparse domination for the bilinear forms associated with Calder\'on-Zygmund operators. We further characterize this oscillatory sparse domination in terms of either the boundedness of $T1$ or local endpoint Orlicz norm estimates. Our method also applies to recover Lerner's Sobolev-type inequality in \cite{L2026}.

papers.title: MMotion: Collaborative Cross-Scale Memory for Text-to-Motion Generation
papers.abstract: Text-to-motion generation aims to synthesize realistic human motions from natural-language descriptions, enabling applications in animation, virtual avatars, and embodied agents. Despite recent progress, existing methods either retrieve motion exemplars or retain long-range context, but rarely exploit memory to jointly reason about semantics, dynamics, and generation history. In this paper, we propose MMotion, a collaborative multi-scale memory framework that unifies scale-conditioned semantic retrieval, latent dynamics modeling, and causal working memory. Specifically, semantic memory provides motion priors at different generation scales, dynamics memory captures latent state transitions, and working memory preserves causal context from previously generated motions. A collaborative fusion mechanism integrates these complementary memories to determine what motion to generate, how it should evolve, and how it should remain consistent with its history. MMotion is architecture-agnostic and can be readily integrated into both diffusion-based and next scale autoregressive models. Extensive experiments across standard benchmarks and diverse backbones demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines.

authors.name: Zeming Liu
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Lili Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: MotionODE: Enhancing Autoregressive Text-to-Motion Generation with Continuous-Depth Modeling
papers.abstract: Autoregressive text-to-motion generation requires local motion predictions to reconcile cross-temporal textual requirements with the available motion context. While existing methods primarily improve motion representations and generation order, the internal formation of conditioned motion representations remains less explored. We introduce MotionODE, a continuous-depth post-training framework that refines hidden-state evolution in pretrained autoregressive generators. MotionODE reinterprets selected Transformer residual branches as local vector fields and replaces their original updates with midpoint Runge--Kutta (RK2) integration, while preserving the motion representation and outer generation mechanism. To address the mismatch between pretrained update paths and newly introduced intermediate states, we propose mixed one-step/two-step RK2 post-training under motion-token supervision, with optional distillation and update-map constraints to preserve pretrained behavior. This minimally invasive framework supports both next-token and next-scale generation without training the generator from scratch. Extensive experiments on HumanML3D demonstrate consistent improvements in text--motion alignment across MoScale, BAMM and LMR, highlighting internal representation updates as a complementary direction for improving autoregressive motion generation.

authors.name: Zeming Liu
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Lili Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Hybrid Reinforcement Learning for One-step Degraded Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
papers.abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion (IVIF) is essential for robust perception, yet existing methods remain limited under complex degradations. While diffusion models (DMs) offer powerful modeling capabilities to combat such degradations, their iterative process incurs high computational cost. One-step distillation effectively accelerates inference but typically leads to over-smoothed results. To resolve these limitations, we propose a one-step fusion framework with hybrid reinforcement learning, termed OneHRL. We treat degraded inputs as intermediate noisy states along a generative trajectory, enabling a distilled one-step generator to rectify them directly to the clean fusion results. Concurrently, to mitigate the over-smoothed results in distillation, we incorporate the Flow-GRPO paradigm to introduce stochasticity into the deterministic one-step generation. This restores the stochastic exploration necessary for sampling-based reinforcement learning. Furthermore, we design a coarse-to-fine reward that integrates a global semantic reward with an object-level reward. This hybrid reward ensures that the generator captures both naturalness and fine-grained texture. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior fusion quality and efficiency.

authors.name: Hongwei Yu
authors.institution: Research Institute of Petroleum Exploration and Development

papers.title: Cascading LO-phonon-mediated resonant energy transfer from excitons to Eu3+ for ultrahigh color purity red luminescence in europium-doped GaN
papers.abstract: High-efficiency, wavelength-stable red micro-LEDs with ultrahigh color purity remain a critical bottleneck for monolithic III-nitride full-color displays. Europium-doped GaN (GaN:Eu) offers a compelling solution, yet the microscopic energy transfer mechanism from the GaN host to Eu3+ ions has remained unresolved for three decades, impeding rational performance optimization. Here we report polaron-mediated resonant energy transfer in high-crystalline-quality GaN:Eu epilayers grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. Eu3+ doping stabilizes a distinct bound exciton (BX3) state at 3.478 eV, which couples strongly with longitudinal optical (LO) phonons via the Frohlich interaction to form cascading polarons with up to seven phonon replicas at a uniform energy spacing of 92.0+/-0.7 meV. The BX3 polaron coupled with 5LO phonons matches precisely the 7F0-->5D3 intra-4f transition energy of Eu3+ at 3.019 eV. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence reveals non-equilibrium phonon emission, evidencing directional resonant energy transfer. After rapid nonradiative relaxation from the 5D3 excited state to the 5D0 metastable state, the hypersensitive 5D0-->7F2 transition yields sharp 622 nm red emission. Time-resolved spectroscopy confirms a single dominant Eu3+ luminescent site with reduced local symmetry, attributed to off-axis EuGa-VN complexes. This work identifies a key energy transfer channel and provides a clear framework for designing high-efficiency GaN:Eu red emitter.

papers.title: RelPRM: Grounding Visual Process Reward Models in Relational Evidence
papers.abstract: Visual process reward models (PRMs) can detect calculation errors yet assign high scores to steps that misread visual relations. Supervision based on subsequent answer success does not directly establish whether a step's relational claim holds. To strengthen visual-relation verification, we first build an automated pipeline that programmatically verifies each claim and identifies the required objects, relations, and image regions. It produces RelProcessTrain and RelProcessBench (RPB), which tests whether scores respond appropriately to relational evidence through controlled image edits and step rephrasings. Building on this pipeline, we further introduce RelPRM, a visual-relation-oriented method for process reward modeling with two training mechanisms. Relation-evidence self-distillation constructs views preserving necessary objects, relations, and dependencies, reducing the burden of finding decisive evidence in complex scenes and transferring reliable evidence-assisted judgments to full images. Relation-evidence-driven consistency training encourages appropriate score changes when relation edits reverse a step's truth, stability under irrelevant edits, and similar score changes across paraphrases. At inference, RelPRM directly scores the current step using only the original image and reasoning context. RelPRM achieves 66.2% on VisualProcessBench (VPB) and 68.4% on RPB, gains of 4.2 and 9.9 percentage points over VisualPRM-8B. These results show that training for visual relations improves both relational verification and step assessment across broader multimodal reasoning tasks.

authors.name: Zhaoxing Zhang
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: False Positives and Innovation Incentives: Contracting for Noisy Experimentation
papers.abstract: In many data-driven organizations, employees propose product changes that are launched only after passing noisy online experiments, and their compensation is often tied to successful launches. Because even low-value features may appear successful by chance, such launch-based incentives can encourage agents to conduct experiments that reduce total surplus. We study this problem in a principal-agent model in which an agent with private knowledge about feature quality chooses whether to conduct a costly experiment and is compensated through an affine contract consisting of a launch-contingent bonus and a long-run value-sharing component, subject to limited liability. We evaluate each contract by the largest fraction of the principal's full-information payoff that it guarantees uniformly across the agent's private knowledge. Our analysis reveals a fundamental tension between experimental noise and limited liability in incentive design. Launch bonuses create incentives for false-positive experimentation by rewarding features that succeed by chance, whereas limited liability can render pure value sharing insufficient to implement socially efficient experimentation. Therefore, the optimal contract balances launch-contingent rewards and long-run value sharing according to the default feature quality, the degree of distributional uncertainty, and the severity of the limited-liability constraint.

authors.name: Nian Si
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
papers.abstract: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or failed pickup with ground-truth object pose, contact, and surface points. WorldReforge turns this ground truth into two training signals without additional inference cost. Interaction Alignment focuses reconstruction on the small object and contact regions that a global loss underweights, and Surface Correspondence trains backbone features to follow the same physical surface points across frames. On Cosmos3 Nano, WorldReforge reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall and by 35.0% on unseen objects, and it lowers the error in predicting how two actions' outcomes diverge by 43.3%. Although trained only in simulation, it also improves reconstruction on DROID and on real failure videos. Controlled data studies show that failed contact and successful holding teach complementary physics: failed contact teaches how objects respond, and holding teaches how a grasped state persists. Our code, data, and models are available at aim-uofa.github.io/WorldReforge/.

papers.title: Near Optimal Pure Stepsize Adaptation Acceleration for Gradient Descent on Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: Existing accelerated first-order methods for nonconvex optimization typically rely on momentum or extrapolation, requiring auxiliary vectors beyond the current iterate and gradient. On the other hand, memory-free stepsize scheduling alone can accelerate certain convex problems, while no guarantee exists for nonconvex problems. This paper closes this gap by proposing Nonconvex Adaptively Clipped Chebyshev (NACC) gradient descent method, which achieves near optimal acceleration while keeping the vanilla gradient descent update. NACC combines an adaptive selection of reversed fractal Chebyshev stepsizes with an epoch-wise clipping mechanism to control the aggressiveness of stepsizes. For nonconvex problems with Lipschitz continuous gradients and Hessians, we establish a near-optimal $\widetilde O(\epsilon^{-7/4})$ complexity. If the problem is convex in addition, then, without modification, NACC automatically achieves an $\widetilde O(\epsilon^{-3/4})$ accelerated complexity. Importantly, NACC guarantees the standard quadratic sufficient descent at every iteration, even when the stepsizes are substantially larger than the conventional choice. These monotonicity properties further facilitate practical implementations that adaptively adjust the estimated gradient and Hessian Lipschitz constants, demonstrating significant advantages in numerical tests against the existing nonconvex acceleration benchmarks.

papers.title: Policy and Value Iteration for Entropy-Regularized Stochastic Control
papers.abstract: We study finite-horizon entropy-regularized stochastic control with action-independent diffusion. To solve the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, we alternate between value and policy updates. Each iteration approximately solves a linear backward equation for the current policy, then approximates the Gibbs distribution defined by the resulting value gradient. We prove a uniform bound on the final policy's excess regularized cost. The bound assigns explicit, summable weights to the evaluation residuals and the Kullback-Leibler divergences from the updated policies to their Gibbs targets. Under the stated assumptions and with exact terminal data, vanishing errors in both steps imply uniform convergence to the optimal value. Two finite-horizon execution problems test value accuracy against a known solution and closed-loop performance when no exact solution is available. We also evaluate the iteration on a discounted infinite-horizon routing problem with twelve modes and an unregularized HJB benchmark in up to 10,000 dimensions.

authors.name: Ruizhe Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models via Agentic Model Editing
papers.abstract: Few-shot adaptation transfers pretrained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to new domains using a small set of labeled images. Most methods fit prompts, representations, or classifiers within an adaptation procedure specified in advance. Yet the visual distinctions needed for recognition can differ substantially across domains, motivating the question: Can an LLM agent use few-shot examples and model observations to design the adaptation procedure itself? We propose Agentic Model Editing (AME), an agentic framework that jointly designs input transformations, encoder edits, feature computation, and classifier fitting as an executable, domain-customized adaptation program. The agent inspects images, class semantics, model parameters, intermediate representations, and activations to formulate hypotheses about the target task. It implements and tests candidate programs on the support set, with aggregate validation accuracy guiding refinement and selection. Each program fits a complete domain model that is fixed before testing. The agent and its tools are shared across domains, while each domain receives its own adaptation program. Across eleven datasets with CLIP ViT-B/16, AME achieves the highest average accuracies of 81.2% without back-propagation and 81.9% with back-propagation among the compared methods. Further experiments demonstrate applicability across VLM backbones and LLM agents.

papers.title: A Simple Yet Effective Agent for Open-World Aerial Object Search
papers.abstract: Open-world aerial object search methods often rely on persistent spatial maps, learned world models, or task-specific policy training. To examine how far a minimal, training-free design can go, we introduce SimpleUAV, an agent built around a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM). SimpleUAV separates current-view target assessment from history-conditioned action selection, combining fresh candidate evidence with lightweight search context. Local geometry converts visual selections into bounded straight-line movements, depth-based checks halt blocked segments, and measured execution feedback guides subsequent decisions. This closed loop sustains search without persistent spatial maps or task-specific training. SimpleUAV achieves 41.61% Success Rate (SR) on UAV-ON and 11.98% on AerialDojo-200K, compared with 23.80% and 3.20% for the strongest prior baselines, respectively. With limited benchmark-specific adaptation, the same core agent transfers to aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) on TravelUAV, improving Full SR by at least 19.66% across all three splits under L1 assistance. These results establish a strong baseline for evaluating when additional architectural complexity benefits aerial search.

authors.name: Zhenyang Li
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jun Yu
authors.institution: National Clinical Research Center for Digestive Diseases

papers.title: Characterization and empirical correction of a spatially coherent spectral artifact in Gemini/GMOS-N IFU observations
papers.abstract: We report a recurring spectral artifact identified in observations obtained with the integral field unit (IFU) of the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph on the Gemini North telescope (GMOS-N). The artifact appears as a vertically aligned structure in reconstructed images of the IFU field of view, associated with a specific group of fibers and exhibiting a broad spectral feature around 8000~\AAng. Similar features were repeatedly identified in observations of different astronomical targets obtained between 2020 and 2022 using the R150 grating in the two-slit IFU mode. Taking advantage of the reproducibility of the artifact in the fiber and wavelength domains, we develop an empirical correction method in which the artifact is modeled as the product of a common spectral profile and a fiber-dependent amplitude distribution, with an overall normalization determined independently for each exposure. The artifact template is constructed from observations in which the affected fibers are largely separated from the astronomical source and subsequently applied to independent observations in which the artifact overlaps the source. The correction substantially suppresses the artificial spatial structure in the reconstructed images. Although the physical origin of the artifact remains unidentified, we present its observational characteristics and correction procedure to facilitate the identification and treatment of similar features by other GMOS-IFU users.

papers.title: CoordRoute: Coordinated Multi-Model Routing for Maximum Compute-Budget Utility
papers.abstract: Model routing sends each request to one of several large language models (LLMs) of different sizes. In practice, requests share a fixed compute budget: a spending cap on rented model APIs or the capacity of a private GPU cluster. Most existing routers do not account for the total budget: each decides a request on its own, so per-request optima are not optimal overall. We advocate coordinated routing, which allocates the budget across requests to maximize its utility, their total satisfaction, along a predict-plan-rectify route: predict what each model would give and cost, plan the choice against later requests, and rectify it during generation. Each step faces a challenge: a request's gain from each model is uncertain before generation, later arrivals are unknown when a request must start, and observing answers during generation consumes the budget itself. CoordRoute addresses them with relative demand prediction, which compares candidate models through past requests that lead to the same routing choices; a lookahead solver, which charges each choice for what its compute could earn for later requests; and budget-aware runtime correction, which drops or upgrades in-flight requests at the same price, inspecting answers only when it pays off. On Azure Conversation and BurstGPT traces, CoordRoute improves total satisfaction by 18.72% over the strongest existing router.

papers.title: Normal abelian subgroups of order 5^6 in finite 5-groups
papers.abstract: A finite 5-group containing an abelian subgroup of order 5^6 has a normal abelian subgroup of that order. If the given subgroup is elementary abelian, the normal subgroup can be chosen elementary abelian. This resolves n=6, the last open case of both parts of Problem~21.51 of the Kourovka Notebook for p=5. Together with earlier results, it follows that 1\le n\le 6 is the exact range in which each assertion holds for every finite 5-group at subgroup order 5^n. In a minimal counterexample, five conjugate abelian subgroups generate a group of class at most three. In class two we construct invariant isotropic subgroups for the commutator pairing. In class three the Jacobi identity produces a nonzero plane cubic over the field of five elements. The five conjugate subgroups give five distinct singular points spanning the plane, which forces the cubic to vanish.

authors.name: Baojun Li
authors.institution: North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: Text-Conditioned Low-Rank Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models for Multimodal Forecasting
papers.abstract: Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) provide transferable numerical forecasting priors. However, forecast-relevant information may be conveyed in text without being reflected in the observed series. Many multimodal forecasting methods integrate such context through model inputs or intermediate representations. We investigate a complementary mechanism: text-conditioned parameter adaptation. We propose Context-to-LoRA for Time Series (C2LoRA-TS), which encodes text and generates temporary Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) updates for selected weight matrices of a frozen TSFM. Both the numerical backbone and text encoder remain frozen, and the method exactly recovers the frozen TSFM output when context is absent. Evaluated on Time-MMD across nine domains and three TSFM architectures, C2LoRA-TS achieves lower aggregate forecasting error than the frozen-TSFM and Static LoRA baselines for every architecture and seed. Replacing the instance-specific text with a single globally fixed context degrades performance for every architecture. These results support text-conditioned parameter generation as a viable strategy for multimodal forecasting with frozen TSFMs.

authors.name: Kunqi Li
authors.institution: Inner Mongolia Academy of Agricultural & Animal Husbandry Sciences

papers.title: A Joint Functional Central Limit Theorem for the $L^p$-Norm Profile of Random Littlewood Polynomials
papers.abstract: For a random Littlewood polynomial $q_n(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\varepsilon_jz^j$ with independent Rademacher coefficients, let $S_n(\theta)=|q_n(e^{i\theta})|^2/n$ be its normalized angular intensity. Its positive moments $T_n^{(p)}=\|q_n\|_p^p/n^{p/2}$ form the moment profile of the intensity distribution under normalized arc measure on the unit circle. We prove a joint functional central limit theorem for this profile. For $p$ in a compact interval $K\subset(0,\infty)$ and logarithmic time $n=\lfloor Ne^t\rfloor$, $t\in[-T,T]$, the piecewise linear interpolations of $\sqrt n(T_n^{(p)}-\Gamma(1+p/2))$ converge to a Gaussian field $G(p,t)$ in $C(K\times[-T,T])$. The corresponding step processes converge in $D([-T,T];C(K))$ with the Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. The limit has the representation $G(p,t)=\sum_{a=2}^{\infty}c_a(p)G^{(a)}(t)$, where $c_a(p)$ are the ordinary Laguerre coefficients of $x^{p/2}$, with $L_a(0)=1$. The independent centered stationary Gaussian modes have covariance $\mathrm{Cov}(G^{(a)}(s),G^{(a)}(t))=2V_a e^{-(a-1/2)|t-s|}$, where $V_a$ is the squared $L^2$-norm of the density of the sum of $a$ independent uniform random variables on $[0,1]$. We also obtain the functional limit theorem for $\|q_n\|_p/\sqrt n$ and identify its joint covariance. At $p=4$, we recover the known scalar autocorrelation fluctuation law and identify its dependence across nested lengths. Finite-mode convergence follows from the multivariate functional de Jong theorem after model-specific variance, influence, and fourth-moment calculations. Maximal estimates control the infinite Laguerre tail and its exponent derivative uniformly over nested lengths.

authors.name: Xiang Fang
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: AIRIS: Benchmarking Social Embodied Intelligence in Egocentric Streaming Videos
papers.abstract: Embodied agents operating around people must not only recognize social cues, but also decide when the available evidence is sufficient, whether to intervene, and how to respond without violating social norms. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate these abilities in isolation or with access to completed videos, obscuring where an online social decision fails. We introduce AIRIS, a causal streaming benchmark that formulates social embodied intelligence as a time-anchored chain of Attention, Intention, Reaction, and Interaction (A-I-R-I). AIRIS contains 8,000 expert-curated questions grounded in 357 egocentric clips across 11 context categories and 36 capability dimensions. At each query, models receive only the observation prefix available at that time; decision-aware metrics reward calibrated waiting and complete reactions while penalizing premature commitment. Evaluating 45 proprietary and open-source general-purpose, embodied, streaming-video, and omni-modal models reveals fragmented and temporally miscalibrated competence. General-purpose VLMs excel at passive cue grounding and intent recognition, whereas embodied specialists lead on isolated reaction sub-decisions; yet across all families, models frequently guess intents before sufficient evidence emerges and fail to jointly align intervention timing, action domain, and concrete execution within the same episode. AIRIS thus provides a diagnostic foundation for bridging the gap between passive social perception and reliable embodied interaction.

authors.name: Jiayu Tang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

papers.title: HoloBrain-0.5 Technical Report
papers.abstract:
We present HoloBrain-0.5, a family of vision-language-action (VLA) models for manipulation across robot embodiments. The policies plan in a shared action space using robot state, kinematic structure, and calibrated camera observations. We standardize joint axes, coordinate frames, and tool-center points in robot descriptions (URDFs) and encode their kinematic graphs in a shared 3D representation. HoloBrain-0.5-Continuous generates action chunks by diffusion, while HoloBrain-0.5-Discrete uses residual finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and delayed autoregression. We pretrain both policies on over 10,000 hours of real-robot, simulation, and human-manipulation data spanning 15 embodiment categories.
  Across six closed-loop simulation settings, the discrete policy converges faster and reaches a higher mean success rate than the continuous policy (56.77% vs. 49.71%). On seven real-robot tasks, it achieves a mean progress score of 87.76% without task-specific post-training. After post-training, the continuous policy outperforms $\pi_{0.5}$ on the seven-task benchmark (94.52% vs. 86.25%) and an 11-task dual-arm benchmark (79.07% vs. 69.41%). The discrete-initialized continuous policy transfers five tasks zero-shot from Piper to Piper-X, scoring 63.28% on average. With target-robot demonstrations, the continuous policy scores 89.2% on Franka Panda and 92.94% on a mobile dual-arm platform. Although pretraining includes no Unitree G1 data, post-training with limited G1 demonstrations yields a mean progress score of 70.24% across three humanoid tasks, compared with 11.00% for $\pi_{0.5}$.

papers.title: Decision-Aligned Value Learning for Selective Adoption of EEG Fusion in Human-Robot Collaboration
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) captures neural activity associated with human perception and decision-making. It provides human-robot collaboration (HRC) systems with measurable evidence for event recognition, situation assessment, and action preparation. External sensing cannot easily provide such evidence. However, the quality and complementarity of this evidence vary across samples, and existing EEG fusion methods do not explicitly determine when EEG improves a prediction. We therefore framed selective EEG use as a sample-wise incremental-value estimation problem and proposed Value Estimation and Constraint-Aware Triage for Adoption (VECTA). VECTA separates the generation of an EEG-informed Fusion prediction from the decision about whether it should replace the existing Base prediction. The framework uses system gain to quantify the loss reduction from Base to Fusion and matching gain to assess whether benefits arise from sample-matched EEG. A signed-value learner estimates system gain from decision-time evidence and prioritizes high-value Fusion outputs under budget constraints. Cross-subject evaluations on three HRC datasets showed that matched Fusion outperformed shuffled controls. Estimated gains tracked realized gains, with Spearman correlations of 0.347-0.612 and positive-gain areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.708-0.842. Under budget constraints, VECTA reduced Brier loss and harmful Fusion adoption and achieved the highest mean normalized AUBC across three datasets among the selective-decision methods evaluated. Validation on three external multi-modal datasets showed that VECTA could be applied directly as a post-hoc decision layer to task-specific predictors without retraining. These results show that selective Fusion adoption can translate the uneven utility of EEG into system-level gains.

authors.name: Tielin Shi
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Digital Manufacturing Equipment and Technology

papers.title: Magnetic Reconfiguration Controls Spin Splitting and Spin-Orbit-Coupled Responses in Compensated Magnets
papers.abstract: Compensated magnets provide a versatile platform for spin-dependent electronic and transport phenomena. Here, we show that magnetic reconfiguration, i.e., selective reversal of local moments without changing the underlying crystal structure, can profoundly transform the nonrelativistic spin splitting and spin-orbit-coupled responses of spin-degenerate antiferromagnets (AFMs), altermagnets (AMs), and compensated ferrimagnets (cFIMs). Strikingly, magnetic configurations with nearly degenerate energies can exhibit qualitatively different spin-split band structures and anomalous Hall responses, allowing a small magnetic-energy scale to produce large changes in physical properties. Combining tight-binding models, oriented spin space group analysis, and first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that converting an AM configuration into cFIM states activates staggered onsite-potential contributions to spin splitting, complementing the anisotropic-hopping mechanism of AMs and removing symmetry-enforced degeneracies. Moreover, cFIM symmetry permits an anomalous Hall response at first order in spin-orbit coupling, in contrast to the higher-order or orientation-constrained responses of corresponding AM states. We demonstrate this regime in Mn2Mo3O8, one of 12 cFIM candidates identified in the MAGNDATA database, and further demonstrate its generality by designing cFIMs from collinear AFMs, exemplified by MnGeO3 and Co2Mo3O8. Our results establish magnetic reconfiguration as a powerful symmetry-guided strategy for dramatically reshaping electronic and transport responses in compensated magnets.

authors.name: Zehao Ji
authors.institution: Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Nonpolynomial entire solutions of the special Lagrangian equation with critical phase
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct smooth nonpolynomial entire solutions of the special Lagrangian equation with critical phase $(n-2)\pi/2$ for every $n\ge4$. Together with the nonquadratic example in dimension two and Warren's example in dimension three, our construction shows that the supercritical condition $|\theta|>(n-2)\pi/2$ in the Bernstein theorem proved by Yuan is sharp in every dimension $n\ge2$.

papers.title: Sharp entanglement and decay thresholds for fractional elliptic operators
papers.abstract: We establish sharp entanglement principles for fractional powers of uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators $L$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge 2$, with smooth real symmetric coefficients. Let $u_1,\ldots,u_N$ and the sum $\sum_{k=1}^N L^{s_k}u_k$ vanish on a common nonempty open set. Assuming that $L$ coincides with the Laplacian outside a compact set, we prove that root-exponential decay of these functions forces every $u_k$ to vanish globally, under sharp dimension-dependent conditions on the fractional orders $s_k$. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal within the stretched-exponential scale, and the sharp logarithmic endpoint is $e^{-a\sqrt{r}/\log r}$ in every dimension. Our approach relies on a novel resolvent characterization of entanglement, which we use both to separate the fractional orders at zero energy and to construct exact cancellations from outgoing waves. For perturbations extending to infinity, this wave construction yields two-dimensional counterexamples with smooth compactly supported inputs and coefficient fields converging to the identity in every fixed unweighted $C^k$ norm. Finally, for a known underlying operator, a single exterior measurement determines the number, orders, and coefficients of the fractional terms, together with a continuous potential.

papers.title: ADClaw: A Programmable Visual Agent for Industrial Anomaly Detection and Understanding
papers.abstract: Industrial anomaly detection (IAD), the task of identifying and localizing deviations from normal product conditions, is essential to automated quality inspection in manufacturing. Many vision-language models for IAD rely on large domain-specific datasets for fine-tuning and make predictions in a single pass, leaving no opportunity to re-examine ambiguous regions. Although tool-using agents can revisit these regions, predefined tool interfaces limit how they can combine intermediate results in a follow-up check. When such checks are insufficient, models may miss subtle defects or misidentify the defect type. To address this limitation, we introduce ADClaw, an inspection agent that uses executable code to test anomaly hypotheses without task-specific fine-tuning. For each hypothesis, a Structured Normality Prior identifies the applicable rules and retrieves normal visual references for the inspection target. Guided by this prior, the agent writes and executes code in a persistent Inspection Workbench to combine masks, anomaly maps, and measurements from earlier steps into a new test of the suspected defect. After each check, Hypothesis-Guided Evidence Reasoning assesses whether the evidence supports the suspected defect and its location, using gaps or inconsistencies in that evidence to guide the next code action. ADClaw achieves competitive results in detection and localization across 2D and 3D industrial anomaly detection benchmarks and in anomaly understanding on MMAD.

authors.name: Chu Li
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University

papers.title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning has achieved remarkable success in sequential decision-making, but learning effective policies often requires substantial interaction experience. Model-based reinforcement learning alleviates this dependence by leveraging world models, which are typically used to support planning or policy optimization. In this paper, we investigate an alternative paradigm in which autonomous LLM-based coding agents directly synthesize control policies by reasoning over readable world models. By examining environment source code, these agents translate environmental knowledge into executable decision rules and iteratively refine their policies using online feedback or offline data, without task-specific RL training. Experiments across diverse decision-making benchmarks show that synthesized policies match or outperform conventional RL methods while requiring substantially less experience. Further analyses reveal interpretable decision rules and how they evolve through feedback-driven refinement. Comparisons with policies generated without source code access and experiments under challenging conditions further demonstrate the benefits of readable world models. These findings suggest that direct policy synthesis can reduce reliance on trial and error, challenging the necessity of task-specific RL training.

papers.title: Who Fills the Gap? Role Similarity and Teammates' Minutes When NBA Players Are Ruled Out
papers.abstract: When a core player is ruled out before an NBA game, do teammates whose statistical role resembles that of the removed set (every rotation player ruled out, about three per case) play more? Using injury reports stamped at least six hours before tip-off and rosters reconstructed after the season, we study 2,441 team-games from 2023-24 to 2025-26 in which a core player was ruled out for a medical reason. Among teammates in the same game, one within-case standard deviation more similarity in role profile (three-point attempts, assists and rebounds per minute) goes with about 0.63 more minutes, holding reference minutes and headroom fixed (p < 0.0001); this compares teammates within a game, not the minutes gained because of the absence. The pattern holds in two earlier seasons and in exploratory within-player and without-and-with comparisons. Whether similarity adds to listed position is not settled. The association is small and yielded no statistically detectable reduction in the error of the retrospective minute forecasts we tested. Role coverage, how much of the missing minutes and roles the remaining rotation could restore, showed no consistent incremental association with team role output or the final margin.

papers.title: DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target's Sparsity
papers.abstract: To avoid the quadratic cost of dense attention over long contexts, models such as DeepSeek-V4 and Hy4 have turned natively sparse, and speculative decoding, which matters most where decoding is slowest, increasingly runs on them. Their drafters, however, still keep a context cache of their own, over the whole prompt or a sliding window. Beyond memory, such a cache costs prefill time, prefix-cache hits and decode concurrency. Drafters that read the target's cache avoid one of their own, but settle only which cache, not which positions, and still read everything or a recent window. Neither rule is made for the query at hand, and computing a selection per query in the drafter would cost more as the context grows. Yet a natively sparse target already picks positions for each query, over a cache it keeps anyway. Both of the drafter's choices are therefore already made, and paid for, by the target: its cache and its selection. We measure how far one selection carries: made a step early, it still covers close to nine tenths of what each later token selects on DS-V4.1-Flash. We present DFly2, a block-parallel drafter that shares the target's sparsity. Each draft layer reads the KV its paired target layer cached (KV sharing), at the positions that layer's indexer selected, a fixed number anywhere in the context (Index sharing). DFly2 thus runs no scoring pass and keeps no cache of its own. On DS-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash and Hy4~flash, whose sparse attention and architecture differ, it accepts more tokens per step than DFlash and DSpark trained on the same recipe, over general, long-context and agentic benchmarks. Its margin over the stronger baseline widens from 3.9%-10.5% on general workloads to 10.0%-31.5% on long-context and agentic ones. At high concurrency on DS-V4.1-Flash, at matched per-user decode speed, its throughput is 62% and 81% higher on two 64K sets.

papers.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
papers.abstract: Video generation models are increasingly evaluated as visual reasoners: given a first frame and a natural-language prompt, can the model produce the video in which the specified task is carried out? The paradigm is considered advantageous because the reasoning is native to the visual medium, unfolding directly in the frames rather than through language or code. Whether this native route is in fact the more reliable path to visual reasoning has not been tested against a symbolic alternative under the same conditions. We therefore pose the same tasks, with identical inputs, output specification and evaluator, to both media: rather than denoising pixels, a coding agent writes a program that renders the answer video, which an unmodified rule-based evaluator scores. On VBVR-Pro-Bench (Xu et al., 2026), a 500-instance suite spanning five cognitive categories with symbolic ground truth, the agent receives the same first frame and prompt as the video model, with no access to ground truth, metadata or generation models, and one attempt per instance. Three closed-model agents (Codex with gpt-6-astra, Claude Code with Fable 5.1 and Gemini CLI with Gemini 3.1 Pro) score 0.923, 0.894 and 0.893, each more than 0.22 above the strongest video model. Among 23 runnable open-weight models, the best, GLM-5, reaches 0.572, above all video models except the RL-trained one. Together, we show that for tasks whose solutions can be computed from a first frame and a prompt, program synthesis is currently a substantially more reliable route to visual reasoning than video generation. We further distinguish depictive programs, which navigate the image to recover a transferable scheme, from propositional programs, which operate on hard-coded values, revealing how visual reasoning unfolds in agent-written programs and what it implies for its nature of reasoning in general.

authors.name: Siyuan An
authors.institution: China Coal Technology and Engineering Group Corp (China)

papers.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
papers.abstract: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions. Existing benchmarks assess report quality along several dimensions, but lack a dedicated knowledge-centric evaluation of which research directions a report covers and how deeply it explores them. We introduce DRBench Pro, a benchmark that makes structured knowledge coverage the primary evaluation target. Our automated pipeline builds local knowledge trees from Wikipedia and uses sampled subgraphs to generate research queries and evidence-grounded rubrics. Each rubric corresponds to a relation in the tree, preserving the structure of the knowledge being evaluated. Agents receive only the research query. This structure allows us to measure breadth across major research directions and depth along related knowledge chains, with their geometric mean giving overall coverage. The benchmark includes 144 cases across 24 domains and 44,102 rubrics. Evaluating 16 deep research agents reveals different strengths in breadth and depth, with the best-performing agent reaching 57.04% overall coverage. Rubric judgments agree closely with human annotations, and agent rankings remain stable across the tested metric configurations.

authors.name: Jie Liu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jin Ma
authors.institution: State Grid Shanxi Electric Power Company (China)

papers.title: One Ocean, Many Tasks: A Data-Grounded Simulation Suite and Benchmark for Marine Robotics
papers.abstract: Simulation is essential for marine robotics, yet existing platforms often trade off between visually realistic worlds, high-throughput experimentation, and ocean-condition realism grounded in real data. We present OneOcean, a data-grounded simulation suite and benchmark built around a unified spatiotemporal ocean-environment product that harmonizes bathymetry with data-driven currents and tides, with optional pollution fields for cleanup-related evaluation. On top of this environment representation, OneOcean defines a task ladder spanning navigation and station-keeping under currents, waypoint and route following, depth-profile tracking, area scanning, pipeline inspection, and multi-agent coordination, including formation transit, fish protection and patrol (herding), and surface pollution localization, containment, and cleanup. The suite supports multi-agent settings with 2-10 vehicles. Our simulator supports three to six Degrees of Freedom (DoF) and produces standardized metrics and reproducible run manifests, enabling consistent aggregation across tasks, difficulties, and scaling settings. Experiments across dataset variants and scenes systematically stress planning and control under data-grounded disturbances and reveal trade-offs among heuristic baselines, Behavior Cloning (BC), and a Large Language Model (LLM)-based planner.

authors.name: Xingwei Chen
authors.institution: State Grid Henan Electric Power Company (China)

papers.title: Point Equivalence, Lie Symmetries, and Laurent Compatibility of the Time-Dependent Modified Dispersive Water-Wave System
papers.abstract: We classify local point transformations between members of the \((2+1)\)-dimensional modified dispersive water-wave class with two nowhere-zero real-analytic time-dependent coefficients. A change of time reduces the class to a single coefficient \(q\). An invertible differential substitution identifies this class with a slice of a previously classified coupled system and supplies a family of point maps. A direct calculation in the original field variables proves that the induced coefficient action \(\widetilde q(F(T))=q(T)/k\), with \(F'>0\) and \(k\ne0\) constant, exhausts all local point identifications. The order and relative sign of the first nonzero derivative classify nonconstant pointed coefficient germs. Constant germs admit arbitrary time generators, regular nonconstant germs admit one independent time generator modulo the zero-time-component subalgebra, and critical nonconstant germs admit none through the base time. On movable analytic hypersurfaces with \(\phi_x\phi_y\ne0\), the double-pole and regular-\(V\) Laurent branches both have an obstruction at resonance \(j=2\) proportional to \(q'\). Both branches are formally compatible exactly for constant \(q\), which is also the precise criterion for point equivalence to the standard system.

papers.title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
papers.abstract: Initialization determines the optimization "fate" of a model, going far beyond just setting the scale of its weights. It establishes a fundamental initial geometry over the input data, dictating certain aspects such as which examples are considered close and which representations gradient descent will naturally refine first. In this paper, we view the initial geometry of a network as an optimization prior and ask whether a network can change its optimization prior by referencing a completely different architecture. To investigate this question, we use an initialization procedure where a target network is aligned to the representational geometry of a randomly initialized guide network before any downstream training occurs. Crucially, alignment to the guide network cannot transfer learned features, never receives gradients, and does not use labels. We demonstrate that this cross-architecture transfer of "fate" benefits the target network in two key domains: (1) instilling the optimization benefits of depth into shallow networks by aligning them to deeper networks, and (2) transferring representational granularity by using fine-resolution networks to shape the geometry of networks with coarser representations. In both cases, the alignment results in improved downstream performance of the target network. Ultimately, this demonstrates that a model's architectural destiny can be decoupled from its physical structure and explicitly modified at initialization.

authors.name: Vighnesh Subramaniam
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

papers.title: Neighbor Crowding Predicts Feature Stability in Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) offer an approach to identify language model representations by breaking apart polysemantic features into more sparse, interpretable ones. Yet, it is challenging to identify which of the learned features are actually stable, rather than artifacts of initialization. One approach is to train multiple SAE seeds, and compare the learned features across seeds by cosine similarity, but this is notably costly. This raises the question of whether stable features can be identified without the computational expense of training multiple seeds. In this work, we examine cross-seed feature stability across differing levels of training tokens, and demonstrate that in TopK SAEs, it is highly predictable using six computationally cheap statistics derived from a single training run. Neighbor crowding, a geometric property of the dictionary, is the strongest single predictor, with features that sit in dense regions of the unit sphere more likely to be stable than isolated ones.

authors.name: Naveen Dasari
authors.institution: International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad

papers.title: Silent on Code? A Computing Lens on Generative AI Guidance at Canadian Polytechnics and Research Universities
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools now write, explain, and debug code, which changes how computing students learn and how their work is assessed. Instructors, however, act within institutional guidance written largely with essays in mind. We report a document analysis of the public, institution-level GenAI guidance of the 13 members of Polytechnics Canada and the 15 members of the U15 Group of Canadian Research Universities, retrieved in October 2026. Using a 27-item codebook spanning governance, integrity and assessment, data and legal issues, values, AI literacy, and a computing lens, we find that both sectors leave course-level decisions to instructors, although polytechnics more often prohibit use unless the instructor permits it (8 of 13 vs. 4 of 14), and converge on disclosure, links to academic integrity policy, and, in most institutions, the expectation that programs adapt rules to their discipline. Polytechnics frame GenAI as workforce preparation substantively far more often (7 of 13 vs. 0 of 14), whereas universities more often address assessment redesign. Twelve of 27 institutions with retrievable guidance mention code, but almost always as one output type among many; none names an AI coding assistant or provides substantive code-specific guidance on attribution, assessment, or licensing. Institution-level guidance is thus not silent on code but leaves programming-specific questions largely to programs and instructors. We propose five elements of discipline-level guidance for computing and release our codebook and coded dataset.

papers.title: Extraneous Cognitive Load in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) shows that human problem-solving is affected by both intrinsic load, arising from task difficulty, and extraneous load, arising from how task information is presented. Large language models (LLMs) show analogous effects: presentation alone can affect model performance, but these effects have not yet been systematically isolated from task difficulty. To address this gap, we introduce CogLoadBench, a controlled benchmark that varies five CLT-inspired presentation factors across three reasoning task families. Across models, we find that higher extraneous load conditions often reduce accuracy by either adding competition or complicating the reasoning path. To support diagnosis and mitigation of load-related effects, we propose the Extraneous Load Score (ELS), a prompt-time metric computed from activations that estimates a model's extraneous load, and show that it generalizes across reasoning task types and load levels. We further show that shifting model representations toward lower-load directions at inference time can improve average model performance without changing prompt content.

authors.name: Arushi Gupta
authors.institution: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar

papers.title: Crossed homomorphisms on Leibniz superalgebras
papers.abstract: In this article, we give characterisation of crossed homomorphisms of Leibniz superalgebras as Maurer-Cartan elements of an associated graded Lie algebra. This characterization enables us to develop a cohomology theory for crossed homomorphisms and to apply it to their formal deformation theory. We show that the infinitesimal of a deformation is a 1-cocycle and that linear deformations are classified by such cocycles. Furthermore, we introduce the category of crossed homomorphisms between two fixed Leibniz superalgebras.

papers.title: Repairing the Trustworthiness of Distilled Language Models
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation enables the deployment of large language models through smaller student models, but the compression process can introduce regressions in trustworthiness even when downstream performance is preserved. Repairing such failures is challenging because the original distillation corpus is often unavailable, while direct preference optimization may alter capabilities inherited from the teacher. We propose a targeted repair framework based on the proximal Bregman response function (PBRF) that addresses both limitations. We estimate the curvature required for PBRF using a surrogate proxy dataset, removing dependence on the original transfer corpus, and extend the framework to preference-based supervision through an odds-ratio objective. This enables the use of preferred and dispreferred response pairs while constraining changes to the distilled model. Our results show that the proposed approach improves targeted trustworthiness behaviors for both pre-training and post-training models while largely preserving downstream performance, providing a practical alternative to re-distillation or unconstrained preference optimization. Our experiment results show that across different distilled models, the trustworthy regression can be improved by up to 8% with less than 1% decrement in perplexity.

papers.title: FreshVLA: Frequency-Regularized Time Scale Hierarchical Latent Actions for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Learning reusable latent actions from action-free videos offers an effective route to improving Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies. However, reconstruction-oriented latent actions do not necessarily benefit policy learning: as they may encode task-irrelevant static appearance with scene identity, or entangle slowly varying task progress with fine-grained execution dynamics in limited discrete code. We propose FreshVLA, a VLA framework built on a frequency-guided, dynamics-sensitive learning paradigm for acquiring temporally hierarchical continuous latent actions. FreshVLA uses a high-pass prior to guide visual transition encoding toward dynamical regions, thereby reducing reliance on static appearance cues. It further organizes latent actions into coarse-grained task progress and fine-grained execution dynamics through cross-timescale sampling and frequency-domain regularization, enhancing their capacity to represent long-horizon behaviors. During policy training, we freeze the pretrained latent action encoder and transfer its representations to robot control through joint flow-matching of latent and robot actions. FreshVLA achieves 98.2% average success on LIBERO and 98.0% on LIBERO-Long, exceeding GR00T-N1.6 on the latter by 3.6%. It also reaches an average sequence length of 4.52 on CALVIN and strong overall success rate of 80.4% in the zero-shot LIBERO-PLUS evaluation. Furthermore, FreshVLA exhibits greater robustness to visual perturbations and a more distinct division of roles between two branches in modeling low- and high-frequency motion, respectively. In 35-step action regression, it achieves a 51.3-percentage-point higher relative error reduction than its hierarchical discrete counterpart. Real-world experiments demonstrate that FreshVLA improves the average success rate over $\pi_{0.5}$ by 7.5%. The FreshVLA project page is available at https://freshvla.github.io/.

authors.institution: Hainan Modern Women and Children's Hospital

authors.name: Boyang Cai
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Embodied-VGGT: Preserving Reliable Local Geometry for Long-Sequence Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Long sequence reconstruction must correct accumulated drift while preserving locally consistent geometry. In robotics and autonomous driving, embodied acquisition provides recurring platform- environment geometry and repeated observations of scene structure and platform motion. We present Embodied-VGGT, which exploits these cues to establish reliable local relationships and selectively preserve them during global refinement. Memory-Augmented Grounded Chunks (MAGC) builds on Scal3R's global context memory and uses relative scale references derived from predicted ground geometry to regularize test-time memory updates, encouraging cross-chunk consistency while limiting changes to reliable local geometry. Superpoint Alignment (SA) and Cross-Loop Optimization (CL) jointly address the robust establishment and preservation of geometric relationships. SA balances ground and non-ground evidence across spatial regions to estimate inter-chunk translation. CL uses geometric and motion consistency across interleaved windows to select coherent chunk groups, each receiving a shared Sim(3) correction that preserves its internal relative transformations during global optimization. Experiments on five public driving benchmarks demonstrate consistent and substantial improvements in long sequence reconstruction. On KITTI Odometry, Embodied-VGGT achieves a mean absolute trajectory error of 7.30 m and a Chamfer distance of 2.67 m, reducing these errors by 46.8% and 23.3% compared with the state-of-the-art baseline under same evaluation protocol. To facilitate reproducibility, we released our code: https://github.com/Ang-Sheep/Embodied-VGGT.

authors.institution: Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics & Chemistry

authors.name: Yiqing Yin
authors.institution: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital

authors.name: Nan Ma
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

papers.title: X-World: Transferring Video Priors to Cross-Embodiment Robot Control
papers.abstract: Language-instructed manipulation requires robust closedloop policies, yet action-labeled robot trajectories are costly and limited in coverage. Human and robot videos provide complementary spatiotemporal priors for crossembodiment control. We propose X-World, which adapts pretrained video diffusion to variable views. A Q-Former compresses hidden states into tokens for a shared flowmatching expert that predicts action chunks. Datasetspecific projections map native states and actions. We adapt the backbone on large-scale robot and human videos, freeze it for action-only pretraining of the Q-Former and action expert, then post-train on the target platform. At inference, X-World responds at 20 Hz and overlaps updates with execution via asynchronous real-time chunking. X-World performs strongly on LIBERO and under zero-shot shifts on LIBERO-Plus. On hardware, it averages 81.7% success across six bimanual tasks on the side-mounted dual-arm UR5e, one of three real-robot configurations presented.

authors.name: Yiming Chen
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology
