Similar bifurcation structures for different ocean models suggest common underlying dynamics across the model hierarchy. Here we propose a unifying framework from tracer conservation, in which surface fluxes are balanced by dissipative and advective tracer transport. We express this flux balance through a large-scale tracer gradient and a transport efficiency that measures how strongly circulation displaces the tracer field from its no-flow "conductive" state. The flux balance quantifies the transport contributions that sustain each circulation state and give rise to abrupt transitions. In a three-dimensional ocean-basin model, we find nonlinear salinity advection dominates the collapse threshold and linear dissipation dominates the recovery threshold. Temperature has additional dissipation from surface restoring, making thermal fluxes more dissipation-dominated than salinity fluxes. The tracer contrasts and boundary layers that a given circulation generates produce distinct transport regimes, approximately quadratic in circulation strength for weak flow and linear for strong flow. With a simple circulation closure, the flux balance reduces to longstanding box-model bifurcation results for the weak and strong flow regimes. Thus, by expressing thermohaline bifurcations through basin-scale transport, this framework connects box-model insight to the continuous equations. Furthermore, as this framework exposes the transport processes that balance a changing forcing, it provides constraints on a thermohaline ocean state and its trend toward tipping that overturning strength alone does not. In Part II, we develop flux-balance closures to forecast such tipping points.

papers.title: InterGenEHR$^+$: An Interactive Framework for Natural Language-Conditioned Generation of Longitudinal Patient Trajectories
papers.abstract:
Objective: To develop and validate InterGenEHR$^+$, an interactive framework for natural language-conditioned generation of synthetic tabular electronic health records (EHRs) and longitudinal trajectories for scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models.
  Methods: An optional large language model (LLM) parser converts clinical requests into structured constraints. Conditional variational autoencoders and diffusion models generate single-time-point records, while diffusion models generate longitudinal trajectories. We evaluate parsing, distributional fidelity, imputation, clinical-constraint adherence, mortality prediction, and clinical plausibility using a multi-institutional cohort of 874 patients receiving venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO).
  Results: Gemma 3 4B with few-shot prompting achieves the highest parsing performance with a low spurious slot rate. IGE-TabDDPM and IGE-PMVAE perform well in single-time-point generation; IGE-CSDI, IGE-FGTI, and IGE-MTSCI lead on different longitudinal fidelity metrics. Across five random seeds and three classifiers, synthetic cohorts retain predictive utility for mortality prediction on real test data. Clinician ratings support trajectory plausibility and alignment with requested scenarios.
  Conclusion: InterGenEHR$^+$ supports clinician-specified generation of EHR trajectories with statistical fidelity and downstream predictive utility in the evaluated VV-ECMO cohort. Extension to other clinical settings requires further validation.
  Significance: The framework supports scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models in data-sparse critical care settings.

authors.name: Yu Yang
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Shared-Harmonic Characterization and Robust Orientation-Selection Certification for Directional Sensing Under Anisotropic Target Motion
papers.abstract: Directional sensors are often oriented using historical target trajectories, while future trajectories remain uncertain at deployment. This letter addresses two post-placement questions: i) when orientation materially affects detection and ii) when a historically selected orientation remains reliable under future target-motion shift. We develop a placement-aware framework for anisotropy-induced detection (AID), showing that orientation sensitivity is governed by harmonic modes shared by the locally visible target-direction distribution and the sensor trajectory-incidence response. The resulting AID measure admits an exact RMS interpretation for the retained-harmonic orientation response. We then introduce a sensor-induced directional discrepancy, derive a conditional bound on future orientation regret, and obtain sufficient certificates for robust orientation selection whenever the future sensor-relevant shift lies within a prescribed discrepancy radius. Using 2025 AIS ship-traffic data near Terrebonne Bay, Louisiana, historical AID is strongly correlated with held-out orientation sensitivity ($r=0.908$). Across four angular-response widths, AID explains orientation-sensitivity variation with $R^2=0.920$, compared with $R^2=0.239$ for target-only anisotropy. At the nominal threshold, 316 of 350 locations are empirically classified as orientation-useful, and all retain gain above the threshold across five held-out windows.

papers.title: A Nationwide Snapshot of Starlink Affordability
papers.abstract: Starlink positions itself as "fast affordable Internet" that can provide service to nearly every household in the United States, and is slated to be responsible for providing the only broadband service to a significant number of US households via the NTIA's BEAD program. However, neither the FCC's National Broadband Map nor Starlink's own availability map captures what service costs. We present the first national census of Starlink's residential broadband pricing. We first identify that Starlink's offers are uniform within H3 resolution 6 grid cells, allowing us to collect plans and prices for every populated cell in the United States, more than 162,000 addresses, in October 2026. We find that while Starlink's service prices are fairly consistent, the effective price of the most affordable plan varies across the country, driven by restricting sales of less expensive plans as well as "demand surcharges" ranging between \$100 and \$1,500. Using a common affordability threshold of 2% of monthly income, we find that service restrictions or surcharges make Starlink unaffordable for approximately 4.3 million households, and in total nearly a quarter of all US households (roughly 25.5 million) cannot afford Starlink. Finally, approximately 80% of locations where Starlink is slated to receive BEAD funding face no constrained pricing today.

papers.title: Equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: We construct explicit symmetric-function realizations of the torus-equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of types B and D. More precisely, we realize the extended $K$-theoretic Peterson algebras as subalgebras of a completed ring of equivariant symmetric functions and identify their Schubert classes in terms of symmetric functions. We introduce two new families of equivariant symmetric functions for each of types B and D and prove that these functions represent the classes of the structure sheaves of Schubert varieties and the ideal sheaves of their boundaries, respectively. We establish several fundamental properties of these functions, including translation factorization formulas and explicit expressions for the classes indexed by small affine Grassmannian elements. In type D, we further describe the action of the affine Dynkin diagram automorphism interchanging the two spin nodes and show how it intertwines the Schubert bases with a nontrivial transformation of the equivariant parameters.

papers.title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
papers.abstract: End-to-end physical-layer learning replaces separate modulation, coding, and detection operations with an autoencoder (AE) that consists of a jointly trained encoder-decoder pair at the transmitter and the receiver. This paper studies AI-native communications with AEs and quantifies the sensitivity to training-test mismatch in channel models. Models trained only on an AWGN channel achieve low bit error rates (BERs) under matched conditions but degrade severely on Rayleigh fading with practical front-end impairments. To reduce the time and energy required to adapt to new channel conditions, we propose a low-latency transfer-learning procedure that starts from an AWGN-pretrained system and fine-tunes only a small subset of transmitter and receiver layers while freezing the remainder. We further formulate layer selection as a budget-constrained optimization problem that identifies the most informative parameters to update during adaptation. This preserves the learned signal geometry and the deep decision structure while adapting lightweight front ends to fading- and impairment-induced mixing. For AE communications, we show that partial updates remove the mismatch-induced error floor and approach the BER of fully retrained models. We provide a layer-wise study and quantify resource-performance trade-offs, showing that modest adaptation substantially reduces BER while cutting training time, multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations, energy consumption, and the fraction of updated parameters for resource-efficient implementation.

papers.title: RegHarness: Regulating What Code-as-Policy Agents Keep from Steps to Skills
papers.abstract: Code-as-Policy agents generate, execute, and revise robot programs, but often lack explicit mechanisms to govern what persists across executions: which actions are retained within a trial and which code modifications carry over to subsequent runs. This leaves two critical aspects of agent behavior insufficiently controlled: step-level execution and cross-run adaptation. We present RegHarness, a two-level harness that governs both forms of persistence for the RATs agent team, without relying on a vision-language-action (VLA) policy or demonstrations. Within each trial, run-time governance evaluates each proposed step from a reset scene, replaying the committed steps, while a fixed-rule controller commits the step only when both RATs' verifier and a task-long LLM auditor approve it. Between runs, a coding agent uses logged failures to develop and test revisions to skills, primitives, and rules, which remain disabled by default until explicitly enabled by the authors. Using a single low-cost model across all run-time roles, RegHarness achieves an 87.8% success rate (158/180) on paired LIBERO-PRO trials, compared with 39.4% for RATs, and a 72.0% success rate on MolmoSpaces trials. A $2\times2$ ablation study of RegHarness's two levels shows that its skill refinement alone increases RATs' successful trials from 71 to 135, whereas run-time governance alone achieves 105 and RATs' native stepwise reset-and-replay mode achieves only 46. These findings suggest that, for Code-as-Policy agents operating with low-cost models, task success depends not only on how generated programs are executed, but also on the quality of the reusable skills they invoke and how those skills evolve across runs.

authors.name: Shengming Liu
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Jinan University

authors.name: Sim Kuan Goh
authors.institution: Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics

papers.title: Searching Ultra-Long Videos with Decision Models
papers.abstract: Understanding ultra-long videos requires retrieving sparse, query-relevant evidence from extensive video histories. Existing similarity-based retrieval methods are efficient, but they encode the question and the video content independently and thus often miss evidence whose relevance requires reasoning over both. Generative large language models (LLMs) can perform such reasoning, but they typically generate text over multiple rounds of search, which makes each query slow and costly. In this work, we introduce DeLoVi (Decision Models for Long Video), a framework that leverages pretrained decision models to retrieve evidence from ultra-long videos. Like an LLM, a decision model reads the question together with the candidate evidence, so it can reason over both. Unlike an LLM, it directly outputs a relevance score without generating text, which makes it fast and inexpensive. We first present DeLoVi-S, a simple method that generates captions for short video clips and uses a decision model to rank those captions by their relevance to a question. A generative LLM then answers the question using the top-ranked captions. Despite its simplicity, DeLoVi-S achieves state-of-the-art performance on three ultra-long video understanding benchmarks, EgoLifeQA, EgoMemReason, and MM-Lifelong, and generalizes effectively to long-video understanding benchmarks, VideoMME-L and LVBench. However, DeLoVi-S scores every caption for every question, so its cost grows linearly with video length. To reduce this cost, we propose an automated policy evolution framework that iteratively refines the memory construction and retrieval policies around a fixed pretrained decision model. The resulting method, DeLoVi-E, maintains comparable performance while reducing input tokens by 34x on average compared with DeLoVi-S. It also runs over 3x faster than the best prior method on EgoLifeQA while achieving higher accuracy.

authors.name: Ce Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Baiqi Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

authors.name: Seongsu Ha
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

authors.name: Gedas Bertasius
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Non-Existence of Eigenvalues and Interface States for the Schr\"odinger Operator with Longitudinal Interface Potentials
papers.abstract: We consider the Schr\"odinger operator in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat interface separating two half-spaces in which the real potential varies only in the directions parallel to the interface. This problem generally possesses no shift invariance. Nevertheless, using the method of multipliers, we prove the absence of eigenvalues. In addition, in the case of periodic potentials on each side of the interface the same method shows the absence of interface states which are quasi-periodic in the directions parallel to the interface and localized in the transverse direction.

papers.title: Bohr inequalities and Landau-type estimates for harmonic Poisson extensions of $L^p$ boundary functions
papers.abstract: This paper establishes sharp quantitative bounds governing the Bohr phenomenon, Landau-type distortion, and geometric univalence for complex-valued harmonic mappings on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ parameterized by boundary data in the Lebesgue spaces $L^{p}(\mathbb{T})$ for $1 \le p \le \infty$, where $\mathbb{T} = \partial\mathbb{D}$. First, we resolve the classical coefficient problem for bounded harmonic mappings by incorporating an integral Parseval constraint rather than crude individual bounds, establishing the sharp Bohr radius as $r_H(a) = \sqrt{(1-a)/(3+a)}$ for a fixed initial term $\vert{}a_0\vert{} = aM$. Second, this framework is extended to the $L^p$ setting under the vanishing normalization $f(0)=0$, explicitly characterizing the sharp Bohr radius as $r_{p} = (2C_{q}+1)^{-1}$, where the structural constant $C_{q}$ is intrinsically linked to the conjugate exponent $q$. Finally, under standard normalization, we determine explicit formulations for both the radius of univalence $r_{0}$ and the corresponding radius of the inscribed Schlicht disk $R_{0}$. The sharpness of all analytical constants and radii is verified through the construction of concrete extremal configurations derived from the Poisson kernel.

papers.title: OrbACE: Orbital and Atomic Cluster Expansion
papers.abstract:
Accurate electronic-structure reference data are expensive, motivating interatomic potentials that learn effectively from limited training sets. We introduce OrbACE (Orbital and Atomic Cluster Expansion), a framework that supplements an E(3)-equivariant cluster-expansion backbone with inexpensive electronic-structure descriptors. On ANI-1x at the $\omega$B97X/6-31G* level, its atom-centered variant, OrbACE-A, trained on 10,000 configurations and evaluated on 442,000 held-out configurations, achieves energy and force mean absolute errors of 3.16 meV/atom and 76 meV/angstrom in direct learning, compared with 9.61 meV/atom and 146 meV/angstrom for MACE with matched backbone settings. This reduces the energy error by a factor of three and approximately halves the force error. Its energy error is also below that of the best delta-corrected MACE baseline, 5.00 meV/atom, although its force error is slightly higher. Combining OrbACE-A with a Hartree-Fock delta baseline further reduces the errors to 1.48 meV/atom and 35 meV/angstrom.
  OrbACE-A builds atom- and pair-resolved invariants from a non-self-consistent extended-Hueckel model evaluated within the differentiable forward pass, yielding forces consistent with the predicted energy. The orbital variant, OrbACE-O, instead uses localized Hartree-Fock orbitals as graph nodes, with scalar and equivariant electronic descriptors. Its forces are evaluated at fixed descriptors, omitting their response to nuclear motion. In direct learning on ANI-1x, its energy error is approximately three times that of OrbACE-A. The three benchmarks considered (ANI-1x, revised MD17, and 3BPA) cover neutral, closed-shell, non-periodic molecules containing H, C, N, and O. Performance outside this domain remains to be established.

papers.title: VibeVideoAgent: Closing the Perceptual Loop for Code-Driven Video Generation
papers.abstract: Code-driven video generation asks a coding agent to write and run rendering programs. This gives exact control over typography, data visualizations, synchronized audio, and multi-shot scenes, and it leaves an editable project behind. A program that exits cleanly can still render overlapping labels, a camera aimed away from its subject, broken object interactions, or narration that drifts out of sync, and none of these raise a runtime error. Feeding rendered frames and audio back into the coding session bloats its long-horizon context, while critiquing only the finished full-resolution render turns early design mistakes into costly rewrites. We introduce VibeVideoAgent, a training-free framework that lets coding agents inspect their drafts throughout production. Multimodal perception runs in short-lived contexts kept apart from the coder and returns compact, grounded Findings. Seven primitives operate on a unified multi-clock representation of assets and drafts: they explore media from coarse to fine, verify quoted requirements with evidence from every required modality, compare a draft with a reference or an earlier revision on separate clocks, and measure stream signals locally. A lightweight staged protocol has the agent test its riskiest decision on a minimal preview first. On all 239 VibeVideoBench tasks, with matched agent runtimes and a fixed perception model, VibeVideoAgent improves holistic audiovisual quality (L3) for Claude Opus 5.5 (4.03 -> 4.43, while L2 rubric compliance rises from 98.87% to 99.35%), GPT-6 Astra (4.03 -> 4.27), and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (3.97 -> 4.10), with the largest gains in audio-visual synchronization (up to +0.56). Controlled ablations show that each component contributes, and trajectory audits show that the granularity of code edits governs the trade-off between rubric adherence and perceptual quality.

authors.name: Muxi Diao
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Quot schemes on projective space
papers.abstract: We develop general methods for studying Quot schemes on projective space, including a new construction of components with no common neighbours. We show that the radius of Hilbert and Quot schemes can grow linearly with the dimension of the subschemes being parametrized, and construct the first examples of Hilbert schemes of curves with radius two. For absolutely split bundles on projective space, we construct a distinguished generically smooth component and classify all smooth Quot schemes. In most cases, we give explicit geometric descriptions in terms of products of generalized flag varieties and projective bundles over Grassmannians.

papers.title: hp-Adaptive Finite Element Modeling of Static Cracks in Density-Dependent Media
papers.abstract: The elastostatic crack-tip fields within a density-dependent continuum are numerically investigated under several macroscopic loading configurations. The governing nonlinear boundary value problem is formulated using an algebraically nonlinear hyperelastic constitutive relationship in which the material moduli are intrinsically coupled to volumetric strain. Existence and uniqueness of the weak solution to the nonlinear displacement-based variational formulation are rigorously established at the continuous level via the Minty-Browder theorem. The variational formulation is then linearized at the partial differential equation level to construct a continuous damped Newton-Raphson scheme. To accurately capture the severe field gradients and internal singularities inherent to this model, the resulting sequence of linear operator equations is discretized and solved via a conforming finite element method within an $hp$-adaptive framework. A comparative analysis is conducted across five distinct boundary loading profiles (encompassing uniform, piecewise-slope, and concentrated point loads) applied to a stationary cracked geometry. Within each configuration, the density-dependent constitutive parameter is systematically varied to assess its regulatory impact on the fracture process zone, focusing on the spatial evolution of normal stress, normal strain, and strain energy density near the crack tip. Numerical results demonstrate that local kinematic deformability is strictly bounded by the strain-limiting nature of the continuum, whereby static equilibrium is sustained through severe, localized stress amplifications. Furthermore, the mechanical influence of the modeling parameter is fundamentally dictated by the topological interplay between internal crack geometry and the spatial distribution of applied macroscopic loads.

authors.name: Saugata Ghosh
authors.institution: R. G. Kar Medical College and Hospital

authors.name: Dambaru Bhatta
authors.institution: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

papers.title: A Quantile-Based Framework for Bimodal Distribution Construction
papers.abstract: This study suggests a novel quantile-based framework to construct bimodal distribution which does not rely on mixture representations or closed-form probability density functions. This proposed approach induces bimodality by transforming the quantile density through a strictly positive modulation function so that it can preserve the support and tail behavior of a chosen baseline distribution with providing explicit control over modal structure. The method is shown to apply broadly across bounded, semi-bounded and unbounded distribution families which include power, reflected power, logistic, Weibull and generalized lambda distributions. Simulation studies and a real-data application were performed which have shown that the proposed construction yields smooth, interpretable and computationally stable bimodal models and it also provides a flexible alternative to classical mixture-based approaches. Also this framework allows gradual transitions between unimodal and bimodal shapes which make it well suited for modeling overlapping regimes which are commonly encountered in real-world data. This proposed methodology therefor offers a robust and interpretable tool for bimodal modeling without requiring latent class assumptions or complex estimation procedures.

papers.title: CLT for Linear Spectral Statistics of sample covariances of superimposition of Separable Covariance Components
papers.abstract: Suppose $\{Z_r\}_{r=1}^K$ are $p\times n$ random matrices with entries having zero mean and unit variance and $p/n \to c \in (0,\infty)$. We construct the sample covariance matrix $S_n = \frac{1}{n}XX^*$ where $X =\sum_{r=1}^K X_r$, where $X_r = A_r^\frac{1}{2}Z_rB_r^\frac{1}{2}$, $K \in \mathbb{N}$ and $A_r,B_r$ are sequences of positive semi-definite matrices of dimensions $p\times p$ and $n\times n$, respectively that are are simultaneously digaonalizable within themselves. As an extension of our previous work related to the L.S.D. of such classes of matrices, we show that the linear spectral statistics arising from the spectra of $S_n$ have Gaussian limits under assumptions of fourth moment bounds on the entries of $\{Z_r\}_{r=1}^K$ and convergence of the joint spectral distribution of $\{A_r\}_{r=1}^K$ and $\{B_r\}_{r=1}^K$ to probability distributions over $\mathbb{R}_+^K$ with compact support.

papers.title: Planetary Habitable Zones around Magnetized White Dwarfs
papers.abstract: White dwarfs are known to host remnant planetary material, indicating that rocky objects can survive post-main-sequence evolution and migrate into very close orbits. However, the decline of white dwarf luminosity makes it difficult for a planet to remain habitable for long when relying only on the white dwarf's irradiative heating. While several non-radiative energy sources have been proposed, the role of white dwarf magnetism in planetary energy budgets remains largely unexplored. We examine whether magnetic unipolar induction could provide sustained heating for close-in rocky planets. By coupling white dwarf cooling tracks with an orbit-dependent induction model, we evaluate the contribution of ohmic dissipation to planetary surface energy budgets and estimate the upper limit with efficient heat deposition. It is possible for the induction heating to supply a nearly steady surface energy flux for certain orbital distances and stellar spins, partially offsetting the decline in the white dwarf irradiation at late times. This leads to a persistent outer temperate region and, in some cases, a narrow inner zone that emerges after substantial cooling, identifying magnetic induction as a viable long-lived supplement to radiative heating.

papers.title: Quantum Metric Connects Bond Delocalization to Phonon Softening
papers.abstract: Delocalized bonding electrons have long been associated with soft bonds and low phonon frequencies. However, a quantitative connection between electron delocalization and phonon softening remains elusive. We identify such a connection through the momentum-space quantum metric, which measures the intrinsic delocalization of the occupied electronic states. We show that a quantum geometric contribution to phonon softening is proportional to the integrated quantum metric. First-principles calculations of more than a hundred compounds demonstrate that greater quantum metric generally accompanies softer phonons. Localized Wannier orbitals reveal the bonding environments associated with this delocalization. In ferroelectric GeTe, LiBeSb, and BaTiO$_3$, polar distortion localizes the bonding orbitals, reduces quantum metric, and stabilizes the soft mode of the nonpolar structure. In PbSe, pressure-induced band inversion is accompanied by an enhanced quantum metric and phonon softening without change in crystal symmetry and bonding. These results establish a common quantum geometric interpretation of bond delocalization and phonon softening across distinct bonding environments.

papers.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Fully online on-policy distillation (OPD) is costly for long-horizon agents because each update depends on fresh environment rollouts. Prefix replay offers an efficient alternative by sampling current-student responses from stored histories, reducing idle time for long-tail rollouts and allowing each collected trajectory to support multiple updates. However, our analysis of the complete prefix replay pipeline identifies two limitations in long-horizon settings. In trajectory collection, teacher-only trajectories miss student-induced histories, while broader history coverage can reduce teacher reliability. In trajectory reuse, fixed position-based schedules cannot identify critical decisions that may occur at any trajectory depth. We introduce CARE-OPD (Collect for coverAge, Replay with Evidence) to address both limitations. Student-seeded teacher completions and response-level confidence gating expand history coverage while filtering unreliable updates. Hindsight replay allocation then uses downstream execution evidence to select consequential turns. Across long-horizon tasks Software Engineering and Deep Research, CARE-OPD outperforms online OPD and prior prefix replay baselines. On SWE-bench Verified, it raises task success to 59.5% while reducing end-to-end training time by 45% and environment actions by 44% relative to asynchronous online OPD.

authors.name: Haowen Hou
authors.institution: Guangdong Laboratory of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Economy (Shenzhen)

authors.name: Ruilin Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Jiaqi Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Confidence scores for gated automation of large language models
papers.abstract: AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong capabilities in automated decision-making. However, LLMs may produce incorrect answers with high confidence, limiting their applicability in decisions that affect individuals and organizations. Reliable confidence scores are necessary to gate such decisions, and existing estimates are frequently unavailable or too coarse to support effective gating. This work uses supervised learning to train models to predict the correctness of LLM-generated answers, enabling automated confident responses and routing uncertain ones for human review. A linear confidence score head is fitted to the final-layer hidden state of the frozen LLM backbone, and text-only metamodels are trained as an alternative for closed models. All results come from a single 2B-parameter backbone, on graded answers that are about 98% SQuAD and the remainder TruthfulQA. Against multiple baselines, the confidence score head outperforms all baselines and metamodels, automating the largest fraction of the workload at high accuracy targets. Prompted confidence scores can appear well calibrated yet lack the resolution needed for thresholding. Although transferability to unseen datasets is modest, the confidence score head remains the most robust approach. The proposed confidence scoring framework enhances the safety of automating LLM-based agents and can be adapted to gate other properties, including safety or compliance.

papers.title: Refinements to precision-information imputation in meta-analysis of survival rates: Boundary correction and cross-study borrowing
papers.abstract: Meta-analyses of survival rates require precision information, such as standard errors (SEs), which is often unreported. We previously proposed imputing missing SEs from reported survival rates, sample sizes, and risk-set sizes. The original method has two limitations. First, it replaces Kaplan--Meier estimates of 1 with 0.99 regardless of sample size. Second, when the risk-set size is unavailable, it uses the total event count as a fallback. The count is often unreported, and the fallback can also substantially overestimate SEs. We propose a sample-size-dependent boundary correction based on a pseudo-event and a method that borrows time-specific event information from studies with available risk-set sizes. In simulations, the boundary correction was more stable than fixed replacement, and borrowing reduced study-level SE imputation bias. Borrowing generally improved precision by retaining studies with missing SEs that lacked both risk-set sizes and event counts.

papers.title: KiRA: Kronecker Input-Gated Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Models
papers.abstract: Full fine-tuning of large pretrained models is expensive, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) is the standard alternative. Most PEFT methods use low-rank updates, whose rank lies far below that of full fine-tuning and is the same for every input. Input-adaptive variants vary the capacity per input but remain within the low-rank bottleneck, and whether a task benefits from input conditioning is not known before training. This paper introduces Kronecker input-gated rank adaptation (KiRA). Instead of the conventional low-rank product, the update $\Delta W$ is the Kronecker product of a frozen random $p\times p$ matrix $A$ and a trainable factor $M(x)$, which overcomes the rank ceiling: because rank is multiplicative under this product, $A$ multiplies the rank of $M(x)$ by $p$ without adding trainable parameters. The factor $M(x)$ is further decomposed as $B_1\,\mathrm{diag}(g(x))\,B_2$, where the input gate $g(x)$, computed once per sample by a network shared across all adapted layers, adjusts the rank of the update to each input in steps of $p$. Where input conditioning is unnecessary, the gate is folded into $B_1$ at deployment. Because the gate changes the rank only in discrete steps, the benefit of input conditioning can be predicted before training from a few hundred labeled inputs. Across six medical imaging and language benchmarks, KiRA attains the highest mean score against five published baselines with 8.7--9.7 times fewer trainable parameters than low-rank adaptation, and the pre-training criterion agrees with the measured benefit of input conditioning on all six tasks.

authors.name: Shaikh Anowarul Fattah
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: Lightweight Reasoning Transfer via Chain-of-Thought Vector Projection
papers.abstract: Transferring reasoning capabilities from large language models to smaller ones often requires extensive teacher supervision or costly student adaptation. We study projected cross-model Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Vector transfer, a two-stage approach that keeps both models frozen. First, we learn a task-level CoT Vector in the teacher using dataset-provided solution traces and final-answer supervision. We then train a lightweight linear projector to map the fixed vector into a smaller student's residual space. Student-side training uses only final-answer cross-entropy on a small subset of task training examples; it requires neither teacher outputs nor intermediate solution traces. We select the student injection layer and intervention scale on a labeled support set and report results on the disjoint remainder of each evaluation split. On GSM8K and MATH, the projected vector improves base students by 10.37-21.98 accuracy points across the evaluated teacher-student settings. On four code-generation benchmarks, the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct student gains 3.23-4.67 pass@1 points, while the base Qwen2.5-7B student gains up to 9.65 points. These results show that a teacher-side reasoning vector can be reused across smaller students with different residual dimensions through projector-only adaptation.

papers.title: Bolognesi's Conjecture for Nonnegative-Charge Iterated Magnetic Bags
papers.abstract: We establish a magnetic-bag limit for smooth $SU(2)$ Bogomolny monopoles associated with finitely many nested smooth surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$. This proves Bolognesi's magnetic-bag conjecture for iterated magnetic bags with nonnegative charge density on each surface.

papers.title: Higher-Order Generation of First-Order Theories
papers.abstract:
We introduce a logic whose formulae are finite descriptions of possibly infinite first-order theories. A theory is a set of first-order sentences, generated in our setting by a higher-order recursion scheme. Such a scheme is a finite grammar whose parameters may denote trees or operations on trees. We consider two interpretations: a model must satisfy every generated sentence under the conjunctive interpretation, and at least one under the disjunctive interpretation. For schemes of order $k=0$, these theories coincide with the regular first-order theories of Mathur et al. (POPL 2025). We generalize this representation by allowing higher-order schemes, while retaining first-order quantification in every generated sentence.
  We study the expressive power, model checking, and satisfiability of this logic. Over finite ordered structures, we show that disjunctive theories of existential sentences generated at order at most $k$ capture $k$-EXPTIME, for every $k\geq0$. Allowing unrestricted first-order sentences captures $(k+1)$-EXPTIME at the same scheme order, where $0$-EXPTIME denotes polynomial time. We also give model-checking algorithms in the corresponding time classes for each fixed signature, variable-name set, and order bound. For satisfiability under either interpretation, we extend several decidability results for regular theories to every order. However, we show that conjunctive satisfiability of quantifier-free theories, decidable at order zero, becomes undecidable already at order one. Finally, we recover decidable conjunctive satisfiability at every order by separating higher-order generation of Boolean structure from independent regular generation of ground atoms. Together, these results show how higher-order generation of first-order syntax captures the exponential-time hierarchy while retaining decidable satisfiability in restricted fragments.

papers.title: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Pursuit Game for Locomotor Agility Pretraining
papers.abstract: Agile humanoid locomotion requires controllers that can adapt to rapidly changing motion demands while remaining stable and robust. Recent locomotion controllers are typically designed with either a dense reward that is carefully shaped to encourage steps and penalize falling, or by using a reference tracking reward which teaches the controller to follow predetermined motions. Once a behavior that maximizes the reward is discovered, the controller ceases to learn. While generally stable, reference tracking methods focus on motor control separately from motion generation. Self-play has been proven as an effective technique for superhuman performance on several multiagent games like Go, Starcraft, hide-and-seek, and capture-the-flag. We train neural networks to play the game of multiagent tag in a physics simulator to study if new motion generation and control strategies can emerge through sparse feedback and competitive self-play. We present MJTag, a task suite for role-conditioned locomotion during competitive pursuit-evasion. Our model is a role-conditioned policy for a low-level locomotion controller and optional planar velocity commands. MJTag's league-based play with sparse feedback enables a locomotion controller to adopt new strategies, including dodging, sprinting, and tackling.

papers.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
papers.abstract: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale. We present DexEngine, a simulation pipeline that turns human manipulation data into train-ready, physically executable arm-hand trajectories. DexEngine first places each clip's hand-object motion where the arms can reach it, finds an arm motion that follows the human hands, and then corrects the motion in physics simulation with residual reinforcement learning. From nine human hand-object datasets, we generate about 5,200 clips for each of four dexterous hands, augmented into 65,000 trajectories (116 h) and 325,000 episodes (578 h) in total. Even with arms attached, DexEngine tracks objects more accurately than prior floating-hand methods and runs over 10x faster than RL-based ones. Policies trained on our data far outperform those trained on the same clips without physics correction or with the arms attached after a floating-hand correction, showing that fine-tuning data need physics correction. Mid-training on our data further improves them at equal fine-tuning budget, in simulation and on a real robot.

authors.name: Wongyun Yu
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Minsu Cho
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: From NP-Hardness to Exact Tractability Through Sample Abundance
papers.abstract: Additional observations can make exact optimization tractable without changing the objective or feasible set. We establish this phenomenon for noisy parity fitting, a worst-case NP-hard problem, with uniformly sampled rank-one sign tensor entries, independent fair factor signs and independent errors. For fixed interaction order $k\ge3$, $n$ signs per block, logarithmic mean degree and known channel biases, $O(n/(\log n)^{1/(k-2)})$ further readings of the same source suffice with high probability for exact optimization in $O(n\log^2 n)$ worst-case work. The leading coefficient is sharp for weak recovery by depth-$O(\log\log n)$ local estimators with independent reading marks. A common signed-field law determines the gain over the generating source, the number of tied optima and the dimension needed for later reweightings. The geometry of the remaining coordinates determines the sharp radius of local verification for high-scoring assignments with high probability.

papers.title: HumblePRM: Improving VLM Abstention in Ambiguous Situations through Process Reward Modeling
papers.abstract: Reliable deployment of Vision Language Models (VLMs) requires that a model's expressed confidence remain grounded in what it can actually see, and that it recognize when the visual evidence is too ambiguous to commit to a confident response. Standard post-training uses outcome reward models (ORMs) that supervise only the final decision, rewarding a confident answer regardless of whether the image supports one, while existing methods either tend to detect uncertainty post-hoc or assume an objective verdict always exists. We instead split multimodal reasoning into two stages: perception, where the model must factually describe the scene, and calibration, where it must judge whether that evidence is sufficient to commit to a conclusion. We introduce HumblePRM, a lightweight process reward model (PRM) that scores each stage independently, rewarding agreement between evidence and expressed confidence rather than outcome correctness alone. Training with HumblePRM increases abstention due to uncertainty on ambiguous inputs considerably while leaving accuracy on clear images roughly unchanged. We also find that the improvement transfers to Gemma 4 E4B, a larger, popular edge model. Our findings show that process reward supervision is a promising route to VLMs with better calibrated abstention, ensuring more reliability rather than unpredictable behavior.

papers.title: RoboJackVR: Turning Robot Tasks into VR Games for Scalable Demonstration Collection
papers.abstract: Scaling robot demonstration datasets requires collection systems that accommodate more participants and diverse tasks, yet teleoperation barriers and task-adaptation effort limit this expansion. We present RoboJackVR, a standalone virtual reality (VR) game in which players manipulate simulated robots to execute combat skills and contribute demonstrations. MuJoCo simulation and demonstration recording run locally on the headset, removing the need for an external PC or simulation server during collection. Tutorials, skill selection, combat consequences, and character progression organize repeated task attempts within a continuing game. Task contracts declare assets, controls, resets, success criteria, and recording semantics; separate game configurations specify guidance, attempt groups, skill effects, and course placement. Shared bindings connect these declarations to task execution, outcome handling, and recording, allowing tasks to reuse the game flow while retaining their control and success semantics. Batch tools package supported resources and generate configurations, with manual adaptation and review for new interfaces and unsupported predicates. We instantiate the approach with SO101-Nexus-derived and LIBERO tasks. On the 66 LIBERO-90 tasks covered by the collected data, ACT policies trained solely on VR demonstrations retain approximately 91% of the full-standard simulation-demonstration baseline's success rate on held-out initial states, averaged over four training seeds. These results support the utility of play-collected VR demonstrations for policy learning in this setting.

papers.title: Rehearse in 3D, Render in 2D: Physically Consistent and Editable Robot World Models
papers.abstract: Embodied world models aim to predict future interactions that are both visually realistic and physically consistent. Yet explicit 3D motion prediction alone does not guarantee that object structure and contact relationships are preserved. Beyond motion prediction, 3D representations provide an explicit state space for imposing structural and physical constraints. Building on this insight, we introduce RehearsalWorld, an editable robot world model driven by 3D Interaction Rehearsal (3DIR). Given an initial RGB-D observation and robot actions, Interaction-Consistent Rehearsal (ICR) uses a pretrained 3D point-flow model as a motion prior. It refines the predicted trajectories through response-aware object grouping, persistent grasp memory, and contact structure refiner, preserving scene stability, object structure, and grasp attachments. Rehearsal-Aligned Video Generation (RAVG) then uses geometric projections of the rehearsal as temporal conditioning. We fine-tune a video generator on projection-video pairs to synthesize realistic interaction videos. Thanks to the decoupling of physical response from visual synthesis, RehearsalWorld also supports independent editing of material properties and camera viewpoints. Compared with PointWorld on real DROID grasping sequences, RehearsalWorld reduces gripper-relative offset by approximately 79% to 84% across deformable, articulated, and rigid objects and lowers reference motion error. For video prediction, it achieves a PSNR of 23.92 dB and an FVD of 149.

papers.title: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL
papers.abstract: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards often yields all-fail groups on long-horizon agent tasks: every sampled trajectory receives zero reward, leaving group-relative methods without a reward-based policy gradient. A common remedy supplies complete solutions from a stronger model, but full trajectories are expensive and expose the learner to long off-policy histories. We introduce SPLICE, which constructs local training targets from failed current-policy trajectories online. For each all-fail group, a proposal model selects a splice point in a current-policy trajectory and generates several bounded options from that point. We estimate each option's value using repeated current-policy continuations, convert positive estimates into a return-weighted local target, and fit the current policy on the options. We evaluate SPLICE across two policy families on two long-horizon agent tasks, Software Engineering with SWE-bench Verified and Deep Research with BrowseComp-Plus. SPLICE outperforms GRPO and full-trajectory guidance baselines in all four settings, improving over GRPO by 2.8--9.8 percentage points. On initially failed SWE tasks, it raises GRPO's graduation rate by 10.8 percentage points. Further experiments show that SPLICE improves performance while reducing costly proposal-model computation.

authors.name: Haowen Hou
authors.institution: Guangdong Laboratory of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Economy (Shenzhen)

authors.name: Jiaqi Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Differentiability of the shape function in the planar corner growth model
papers.abstract: We prove that the shape function of planar directed last-passage percolation with general i.i.d.\ real-valued weights is differentiable on the open first quadrant, under a moment assumption of order $p''>4$ on the positive part of the weight and a nearly optimal order $p'>1$ on the negative part. Due to known results, only directions outside a percolation cone need be considered. The proof is a multiscale path-counting argument that uses the shape theorem, oriented percolation on a coarse-grained lattice, a simple change of measure in a finite region, and the van den Berg--Kesten inequality. Our Lean-formalized proof is an AI-assisted adaptation and improvement of the OpenAI proof of differentiability in planar first-passage percolation.

papers.title: VoroPlex: A Python Framework for Multi-Threaded and Differentiable Voronoi Tessellation
papers.abstract: Voronoi tessellations are widely used in computational physics, for example to measure local structure in particle systems and to generate meshes. We present VoroPlex, an open-source Python package for computing Voronoi tessellations in two and three dimensions. VoroPlex is built on the multi-threaded version of the C++ library Voro++, so that large tessellations can be computed in parallel. The package also makes the tessellation differentiable. Each Voronoi vertex is labeled by the generators that define it, and VoroPlex uses these labels to compute the derivative of the vertex with respect to the positions of these generators. PyTorch can therefore compute gradients of quantities such as cell areas, volumes, and interface areas with respect to the generator positions, so that these quantities can be optimized using standard gradient-based methods. The package also includes tools for extracting interfaces between groups of cells and for exporting meshes. For one million points using 28 threads, VoroPlex is 46 times faster than SciPy in 2D and 39 times faster in 3D. We demonstrate the package with three applications: centroidal Voronoi tessellations with a variable density, meshing of 2D shapes defined by signed distance functions, and the design of foams with a preferred cell orientation.

authors.name: Mucheng Zhu
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Ying Jiang
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A predictive scaling framework for hierarchical living systems: From biomacromolecule to the Anthropogenic Earth system
papers.abstract: Living systems, from biomacromolecules to the biosphere, are organized hierarchically with quantitative traits (such as size, mass and lifespan) spanning many orders of magnitude. However, qualitative traits such as structure differ between adjacent levels, and similarities among non-adjacent levels have been recognized only case by case. Yet no framework integrates quantitative and qualitative traits across the hierarchy of living systems. Here, we propose HELIX, a model that couples exponential scaling across levels with trait-based classification. Clustered by 16 traits, the 14 known levels are classified into three groups: Autonomous, Component, and Repeat-autonomous living systems. Levels within each group are self-similar, and the three groups alternate periodically in a helical belt and the quantitative traits follow scaling law. HELIX integrates existing principles from multiple disciplines to form a unified theory. HELIX further predicts three newly emerged levels, illustrating that it can guide cross-level and interdisciplinary research on living systems.

authors.name: Yong Min
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Power System Operation and Control

authors.name: Feng Mao
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: One Model, Many Modes: Evolving System Prompt Ensembles for Creative Generation
papers.abstract: Preference-aligned LLMs can exhibit mode collapse, concentrating their output distributions around a narrow set of high-reward responses. This limits creative generation, which requires quality, novelty, and diversity. Existing test-time methods often emphasize diversity, giving less attention to whether individual responses are both high-quality and novel. This distinction matters in practical use, where users may seek a single compelling, original response. We formalize creative generation as a multi-objective distributional optimization problem and introduce SEPO, a training-free framework for System Prompt Ensemble Optimization. The framework combines prompt evolution with greedy max-min selection to identify behaviorally distinct system prompts under a quality constraint, then uniformly samples one prompt per response at inference time. Across four creative generation tasks with increasing quality requirements and three open-weight models, SEPO ranks first in 8 of 12 settings on the harmonic mean of quality, diversity, and novelty, while no baseline leads in more than two. On average, it raises LLM-judged diversity from 1.92 to 3.43 and novelty from 1.00 to 3.34 over base sampling (1-5 scale), with quality decreasing from 3.72 to 3.30. We further show that expanding the optimized ensemble increases separation among prompt-conditioned response distributions. These results support system prompt ensemble optimization as a promising approach to improving LLM creativity at inference time.

authors.name: Daiwei Chen
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China
