papers.title: Sharpness of the Kadec'-type theorem for the union of intervals
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish the sharpness of a Kadec'-type theorem for finite unions of intervals admitting the integers as an orthonormal spectrum by constructing an explicit counterexample.

papers.title: Concept Generalization in Visual Brain Decoding via Encoder-Generated fMRI
papers.abstract: Visual brain decoders are typically trained and evaluated on stimuli drawn from similar semantic distributions, leaving their ability to reconstruct unseen concepts poorly understood. We study this concept generalization problem by withholding semantic concepts from a target subject's training data. We find that three recent fMRI-to-image decoders degrade substantially for the held-out concepts, even when the concept remains available for multi-subject models. In contrast, brain encoders that map a pretrained visual representation directly to voxels are markedly more robust to the same semantic holdout. Motivated by this asymmetry, we use such an encoder to generate synthetic fMRI responses for new images and add the resulting image-fMRI pairs to decoder training. Across three decoders, four subjects, and twelve semantic concepts, synthetic data recovers a substantial fraction of the performance lost on unseen concepts without requiring additional, time-consuming fMRI acquisition. We further show that the same approach improves general decoding performance across a wide range of data budgets. Analyses of encoder training conditions, encoder designs, and synthetic-data controls show that the gains depend on both encoder generalization and the semantic content of the synthetic supervision, rather than merely increasing the amount of training data. Together, our results show that encoder-generated fMRI can transfer semantic generalization to decoders.

authors.name: Yansen Wang
authors.institution: Sinopec Beijing Research Institute of Chemical Industry Co., Ltd. (China)

authors.name: Dongqi Han
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
papers.abstract: There are several approaches to AI-driven mathematical discovery. One of these involves the use of large language models (LLMs) to resolve well-specified conjectures via text-based reasoning, while another uses narrow models and interpretability for more open-ended, human-in-the-loop exploration using object-based mathematical data. The latter is limited in its ability to move beyond simple empirical pattern detection while the former is not well-designed for direct, open-ended exploration of large mathematical datasets. In this paper we introduce PatternMiner, a system that combines these two paradigms. In PatternMiner, an LLM agent generates mathematical datasets based on an initial broad question, trains narrow machine learning models on them, uses interpretability techniques to extract patterns from these trained models, and uses these patterns to formulate conjectures. Once an initial conjecture has been formulated, PatternMiner instructs the agent to search for counterexamples using calls to mathematical software. If a set of counterexamples can be found, these are used as feedback for conjecture refinement or another round of training and interpretability. The conjecture progressively evolves through this iterative sequence with the agent allowed to try to prove it at any point. We describe the results of applying PatternMiner to five well-known positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics. PatternMiner proves several new theorems related to Schubert positivity and projection, a character-row evaluation formula, a restricted version of the Kazhdan--Lusztig combinatorial invariance conjecture, and Schur positivity for a family of immanant coefficients. We end by analyzing the most common routes to conjecture generation that are used by PatternMiner in our case studies as well as documenting the most common failure modes.

papers.title: Functional Direct Binomial Regression for Right-Censored Competing Risks Data
papers.abstract: Existing regression-based methods for functional predictors often overlook right-censored competing risks outcomes, limiting their applicability in many biomedical studies. To address this gap, this article proposes a functional direct binomial model for right-censored competing risks data, where a binary outcome indicates the occurrence of an event of interest before a fixed time horizon. The model enables straightforward prediction of the cumulative incidence function, can be fitted using standard, scalable algorithms for large-scale studies, and has broad applications to functional predictors, such as wearable device data. We establish large-sample theory to facilitate inference, including hypothesis testing and the construction of confidence intervals and bands for both scalar coefficients and functional parameters. The methodology is further extended to accommodate multiple functional biomarkers and to handle missing failure causes. Simulation studies confirm that the proposed method provides accurate estimation and valid inference. We illustrate the approach with an application to modeling time to advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) in the presence of the competing risk of death, leveraging continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data and baseline covariates. The analysis shows that CGM is both a significant predictor and a viable alternative to the traditional HbA1c biomarker for CKD.

papers.title: Do Machine Learning Ensembles Beat Published Quotas? Target Parameterization, Censored Baselines, and Conformal Intervals Under Admissions Reform
papers.abstract: Public admission capacity caps published prior to matriculation are widely used by ministries and institutional analysts as default intake projections in centralized postsecondary clearinghouses. Using an audited 2022 to 2026 Vietnamese undergraduate panel (26,895 program-year records across 309 universities) linked to strictly lagged t-1 occupational vacancy signals, this paper evaluates machine learning, multilevel, and censored econometric estimators against published quotas across 5,385 continuing 2024 programs (five-fold university-grouped cross-validation) and 3,348 matched (2,179 grain-consistent) 2025 programs strictly out of time. Because 62.8% of 2024 programs enroll their exact published quota, unanchored log-growth ensembles degrade accuracy, while the worst 5% generate half of total quota error via unfilled "phantom capacity." Controlled target ablations, including a single-factor test under widened non-binding clipping, show that parameterizing the log fill ratio ln(D_it / S_it) instead of log growth reduces 2024 MAE by 21.5% (14.86 to 11.67), aligns ML with Tobit, Cragg, REML HLM, and capped L1 baselines, and lifts combined tuition and institutional-tier TreeSHAP attribution from 2.5% to 45.8%. Hurdle stacking attains the lowest full-census 2024 MAE (H-Hard 11.29; H-Soft 11.32 vs. 12.35, p = 0.022, clearing 10% not 5% FDR; fold-overlap p = 0.134), whereas continuous QA-Stack outperforms H-Soft on mixed-reporting campuses, Tobit (median) ties H-Soft across both 90% MCS sets, and interior-only Cragg-ML lowers RMSE to 28.1. Under Vietnam's 2025 unified-clearing reform, exact filling falls to 10.4%, H-Soft and capped L1 tie quotas (p = 0.979), and 90% cluster-weighted conformal coverage drops from 89.3% to 74.6%. Across 257 reporting campuses, reconciled 2026 national totals (627,114 to 629,256) lie squarely within 604,533 to 662,044.

papers.title: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration
papers.abstract: Executing monolithic neural weights, frontier foundation models, or entire multi-agent workflows uniformly on every input incurs substantial computational, latency, and monetary overhead. Conditional computation mitigates this cost by deciding dynamically which internal experts, model endpoints, or specialized agents to invoke per request. Yet token-level gating in sparse neural architectures, query-level model cascades, and task-level multi-agent coordination have largely progressed in disconnected research silos, obscuring recurring system failures and transferable fixes. In this systematic review, we synthesize 2,289 studies published between 2017 and September 2026 (selected from 13,884 unique records) across 20 methodological families under a unified two-step inspect-then-allocate framework. Discrete hard selection accounts for 70%, 83%, and 91% of token-, query-, and task-scale literature respectively, and computational overhead appears as a top operational bottleneck across every layer. Engineering safeguards remain sharply asymmetric: intra-layer gating prioritizes load balancing while rarely incorporating uncertainty estimation, whereas model selection and agent orchestration rely on confidence thresholds and budget rules while confronting miscalibration and cascading errors. At the same time, publication volume is accelerating fastest in agentic task delegation, where routing mechanisms are least often isolated experimentally and methodological bias risk is highest.

papers.title: A Global Solver for Minimum-Time Connectivity Restoration in UAV Networks
papers.abstract: Node failures can split an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network into disconnected groups. Restoring communication requires moving the surviving aircraft, and the operator needs both an executable movement plan and an assessment of how much shorter the recovery could be. We develop Connectivity Restoration Branch-and-Bound (CR-BB), which returns a feasible plan and numerical displacement bounds; dividing these bounds by the common speed gives the corresponding time interval. Exact-arithmetic guarantees are established by the theorems. When the gap is not closed, the plan is feasible but not certified optimal. A fixed-tree subproblem is a second-order cone program. CR-BB searches over spanning trees and uses a Joint Mandatory-Link Bound (JMLB) to remove tree families that cannot improve the incumbent; Progress-based Adaptive Stopping (PAS) controls the search budget. On 200 matched cases, enabling the JMLB in the branch bound raised the number of cases meeting the prescribed displacement gap from 182 to 200 and reduced mean expanded nodes from 49.6 to 0.7. On a 60-case exact comparison, CR-BB met the gap in 90.0% of cases, compared with 55.0% for a spanning-tree mixed-integer conic formulation and 37.5% of the eight runs completed by an independent optimizer. On 1,000 paired recovery cases, CR-BB planned first restored connectivity in 72.35 steps on average, compared with 124.32 for an edge-augmentation baseline with conic refinement, a 41.8% reduction; on the common 50% subset the reduction was 28.1%. Across 2,466 cases, PAS reduced cumulative solver time by 20.9% and expanded nodes by 31.1% relative to a fixed search budget, with a 0.36-step mean increase in planned steps; most of the saving came from cases where neither configuration met the gap, and 60 plans became longer.

papers.title: VersionGS: Compact and Motion-Robust Dynamic Gaussian Splatting via Versioned Gaussians
papers.abstract: Recent dynamic Gaussian splatting methods encode temporal change, either as smooth functions of time or as constrained updates between frames. We observe that their reconstruction quality degrades significantly under fast motion. In challenging dance sequences, their PSNR drops by 1.1-4.0 dB on high-motion frames compared to low-motion frames. To overcome this limitation, we propose VersionGS, a method that directly encodes per-frame Gaussian states and uses motion estimation only to guide reconstruction. Within each group of frames, unchanged Gaussians keep their current versions in a shared dictionary, while modified Gaussians are appended as new versions. To maximize version reuse, we introduce selective sequential construction, which refines the Gaussians selected by optical flow, photograph differences or rendering errors and leaves the others unchanged. The dictionary is then pruned, fine-tuned with simulated quantization and encoded as images. Adjusting the pruning ratio trades off storage and quality without rebuilding the dictionary. On the fast dance sequences of DanceNet3D, VersionGS improves foreground PSNR by 2.7 dB over the best baseline, and its PSNR decreases by less than 0.3 dB on the highest-motion frames. On N3DV and Technicolor, it requires 6.0x and 5.7x less storage than TAD-GS, the strongest baseline overall, while achieving even higher PSNR. Finally, playback is fast and requires no motion model or neural network, only a 3DGS rasterizer.

authors.name: Shihang Wei
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Gaussian priors from nonlinear PDEs with the semiclassical approximation
papers.abstract: Probabilistic numerical methods for partial differential equations (PDE) combines the governing physics with observations to treat solving the PDE as a Bayesian inverse problem. This allows techniques to quantify the uncertainty in the field reconstruction under model-form error. In the majority of cases, a Gaussian prior is assigned to the field of interest, and Bayes's theorem in the infinite-dimensional setting is used to derive the posterior. While Gaussians have been shown to be well-suited for linear PDEs, a similar treatment for nonlinear PDEs remains open-ended. In this work, study the use of the semiclassical approximation to construct Gaussian priors from variational energies or integrated square residuals for probabilistic numerics. The prior is derived by expanding the PDE energy about a stable solution and uncovering a Gaussian form. We then analyze the different characteristics of the resulting priors as they pertain to the inverse problem. In particular, we find that the covariance operator is given by the inverse of the Hessian of the energy whose associated Cameron-Martin space is the solution space of the PDE. We also find that the prior responds to model-form error by sharpening or flattening itself depending on the distance between the ground truth and the solution of the assumed model.

papers.title: Separating Environment and Sensor Shift from Acquisition Protocol in Physical Vision Benchmarks
papers.abstract: In real-world deployments, vision systems must operate under varying environmental conditions, such as illumination changes. Recent work has explored adaptive sensing strategies that select camera parameters according to the current environment and downstream task to improve task performance. Reliable physical benchmarks are therefore essential for evaluating such strategies. We study ImageNet-ES-Diverse, a physical benchmark that evaluates the adaptive exposure control strategy Lens by recapturing printed ImageNet images under varying illumination conditions. We construct four controlled acquisition pipelines that vary printed-image scale and camera zoom, and conduct a pilot study with directly captured physical objects. We find that the acquisition choices substantially change benchmark difficulty on all downstream baselines. Moreover, the average classification-accuracy advantage of Lens over auto exposure observed on the original benchmark does not persist in either our collected pipelines or real-object pilot study. Oracle exposure selection nevertheless retains substantial gains, indicating remaining potential for sensor control. These findings highlight acquisition protocol as an important factor in physical benchmark evaluation and motivate explicit protocol reporting and evaluation across multiple acquisition setups when assessing adaptive-sensing benefits.

authors.name: Jianpeng Yao
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hang Qiu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: 3D Shape Recovery of Human-Made Space Objects from Light Curves with Image Denoisers as Priors
papers.abstract: This study presents a denoiser-regularized framework for recovering the three-dimensional convex shapes of human-made space objects from unresolved light curves. These shape estimates support object characterization for space situational awareness and mission support. Conventional methods for recovering the extended Gaussian image (EGI) using nonnegative least squares and directional refinement can discard surface-normal information needed to represent curved surfaces. The proposed framework represents the EGI as an area image on an equirectangular grid and recovers it in a randomly rotated frame using the plug-and-play alternating direction method of multipliers with a domain-adapted DRUNet denoiser. It then reconstructs a convex polytope from the recovered area image using scale-invariant support optimization with analytical gradients and volume normalization. Across seven faceted and curved shapes, with 10 runs per condition, the proposed method increases mean convex-hull intersection over union (IoU) from 0.615 for the baseline to 0.872 at a signal-to-noise ratio of 30 dB. Mean Hausdorff distance decreases from 0.198 to 0.050, and mean Chamfer distance decreases from 0.167 to 0.041. All three metrics improve for six of the seven shapes. The proposed method also retains much of its accuracy under noise, with mean IoU decreasing from 0.881 for noiseless measurements to 0.854 at 20 dB.

papers.title: A fast tangential rational Krylov subspace method with randomized sketching for large Lyapunov matrix equations
papers.abstract: We propose a tangential rational Krylov subspace method augmented with randomized sketching for solving continuous-time Lyapunov equations $AX + XA^T + BB^T = 0$, where $A$ is large and sparse and $B$ has a rank much higher than one. Numerical solutions require high-dimensional rational Krylov subspaces (e.g., of dimensions up to $\sim 1000$), leading to substantial computational cost and long runtime. Building on the adaptive strategies of [SIAM\,J.\,Matrix\,Anal.\,Appl., 35\,(2014), pp.\,476--498], which expand the subspace using the most relevant directions, we introduce several enhancements: selective orthogonalization of basis vectors and fast residual-norm estimation enabled by randomized sketching, and the option to use either adaptive distinct poles or a small set of repeated poles. We derive a new computable error bound for the approximate solutions and show that sketching does not degrade the convergence rate relative to the standard (non-sketched) algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved robustness and efficiency, with reduced runtimes and often higher accuracy than the standard tangential method.

authors.name: Tianqi Zhang
authors.institution: Capital University of Economics and Business

papers.title: PRISM: Perceptual Rate-Controllable Extreme Image Compression with Visual State-Space Models
papers.abstract: Generative codecs built on pretrained diffusion priors achieve high perceptual quality at ultra-low bitrates (below 0.05 bpp). However, most methods still require a separate model for each bitrate, and offer no control over the amount of detail synthesized. Their rate efficiency also depends on the entropy model, where Mamba-based state-space models (SSMs) have recently improved autoregressive context modeling. However, conventional SSM scans are not aligned with the decoding order, and each decoding pass restarts from an empty state, discarding context accumulated in previous passes. We propose PRISM, an extreme image compression method that addresses these limitations. A single model provides two continuous controls: a rate knob that traverses the rate-distortion curve and a realism knob that adjusts the level of detail synthesized. Its visual state-space (VSS) context model introduces a decode-order-aligned (DOA) scan, which predicts each latent from a state that summarizes all decoded context, and cross-tap state carry, which initializes each tap with a summary of the previous one. Experiments show that PRISM outperforms both variable-rate and fixed-rate codecs, requiring on average 22% less bitrate than the strongest baseline at equal FID while also achieving higher PSNR.

papers.title: Conjugation-preserving polynomial and rational interpolation for limited-memory matrix-function actions
papers.abstract: Approximating $f(A)b$ for a large nonsymmetric matrix can require substantial storage if a long Krylov basis is retained. We develop polynomial and rational interpolation schemes that use a fixed number of large recurrence vectors and preserve conjugation symmetry. Starting from a prescribed scalar approximation region, the schemes organize real nodes and complex-conjugate pairs into Newton-like bases with real interpolation coefficients. The polynomial and single-real-pole recurrences use real arithmetic in the matrix-action stage; the multi-pole construction also exploits conjugate pole pairs. A conjugation-preserving AAA procedure supplies interpolation data for the latter. We establish the interpolation and basis properties and compare the resulting realizations with Leja, Taylor, and Krylov methods on matrices from differential equations, model reduction, and networks. The experiments demonstrate arithmetic savings relative to complex-arithmetic counterparts and identify the influence of shifted solves and orthogonalization requirements. The methods are intended for memory-constrained computations in which useful approximation-region information is available.

authors.name: Tianqi Zhang
authors.institution: Capital University of Economics and Business

papers.title: Supporting Without Taking Over: AI Support in Gratitude Writing
papers.abstract: Gratitude writing can support well-being, but independent practice may lack guidance. Generative AI could help while shaping reflection, agency, and ownership. We investigated how gratitude-writing format and AI-assistance mode influence well-being and writing experiences. In a 2x2 between-subjects study (N=401), participants completed a gratitude reflection or a gratitude letter using two AI-assistance modes: scaffolding, which provided reflective questions after inactivity, or co-writing, which offered inline text suggestions. Participants' well-being improved after using our AI-assisted gratitude-writing system, consistent with the activity's intended benefits. However, participants' experiences revealed a trade-off between the AI-support types: co-writing received higher usability ratings, yet its immediacy could disrupt writing, and greater suggestion acceptance was associated with weaker perceived agency. Scaffolding supported stronger perceived human ownership but was sometimes overlooked. These findings extend human-AI writing research beyond productivity and text quality by showing how AI involvement shapes psychological outcomes and the experience of self-guided, emotionally meaningful writing.

authors.name: Sooyeon Jeong
authors.institution: Korea University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Failure Broadens, Success Sharpens: Continual Adaptation of Tool-Use Agents Across Diverse Tasks with Dual-Polarity Memory
papers.abstract: Large language model agents can self-improve over time by utilizing procedural memory derived from prior task trajectories, yet the distinct utilities of memories derived from local successes and failures remain underexplored. This work studies this question in a realistic setting with heterogeneous streams of multi-domain tool-use tasks and various environment constraints common in real-world scenarios. We develop \emph{Dual-Polarity Memory with Periodic Maintenance} (DualPM), a simple, retrieval-free memory workflow characterized by (1) customizable reflection and procedural memory generation from both local successes and failures within each trajectory, and (2) periodic memory consolidation over long task streams under a given memory capacity, preventing memory explosion. Online prequential evaluation with fine-grained metrics reveals that failure memory more strongly broadens coverage, success memory better streamlines execution, while combining both polarities effectively integrates both benefits. Further studies demonstrate that DualPM enables cross-domain memory generalization and continual memory adaptation, while external evaluation on EvoMemBench reveals the portability and effectiveness of DualPM as a general long-term procedural memory method.

papers.title: Two 3-Dimensional Coefficient Inverse Problems for Wave-like Equations With a Single Location of the Point Source
papers.abstract: In this paper two long standing open questions are addressed for the first time. Those questions are about Lipschitz stability estimates and uniqueness theorems for two Coefficient Inverse Problems (CIPs) for 3-Dimensional wave-like Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) with formally determined input data. We assume that a certain associated PDE is written in finite differences with respect to time t. The unknown coefficients depend on all three spatial variables. The key novelty here is that the input data for these CIPs are generated by only a single location of the point source at the moment of time {t = 0}. In the first CIP (CIP1) the unknown coefficient is the potential of a wave-like PDE. The second CIP (CIP2) is concerned with a far more challenging case when the unknown coefficient is involved in the principal part of the hyperbolic operator. In addition to Lipschitz stability and uniqueness results, numerical methods are developed for both CIPs. Their convergence analysis establishes the global convergence property of both numerical techniques. The latter is unlike the local convergence of conventional numerical procedures for CIPs. The method for CIP1 is tested computationally. Its extensive numerical testing for complicated media structures consistently demonstrates a very accurate performance of this method for noisy input data. The authors declare that artificial intelligence was not used for any part of this work.

authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

papers.title: LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts?
papers.abstract: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures revisit layer parameters across depths. This design increases effective depth without adding parameters. Recent looped MoE studies report substantial gains over the standard MoE at matched budgets (parameters, FLOPs and KV cache). However, the reported gains still confound parameter revisit with other design choices, e.g., network shape and residual scale. We ask, what does parameter revisit itself buy? Using matched non-revisit controls, we find that parameter revisit itself buys almost nothing. We argue that revisit only offers a freedom an MoE already has, i.e., trading experts for depth (more layers, fewer experts each) at fixed parameters. First, at matched budgets, we decompose the state-of-the-art looped recipe, with revisit last. A non-revisit control retains all the gain. Most comes from network shape, and the rest from residual scale. We prove this scale acts as a lower learning rate on revisited layers. This helps under AdamW's uneven layer step sizes, but disappears under Muon, which keeps them nearly equal. Second, beyond matched budgets, we evaluate revisit by adding compute at fixed parameters. One extra visit gains more than doubling the experts. Yet without revisit, a deeper standard MoE at equal parameters and compute obtains 90.2% of that gain under Muon. Overall, gains come from network shape, the optimizer and added compute, which a standard MoE can adopt. Accordingly, we propose LoopTitan-Base as a stronger MoE baseline. Under Muon, it matches the strongest looped recipe without revisit or residual scale. We open-source LoopTitan and release 17 pretrained models (including LoopTitan-Base and the control). Our experiment record is public as GitHub issues, with predictions pre-registered and the full exploration history kept. This is our Phase 1 technical report, laying the foundation for follow-up studies.

authors.name: Guanchu Wang
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

papers.title: Adaptive confidence bands for a continuous treatment effect curve under shape constraints
papers.abstract: In causal inference with observational data new inferential targets arise when treatment is continuous rather than discrete. Here we form (simultaneous) confidence bands over the continuous treatment effect curve. We form confidence bands based on assuming the curve satisfies shape constraints of either monotonicity or concavity, under the assumption of no unmeasured confounding. As is commonly the case, two nuisance functions arise, and our bands are asymptotically valid if the product of the error rates of the two nuisance functions is small enough. We also develop non-causal shape constrained bands in regression with fixed or random non-uniform grid which are of independent interest. Furthermore, our bands are adaptive to a range of function flatness and smoothness levels in that when the true flatness/smoothness level is unknown the bands still achieve the same (optimal) rate of convergence (in sup-norm) as when the true smoothness level is known. We demonstrate these bands through simulations and an application to the effect of nurse staffing on hospital performance.

papers.title: Small Leaks Sink Great Ships: Automated Analysis of Protocols That Tolerate Low-Entropy Keys
papers.abstract: Modern cryptographic protocols such as WPA2-PSK, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), and Bluetooth Classic (BC) tolerate low-entropy keys for user-friendliness, backward compatibility, or resource-constrained deployment, yet existing symbolic protocol verifiers rely on the perfect-encryption assumption and therefore cannot reason about brute-force attackers. Prior work addresses this gap only through protocol-specific, manually encoded reveal rules, which neither generalize across protocols nor systematically explore compound-key decomposition. We introduce the first protocol-agnostic, automated symbolic methodology for low-entropy keys, built on three abstractions: the message-derivation fact MDerive, which captures brute-force prerequisites independently of concrete function symbols; a three-tier breaking-oracle design (value-breaking, relationship-breaking, message-derivation) that composes with the standard Dolev-Yao attacker; and a graded bit-level attacker model that bounds the key length an attacker is allowed to exhaust. We realize the methodology as EntropyVerif, a syntax-sugar extension of Tamarin that requires no kernel modification. Using EntropyVerif we automatically rediscover the PMKID, KNOB, and Method Confusion attacks, and uncover a new attack on BC which we call the Unilateral Multi-Downgrade (UMD) attack: by repeatedly downgrading one side of a BC session and recombining the recovered key fragments, an attacker reduces session-key recovery against devices using the maximum 128-bit key from $2^{128}$ to $n \cdot 2^{128/n}$, bottoming out at $2^{12}$ for $n=16$---a factor of $2^{116}$ reduction that has been responsibly disclosed to the Bluetooth SIG. Across three real-world protocols and six BC device configurations, our results show that entropy-aware symbolic analysis is both feasible and necessary.

authors.name: Jing Chen

papers.title: Optimization of a Locally Shielded 16-Channel Transmit Array for Human Brain MRI at 10.5 T via Electromagnetic/Circuit Co-Simulation and Parallel Transmission Strategies
papers.abstract: Modern neuroimaging and neuroscience increasingly demand high spatial and temporal resolution, driving the use of ultrahigh-field (7 T and above) MRI for improved signal-to-noise ratio. Realizing this advantage depends critically on advanced radiofrequency (RF) and gradient technologies, particularly multi-channel transmit arrays and high-performance head-gradient systems. In integrated systems, a local RF shield must provide sufficient field confinement while preserving transmit performance and minimizing sensitivity to nearby conductive structures. In this work, we sought to optimize a locally shielded 16-channel transmit RF array for human neuroimaging at 10.5 T using electromagnetic/circuit co-simulation combined with parallel-transmission strategies. Candidate transmit-array and RF-shield configurations were evaluated before and after gradient-shield integration to identify a configuration with suitable RF transmit and shielding performance for the integrated system. The results show that no single standalone metric, including static RF shimming performance, dynamic parallel transmission (pTx) performance, or external-field leakage, reliably predicts robustness after gradient-shield integration. Progressive screening identified the aligned loop-folded dipole (LFD) array combined with a compact cylindrical shield featuring a conical top and three windows (160-mm radius and 70-mm window length) as the final configuration. Without RF-circuit retuning, the selected design maintained external-field leakage below 1% and after gradient shield integration achieved whole-brain excitation coefficient of variation (CoV) of approximately 27% with static RF shimming and 9% with dynamic pTx. Experimental validation of the unshielded LFD array showed good agreement between simulated and measured B1+ efficiency distributions, with a normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE) of approximately 8%.

papers.title: Inverse Radiative Transport on Non-Convex Domains
papers.abstract: This paper addresses an inverse source problem for the radiative transport equation in non-convex domains with a single "corner", generated by the union of two convex domains, asking whether an observer restricted to one part of the boundary of such a domain can "see around the corner" and recover a boundary source restricted to a part of the boundary hidden from the observer. The main result shows that with a condition on the geometry of the corner, an analyticity condition on the coefficients of the equation, and a finiteness condition on the scattering kernel, an isotropic boundary source hidden around the corner from the location of the observations can be recovered by measurements of the scattered light.

papers.title: Decision and Support Mechanisms under Platform Information Overload: A Generative-Agent Experiment on College Application
papers.abstract:
People now make major personal decisions surrounded by far more online information than they can read, yet research says little about why information overload affects some people more than others. We study this question in Chinese college applications, a high-stakes decision made amid heavy online content where each list can be scored objectively once admission cutoffs are released.
  We simulated 90 applicants using language-model agents with family backgrounds from a national household survey. Each applicant wrote a list of eight programs alone and revised it four times: after parent and teacher advice, after reading a feed of twenty real online items, after a mentor gave advice based on the applicant's rank, and after a second mentor offered only emotional support. After each step, we scored the list and asked how anxious the applicant felt.
  When applicants decided alone, admission rates were similar across socioeconomic status (SES) groups. The gap appeared once family background entered through parents and teachers: low-SES parents asked for low tuition and schools near home, leaving fewer reachable programs, so admission was 100% for high-SES vs. 77% for low-SES applicants. The platform feed gave everyone the same amount of information but did not narrow this gap; applicants maintained their decisions while reporting higher anxiety. Personalized advice cut the gap to 3 points by raising low-SES admission from 80% to 97%, but led students to higher tuition and less preferred majors. Emotional support did not further lower anxiety, but helped applicants go back and use helpful items they had ignored.
  These simulation results suggest that when information is abundant, more of it neither improves decisions nor reduces inequality. Personalized information does both, while moving inequality from the outcome to its cost.

authors.name: Tingyu Dai
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: HoMe: Toward Practical Harness Optimization of Memory Systems for AI Assistants
papers.abstract: The behavior of memory systems for long-running AI assistants is governed by a harness, which consists of the code, prompts, and configurations for memory construction, maintenance, retrieval, and answer generation. However, optimizing the harness of a memory system remains largely manual, and unrestricted editing alone does not ensure structural improvements. In this paper, we introduce HoMe, an evaluation-driven framework that iteratively evaluates candidate harnesses and derives each new candidate from any previously evaluated harness by editing any part of it. HoMe combines session-level memory versioning with execution traces to identify shared failure mechanisms across cases and localize them to the responsible sessions and harness components. It encourages early structural exploration through candidate gating and reduces evaluation cost through smoke tests, adaptive sampling, and the reuse of constructed memory. We validate HoMe with the open-source memory system ReMe on two large-scale long-horizon memory benchmarks, LongMemEval-S and BEAM. With six formal candidate evaluations per benchmark, after a full initial evaluation, HoMe discovers harnesses that improve end-task performance over the originally strong harness while consuming far fewer query-time tokens. The code is available at https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe.

papers.title: Shooting for Fit: Risk-Averse Stochastic Roster Construction from Bayesian Shot-Pattern Models
papers.abstract: Roster construction is a critical decision problem in professional basketball, requiring teams to balance player quality, player complementarity, and financial constraints under uncertainty. Existing roster optimization models primarily rely on individual player ratings and aggregate performance statistics, which provide limited information about how players' offensive contributions vary with their teammates. Recent advances in player-tracking technology have enabled statistical analyses of spatial shooting patterns, but these insights have rarely informed roster construction. We bridge this gap by developing a data-driven, risk-averse two-stage stochastic optimization framework for NBA roster construction. We first develop a Bayesian modeling framework that combines player statistics and spatial shot-chart data to identify player roles and estimate how teammate composition influences shot selection, shooting frequency, and scoring efficiency. The resulting model provides uncertainty-quantified offensive values for hypothetical five-player lineups, including combinations that have never played together. We then formulate roster construction as a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer program that optimizes player acquisitions under NBA salary-cap regulations while allowing lineup playing-time allocations to adapt to uncertain player roles. We evaluate the framework using 240 team-offseason decisions over eight seasons and two additional held-out seasons. The results demonstrate that incorporating spatial shooting compatibility substantially changes optimal roster decisions and improves predicted offensive performance relative to approaches based on individual player values. We further find that flexibility in allocating playing time across lineups absorbs much of the uncertainty about player roles.

authors.name: Cong Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A degree-stability method for the $p$-spectral Tur\'an-type problem for disjoint color-critical graphs
papers.abstract: Let $F_1,\ldots,F_t$ be pairwise vertex-disjoint color-critical graphs with $\chi(F_i)=r+1$ for each $i\in[t]$. For $r\ge 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, Simonovits [Discrete Math. 7 (1974) 349--376] proved that the graph $K_{t-1}\vee T_{n-t+1,r}$ uniquely maximizes the number of edges among $n$-vertex graphs containing no copy of $\cup_{i=1}^tF_i$. In 2024, Lei and Li [Electron. J. Combin. 31 (2024), P1.25] established the corresponding result for the adjacency spectral radius. We prove that, for every fixed $p>1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the same graph uniquely maximizes the $p$-spectral radius in this class. The proof reduces the problem to forbidding $t$ disjoint copies of a single color-critical graph and applies degree stability after deleting $t-1$ such copies.

papers.title: WADJET: Whole-Job Authorization and Dispatch for Job Execution Trust on FPGA System-on-Chip Accelerators
papers.abstract: On an FPGA system-on-chip, the software that submits work to an accelerator also decides what the accelerator does. It writes the registers one by one, and the hardware runs whatever it finds, so faulty or compromised software can change one address or resend a job. Existing protections decide who may reach an accelerator or keep its data safe. Deciding whether one job was approved and is still unused takes three things in one place: the only way to the accelerator, the whole job held back until checked, and a record of used approvals. WADJET puts the three in one gate in FPGA logic. A separate authority encrypts and authenticates each approved job, with a sequence number, using Ascon-AEAD128. The gate verifies the whole job before releasing any part, accepts only a newer sequence number, uses it up, and writes the registers of an unmodified accelerator itself. The gate replaces only the processor's direct line to the registers and works beside the existing protections. In a software model, a check on each write ran jobs mixed from two approved ones; the whole-job rule released none. Its release path is proven on the Verilog for all inputs. On a Zynq-7020 running a language model, it released all 21,000 approved jobs and none of 14,700 altered or repeated ones. It needs a third of the lookup tables of ShEF's register protection, which protects more, and adds about ten microseconds to starting a job. It assumes trusted control of its key, reset, and configuration.

papers.title: Benchmarking Open-Ended Vulnerability Discovery in Windows Kernel Binaries
papers.abstract: Frontier models are increasingly used to discover real-world security vulnerabilities, making it critical to systematically evaluate their cybersecurity capabilities. However, existing security benchmarks primarily focus on known vulnerabilities in open-source projects, largely overlooking closed-source binaries, which underpin much of the software industry. In this paper, we ask: how effective are frontier models at uncovering deep vulnerabilities in production binaries? To answer this question, we present DeepBinary, the first comprehensive benchmark for open-ended vulnerability discovery in Windows kernel binaries. Given a target binary, an agent analyzes it using a disassembler and kernel debugger in network-isolated VMs and reports each vulnerability with a crashing proof of concept (PoC). Unlike existing benchmarks, DeepBinary replays every report on fresh VMs and employs an LLM-based judge to assess its validity, uniqueness, and impact (estimated by bug bounty values). Beyond known vulnerabilities, DeepBinary also enables the discovery and validation of previously unknown (0-day) vulnerabilities. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of representative open- and closed-weight models (including GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) across diverse coding agents (including Codex and Claude Code) on 12 target binaries. In total, they discover over 200 vulnerabilities with an estimated aggregate bounty of $661,000, including 146 distinct previously unknown vulnerabilities across all experiments. Our results further reveal substantial differences in models' ability to analyze binaries, conduct experiments, and sustain vulnerability discovery over long horizons. Overall, DeepBinary makes long-horizon, open-ended vulnerability discovery in complex binaries measurable, revealing fundamental differences in how frontier models analyze and explore such systems.

papers.title: RankCast: Phase-Aware Rank Balancing in MoE Serving
papers.abstract: Modern large language model (LLM) inference increasingly adopts disaggregated architectures that separate Prefill (P) and Decode (D) phases. Meanwhile, Expert Parallelism (EP) has been widely adopted in large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model serving. However, load imbalance still slows down MoE inference because each layer must wait for the busiest EP rank. The main source of latency differs between prefill and decode. Prefill is compute-bound, and its MoE layers' latency is determined by the maximum token count of the busiest rank. At the same time, under moderate batch sizes, Decode is memory-bound, so the latency is dominated by the maximum active-expert count across ranks. To solve both problems under a unified framework, we present RankCast, a system that reduces rank-level maximum token counts during prefill and active-expert counts during decode. For every token, RankCast preserves the predicted Top-p experts and chooses the remaining k-p from its Top-L candidates (L > k). In prefill, RankCast yields a price per rank that steers flexible assignments to less loaded ranks. In decode, RankCast closes experts on the busiest ranks while preserving the constraints for each token. Both paths are implemented and tested in the state-of-the-art inference frameworks SGLang and DeepEP. We overlap RankCast's kernels with model execution and reuse the existing DeepEP communication channel for metadata transmission. On Qwen3-235B-A22B with EP=8 and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B with EP=16, RankCast removes over 75% of the busiest rank's excess prefill load, improves prefill input throughput by up to 19%, and reduces decode time per output token by up to 10%. The quality cost is below one percentage point.

authors.institution: Key Laboratory on Development and Application of Rural Renewable Energy

authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: PowerFix: Physics-Guided Iterative Repair for LLM-Assisted Power Converter Design
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly being explored for automated engineering design. However, repairing power-converter designs that fail engineering validation remains challenging: the system must identify physical causes, locate responsible design variables, and resolve violations without compromising other constraints. We introduce PowerFix, a physics-guided iterative repair framework that converts validation failures into structured diagnoses and executable patches while preserving topology and design requirements. PowerDiagGraph links failed checks to possible physical causes and constrains repair routes. An LLM prioritizes these routes, while a deterministic compiler translates selected repairs into authorized field-level edits. Candidates are validated on isolated design copies and committed only after all required engineering checks pass; failed validation can guide replanning. On our constructed 96-task flyback repair benchmark, comprising injected single faults, coupled faults, and held-out natural failures from our design generator, PowerFix achieves 78.7% verified repair success rate (VRSR), compared with 30.1% for the strongest of three LLM baselines. Three additional replanning rounds increase VRSR to 88.4%. These offline results provide pilot-stage evidence within a simulation-based design workflow, with hardware prototype validation and transfer to a second converter topology as the next steps toward deployment.

authors.name: Can Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Shi Qiu
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Missing Root: Geometric Imagination Without Images in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new paradigm and method for giving large language models spatial understanding. Standard language models operate exclusively over discrete words (secondary representations of things rather than continuous space itself), forcing them to guess geometry verbally. Whereas most multimodal approaches equate spatial grounding with camera images or video frames, spatial structure itself is not a picture: it consists of coordinate frames, solid boundaries, and how objects move and relate to each other in continuous space. Motivated by this distinction, we place continuous object tokens combining pose (position, orientation, and scale) and signed-distance shape embeddings alongside word tokens inside a single uninterrupted transformer sequence, allowing language and geometry to attend to each other as object scenes are built and updated step by step. Control tokens switch output automatically between natural-language words and continuous object state updates to a persistent object workspace, while an attention mask blocks earlier prose when generating the answer, so responses must be read directly from settled geometry. To prove this method works, we attach a narrow parallel spatial stream (+4.4% weights) alongside unfrozen Qwen3-1.7B layers. In our two-dimensional tests, the model spawns and transforms multi-object scenes from English descriptions, transfers shapes to held-out nouns, and relies causally on the workspace to answer spatial questions.

papers.title: Typical Angina, Reversed: A Long-Standing Documentation Error in the UCI Heart Disease Data
papers.abstract:
The UCI Heart Disease data are a widely used machine-learning benchmark. We show that their chest-pain variable is stored in reverse of its documentation. At all four sites, the code documented as "asymptomatic" (4) marks patients with typical angina, and the code documented as "typical angina" (1) marks patients with almost none of the classical angina features (at Cleveland, no chest pain).
  Two complementary checks establish this: (i) the chest-pain table and regression coefficients of the original 1986 Cleveland study are reproduced only under the corrected reading; (ii) in the Budapest, Switzerland and Long Beach files, 93-96% of patients coded 4 have all three classical angina features. A 1990 word-labeled Cleveland file already uses the documented labels, and Statlog (Heart), a Cleveland subset, stores the same codes. OpenML, PMLB and two highly voted Kaggle copies that name the categories use the same documented labels (about 400,000 downloads combined).
  We audited a seeded random sample of 150 records from a pre-specified Scholar query for SHAP studies of these data mentioning asymptomatic chest pain (124 readable). Of 32 papers that state a direction for a named category, 25 (78%; 95% CI 61-89%) state one inconsistent with the corrected category identities; 22 (69%; 51-82%; post hoc) are attributable to the documentation error, and nine of these explain it clinically. None of the 124 readable papers identifies the reversal.
  Conventional models are essentially unaffected, one reason the error went unnoticed. Interpretations that attach the documented names to model effects are reversed, and zero-shot language-model classifiers that read the labels are misled: with the documented labels, three open-weight models lose 0.12-0.33 in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) given age, sex and chest-pain type. We give the corrected mapping, evidence and code.

papers.title: Topological Clique Exclusion in Positively Curved Graphs
papers.abstract: We study locally finite graphs of positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature and minimum degree at least $t-1$ under two exclusions: a topological $K_t$, denoted $TK_t$, and its locally topological version $TK^{(\leq2)}_t$, in which every replacement path has length at most two. The ordinary exclusion gives an $O(t^{7})$ maximum-degree bound by combining the classical density theorem for topological cliques with a curvature-driven rainbow-clique argument. For $K_t$-minor-free graphs, a Hall-matching refinement improves the maximum-degree bound to $O(t^3(\log t)^{3/2})$ and, for connected graphs, the order bound to $O(t^{19}(\log t)^9)$. For the weaker local exclusion, a codegree graph and Ramsey's theorem give the bound $\exp(O(t\log t))$. We also prove an exponential maximum-degree bound when the full 1-subdivision $K_t^{(2)}$ is forbidden as a subgraph, assuming minimum degree at least $t$.

papers.title: WorldUAV: Scaling UAV Data Synthesis via World Models
papers.abstract: UAV detection and tracking remain constrained by the scarcity of high-quality training data. Existing game-engine-based synthetic UAV data suffer from a substantial synthetic-to-real gap, while the high cost of manually collected real-world UAV data limits dataset scale. Therefore, we introduce WorldUAV, a high-quality UAV dataset constructed through an efficient framework powered by world models. Specifically, WorldUAV directly integrates UAVs into readily available real-world videos, naturally preserving realistic backgrounds, illumination, and scene dynamics. Leveraging the spatiotemporal priors of world models, it generates UAV videos with plausible motion, pose variations, and cross-frame consistency, effectively narrowing the gap between synthetic and real data. We further develop an agentic pipeline orchestrated by a multimodal large language model that acquires sources, plans UAV trajectories, invokes synthesis, and verifies generated videos, enabling fully automated dataset construction. WorldUAV comprises 6,878 UAV videos and 205,778 UAV images. Experiments show that WorldUAV significantly improves the performance of UAV detectors. Moreover, it substantially reduces dataset construction costs, requiring only 15 seconds and USD 0.0005 API cost per high-quality UAV image. Our work offers both a high-quality dataset and a scalable data generation paradigm for UAV detection and tracking.

authors.name: Zuoxiu Zhang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yue Dong
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Zhikai Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Tensor products of finite groups without compatibility conditions are finite
papers.abstract: It has been an open question whether Inassaridze's tensor product $G\otimes H$ is finite whenever $G$ and $H$ are finite. In this paper, we answer this question in the affirmative, and, as a consequence, we prove that the low dimensional nonabelian homology groups $H_i(G,A)$, $i=0,1$, are finite whenever $G$ and $A$ are finite. We achieve this by introducing a much more general tensor product $G\bt H$, defined for groups acting on themselves and on each other by arbitrary automorphisms, with no compatibility conditions, and subject only to the two defining relations of the nonabelian tensor product. We prove that $G\bt H$ is finite whenever $G$ and $H$ are finite. Since the nonabelian tensor product of Brown and Loday, Inassaridze's tensor product and the box-tensor product are all quotients or special cases of $G\bt H$, this brings the finiteness results for all these tensor products under one umbrella.

authors.name: Sathasivam Kalithasan
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Thiruvananthapuram

authors.name: Viji Zachariah Thomas
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Thiruvananthapuram

papers.title: Federated Learning with Uncertainty Quantification on Pseudo Label Exchange
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate federated stochastic operator learning for stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), with an emphasis on heterogeneous client data distributions and uncertainty quantification. Federated learning enables clients to collaboratively train models without exchanging their original solution data, but conventional federated averaging can suffer significant performance degradation when client distributions differ, particularly when their input function supports are disjoint. To address these challenges, we propose the Federated Stochastic Operator Network (FedSON), a two-phase framework that combines auxiliary data construction with stochastic operator learning. In the first phase, locally trained deterministic neural operators and their corresponding input functions are exchanged to generate pseudolabeled auxiliary data, enabling the federated model to learn across heterogeneous input distributions without sharing original solution trajectories. In the second phase, a stochastic operator network is trained on top of the frozen deterministic operator to characterize stochastic fluctuations and quantify uncertainty in the predicted solutions. Numerical experiments involving the heat equation, viscous Burgers' equation, and two-dimensional advection-diffusion equation demonstrate the FedSON substantially improves deterministic prediction accuracy under heterogeneous client distributions while producing uncertainty estimates comparable to those obtained through centralized training.

authors.name: Feng Bao
authors.institution: Innovation Academy for Precision Measurement Science and Technology, CAS

papers.title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Designing surface-capping ligands for high-performance halide perovskite nanocrystals requires navigating a vast molecular space while discovering design rules that govern ligand-surface interactions. Here, we introduce PerovAgent, an autonomous multi-agent framework that combines large language model (LLM)-driven scientific reasoning with computational tools for atomistic model construction, machine-learned interatomic potential evaluation, and statistical validation. Across ten independent campaigns on CsPbBr3 surfaces, PerovAgent adaptively explored and refined diverse ligand chemistries while progressively improving the binding-energy objective. Beyond optimization, the framework converts recurring chemical observations into explicit design principles that can be statistically evaluated. Of 35 formulated principles, 19 were prospectively supported, of which seven also passed the confound audit, highlighting the need to systematically validate plausible LLM-generated hypotheses during autonomous discovery. A recurrent alkynyl-phosphonate principle was further examined using density functional theory, which reproduced the predicted energetic preference. These results demonstrate an autonomous discovery framework that not only searches molecular space and optimizes the scalar objective but also transforms its search trajectory into systematically testable design principles. The framework can also be extended to more complex ligands, including zwitterionic, multidentate, and polymerizable ligands, to explore a wider range of ligand-surface interactions and uncover new design principles for halide perovskite nanocrystals.

authors.name: Amanda Conde Del Moral
authors.institution: University of Puerto Rico at Río Piedras

papers.title: MAFNet-UR$^3$: Mask-Aware Fusion Network for Unified Raindrop and Reflection Removal
papers.abstract: Raindrops and reflections frequently co-occur on windshields and jointly obscure scene content, making their unified removal, referred to as UR$^3$, a highly ill-posed problem. Existing approaches are mainly based on diffusion models and thus can produce visually plausible restorations. However, they may generate scene-inconsistent structures in severely corrupted regions. To address this limitation, we propose MAFNet-UR$^3$, which adopts a three-stage framework to exploit multiple observations for scene-consistent unified raindrop and reflection removal. Specifically, Stage I suppresses raindrops while preserving the reflection layer, and Stage II performs prior-guided reflection removal followed by image-space refinement. Stage III estimates degradation masks from intermediate restoration results to provide degradation cues and performs mask-aware multi-scale fusion across observations to preserve scene structure and fine details. As a result, our proposed MAFNet-UR$^3$-L achieves state-of-the-art performance on the RDRF-testing benchmark, outperforming DiffUR$^3$ by 2.33 dB in PSNR and 2.7634 in the challenge score. Our method ranked third in the LoViF 2026 UR$^3$ Challenge, achieving a final score of 41.1416.

authors.name: Jae Woong Soh
authors.institution: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Simulation-Assisted Radio Map Reconstruction with Sparse Field Measurements
papers.abstract: Field measurements are essential for evaluating radio map reconstruction under real-world conditions, but their acquisition is costly. This letter proposes a simulation-assisted parameterized-background data-weak (SA-PBDW) method that combines propagation simulations with sparse field measurements, which jointly estimates background coefficients and a spatial correction to account for discrepancies between simulated and measured power distributions. Dense field measurements are collected for multiple transmitter positions at an urban site. Evaluations on the collected data and RadioMapSeer demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy and structural fidelity over benchmark methods at reduced sampling rates.

authors.name: Jian Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Spe3DUp: Faithful Trajectory Distillation for Fast Image-to-3D Generation
papers.abstract: Recent 3D generative models can produce high-quality meshes with complex structures and fine geometric details, with broad applications in games, film, and digital design. However, high-quality generation typically relies on long multi-step sampling processes that repeatedly evaluate large networks, leading to long inference times. At the same time, reference-driven tasks such as game-asset reconstruction and product digitization demand close correspondence to the input image: generated geometry must faithfully reconstruct the specific reference object. Acceleration must therefore reduce sampling computation while preserving the model's ability to reconstruct that object. To enable fast and faithful 3D generation, we introduce Spe3DUp, a coarse-to-fine framework based on Faithful Trajectory Distillation (FTD). FTD directly supervises few-step students with the teacher's input-conditioned denoising trajectories to preserve its generation behavior. We apply FTD separately to coarse geometry generation and geometric refinement, compressing both sampling processes while maintaining correspondence to the reference input. We further accelerate the complete mesh-generation pipeline with efficient geometry decoding and parallel remeshing. Experiments show that Spe3DUp maintains geometric quality and input correspondence close to those of the teacher, accelerates the coarse and refinement DiTs by 10.0x and 19.9x, respectively, and achieves a 7.7x end-to-end speedup over the original teacher pipeline.

papers.title: Mortgage Backed Securities with p-Laplacian Diffusion and Random Prepayment
papers.abstract: In this note we consider deterministic and stochastic versions of a PDE pricing model for mortgage backed securities, driven by p-Laplacian motion. We show the existence of weak solutions in the $1<p<2$ case, for sufficiently small initial data. In the stochastic case, we consider a random prepayment function, when $p=2$. Herein we derive results concerning the uniform first order sensitivity and mean squared sensitivity of the solution, to the pricing model.

papers.title: Two-timescale variational Q-learning for ergodic risk-sensitive control of Markov chains
papers.abstract: We propose a variational Q-learning algorithm for the ergodic risk-sensitive control of a discrete-time Markov chain with finite state and action spaces and an unknown transition kernel. The proposed algorithm is a two-timescale stochastic approximation algorithm, where the slow iteration solves for the fixed point of the multiplicative Bellman equation cast in a variational form, while the fast iteration solves the associated optimization problem over the probability simplex that stems from the variational representation. We prove that the iterates converge almost surely to the risk-sensitive Q-function and maximizing transition kernel. The proof adapts the ODE method for two-timescale stochastic approximation, where we analyze the global asymptotic stability of the equilibria of the corresponding fast and slow ODEs as well as bound the trajectory of the fast ODE away from zero. The main challenge lies in proving that, almost surely, the slow iterates are norm-bounded and the fast iterates are bounded below away from zero on the support of the transition kernel. We address this by using a fluid scaling approach for the slow iteration combined with tailored estimates for the fast iteration to control a certain fluid-scaled relative entropy error that arises in the ODE approximation. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithm and compare it with the existing risk-sensitive Q-learning algorithms.

papers.title: DualCast: Dual-Image Conditioned Diffusion Transformers for Digital Human E-Commerce Video Generation
papers.abstract: Recent advances in world models for game interaction and control have increased the demand for large-scale gameplay videos paired with camera trajectories. However, capturing synchronized camera trajectories often requires game-specific pipelines, limiting scalability. We therefore propose GameWeaver, a unified diffusion framework that automatically produces paired video--camera data through three complementary tasks: camera pose estimation from observed video, video generation along a prescribed camera trajectory, and joint video--camera generation from a reference image and text. First, each tipxel stores the normalized 3D coordinates of a pixel ray's endpoint in a reference coordinate frame. The resulting three-channel tipxel fields and RGB frames share the pretrained video model's VAE. Next, a fully trainable dual-stream Transformer exchanges appearance and geometry features through bidirectional gated attention and conditions both streams on shared text features. Finally, deterministic fitting recovers camera intrinsics and normalized trajectories from generated tipxel fields. In our evaluation tasks, GameWeaver achieves a normalized translation MSE of 0.0029 for camera control; for joint generation, it scores 85.48 out of 100 on instruction adherence versus 64.71 for the best cascade on that metric, validating the feasibility of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Pietsch's favourite problem on singular traces
papers.abstract: In 2023, A. Pietsch formulated twenty-seven open problems concerning traces on operator ideals. We give an affirmative answer to Problem 16, which Pietsch singled out as his personal favourite, by constructing a nonzero bounded singular spectral trace on the weak Weyl ideal over the class of all Banach spaces.

authors.name: Gustavo Araujo
authors.institution: Instituto de Cardiologia de Santa Catarina

papers.title: Atheism and Cross-Country National Cognitive Skills: Evidence from a Beta Regression Analysis
papers.abstract: This study performs a beta regression analysis to investigate how country-level cognitive skills---measured using harmonized large-scale international educational assessments and expressed on an IQ-type scale---are associated with the prevalence of atheism in 131 countries. We find that this association is nonlinear: at low levels of cognitive skills, increases are associated with lower expected levels of atheism, whereas beyond a threshold, they are associated with higher expected atheism rates. This turning point is estimated to occur at approximately 65 on the IQ-type scale. The strength and location of the relationship vary across regions. We estimate elasticities of expected atheism rates with respect to cognitive skills for all countries in the sample and introduce the concept of the atheism gap to identify countries where observed prevalence is substantially higher or lower than predicted by their conditioning variables.

papers.title: TAT-Det: A Dataset for Testicular Appendage Torsion Detection and Segmentation in Ultrasound Images
papers.abstract:
Background: Testicular appendage torsion (TAT) is the leading cause of acute scrotal pain in prepubertal children. Yet, its diagnosis remains challenging due to nonspecific clinical manifestations and the absence of standardized datasets for pediatric acute scrotal emergencies.
  Results: We present TAT-Det, an expert-annotated ultrasound dataset specifically designed for TAT. TAT-Det comprises 2,600 ultrasound images from 1,203 patients collected at the Children's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. Each TAT-positive image is accompanied by lesion-level bounding boxes for detection and pixel-level segmentation masks for fine-grained delineation. Annotations were produced through a multi-stage workflow involving independent annotation by board-certified pediatric sonographers, consensus review, and refinement. Baseline benchmarks for object detection and semantic segmentation using representative deep learning models are further provided, with YOLO11m achieving the best detection performance and RWKV-UNet the best segmentation performance.
  Conclusions: TAT-Det addresses the lack of publicly available resources for pediatric emergency ultrasound and establishes a foundation for developing and evaluating artificial intelligence methods for automated TAT analysis.
