papers.title: Bistable waves and propagation success on hexagonal lattice
papers.abstract: Inspired by propagation phenomena occurring on media with hexagonal structures, we propose an idealized system of bistable reaction-diffusion equations posed on a hexagonal lattice, and investigate the existence and speed of traveling wave solutions. We establish a sharp criterion for propagation success (nonzero wave speed) and failure (zero wave speed), where the criterion is determined by an angle-dependent periodic threshold function and the ratio of two parameters in the nonlinearity. Moreover, the sign of the wave speeds is governed by the angle and the parameter ratio. Our results imply that the hexagonal structure and bistability significantly affect the propagation dynamics.

authors.name: Jian Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Lost in Translation, Not in Confidence: Benchmarking and Calibrating Multilingual Decision Models
papers.abstract: Decision models are language models fine-tuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. They are built on multilingual bases but ranked almost entirely in English. We evaluate 25 top-ranked open-weight decision models on 17 tasks in 14 languages, comparing each language with English on parallel items. Every model loses accuracy in every language, from about 2 points in high-resource languages to 8 in Tamil, while confidence falls only half as much: a threshold set for 95\% accuracy in English yields 90% in Tamil. The size of the loss is set by the language and the base model rather than by leaderboard rank. In 81 controlled fine-tuning runs, task skill learned in English transfers to other languages and a few thousand target-language items narrow large losses, but neither more data nor full-parameter tuning closes them. Finally, the same test items are answered more accurately in all 23 benchmark--language pairs we compare when an LLM rather than a person translated them, so LLM-translated test sets understate the gap.

authors.name: See-Kiong Ng
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: StyleID++: Position-Decoupled and Structure-Coherent Style Retrieval across Diffusion Architectures
papers.abstract: Attention injection offers a remarkably simple route to training-free style transfer: content queries retrieve style keys and values inside a pretrained diffusion model. We show that this operation also creates an overlooked failure mode. Position signals that are useful within one image become a spurious shared coordinate system across two spatially unrelated images, causing content tokens to favor style tokens at similar coordinates. This cross-image positional leakage appears in both convolutional U-Nets and diffusion transformers (DiTs), despite their different position mechanisms. Removing the positional shortcut exposes a second problem: unconstrained global retrieval lets related content tokens select incompatible style regions, producing fragmented appearance. We present StyleID++, a training-free framework that addresses the two problems jointly. Position-Decoupled Retrieval reduces coordinate-dependent matching through circular padding in U-Nets and injection-only RoPE removal in DiTs, while preserving native position modeling elsewhere. Affinity-Coherent Refinement then regularizes style assignments with the content self-attention graph, encouraging structurally related tokens to retrieve compatible style evidence. We quantify the leakage with a coordinate--centroid correlation and a permutation test on the style reference. The permutation error can be driven to zero in both backbones, which identifies the position mechanism as the carrier of the leakage, and StyleID++ obtains the best ArtFID of all methods we compare.

papers.title: MotifFlow: Training-Free, Self-Contained Style Transfer from Color to Motif in Rectified Flow Transformers
papers.abstract: Expressive style transfer must reproduce a painting's palette, brushwork, and characteristic motifs while retaining the content image's structure. Attention injection is effective in U-Net-based diffusion models, but adapting it to FLUX often transfers color without capturing the style's distinctive brushwork. Our analysis across backbones links this gap to how injected features are integrated across neighboring spatial locations. We introduce MotifFlow, a training-free, self-contained framework that combines style injection with style-alignment guidance in FLUX. Injection supplies style features during generation but does not explicitly encourage the model's native attention output to align with them. We therefore use the discrepancy between native and injected attention outputs to guide latent-space updates, encouraging the evolving image to develop the style's distinctive brushwork and motifs. Style encoding, guidance, and synthesis all use the same frozen backbone, without auxiliary image encoders or trained adapters. A single strength parameter controls the transition from color transfer to pronounced brushwork and motifs, with additional support for regional stylization and style mixing. Experiments on 1,000 content-style pairs show that MotifFlow better matches the local textures of the style image than baseline methods and produces more consistent stylization than injection alone. The same design extends to FLUX.2.

papers.title: APEX: Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration
papers.abstract:
Ensemble-based methods provide a practical framework for history matching, prediction, and optimization of subsurface models. In methodological studies, however, performance is rarely assessed from a single run. Comparisons typically span cases, configurations, and random seeds, while each evaluation may require an expensive external simulator. Keeping such studies computationally bounded, auditable, and reproducible therefore requires more than implementing a numerical method: experiments must be validated before execution, computational costs estimated, repeated runs organized consistently, and configurations and outputs made traceable. To address these needs, we developed APEX (Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration), an open-source Python platform that provides a common framework for configuring, validating, executing, recording, and comparing ensemble-based experiments.
  APEX is organized around three concepts: an experiment defines what is executed, a run records a single execution, and a study coordinates and compares multiple experiments or runs. Experiments are specified through validated configurations, which can also be generated by a planner agent. Before execution, APEX estimates the maximum number of forward simulations required. If the estimate exceeds a user-defined threshold, submission is held for approval. Each run records provenance information, while studies repeat problems across variants and paired replicates and compare results using paired statistical analyses. Scientific and computational components, including methods, simulators, metrics, and optimizers, are implemented as plugins. A command line interface, Python client, REST service with a web interface, and tools for language model agents access these capabilities through a common service layer.

papers.title: Differentially Private Policy Optimization in Linear MDPs with Adversarial Rewards
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) in personalized services often relies on sensitive interaction data. Motivated by the need to protect these data, we study differentially private (DP) policy optimization in episodic linear Markov decision processes (MDPs) with unknown transitions and adaptive adversarial linear rewards under full-information feedback. This setting poses two key challenges: past trajectories are repeatedly reused for policy evaluation, and reward choices may depend on previously released private statistics. The proposed algorithm combines batched proximal policy optimization (PPO) updates with optimistic policy evaluation, using private regression statistics and reward estimates to protect both trajectories and reward functions under joint differential privacy (JDP). With all other parameters fixed, our high-probability regret bound retains the same leading $\widetilde{O}\left(K^{3/4}\right)$ dependence on the number of episodes $K$ as the corresponding non-private bound for batched optimistic PPO. The additional privacy terms scale as $\widetilde{O} \left(K^{5/8}\right)$ and $\widetilde{O} \left(K^{1/2}\right)$. Thus, privacy incurs only lower-order additive costs in $K$, even under adaptive adversarial rewards.

authors.name: Yi He
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: LLMVC: Large Language Model-Guided Generative Video Compression
papers.abstract: Recent generative video methods achieve strong perceptual compression by encoding videos into compact latent representations and reconstructing them with powerful generative decoders. However, visual encoders must compress both high-level semantics and dense visual details into a unified latent space, which complicates entropy coding and decoding and may cause semantic drift under aggressive compression. In this work, we propose Large Language Model-Guided Video Compression (LLMVC), which leverages the summarization capability of frozen video large language models (Video-LLMs) to generate compact semantic tokens aligned with temporal latent slices for guiding video compression. Specifically, Hybrid Bidirectional Bimodal Attention (HBBA) enables bidirectional interactions between visual and semantic features during encoding and decoding. Semantic-Conditioned Cross-Attention (SCCA) incorporates semantic features into probability modeling during entropy coding. These semantic features provide high-level guidance throughout the pipeline, improving representation quality and encouraging semantic consistency through a transmitted text side channel. Experiments on UVG, MCL-JCV, and HEVC show that LLMVC consistently improves compression performance over traditional and recent neural video compression methods in terms of LPIPS and DISTS, while also achieving better fidelity than recent perceptual codecs.

authors.name: Wei Jiang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Differential coupling drives Turing pattern formation in neural fields: a mechanism for Parkinson's disease and deep brain stimulation
papers.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is an effective treatment for the motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet its mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. Abnormal beta-band synchronization in the basal ganglia and thalamocortical circuit is a hallmark of PD, but a theoretical framework linking network synchronization to spatial pattern formation is lacking. Here we show that a two-layer neural field model with differential interlayer coupling undergoes a Turing instability, spontaneously generating a diverse repertoire of spatially ordered patterns, including stripes, spots, rings, and spiral waves. The model yields the critical conditions and wavelengths for this instability, quantitatively predicting the observed pattern morphologies. Crucially, the interlayer difference, a natural measure of synchrony, exhibits strongly regime dependent dynamics. These findings establish a dynamical framework linking spatial pattern formation to pathological beta-band synchronization, providing a theoretical mechanism for DBS modulation of network states and a mathematical basis for optimizing stimulation parameters.

papers.title: Exact Minimum Distances of Primitive Narrow-Sense BCH Codes: At and Beyond the Bose Distance
papers.abstract: We determine the exact minimum distances of two families of primitive narrow-sense BCH codes of length $q^m-1$, where $q$ is a prime power and $m\geq 4$. For $1\leq i\leq\lfloor m/2\rfloor$, codes with designed distance $q^m-q^{m-1}-q^{m-1-i}-1$ have minimum distance and Bose distance both equal to their designed distance. Furthermore, for integers $\ell, i, s$ satisfying $3\leq\ell<m-1$ and $\lfloor m/(\ell+1)\rfloor\leq i\leq s<\lfloor(m-1)/\ell\rfloor$, codes with designed distance $q^m-q^{m-1}-q^{m-1-i}-q^s-1$ have Bose distance equal to their designed distance and minimum distance $q^m-q^{m-1}-q^{m-1-i}-1$. Consequently, the gap between the minimum distance and the Bose distance in this family is exactly $q^s$ and grows without bound as $m$ increases, with fixed $\ell$.The proofs proceed by constructing good zero-sets from quadratic forms for the first family, and by combining upper bounds provided by the first family with lower bounds derived from the divisibility of codeword weights in punctured generalized Reed--Muller codes for the second. We also derive explicit dimension formulas by counting cyclotomic cosets.

papers.title: Controllable CAD Generation and Interactive Editing of Fluid Rotors
papers.abstract: Computer-aided design (CAD) provides the geometric foundation for rotors in fluid rotating machinery. However, creating models for different rotors requires different modeling processes, making it difficult to control geometry through design intent and reuse existing models. We introduce VaneCraft, an agent-driven framework for rotor generation, inverse recovery, and editing through a unified analytical representation. The agent interprets design requests and invokes geometric modeling operations. The representation defines geometric controls through meridional geometry and independent boundary angle laws. An anisotropic partial differential equation (PDE) maps these controls to the blade surfaces. Geometric parameter correction (GPC) uses a joint geometric encoder and a parameter decoder to refine controls initialized from rotor category and dimensions. Inverse recovery maps existing CAD to the same geometric controls for reconstruction and continued editing. Experiments demonstrate that VaneCraft supports anisotropy control and parameter editing and outperforms representative baselines in rotor CAD generation tasks. Project page is available on \href{https://github.com/shenchen333/vanecraft}{GitHub}.

authors.name: Shen Chen
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

authors.name: Lei Li
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: OneQuery: Unified Sequence-to-Structure Generation for Multilingual E-commerce Query Understanding
papers.abstract: Multilingual e-commerce search requires robust query understanding to convert cross-lingual user queries with varied linguistic patterns into standardized semantic representations that support retrieval and ranking. However, traditional Query Understanding systems suffer from error accumulation, separately optimized subtasks that ignore their mutual correlations, and high maintenance costs. To address these issues, this paper proposes OneQuery, a unified generative framework for multilingual query understanding based on domain-specific large language models in e-commerce. We reformulate four subtasks, namely Language Recognition, Spelling Correction, Translation, and Query Tagging, into a unified Sequenceto-Structure autoregressive generation process constrained by predefined schemas, and design a three-stage progressive training pipeline with multi-task reinforcement learning alignment. OneQuery demonstrates consistent gains over baselines across all tasks and remains effective across different backbone sizes, and online experiments in the AliExpress e-commerce search scenario further confirm its practical value for industrial deployment.

papers.title: Recall4D: Forgetting, Not Misalignment, Limits Long-Horizon Feed-Forward 4D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 4D trackers recover camera motion, depth, and point trajectories from short video clips, but chaining windows over long videos degrades their accuracy. We find that replacing inter-window alignment with ground-truth transforms leaves tracking error essentially unchanged. Static-point error instead grows with time since last observation: repeatedly predicting a static point from windows that no longer observe it corrupts previously recovered geometry. We call this failure forgetting. Merely retaining the last observed positions of unseen points reduces error by 26% on PointOdyssey without modifying the tracker. We introduce Recall4D, a training-free framework that augments a frozen tracker with a persistent world state and sparse motion anchors. Static points retain their world-space positions outside the camera view and are refined by averaging observations decoded at sparse keyframes while in view. For dynamic objects, the tracker decodes sparse representative anchors, while geometric skinning propagates their displacements to dense queries. Across two long-horizon benchmarks, Recall4D improves the accuracy of its backbone while running 7.6-9.0$\times$ faster, and its accuracy gains carry over to five further backbones and three other long-sequence tasks, demonstrating its generality.

papers.title: Asset4D-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Editable 3D and 4D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: A cart can follow its reference trajectory while its cargo floats above the deck. Asset4D-Bench tests whether coding agents recover objects, motion and interactions from visual references as editable Blender scenes. Its 114 conditions span image editing, video reconstruction with matched full or partial starter assets, and independently selected from-scratch tasks. We independently reopen projects and measure them against native reference states. The 228 archived scores include original delivery outcomes and versioned measures of scene quality. On 24 from-scratch tasks, each model earns full dynamics credit on 14. Of these, three GPT-6.1-Sol and eight GPT-6-Astra reconstructions earn zero relation points. Under the fixed scoring weights, relations contribute 5.15 points to the 6.50-point Sol-minus-Astra difference in mean recovered fidelity. Differences in execution and recovery policy across archived runs preclude a causal estimate of starter-asset effects.

authors.name: Chengyi Sun
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou Medical University

papers.title: FlashProve-Next: Verifiable Inference for Production LLM APIs
papers.abstract:
Clients of closed-weight LLM APIs cannot verify whether a provider ran the advertised model, precision, hidden prompt, and reasoning budget. Existing approaches either trust hardware or third parties, or re-prove every layer of an integer surrogate at high cost while diverging from native floating-point serving.
  FlashProve-Next produces verifiable, zero-knowledge-masked proofs for individual LLM API responses without modifying native serving (bf16/fp8/mxfp4, random sampling, FlashAttention, CUDA graphs, batching, prefix caching) and without disclosing weights, hidden prompts, hidden reasoning, or activations (dense profiles fix coarse geometry; cross-architecture hiding is deferred). A non-depleting Reed-Solomon weight commitment model_id opens inside proofs via hidden column openings, while local per-operator rounding contracts remove integer surrogates and the refusal-bit leak. Cost-weighted spot-checking supports non-interactive public verification (NI-315, $\varepsilon \le 2^{-40}$, $Q \le 2^{64}$) and external-seed C_pre mode (ExtSeed-153, $\varepsilon \le 2^{-20}$, $Q_{\rm samp} \le 2^{30}$).
  Twenty-eight Lean 4 modules (696 declarations, zero sorry, standard axioms only) mechanize round-by-round soundness, bucketed sampling, $\mathbb{F}_{p^3}$ constrained-mask binding, causal masking, six IR gadgets, and executable FPN2 verifiers. Five-model Blackwell calibration gives zero false rejections across 1.85M GEMM/MoE blocks and 1.96M non-GEMM rows. Our zero-Phase-2 folded backend (folded ZK simulator open) proves Qwen3-0.6B ExtSeed-153 (1.47B cells, 8 MiB) in 450.2 s GPU (10.76 s CPU) at unique-decoding $Q=128$, passes a 14/14 cheating matrix, and scales to 36-layer Qwen3-4B (dev $4+2$) and live vLLM Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 Relation 6 (1.49 s prove, 23.4 ms Rust verify, public weight tiles). Rust fpn-verify checks 8 MiB FPN2 Relation 2 proofs in 10.1 ms on CPU.

papers.title: Universal Stabilization with Six Records
papers.abstract: This letter shows that a single feedback controller needs only six retained observation records to handle the largest universally stabilizable uncertainty range for the scalar discrete-time benchmark model of Xie and Guo, when uncertainty is measured by the radius of a generalized Lipschitz ball. Existing constructions can require arbitrarily many records along bounded trajectories. Our controller retains at most six genuine state-response pairs and five auxiliary real scalars. Each update requires a uniformly bounded number of elementary operations. No knowledge of the plant, its generalized Lipschitz constants, or the disturbance bound is required.

authors.name: Senhan Yao
authors.institution: Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science

papers.title: EMMA: Efficient and Effective Cooperative Multi-Modal Analytics over Embodied AI Data
papers.abstract: Embodied AI has seen growing real-world deployment, particularly in autonomous vehicles and robots. These vehicles and robots continuously capture large collections of multi-modal data, such as video, LiDAR point clouds, and GPS trajectories. Historical collections of these data support model improvement and safety assessment through scene retrieval, object trajectory extraction, and corresponding analysis. Processing such analytical queries is challenging because answering them may require combining information from different modalities and observations captured by different moving vehicles or robots, while extracting that information with deep models at every scene incurs prohibitive cost. We present EMMA, an operator-oriented query-processing framework for embodied AI data. EMMA compiles analytical queries into composable operators and executes them on demand. To support accurate query evaluation, EMMA performs modality-aware staged predicate evaluation and selectively combines overlapping observations. To reduce query cost, EMMA uses a temporal co-location index to identify joint-analysis candidates, adaptive scene skipping to reduce model calls, and a shared world store to reuse extracted information across operators and queries. EMMA trains execution policies offline and deploys them as plug-ins. Based on lightweight observations, these policies determine whether the current scene is analyzed independently or jointly and how many subsequent scenes can be safely skipped, balancing analytical accuracy and execution cost. Experiments show that EMMA substantially reduces query execution cost while preserving query accuracy.

authors.name: Zheng Wang
authors.institution: State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: FlipVLA: Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action(VLA) Models Only Through Bit Flips
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions in real-world environments, making malicious model tampering a potential threat to physical safety. We study whether object-triggered backdoors can be implanted through a small, fixed set of parameter bit flips without retraining. The central challenge is to make persistent weight modifications disrupt trigger-present behavior while preserving performance on non-trigger inputs. We propose FlipVLA, a two-stage selector-amplifier method that exploits existing visual features within an FC-GELU-FC structure. The selector constructs a trigger-dependent response in a selected channel, using GELU to attenuate background activity. The amplifier modifies a connected downstream weight to convert this response into an action-relevant perturbation. Channel screening and discrete bit search construct both components under a limited modification budget. Experiments on OpenVLA-OFT and GR00T N1.7 across four LIBERO suites achieve attack success rates of 90.22% to 100%, with task success decreasing by at most 1.5 percentage points on clean scenes.

papers.title: Spectral Optimal Transport for Dynamics-Aware Sign Language Generation
papers.abstract: Sign language generation (SLG) translates spoken-language text into pose sequences that convey its meaning. Recently, flow-based models with optimal transport (OT) have become a strong SLG baseline by handling the one-to-many nature of text-to-sign. While classifier-free guidance (CFG) could be applied to further strengthen the semantic alignment theoretically, its training involves conditional and unconditional training, which may contradict the pose-space OT, thus reducing the generation quality. Under the condition dropout, one noise sample can be paired with target motions exhibiting incompatible motion dynamics, interfering with the semantic guidance when the text condition is present. To address this issue, we propose Spectral Optimal Transport (SOT), which augments the pose-space cost with a spectral feature distance, reweighting the coupling toward the temporal-frequency structure of the target motions, thereby improving the performance when using CFG. The quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: RadOncGym: An Agent-Based Framework for Radiotherapy Dose-Mimicking Optimization
papers.abstract: AI dose-prediction models generate patient-specific 3D dose distributions from patient anatomy, providing an important intermediate representation for automated radiotherapy planning. However, an AI-predicted dose must undergo downstream optimization to produce a physically constrained treatment plan, a process that requires balancing competing planning objectives. We present RadOncGym, an agent-based framework that enables an LLM agent to iteratively tune 12 planning-objective weights for dose-mimicking optimization. To reduce iterative evaluation cost, RadOncGym incorporates a surrogate verifier that provides rapid feedback while allowing the agent to decide when to request a full planning solve within a fixed solve budget. We evaluate RadOncGym on 60 OpenKBP head-and-neck patients, each paired with 10 predictions from OpenKBP-Opt dose-prediction sets, yielding 600 patient-prediction contexts per experimental configuration. Under RadOncGym's 16-turn setting with a three-solve budget, a GPT-5.6 Sol agent reduces mean clinical-criterion violation by 0.6131 Gy and improves DVH and dose scores by 0.5986 and 0.2204 Gy relative to leaving all 12 weights fixed at 1, outperforming all evaluated non-agent weight-tuning methods under the same solve budget. It remains competitive with the 16-solve variants of these methods while requiring 75.0-77.6% less normalized runtime. RadOncGym demonstrates the potential of LLM agents as optimization planners in downstream radiotherapy plan optimization and provides a public testbed for their systematic evaluation. Code and configurations are available at https://github.com/miaot-usc/RadOncGym.

papers.title: Fairness-Regularized Principal Component Analysis
papers.abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) optimizes aggregate reconstruction accuracy but may represent heterogeneous groups unevenly. We study fairness-regularized PCA, which balances aggregate reconstruction risk against worst-group reconstruction regret, and establish its population and statistical properties. First, we characterize the reconstruction-fairness trade-off and show that, under a nondegeneracy condition, a small fairness penalty reduces worst-group regret to first order while increasing aggregate reconstruction risk only to second order. This reveals a vanishing initial marginal cost of improving fairness. We also identify conditions under which the regularization path remains locally constant. A minimax spectral characterization shows that, under an optimal effective eigengap condition, the convex relaxation is exact and Fair PCA is equivalent to ordinary PCA with endogenously adjusted group weights. Second, we develop a statistical theory for estimating fairness-regularized principal subspaces. A uniform eigengap over the set of possibly nonunique dual optimizers implies polyhedral identification and quadratic growth, yielding first-order perturbation bounds and convergence rates that accommodate growing dimensions, ranks, and numbers of groups. Third, we establish uniform recovery of the reconstruction-fairness path and theoretical guarantees for data-adaptive penalty selection. Simulations and an NHANES accelerometry application demonstrate substantial improvements in worst-group representation quality with minimal loss of aggregate reconstruction accuracy.

authors.name: Chuang Xu
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Continuous Foundation-Guided Pseudo-Label Weighting for Breast Ultrasound Domain Adaptation
papers.abstract: Breast ultrasound segmentation models often generalize poorly across scanners, institutions, and patient populations. We investigate continuous foundation-guided pseudo-label weighting for unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA). An exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher generates target-domain pseudo-labels, while a frozen ultrasound segmentation model (AutoSAMUS) modulates their contribution using a bounded weight that combines the prior's certainty with its probabilistic agreement with the teacher. In contrast to our earlier selective BiRP rule, the proposed formulation supervises every target pixel with a weight in [0.5, 1] and requires no foundation-model inference at test time. We evaluate the method on five public breast ultrasound datasets, spanning three source domains and eleven source-target directions. Under the TransUNet protocol, continuous weighting outperforms both all-pixel EMA and original BiRP on all four BUSI-source targets, and achieves the highest mean Dice and lowest HD95 among the compared methods on all four BUS-BRA-source targets. Results with BrEaST as the source are mixed: continuous weighting performs best on BUSI and comparably to original BiRP on OASBUD, whereas none of the adaptation methods surpasses source-only training on BUS-UCLM. In a separate U-Net pipeline, agreement-only weighting performs comparably to the full formulation, leaving the incremental value of prior certainty unresolved. Because the weighting rule was developed after some target-test results had been examined, we treat the study as exploratory and report adverse as well as favorable outcomes.

papers.title: Self-Assembled Triangular Sc-rich Nanodomains: The Orign of Anomalous Alloy Scattering in ScAlN/GaN Heterostructures
papers.abstract: Wurtzite scandium aluminium nitride (ScAlN) alloys hold substantial potential for GaN heterostructure high-electron mobility transistors, owing to their large spontaneous polarization gradient and the ability to achieve precise lattice matching at heterointerface. Nevertheless, despite continuous advances in epitaxy and device fabrication, the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) mobility in ScAlN/GaN heterostructures remains persistently limited, and the underlying microscopic origin remains elusive. Here, we uncover an anomalous electron scattering mechanism from laterally correlated alloy disorder that spontaneously develops within the ScAlN barrier driven by strain-field undulations imposed by threading dislocations. Dislocation strain field partitions the growth front into nanoscale domains with distinct strain states, driving anisotropic diffusion of Sc adatoms and yielding crystallographically oriented triangular Sc-rich nanodomains. Reducing the threading dislocation density from 2.8E10 to 4.4E8 cm^-2 suppresses areal density of nanodomains by more than two orders of magnitude. As a result, low-temperature Hall mobility increases from 1800 to 11995 cm^2*V^-1*s^-1. These findings establish dislocation-mediated Sc-rich nanodomains as the dominant source of anomalously strong alloy scattering, resolving the mobility bottleneck for high-performance nitride electronics.

papers.title: Free boundary MHD equilibria with surface tension
papers.abstract:
Free boundary equilibria of an ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) plasma, at rest, with surface tension and an exterior vacuum are studied. Within the frozen-in orbit of a reference magnetic field, every equilibrium is a critical point of the magnetic plus surface energy over the space of volume-preserving embeddings; the capillary boundary condition is the first-variation boundary term, and no assumption on the connectivity of the boundary is required.
  In the plane the frozen-in law fixes the distribution of the stream function and turns the energy into a rearrangement functional. For a single-axis reference field a sharp lower bound is proved that depends only on that distribution and is attained by an explicit area-preserving diffeomorphism, smooth across the axis, which yields a classical equilibrium. For Morse stream functions sharper bounds governed by the level-set topology are obtained, with a strict gap at an isolated simple saddle merge. In three dimensions no such reduction is available: the energy does not control the full gradient of the embedding, no scalar rearrangement principle applies, and the axisymmetric reduction yields only a conditional lower bound.

papers.title: CondUQ: Calibrated Conditional Uncertainty Quantification Using Distribution Matching
papers.abstract: Many applications, especially reliability- and safety-critical ones, require accurate uncertainty quantification for the outputs of model- or learning-based measurement, estimation, and prediction systems. The errors of such systems often vary with factors such as input quality and operating conditions, and thus cannot be accurately described by a single Gaussian model. Although Gaussian mixture models and calibrated quantiles can approximate such error distributions, their unconditional forms do not capture how the error behavior depends on these factors. Hence, we propose condUQ, an approach that conditions error models on observable factors for enabling accurate and reliable uncertainty quantification. condUQ is built on top of an existing system without modifying it and applies even when the system is a black box. First, condUQ maps the observable factors to a latent quality index (QI) such that errors sharing the same QI follow a common, approximately Gaussian conditional distribution. The QI predictor is trained end-to-end with a distribution-matching objective, without requiring quality labels. Second, for each QI, a Gaussian error model is then fitted and calibrated on a large held-out dataset. condUQ is demonstrated on three examples: (a) GPS multipath errors conditioned on satellite elevation and signal strength, (b) relative attitude errors of a transformer-based visual relative pose regression model conditioned on its internal features of the image pairs, and (c) prediction errors of a world model conditioned on the input observations and actions. In all three examples, condUQ substantially reduces the discrepancy between the modeled and empirical error distributions compared with a single global model. Moreover, the learned QIs reveal how the underlying factors affect the error characteristics in a manner consistent with physical principles.

papers.title: MixMoMo: Accelerating Extra--Large MoE Inference with Mixed--Precision GPU--NPU Execution on Mobile Devices
papers.abstract: Mobile agents and on-device intelligence increasingly demand more capable models on smartphones. Through sparse expert activation, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) scales model capacity, yet growing numbers of fine-grained experts complicate loading and computation. Model compression complements expert offloading by reducing storage and computation costs. Among compression techniques, mixed-precision quantization assigns lower expert bitwidths to balance model quality and inference efficiency. However, existing offline metrics and routing scores fail to reflect expert quantization sensitivity, undermining precision assignment. Diverse bitwidths also complicate balanced expert allocation across GPUs and NPUs with distinct execution characteristics, while tile-wise dequantization underutilizes NPU vector parallelism. We present MixMoMo, an efficient mixed-precision inference runtime for extra-large MoE models on heterogeneous mobile SoCs. MixMoMo combines offline quantization-impact profiles with activation-based runtime risk estimates for quality-constrained expert bitwidth assignment. It further adopts precision-structured execution for balanced GPU-NPU expert allocation and HVX-parallel dequantization for efficient NPU vector utilization. Across three MoE models and five benchmarks on two mobile platforms, MixMoMo achieves average decoding speedups of 3.72x over uniform Q4_0 and 1.53x over the strongest mixed-precision MoE baseline.

authors.name: Jiayu Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Asymptotically Efficient Finite Impulse Response System Identification without Noise Knowledge
papers.abstract: Efficient identification of finite impulse response systems under unknown or heavy-tailed noise remains a challenge in system identification. Classical estimators, including least squares (LS) and robust alternatives like least absolute deviations (LAD), are often sensitive to outliers or statistically inefficient when noise characteristics deviate from their underlying assumptions. To address this, we propose a novel class of adaptive estimators that achieves asymptotic efficiency without requiring prior knowledge of the noise distribution. Our approach leverages kernel density estimation to construct two nonparametric maximum likelihood-type estimators: the estimated maximum likelihood estimator (eMLE) and the estimated profiled MLE (epMLE). These estimators approximate the likelihood using residuals from consistent initial estimates, avoiding parametric assumptions on the noise. We establish theoretical guarantees showing that, under mild regularity conditions, both eMLE and epMLE are consistent, asymptotically normal, and attain the Cram\'er--Rao lower bound, thereby achieving asymptotic efficiency. Additionally, we develop computationally efficient one-step Newton--Raphson algorithms that implement these estimators without sacrificing asymptotic efficiency. Extensive simulations across various noise distributions confirm that the proposed methods outperform classical LS and LAD estimators in both robustness and accuracy, often matching oracle MLE performance.

papers.title: CARE-WM: Same-Horizon Self-Conditioning with Constraint-Adaptive Regularization for Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Planning with latent world models requires both accurate multi-step predictions and latent distances that reflect physical proximity to the goal. However, models are typically trained on ground-truth observations but must rely on their own imaginations during planning, while closer latent distances do not necessarily correspond to better task outcomes. Existing methods resort to auxiliary training objectives or additional task-cost readouts, which respectively incur extra training overhead or leave the latent geometry itself misaligned with task cost. We introduce CARE-WM, a drop-in training method that meets both requirements without additional supervision, a separate cost model, or any change to LeWM's architecture and Euclidean-cost planner. CARE-WM trains the predictor on its own predictions and adaptively calibrates the strength of latent regularization. With a single hyperparameter configuration, CARE-WM improves mean planning success over LeWM across all evaluated continuous-control tasks and matches or exceeds the best results of other LeWM-family methods on most tasks. Further analyses show lower open-loop latent prediction error and closer agreement between latent-cost rankings and physical task costs.

papers.title: Design-based causal inference for ROC curves
papers.abstract: In randomized experiments, causal inference traditionally focuses on the average treatment effect, yet comparing the treatment and control potential outcome distributions is often of interest. Under complete randomization, we adopt a design-based framework without imposing an outcome model to study the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, which measures the proportion of treated outcomes exceeding each upper quantile of the control distribution. We propose an estimator that depends only on pooled outcome ranks, establish its asymptotic normality, and construct conservative variance estimators and confidence intervals. We also develop covariate adjustment directly for the ROC estimator, preserving the target estimand while achieving an asymptotic variance no larger than that of the unadjusted estimator. We further construct simultaneous confidence bands over an interior range of quantile levels and extend pointwise inference to the extreme upper tail of the control distribution, with both extensions accommodating covariate adjustment. Simulation studies and an application to a large-scale online learning experiment illustrate the proposed methods.

papers.title: Surf-Style: Surface-Based Scene Stylization
papers.abstract: Consistent and controllable 3D stylization is critical for visual computing applications such as immersive visualization, augmented and virtual reality content creation, and artistic scene rendering. While 2D image stylization has advanced significantly, extending these methods to 3D remains challenging due to the need for cross-view consistency, where stylized renderings must align across all viewpoints. Applying 2D stylization independently to each rendered view often results in inconsistencies across perspectives. Existing methods attempt to improve consistency by leveraging implicit radiance field representations, which model scene appearance as a function of spatial locations. However, these methods struggle with ambiguity in updating colors, as the indirect dependence between pixel appearance and learnable scene parameters makes it difficult to enforce consistent stylization during optimization. This work presents Surface-based Scene Stylization (Surf-Style), which reconstructs object surfaces in a 3D scene and uses these surfaces to achieve geometric consistency and localized stylization. Surf-Style defines a learnable appearance model over 3D space, which is modified to replicate the visual style of a reference image. Compared to state-of-the-art methods, our method achieves superior consistency and offers greater flexibility in controllable stylization, including the ability to target specific surface regions and combine different styles.

papers.title: Projector Subspace Optimization for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance through instruction tuning, yet adapting them to sequential tasks requires Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT). Existing replay-free methods expand prompts or routed LoRA experts across multi-layer decoders, incurring heavy parameter and routing overhead while shifting internal feature distributions. Instead, we identify the final linear layer of the vision-language projector as a high-capacity, coordinate-stationary bridge, where sequential updates easily induce interface drift by displacing historical visual tokens. While low-rank subspace adaptation offers a compact remedy, selecting directions solely from historical statistics or task gradients sacrifices plasticity or stability, and unconstrained multi-step updates still accumulate large drift. To resolve both issues, we propose Projector Refinement through Optimized Update Directions (PROUD), a continual subspace optimization framework for the terminal projector layer. At task onset, PROUD combines retained input statistics with initial gradients to analytically extract a metric-orthonormal subspace maximizing first-order task gain under a drift budget. During training, it regularizes updates within this fixed subspace via an exact Frobenius penalty before losslessly merging them with zero inference or routing overhead. Experiments on UCIT and CoIN across MLLM backbones show that PROUD outperforms recent replay-free baselines in continual accuracy while curbing forgetting with a fraction of trainable parameters.

authors.name: Lijun Zhang
authors.institution: Yunnan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: On canonical projections of the bipartite graph $D(k,q)$
papers.abstract: The bipartite graphs $D(k,q)$, constructed by Lazebnik et al. in 1995, are $q$-regular, edge-transitive, and of large girth. In this paper, we primarily instigate the canonical projections of $D(k,q)$. First, as a generalization of $D(k,q)$, we define a bipartite graph $\Gamma(\Omega,q)$, where $\Omega$, referred to as a rooted binary tree, is a finite subset of binary sequences closed under the deletion of any suffix. We then derive several significant properties regarding the symmetry, connectivity and girth of $\Gamma(\Omega,q)$. For arbitrary nonnegative integers $m$ and $n$, we fully characterize the connected components of $\Gamma(\Omega_{m,n},q)$, which is isomorphic to a canonical projection of $D(k,q)$ with $k\geq 2m+2$. Our results demonstrate that the connected components of $\{\Gamma(\Omega_{m,n},q)\}_{2\leq |m-n|\leq 3}$ form a novel family of graphs with large girth in the sense of Biggs.

papers.title: Detectable by Design: Learning a Continuous 3D Saliency Field from 2D Detector Responses
papers.abstract:
The 3D points kept in a map decide whether a camera can be localized against it, and this choice matters more as the map becomes sparser. Existing 3D keypoint detectors usually define saliency by semantics, repeatability, reconstruction or descriptor matchability. None of these definitions asks whether a point will actually be detected in an image, and as a result most of the points they select are not detected again in images.
  In this paper, we define 3D saliency as image detectability: the response of a 2D interest-point detector at a surface point, aggregated over all views in which the point is visible. We propose DetField, a continuous field over 3D space that takes a point cloud as input and predicts detectability at any location around it. The supervision is the response of a 2D detector, back-projected from images onto the point cloud. Multi-scale curvature invariants are passed to the decoder at every query point, bypassing the voxel pooling of the encoder.
  In a localization benchmark that isolates the choice of 3D points, DetField outperforms Harris-3D and five learned 3D keypoint methods on objects and on real indoor scenes. On unseen rooms, it improves localization success by 7.4 points over Harris-3D, the strongest baseline. On objects, it also leads under a 2D detector not used in training. On sparse maps, it stays ahead of Harris-3D on both objects and real scenes.

papers.title: An Image Detectability Field as a Viewpoint Utility for 2D-3D Localization in Sparse Maps
papers.abstract: In 2D-3D localization, a camera estimates its pose by matching an image to a 3D map. A camera held in a hand or mounted on a robot can often choose its viewpoint before it takes the image. In this work, we ask whether an image detectability field is a useful viewpoint utility when the planner reads only the geometry of the map. The field can be queried at any 3D point near a surface. From the local geometry around the point, it predicts how likely a 2D image detector is to fire at the projection of the point. We use the trained field as it is, without fine-tuning it for view selection. A fixed SuperPoint and EPnP-RANSAC localizer then estimates the pose from the chosen view. We answer in two settings, each with a test registered before the runs. On synthetic ShapeNet objects with sparse point maps, summing the field over the visible landmarks beats counting them by +2.0 points of localization success rate (object-clustered 95% interval [+0.7, +3.2]). It also beats summing Harris-3D ranks by +2.2 [+0.8, +3.5]. On real indoor scenes from SceneFun3D, our adaptation of the learned view scorer LWL falls below counting on the test rooms. We therefore add the field to a learned per-landmark planner. On the test rooms with sparse maps whose landmarks the field also selects, the planner with the field beats the same planner without it by +1.8 points. It beats the planner with Harris-3D or curvature in its place by +1.0 and +0.8 points. All three room-clustered intervals lie above zero. In both settings, the field helps in sparse maps and is on par with Harris-3D in dense maps.

papers.title: Admoab-DETR: Resolution-Tiered Fusion for Infrared-Visible Object Detection with Missing Modalities
papers.abstract: Infrared and visible images offer complementary cues for all-weather object detection, yet real-world sensor dropouts can leave one stream unavailable and degrade paired-input detectors. Meanwhile, existing modality-adaptive methods apply heavy cross-modal attention uniformly across scales, incurring prohibitive token overhead on high-resolution maps. We propose Admoab-DETR, a unified real-time detector supporting infrared-only, visible-only, and paired inputs with a single set of weights. Specifically, \emph{Resolution-Tiered Fusion} (RTF) allocates fusion capacity by spatial token density and feature granularity: a lightweight Spatial Modality Gate governs fine local fusion at the highest-resolution scale with zero-cost single-view pass-through, while channel-compressed deformable Admoab necks capture cross-modal correspondence at coarser semantic scales. Furthermore, \emph{Mode-Matched Feature Distillation} (MMFD) aligns multi-scale encoder features with an availability-synchronized full-fusion teacher, avoiding ill-posed cross-modal hallucination while cutting parameters by 18.1\% and paired latency by 39.6\% at zero inference overhead. We also construct Admoab, a strictly registered 20,000-pair infrared--visible benchmark across diverse scenes. Experiments show Admoab-DETR achieves state-of-the-art accuracy--efficiency trade-offs across missing-modality and paired benchmarks. Our code will be available at https://github.com/liwenchao0615/Admoab-DETR.

papers.title: Multi-view fnirs identifies neurophysiological subtypes in post-stroke aphasia
papers.abstract: Post-stroke aphasia is clinically heterogeneous, and conventional classifications may not capture differences in brain functional organisation. We tested whether resting-state and task-based functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) could identify neurophysiological subgroups alongside clinical assessment.Seventy-nine patients underwent unsupervised clustering using three fNIRS feature views: resting-state activity and connectivity, language-task activation, and rest-to-task connectivity reconfiguration. Similarity network fusion and spectral clustering integrated the views. Clinical and behavioural measures were excluded from clustering.Three clusters (n = 32, 17 and 30) were identified. This solution had the largest eigengap and was the only candidate significant after permutation testing and Holm correction (adjusted P = 0.001). It was stable under subsampling (mean adjusted Rand index, 0.773), but agreement fell to 0.217 when the resting-state view was removed. Clusters differed in most regional intrinsic-activity measures and all resting-state connectivity summaries, with few differences in task activation or connectivity reconfiguration. Their profiles showed higher right anterior prefrontal activity, distributed fronto-sensorimotor and parietal alterations, and reduced interhemispheric connectivity, respectively.Cluster membership was not significantly associated with conventional aphasia subtype (Cram\'er's V = 0.287), and baseline clinical language scores and task performance did not differ between clusters.These findings identify three neurophysiological subgroups distinguished mainly by intrinsic activity and resting-state functional connectivity, not clearly aligned with conventional aphasia classifications or baseline clinical measures. Multi-view fNIRS analysis may complement clinical characterisation, requiring independent and longitudinal validation.

authors.name: Bingbing Lin
authors.institution: Fujian University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Jinglei Ni
authors.institution: Fujian University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Meifang Tian
authors.institution: Fujian University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Wai Ting Siok
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Agentic-Level Adversarial Purification: Revisiting Diffusion Purifiers on Native-Resolution Agentic Inputs
papers.abstract: Vision-language agents act on native-resolution renders of multi-element pages, where one perturbed photo or a few altered text strokes can redirect the decision. Any content provider can craft such a perturbation on the open model behind the agent, so a plug-in purifier is the natural first line of defense. Yet diffusion purifiers were designed and evaluated at the fixed resolution of the diffusion model on classifier or natural-image benchmarks, and defense evaluations for agents test JPEG, blur and noise but no diffusion purifier. We present the first study of adversarial purification at the agentic level, for an agent built on Qwen3-VL-8B: purifiers run at native resolution on multi-element inputs, face grey-box attackers who know the agent's model but not the defense, and are compared at matched clean cost. We show that treating agentic inputs as classifier inputs misleads both evaluation and design. Resizing the input to the resolution of the diffusion model, as existing purifiers do, raises the TextVQA clean cost of the Divide-and-Conquer purifier (DC) from 4.0 to 35.7 points. On web-shop pages, DC keeps 85.0% grey-box robust accuracy against web-hardened perturbations, where cheap input transformations at matched clean cost keep at most 40.0%, and this robustness comes from the global noise level: input-estimated masks and noise levels add none. These findings hold on a disjoint held-out set and on a second VLM and yield three requirements for defenses, we release the protocol.

papers.title: TigerTTS: Draft-Guided Multi-Frame Parallel Speech-Token Language Model for Fast and Robust Text-to-Speech
papers.abstract: Autoregressive speech-token language models enable high-quality TTS but suffer from latency growth with sequence length, word omission or repetition without explicit alignment, and fidelity limits from discrete codebooks. We present TigerTTS, a production-grade LLM TTS system built around a lightweight non-autoregressive NAR model. With explicit alignment, the NAR model drafts tokens for the entire utterance, which are refined frame-by-frame by a compact autoregressive LLM. The draft is aligned frame-for-frame with LLM targets and injected at the input, ensuring training-inference consistency. Leveraging its accuracy, the LLM predicts 12 tokens per step across 3 frames and 4 groups, while a conditional-total-correlation bound keeps parallel prediction nearly lossless. We use a codebook-free FSQ tokenizer with four parallel groups and about 1800 bps to avoid codebook collapse. The backbone keeps positional information only in input embeddings, enabling exact MLA weight absorption and a four-fold KV-cache reduction. Decoding uses CUDA Graphs with a graph-safe multinomial sampler. A Fast mode further reduces first-packet latency: the NAR generator acts as a prefix synthesizer with RTF 0.03, producing the first 500 ms before LLM decoding. With CUDA-Graph decoding, TigerTTS reaches RTF 0.05, about 20x real-time, on one GPU. Despite using a 0.15B backbone, it outperforms standard PyTorch inference of VoxCPM2 2B by 5x and CosyVoice 2 by 16x. TigerTTS achieves the lowest CER and WER on SEED, 1.09 and 1.67, and strong WER, NMOS, and speaker similarity on LibriSpeech test-clean, 2.22, 4.36, and 0.820. Fast-mode guided semantic tokens provide a well-aligned content prior, reducing dropped words, loops, and runaway generation without sacrificing speed.

papers.title: Several classes of few-weight linear codes based on Weil sums
papers.abstract: Linear codes over finite fields with few weights are of significant interest due to their applications in areas such as secret sharing schemes, strongly regular graphs, and association schemes. In this paper, we construct several classes of p-ary linear codes based on Weil sums via the defining-set construction of bivariate form, where p is an odd prime. Utilizing the theory of quadratic forms and Weil sums over finite fields, the parameters and weight distributions of the codes are completely determined. As a result, several families of three-weight or four-weight linear codes are obtained from our construction. In addition, it is shown that most of our codes are minimal.

papers.title: Four Classes of Few-Weight Linear Codes over $u\mathbb{F}_q+u^2\mathbb{F}_q+u^3\mathbb{F}_q$ from Simplicial Complexes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct linear codes over the commutative non-unital ring $u\mathbb{F}_q+u^2\mathbb{F}_q+u^3\mathbb{F}_q$, where $u^4=0$, using simplicial complexes in $\mathbb{F}_q^m$ and their complements. For codes defined by two arbitrary nonempty simplicial complexes, we determine the lengths and $\mathbb{F}_q$-dimensions. When each complex has a single maximal element with nonempty proper support, we use an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear Gray map and exponential sums to determine the parameters and Lee weight distributions of four classes of codes. These classes have two, at most five, at most four, and at most eight nonzero Lee weights, respectively. Puncturing the Gray images yields projective codes with dual minimum distance three. Using the Griesmer bound, we obtain families of distance-optimal projective codes, including a binary family whose lengths exceed the bound by three. The Gray images are Euclidean self-orthogonal for $q=3$ and for $q=2$ under an additional condition, and Hermitian self-orthogonal for $q=4$. We also give sufficient conditions for minimality of both the Gray images and the projective codes.

papers.title: T-type brown dwarfs in Euclid DR1: from spectral classification to physical parameters
papers.abstract: The wide-area coverage and near-infrared spectroscopy of Euclid provide an opportunity to identify and characterize ultracool dwarfs. Its NISP slitless spectra cover prominent molecular absorption features of T-type brown dwarfs (T-BDs). We aim to identify T-BDs in Euclid DR1, determine their spectral types and atmospheric parameters, and estimate their masses, ages, radii, and distances. We select candidates using morphological criteria, near-infrared colour cuts, and spectral fitting, followed by visual inspection of multi-band images. Spectral types are determined using the SPLAT toolkit. Atmospheric parameters are derived independently using the Sonora Elf Owl and LOWZ model grids with Bayesian MCMC fitting. Evolutionary models are then used to estimate fundamental physical properties. We identify 141 T-BDs, including 134 newly identified objects. Effective temperature shows the best agreement between the two atmospheric models, with a mean absolute difference of 94 K, while other parameters exhibit larger discrepancies. The inferred mass-radius distribution shows decreasing radius with increasing mass, and older objects generally have smaller radii. We also identify 21 unusually blue T-BDs with I_E-H_E < 2.5. Their SEDs and colour overlap with previously reported white dwarf-brown dwarf (WD+BD) candidates suggest that some may be unresolved WD+T-BD systems. The two distance estimation methods show a mean absolute difference of approximately 37 pc. Three additional sources have nearby objects in Euclid images and are potential multiple-system candidates.

papers.title: Recoverability policy editing for closed-loop safety in autonomous driving
papers.abstract: Autonomous driving powered by neural network models lacks safety guarantees. We propose a state-level policy editing technique that guarantees closed-loop safety under recoverable disturbances while reusing the model's existing driving capabilities. Closed-loop safety means that the vehicle remains free of collisions at all future times. We introduce the concept of policy recoverability to characterize whether a vehicle can safely return to the original policy's feasible set in finite time. Our method identifies states that are unsafe in the long term under the original policy but recoverable, and selectively edits policy outputs within this region. The vehicle corrects its actions upon entering this region and resumes the original policy upon recovery. Closed-loop simulations on nuPlan urban driving scenarios show a 48% reduction in safety incidents under the original policy while largely preserving its driving performance.

papers.title: SPGSR: A Small Pixel-Space Generator for One-Step Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: In one-step super-resolution (SR), vision-only models extract semantic cues directly from the low-resolution (LR) image, keeping those cues spatially aligned with the structures they help restore. Recent models achieve high restoration quality with generators of up to 1.4 billion parameters. Given how much structure the LR image already provides, could a much smaller generator achieve comparable quality? We introduce SPGSR, a vision-only framework that adds a learned RGB correction to the LR image. A frozen DINOv2 guides prediction, and a lightweight block refines the correction locally. SPGSR achieves higher PSNR/SSIM and lower LPIPS/DISTS than VOSR, a leading vision-only SR method, across three benchmarks. Its $31.8\mathrm{M}$-parameter generator is just $6.5\%$ the size of VOSR-0.5B's. SPGSR also achieves competitive quality against T2I-based SR methods. SPGSR's generator uses only $0.60\%$ of the HR pixels used to train and distill VOSR's generator. For $512\times512$ outputs, SPGSR achieves $2.80\times$ and $3.35\times$ GPU-pipeline speedups over VOSR-0.5B and VOSR-1.4B, respectively.

papers.title: Prandtl Batchelor flow in a Periodic Channel with Counter Moving Walls
papers.abstract:
We study the vanishing viscosity limit of steady two dimensional incompressible Navier Stokes flows in a horizontally periodic channel with counter moving walls. The prescribed wall velocities are small periodic perturbations of constant velocities with opposite signs. The Batchelor Wood relations select an affine Euler shear with constant vorticity and a unique interior zero. We establish the existence of steady Navier Stokes solutions that are uniformly approximated by the selected Euler shear together with two Prandtl boundary layers. Moreover, the vorticity converges locally uniformly to the selected constant vorticity.
  The principal analytical difficulty is the loss of global coercivity caused by the interior zero of the Euler shear. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness rigidity argument that combines signed near wall positivity estimates, interior vorticity estimates, adjoint tests eliminating the affine limiting modes, and a streamline circulation equation ruling out concentration near the walls. These ingredients yield an estimate for the linearized inverse, which, together with a high order Euler Prandtl approximation, enables us to solve the nonlinear error equations. Our result provides a rigorous realization of the Prandtl Batchelor selection principle in a periodic channel with counter moving walls.

papers.title: Lone Wolves and Lattices in Bayesian Matching with Transfers
papers.abstract: I study the Lone Wolf and lattice properties of stable outcomes in one-to-one matching with transferable utility and one-sided incomplete information, using the Bayesian stable market states of Liu (2020) and Chen and Hu (2024). With transfers, the wage in a blocking offer screens the worker's types, so it determines both whom the firm attracts and what the firm learns. I show by example that the firm-side and matched-set versions of the Lone Wolf property, as well as the lattice property, can fail even when outcomes are compared under the same information structure. I then assume that each worker's matching value is additively separable in his type and the firm's identity. Under this condition, a firm that is unmatched in some stable outcome earns zero in every stable outcome with the same type profile and information structure. Workers can retain information rents, so the worker-side property can fail. Nevertheless, outside a finite union of affine hyperplanes in the space of firm values, all such stable outcomes leave the same agents unmatched. Whenever they do, the stable payoff vectors form a lattice, and worker-optimal and firm-optimal outcomes exist. The results extend to comonotonicity of relative preferences when posterior beliefs are independent across workers.

papers.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta-function: a local multiplicity test and long mixed moments
papers.abstract: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we show that at least 71.274066\% of the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$ are simple, and at least 85.368230% are distinct. The previous bounds were 19/27 $\approx$ 70.37%, due to Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek and to Bui and Heath-Brown (2013), and 84.77\%, due to Chirre, Gon\c{c}alves and de Laat (2020). The method combines the two classical approaches to simple zeros. Montgomery's pair correlation argument rests on a pointwise consequence of the explicit formula: at a zero of multiplicity $m\ge2$, a Dirichlet polynomial $J$ over prime powers of length $T^{\psi}$, $\psi<1$, is forced to have real part at most $-a<0$. The mollified derivative $\zeta'(\rho)M(\rho)$ of Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek vanishes there. Both facts are used at the same zero, in a single least-squares inequality. The new analytic input is the mixed moment $\sum_\rho\zeta'(\rho)M(\rho)J(1-\rho)$ with $J$ much longer than the mollifier. We evaluate it under the Riemann Hypothesis alone; the long prime sum stays in the numerator and the mollifier variable is the modulus, so the barrier at $T^{1/2}$ does not arise. A second-order version of the argument gives $0.70736$. We show that no second-order certificate of this type can exceed $0.7073646063$, and pass this ceiling with fourth moments of short Dirichlet polynomials and with mixed moments against products of a bounded number of primes. All constants are certified in exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: On the Gorenstein property of local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$
papers.abstract: Local models are used to model, \'etale-locally, the singularities of integral models of Shimura varieties. They are defined in terms of linear algebra and admit explicit descriptions by matrix equations. We determine exactly which local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ are Gorenstein. On one hand, this gives the analogous information for integral models of Shimura varieties for unramified unitary groups with parahoric level structure, and on the other hand also results in certain natural matrix equations defining non-Gorenstein singularities.

papers.title: Uniform Guarded Bootstrapping for Topology-Sensitive Directed Shortest Paths
papers.abstract:
On a source star, every leaf distance is an input weight. Thus computing labeled distances need not reveal their order. For a rooted directed topology, let $K$ be the least worst-case sum of comparisons and additions among finite deterministic programs specialized to that topology and correct for every nonnegative weighting.
  We give one deterministic program that takes the graph as input. This graph-input-uniform algorithm has total comparison-addition RAM time $O(m+n+K\Phi(K)\exp(O(\log_2^*(K+2))))$, where $n$ and $m$ count vertices and arcs, and $\Phi$ is a regularized product of successive logarithms. An active core is the small graph remaining after directly recoverable distances are separated. The algorithm chooses its parameters from the core size.
  Frozen entry ceilings let each interrupted local call be replayed on a small completion, whose complete-run bound controls the stopped work. The cost coefficient satisfies a linear one-step recurrence, yielding at most exponential growth in the number of generations. This permits a depth chosen from the measured core size.
  For $m=O(n)$, the solver gives $O(n\sqrt{\log n}(\log\log n)^{1/4+o(1)})$ time, improving the sparse directed bound of Duan, Mao, Shu, and Yin. A complementary result uses reusable dominator calibration for changing seed vectors on a fixed weighted graph.

papers.title: Induced Independence Levels and Signed Enumeration in Powers of Cycles
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ we study the distribution of the independence numbers $\alpha(G[S])$ over its vertex-induced subgraphs, together with signed Boolean-lattice sums over fixed independence-number levels. For the $r$th power $C_n^r$ of a cycle, we establish, in the range $n\ge 2rk+r+1$, a unique representation of each subset $S$ with $\alpha(C_n^r[S])=k$ by an independent $k$-set and its forward neighborhood. The resulting Boolean-interval partition gives exact enumeration by subset cardinality. We also prove reconstruction of partially deleted forward neighborhoods and determine the support, signs, and multiplicities of the corresponding upper M\"obius transform. For cycle squares we develop a complementary greedy-chain method for signed enumeration, with a five-transition classification and explicit staircase and two-gap cancellation identities.

papers.title: Analytical Wald Power for Lagged Coefficients in the Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
papers.abstract: In a longitudinal study, the number of participants and the number of waves both affect how much power the study has to detect a lagged effect. The random intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) is widely used to study within-person dynamics, but existing approaches to power analysis for this model typically rely on simulation or target likelihood-ratio tests. Starting from the likelihood score, we derive analytical Wald power for each lagged coefficient in the bivariate RI-CLPM. Across 30 designs, we compared our analytical results with power estimates from two R packages, powRICLPM for simulated Wald power and semPower for analytical likelihood-ratio power. The mean absolute difference was less than one percentage point in each comparison. By avoiding repeated simulation and model fitting, the analytical method saves time when evaluating power for a target path across many combinations of sample size (N) and number of waves (T).

papers.title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model as a Statistical Model: Identification, Estimation, and Model Comparison
papers.abstract: The random intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) distinguishes stable differences between people from lagged associations within individuals. We use a matrix representation to study its statistical properties for p variables measured across T waves. We derive a necessary and sufficient rank condition for global identification when transition matrices and innovation covariances vary by wave. Under time-invariant transitions, the condition specifies when three waves suffice. For complete Gaussian trajectories, matrix differentiation yields the profile likelihood score for each covariance and transition block. We also derive the population parameters of the conventional cross-lagged panel model (CLPM) when an RI-CLPM with fixed parameters generates the data. Our formulas quantify how CLPM slopes for observed variables differ from RI-CLPM slopes for within-person deviations at each transition. When the RI-CLPM transition matrix is time-invariant, the comparison also covers CLPM slopes pooled across waves. The formulas recover earlier bivariate results and show when cross-lagged slopes can appear, cancel, reverse sign, or change their ordering across models.

papers.title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
papers.abstract: Scaling robot learning requires demonstrations that combine realistic visual observations with reliable action supervision. Simulation-based synthesis faces a substantial visual gap relative to real environments, while video-only generation struggles to maintain physically consistent interactions and provide aligned action labels. We present DemoFoundry, an automated framework that couples coding agents with generative rendering to synthesize photorealistic and physically grounded robot demonstrations. Coding agents both construct aligned real--proxy video pairs from existing robot episodes to train a video renderer and write executable interaction programs to generate new demonstrations. Given a scene reference and task instruction, an agent reconstructs task-relevant geometry and writes a control program without requiring target-task human demonstrations. Program execution in a physics simulator produces proxy videos with aligned robot states and actions. The video renderer translates these proxy videos into scene-consistent, photorealistic observations, reducing the need for detailed appearance modeling in each scene. Automated task-execution checks select successful trajectories for rendering and policy learning. Experiments show improved visual quality and action--video consistency. Policies trained on the generated demonstrations outperform raw-simulation training and approach the performance of training on an equal number of real demonstrations.

papers.title: Boundary Observability for a Class of Degenerate Kolmogorov-Type Equations in a Cylindrical Domain
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the boundary observability for a class of multi-dimensional degenerate Kolmogorov-type kinetic equations in a cylindrical domain $\Omega = \mathbb{T}_{x_1} \times (0,1)_{x_2}$. The model features a horizontal drift term $x_2^\gamma \partial_{x_1} \varphi$ coupled with a boundary-degenerate diffusion operator $\partial_{x_2}(x_2^\alpha \partial_{x_2} \varphi)$ acting solely on the velocity variable, where $\gamma = 1$ and $\alpha \in (0,1)$. By leveraging the structural advantages of the cylindrical domain, we establish an analytical framework based on the method of separation of variables. Crucial Carleman estimates tailored to the degenerate dual operator are derived to capture the subtle dissipation effects under the influence of the transport term. Consequently, by virtue of a uniform a priori estimate, we establish the quantitative boundary observability inequality for the state function.

papers.title: InterConRank: Joint Node Centrality in Interconnected Heterogeneous Networks
papers.abstract: Two nodes with identical connections within their own layer can differ in importance if their neighbors in another layer occupy different positions in the network. We introduce InterConRank, a centrality algorithm that computes a separate node ranking for each layer of an interconnected network. Directed dependencies specify which layers supply scores to each receiving layer. InterConRank normalizes each type of link separately and updates all layers together, so a score can cross into a layer in one iteration and propagate along its internal links in the next. We prove convergence of this joint update and evaluate the resulting rankings on four scholarly networks. On all four networks, InterConRank gives the highest rank correlations with both h-index and total citations for nodes in the collaboration layer.

papers.title: $\mathsf{AC}^0 \not\subseteq \mathsf{BQAC}^0/\mathsf{qpoly}$ via Sublinear-Degree Pauli Approximation
papers.abstract:
We prove $\mathsf{AC}^0 \not\subseteq \mathsf{BQAC}^0/\mathsf{qpoly}$ in the single-copy, single-output model via an explicit $\mathsf{P}$-uniform family of linear-size monotone depth-2 CNFs. Every $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuit with arbitrary quantum advice achieves only an inverse-polynomial worst-case advantage over random guessing on this family. To prove this, we approximate the acceptance operator of any such circuit in operator norm by an advice-independent Hermitian operator of sublinear Pauli degree on a designated register alone, with degree exponent independent of width. Product-projection localization and Pauli twirling produce an auxiliary-register spectral cutoff that folds into contractions during backward peeling.
  The same approximation yields two stretched-exponential bounds against $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuits on $m$-qubit states. First, given polynomially many copies and input-independent quantum advice, single-output circuits distinguish exact or exponentially approximate state $2$-designs from Haar-random states with advantage at most $e^{-m^\alpha}$. Second, any state prepared from fewer than $k$ arbitrary input qubits and remaining $|0\rangle$ inputs has spectral weight at most $2e^{-m^\alpha}$ in a constant-energy-density band of an Anshu--Breuckmann--Nirkhe NLTS Hamiltonian encoding $k$ logical qubits. Both bounds hold for every fixed $\alpha\in(0,1)$.
