papers.title: LuxAvatar: Real-Time Relightable Head Avatars via Causal Neural Shading of 3D Intrinsic Proxies
papers.abstract: We present LuxAvatar, a feed-forward framework for real-time head avatar animation and relighting from a single portrait. To achieve both 3D controllability and complex facial light transport, we factorize avatar synthesis into an animatable 3D intrinsic Gaussian proxy and a causal autoregressive neural shader. This proxy disentangles canonical geometry and reflectance attributes, rapidly rasterizing deformed Gaussians into view- and motion-consistent PBR buffers. Conditioned on these buffers, our neural shader formulates forward rendering as a conditional video diffusion process, bypassing explicit PBR computation to synthesize realistic shading effects under target illumination. We achieve real-time streaming through heterogeneous distillation from a pretrained multi-step bidirectional relighting teacher to a two-step causal autoregressive neural shader, inheriting broad synthetic lighting priors while minimizing conditioning and decoding latency. To further specialize these priors to human heads, we construct a hybrid relighting dataset for domain-specific fine-tuning, capturing authentic facial dynamics and physically grounded light transport. Extensive experiments show that our framework enables 3D-controllable, real-time portrait animation and relighting, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in visual fidelity, motion control, and lighting accuracy.

authors.name: Jiapeng Zhu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: One Token, Many Lessons: Sliding-Window Attention within Gated Delta Networks
papers.abstract: Linear attention compresses historical context into a fixed-size recurrent state, reducing the computational and memory costs of long-sequence modeling. From the perspective of test-time regression (TTR), the state matrix can be viewed as an online-learned regression model, where keys and values serve as inputs and targets respectively, and queries are used to read from the model. From this perspective, the effectiveness of state learning depends not only on the update rule but also on how the key-value learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. While existing work has largely focused on how the state is updated and organized, we investigate how the learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. To this end, we propose Sliding-Window Gated DeltaNet (SWGDN), which replaces short convolutions in Delta-Rule linear attention with sliding-window attention to perform content-dependent local aggregation of projected queries, keys, and values. Our experiments show that SWGDN makes the key-value pairs used in consecutive updates more similar in both GDN2 and KDA. In SWGDN, carrying information from the same token across updates can help the recurrent state reinforce a previously learned association. The local mixing strategy can be incorporated into any Delta-Rule-based linear attention architecture without changing its state update equations or chunkwise parallel algorithms. We apply this strategy to two Delta-Rule variants, GDN2 and KDA, and experimental results demonstrate that SWGDN outperforms the original Delta-Rule baseline across multiple benchmarks.

papers.title: Anderson-Accelerated Landweber Iteration with Regularization Guarantees for Nonlinear Ill-Posed Problems
papers.abstract: Anderson acceleration (AA) can markedly reduce iteration counts for fixed-point solvers, but its unrestricted signed history extrapolation need not preserve the stability required for iterative regularization of ill-posed problems. We introduce a regularization-guaranteed Anderson-accelerated Landweber method (\RG) in which finite-memory AA generates a proposal while the committed iterate is a controlled perturbation of a certified Landweber anchor. Under a local tangential cone condition and a scale-normalized localization condition, we prove strong convergence of the exact-data trajectory to a solution, stability at every fixed iteration, finite discrepancy stopping, and strong convergence of the discrepancy-stopped noisy reconstructions to the same exact-data limit; local uniqueness is needed only if that selected limit is to be identified with a prescribed solution $x^\dagger$. Under the additional benchmark source condition $x^\dagger-x_0=F'(x^\dagger)^*\lambda^\dagger$ and a standard range-invariance condition, we obtain the discrepancy-principle rate $\norm{x_{k_\delta}^\delta-x^\dagger}=O(\delta^{1/2})$. The rate proof controls data-dependent Anderson coefficients through fixed memory, a fixed-reference ridge in the small AA least-squares problem, and an outer correction budget with an $O(k^{-1})$ tail. The numerical examples verify the efficiency of the proposed method.

papers.abstract:
We study the following fully nonlinear $k$-Hessian equation on a spherical cap $\mathcal{C}_{	heta}$ for $1\leq k\leq n$ and $0<	heta<\pi/2$: $$ \left\{  egin{aligned} \sigma_k(

In the critical case $p=q>1$, scaling invariance prevents uniform $C^0$ estimates without normalization. papers.title: Min-Plus Products and Dynamic Programming with Few Violations of the Adjacent Monge Inequalities
papers.abstract:
Local rewards can introduce negative adjacent mixed differences into a convex transition cost. If a cost array $B$ has $s(B)$ such differences, we express it as a Monge array minus $s(B)$ weighted rectangles and sweep its columns, maintaining the lower envelope of the active rows. For explicit finite $n\times n$ matrices $A,B$ and $L=\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil$, we compute $A\otimes B$ and the smallest minimizing index for every entry in $\mathcal{O}(n^2L+ns(B)L^3)$ time and $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ space, giving near-quadratic time for arbitrary $A$ when $s(B)=\mathcal{O}(n)$, including right factors with $\Theta(n^2)$ positive differences.
  For block costs given by a constant-time Monge oracle and $r$ signed rectangle corrections, the sweep activates each row when its prefix optimum becomes available and computes an optimal contiguous partition in $\mathcal{O}((n+r)L^3)$ time and $\mathcal{O}(n+r)$ working space. The sweep handles convex transitions with interval rules and assigns one rectangle to each internal edge or hyperedge reward in a convex block cost, giving near-linear exact algorithms on sparse inputs for ordered graph modularity, weighted contiguous cluster editing, all-or-nothing HyperLam, and bounded-rank strict hypergraph modularity.
  Let $c_{\mathrm{APSP}}$ denote the deterministic exponent of all-pairs shortest paths with polynomially bounded integer weights. For fixed $3-c_{\mathrm{APSP}}<\alpha\le1$, any deterministic $\mathcal{O}(n^\beta)$-time min-plus product algorithm for polynomially bounded integer matrices with $s(B)\le n^{1+\alpha}$ satisfies $\beta\ge c_{\mathrm{APSP}}-1+\alpha$. The reduction from general integer min-plus multiplication uses right factors obtained from $(j-k)^2$ by at most $n^{1+\alpha}$ interval discounts, with $\Theta(n^2)$ positive differences and all remaining differences negative.

papers.title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on external memory, yet they still hallucinate about what they remember. Often the correct memory is retrieved and placed in the prompt, but the answer contradicts it or the memory is applied to the wrong question. We call these use-time memory hallucinations. Across five open models, we find that they arise from the conflict between parametric knowledge and external memory and take three forms: memory-ignoring, where the model returns to a stale fact in its weights (up to 46% of queries); memory-misapplying, where it attributes the memory to unrelated entities (up to 24%, and 49% when retrieval is combined with weight editing); and version confusion, where 53% of answers about revised facts assert the superseded value when both versions remain stored. We propose TASK memory, which goes beyond text-only memory by combining a Text note with Activation Steering and Knowledge editing that share one in-model address. The text holds the content. A removable knowledge edit supplies the address through its subject key and supports multi-hop composition. A pair of steering vectors decides, query by query, whether the model adopts the memory or keeps its own answer; the vectors store no content and control how the text memory is used. On frozen models under a pre-registered, test-once protocol, TASK reduces memory-ignoring hallucinations to at most 1.5% in all ten model-dataset cells and cuts neighbour misuse from 39.2% to 7.5% (+10.8 pp composite on CounterFact). It improves a 300-memory library over BM25 RAG by 16.4 pp, an advantage that holds at 3,000 memories, resolves fact revisions without fact IDs, and adds 7.5 pp of multi-hop accuracy on MQuAKE. 21 of 23 cross-model comparisons (8B-27B, four families) are significant, and TASK beats three recent context-steering methods in 9 of 10 model-dataset cells.

authors.name: Jinkun Zhao
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology - Beijing

papers.title: MulCLIP: A Multi-level Alignment Framework for Enhancing Fine-grained Long-context CLIP
papers.abstract: Vision-language models such as CLIP excel at image-text alignment but struggle with long, detailed descriptions due to training on short captions. Recent methods address this limitation using region proposals to align visual regions with sentences, but at substantial deployment cost. We present MulCLIP, an end-to-end multi-level alignment framework that directly exploits natural long-text structure without region proposals. Instead of simply stacking objectives, MulCLIP aligns different textual granularities through compatible training signals: global contrastive alignment for long captions and short summaries, Word-Patch Reconstruction over locally calibrated features for within-sample word-patch semantics, and Subcaption-Aggregated Patch alignment for context-rich subcaption grounding. Experiments on benchmarks spanning varying caption lengths show consistent gains, and ablations confirm that the proposed objectives are complementary and jointly improve the overall framework. Code will be released at https://github.com/truongchau2602/MulCLIP.

authors.name: Chau Truong
authors.institution: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

papers.title: $E_d$-Enhancements of $L_\infty$-Algebras Associated to Secondary Polytopes
papers.abstract: We study $E_d$-enhancements of the geometric $L_\infty$-algebras associated to secondary polytopes of finite configurations in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$. We construct an action of the semialgebraic chains of the Fulton--MacPherson operad on the shifted algebra $B_A=\mathfrak g_A[1-d]$ when $|A|\leq3d$. The action recovers the prescribed higher Lie operations on fundamental chains. The construction is obtained from a general extension theorem for weighted shifted $L_\infty$-algebras, using reflection to control relative cohomology obstructions. For $|A|\leq3d-1$, the resulting reflection-compatible integration actions are homotopic relative to their shifted Lie structure. We also give an abstract enhancement without a cardinality bound, direct formulas for circuits, and explicit operations for convex pentagons and hexagons.

papers.title: Connecting AI Agents to Live Discrete Element Simulations via the Model Context Protocol
papers.abstract: This paper describes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server through which a general-purpose AI agent operates a discrete element engine, commercial or open-source, while the simulation runs. The agent submits a long simulation to the engine and, while it computes, reads the running model, changes it, or stops it. The human modeler stays at the engine's console and graphical interface throughout, and the agent sees what the modeler does there. The tools are derived from what the agent needs to do at the engine and are held to four principles: correctness, coverage, orthogonality and simplicity. Two documentation tools let the agent search the engine's manual and browse it level by level. Five execution tools let the agent run code in the engine, submit long simulations in the background, check on them, read the running model, and stop them. A bridge inside the engine serves these tools in a commercial DEM engine, PFC, and an open-source one, YADE. In a case study, a general-purpose agent calibrated a drained triaxial model of dense Toyoura sand against laboratory data in both engines, while the modeler worked at the same engine; the agent noticed the modeler's actions at the console and acted on them. The same calibration on YADE was then given to seven language models, three sessions each and without human intervention. Twenty of the twenty-one sessions reached the targets, and nineteen of the parameter sets lie in one small region of the admissible ranges. The server and the bridge are released as two open-source packages, itasca-mcp, which also serves FLAC, 3DEC, MPoint and MassFlow, and yade-mcp.

papers.title: Exclusion and internal structure in the association/dissociation kinetics of DNA-binding proteins in the fast diffusion limit
papers.abstract: In many canonical biophysical and biochemical contexts, complex diffusing DNA-binding proteins undergoing nonspecific adsorption and desorption can exist in different conformational states. Equilibrium binding theories and kinetic models of competing ligands provide a basis for describing these systems. Coupling the internal conformational kinetics of bound proteins to exclusion and diffusion requires tracking both protein positions and binding states. Closed-form, tractable mathematical models that accurately describe the stochastic dynamics of structured proteins that bind to and diffuse along DNA are lacking. Here, we develop a new coarse-grained stochastic model of nonspecific DNA-protein binding in the fast diffusion regime, from which we derive an effective Markov model and its corresponding mean-field approximation that incorporates protein footprint size and conformational switching. We fit our new model quantitatively to previously measured dynamics of Replication Protein A (RPA) binding to ssDNA. Finally, by including multisegment binding states, our analysis captures facilitated exchange, revealing how multisegment architecture balances high affinity with rapid remodeling. Our theoretical model applies broadly to many other DNA-binding protein systems, including nucleosomes, ssDNA-binding proteins, and other multisegment complexes, providing accurate predictions and new strategies for evaluating experimental data.

papers.title: From Diagnosing Alignment to Joint Supervision in Multimodal Draft Training
papers.abstract: Multimodal drafts learn from multimodal (MM) and text-only (TXT) supervision, yet their effects on alignment and how to combine them remain unclear. We diagnose draft-target alignment through paired predictions with and without visual input, decomposing distributional error into text-conditioned and visual-response components. Drafts with similar text-conditioned alignment can still differ markedly in visual-response risk and acceptance. Controlled continuation training shows that high-risk groups outperform random and low-risk groups, and visual-response risk guides MM training more effectively than aggregate risk. Building on these diagnostics, we propose MNRS-Joint, which configures joint supervision from a given draft's component-risk distributions, using modality-specific mean risks to determine the MM:TXT mixture. Across three warm-ups, its distinct mixtures fall in high-performing regions of the ratio sweeps. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, MNRS-Joint improves mean accepted length from 3.35 to 3.53 and mean speedup from $2.04\times$ to $2.16\times$ over composition-matched random training under greedy tree decoding. The gains also hold under stochastic chain decoding.

authors.name: Daming Cao
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Extremals and Normalized Solutions for a Critical Weighted Choquard Equation
papers.abstract: We study normalized solutions to the weighted Choquard equation \[ \left\{ \begin{aligned} -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u) &=\lambda |x|^{-2a}u+\beta |x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u\\ &\quad+|x|^{-bp} \left( \int_{\mathbb R^N} \frac{|u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{\mu}|y|^{bp}}\,dy \right) |u|^{p-2}u &&\text{in }\mathbb R^N,\\ \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx&=\rho^2, \end{aligned} \right. \] where $N\ge3$, $a<(N-2)/2$, $a<b<a+1$, $2<q<2^\sharp$, $0<\mu<N$, $p=(2N-\mu)/(N-2d)$ is the upper Stein--Weiss critical exponent, $d=1-b+a$, $2^\sharp=2N/(N-2-2a+2b)$, $\rho>0$ is prescribed, $\beta>0$, and $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplier. Assuming $p>2$, we establish existence and multiplicity of normalized solutions in different mass regimes, including negative-energy ground states for small $\beta$ and positive-energy second solutions under suitable assumptions, as well as ground states in the mass-critical and mass-supercritical cases under explicit conditions

papers.title: Technical Report MEG2text: Beyond Alignment in Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text
papers.abstract: Non-invasive brain-to-text seeks to recover language from brain activity without surgery. A central challenge is turning learned brain-language representations into accurate word predictions. We present MEG2text, a decoding system that combines corrected training and evaluation, brain-text alignment, a class-balanced word readout, and target-word language-model fusion. On LibriBrain100's word-ranking task, MEG2text reaches 64.12% mean Top-10 balanced accuracy, improving on published MEG-XL by 16.92 percentage points across four corpora, with gains on each corpus. Controlled comparisons show that both implementation corrections and a learned readout contribute to this improvement. Candidate-level analysis reveals that some words receive informative scores yet consistently lose to competing candidates, while an identical-feature comparison shows that learning the classification rule improves decoding without changing the representation. These findings identify the decoding rule as a consequential part of non-invasive brain-to-text and show how system improvements can make better use of aligned neural features.

papers.title: Enhanced Helgason-Johnson bounds for classical groups of type $B$
papers.abstract: This paper improves the Helgason-Johnson bound in 1969 for non-Hermitian real classical groups of type $B$.

papers.title: AlignPre: Skill-Aligned Post-Training for Latent-Free Generative Precipitation Nowcasting
papers.abstract: Precipitation nowcasting requires accurate short-term predictions under rapidly evolving spatiotemporal dynamics. Generative diffusion models can produce detailed and competitive radar forecasts by modeling conditional distributions. However, most existing approaches rely on separately trained components, such as deterministic branches or latent compression modules. More fundamentally, distribution matching alone fails to explicitly optimize operational forecast skill. We propose AlignPre, a streamlined pixel-space nowcasting framework that bridges this gap via skill-aligned post-training (SAPT). AlignPre employs an end-to-end flow-matching forecaster with a hierarchical spatiotemporal architecture for distribution matching and direct radar-field synthesis, without latent compression. During post-training, SAPT exploits the analytic structure of forecast verification scores to construct a differentiable objective. By backpropagating gradients of this objective from radar fields to the generator, SAPT turns forecast verification into direct training feedback. Across three real-world benchmarks spanning different forecast horizons, AlignPre consistently surpasses state-of-the-art deterministic and generative baselines in forecast skill, demonstrating that aligning generative modeling with domain-specific verification provides an effective paradigm for meteorological forecasting.

papers.title: Conformal Risk Control for Sentinel-1 Flood Maps under Event Shift and Local Recalibration
papers.abstract: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) selects a threshold to limit missed labeled positives under exchangeability, but low omission risk can come at the cost of an excessively large flood map. We examine this trade-off with a frozen bi-temporal Sentinel-1 predictor, 403 expert-labeled source groups, and ten evaluable leave-one-event-out folds. At a target risk of 0.10, source-calibrated thresholds produce mean group losses of 0.1726 in Somalia and 0.1985 in Nigeria (four groups). The other eight folds select zero thresholds, labeling every valid pixel as flooded; their excess predicted area is 3.15-20.55 times the labeled positive area. Local threshold recalibration is feasible in 559 of 570 scheduled splits. The equal-event frequency of meeting the observed risk target with a positive threshold is 0.95% at ten labeled groups and 8.00% at twenty, using different predefined event pools. At fifty groups, exploratory recalibration meets both conditions in 24/30 Paraguay splits and none in India or the United States. Labels include permanent water, so the loss does not isolate newly flooded land. The results show why omission risk should be reported alongside mapped area, calibration feasibility, and event-specific outcomes.

papers.title: Conditional Independence Graph Learning from Dependent Data Via Time-Delay Embedding
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of inferring the conditional independence graph (CIG) of a high-dimensional stationary multivariate Gaussian time series which could be short-range dependent (SRD) or long-range dependent (LRD). In a time series graph, each component of the vector series is represented by a distinct node, and associations between components are represented by edges between the corresponding nodes. We consider a time-domain approach based on time-delay embedding, casting the problem as one of multi-attribute graph estimation for random vectors where a vector is associated with each node of the graph. For an embedding dimension $d$, at each node the associated $(d+1)$-dimensional random vector consists of a time series component and its $d$ delayed copies, with integer delays up to $d \ge 1$. Graph estimation from dependent data has been investigated in the past using frequency-domain methods whose analysis is restricted to SRD data. We consider a penalized negative pseudo log-likelihood function with convex lasso or non-convex regularizations to estimate the CIG. Non-convex regularization functions are log-sum, smoothly clipped absolute deviation (SCAD) and minimax concave penalty (MCP). We exploit an existing alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) approach to optimize the objective function. We establish sufficient conditions in a high-dimensional setting for consistency, local convexity when using non-convex penalties, and graph recovery, for both SRD and LRD series. We illustrate our approach with both synthetic and real-data examples. For a $p$-dimensional time series, the computational complexity of the ADMM algorithm is ${\cal O}((d+1)^3 p^3)$. Based on the numerical examples, a heuristic is suggested and illustrated for selection of $d$ which, in theory, should tend to infinity to infer the time series graph.

papers.title: The regular polygon maximizes the first positive Steklov eigenvalue among simple polygons at fixed area
papers.abstract: For $N\ge5$ and every simple planar polygon $P$ with at most $N$ sides, $\sqrt{|P|}\,\sigma_1(P)\le\sqrt{|R_N|}\,\sigma_1(R_N)$, where $\sigma_1$ is the first positive Steklov eigenvalue and $R_N$ is a regular $N$-gon. Equality holds precisely for polygons similar to $R_N$. This answers Oudet's fixed-area open problem \cite{AIM} for all $N\ge5$.

papers.title: Simultaneous coordinate-wise Wasserstein central limit theorem in high dimensions
papers.abstract:
For independent centered random vectors $(X_i)_{i=1}^n$ of finite fourth moments, we obtain dimension free Wasserstein bound between its normalized sum $W_n = n^{-1/2}\sum X_i$ and a Gaussian whose covariance equals that of $W_n$. The coupling between $W_n$ and the Gaussian is strong in the sense that a single coupling controls controls every projection onto a subset of those eigen coordinates. The proof combines stochastic localization, Hermite expansion on a Gaussian prior with exchangeable pairing. This proves the Conjecture surmised in \cite{fang2026sharp} and improves the coefficient on the fourth-moment term from $2$ to $197/108$.
  The same Wasserstein error bound extends to real separable Hilbert space. For Hilbert-valued i.i.d. observations, the $L^2$ prediction error bound has an order of $O(n^{-1/2})$, with no dimension factor or restriction on covariance eigenvalue decay, and the same coupling retains bounds for every spectral projection. In an $\ell^2$ example, we demonstrate that the coordinate-wise error gives sharp error order of $n^{-1/2}$.

authors.name: Yuanlong Ruan
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The pentagonal tensor and the fourth obstruction to formality
papers.abstract: Let \(A\) be a connected graded commutative differential graded algebra over \(\mathbb Q\) whose cohomology is a finite-dimensional Poincar\'e duality algebra of formal dimension \(N\ge2\). Assuming that its Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes, we prove that the normalized pentagonal tensor of Nagy and Nordstr\"om, in [preprint (2021), arXiv:2105.13660], vanishes if and only if the fourth Harrison obstruction vanishes after eliminating the third operation. This gives a fourth-order counterpart to the third-order comparison of Fiorenza and L\^e, in [Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5), published online 7 March 2025], and answers the vanishing question in L\^e's proposed comparison, in [preprint (2026), arXiv:2603.01219], under the hypothesis that the Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes. The result applies to closed, connected, oriented manifolds with no upper dimension bound. We also extend Zhou's sphere-bundle formality criterion in [Algebr. Geom. Topol. 25 (2025), pp. 2297--2315] to two-stage oriented sphere bundles with positive odd fibre dimensions over a closed, connected, oriented, rationally formal base, provided that the second Euler class is pulled back from the original base. Their total spaces are rationally formal precisely when the Bianchi-Massey and normalized pentagonal tensors vanish. Our method develops the model-based strategy in Zhou's proof within a commutative bar-cobar framework, providing a starting point for constructing higher tensors and comparing them with higher-order formality obstructions.

papers.title: Tian-Yau-type metrics from K3 divisors with ADE contractions
papers.abstract: We construct complete Ricci-flat K\"ahler metrics on the complement of a smooth anti-canonical K3 divisor in a compact K\"ahler threefold, assuming that the normal bundle of the divisor is nef and big. Such a metric exists in every K\"ahler class whose exceptional periods are positive. We use a generalized Gibbons-Hawking ansatz to construct an approximate model on the normal bundle. When the normal bundle contracts an ADE configuration, this model combines an expanding Ricci-flat orbifold K3 metric with ALE metrics whose exceptional periods remain fixed. After improving the model by a finite iteration and transferring it to the divisor complement, we apply the Tian-Yau-Hein existence theorem.

papers.title: Atunda: Building an Afrogenic Dance Movement Dataset for AI-Driven Classification
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Atunda, the first systematically collected video dataset of Afrogenic dance moves, designed for training and evaluating deep learning models for movement classification. The first phase of the dataset includes nearly 400 videos covering 13 distinct dance moves from African and African Diaspora performative culture, making it the first AI-ready resource of its kind. Using this dataset, we train and evaluate various configurations of temporal convolutional neural networks, achieving a classification accuracy exceeding 95%. The baseline results provide a benchmark for future studies in movement classification, especially in the understudied area of Afrogenic performative culture and tradition. This work lays the foundation for developing in the future digital metrics of similarity, automated attribution systems, and tools that preserve and promote the cultural heritage of Afrogenic dances.

papers.title: Symplectic bumpless pipe dreams
papers.abstract: Bumpless pipe dreams are combinatorial objects in bijection with alternating sign matrices. Double Grothendieck polynomials can be expressed as weighted sums over bumpless pipe dreams, a perspective that has led to many advances in the combinatorics of Schubert calculus and connections with integrable systems. We introduce symplectic bumpless pipe dreams and present an analogous formula for symplectic Grothendieck polynomials, which represent the equivariant K-theoretic classes of Sp(2n)-orbit closures in the flag variety. To prove this result, we construct an analogue of Lascoux's inflation on these objects, providing a combinatorial realization of the symplectic transition equations that appear in work of the first author, Marberg, and Pawlowski. We also show that certain marked symplectic bumpless pipe dreams correspond to set-valued reverse plane partitions. This allows us to give a tableau formula for a class of symplectic Grothendieck polynomials and to compute principal specializations of the corresponding symplectic Schubert polynomials, answering a question of Hamaker-Marberg-Pawlowski in the fixed-point-free case.

papers.title: Evacuation Traffic Prediction for Dynamic Transportation Networks over Multiple Hurricanes: A Generalized Graph Learning Approach
papers.abstract: High traffic demand during hurricane evacuations causes severe congestion on major highways, leading to delays and safety risks for evacuees. Predicting evacuation traffic in real-time can significantly enhance evacuation management efforts. However, evacuation traffic is highly dynamic and uncertain due to evolving hurricane characteristics and diverse population response. Each hurricane has unique characteristics and evacuation contexts, resulting in different spatial-temporal traffic patterns. Moreover, the structure of detector-based transportation networks varies across multiple hurricanes. Hence, a model trained on the data from one hurricane may not generalize well for others. This study proposes a generalized dynamic graph learning framework using traffic detectors and evacuation data from 12 historical hurricanes. Leveraging the dynamic nature of transportation network, we develop a Graph Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (GCN-LSTM) model that predicts evacuation traffic up to 6 hours in advance. For an unseen hurricane (Milton, 2024), the model shows strong generalizability, achieving an RMSE of 280.6 and R2 of 0.96 for 1-hour prediction, and an RMSE of 459.8 and R2 of 0.89 for overall 6-hours prediction. We also introduce a modular training approach, where we evaluate performance improvements by sequentially incorporating data from multiple hurricanes. The proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models for overall 6-hour prediction horizons. Ablation experiments show an 8.4% improvement in RMSE for the proposed dynamic GCN-LSTM model compared to its static counterpart. Traffic management officials can use the developed model to understand future traffic conditions during hurricane evacuation in advance and take proactive measures to reduce delays during evacuation.

papers.title: Barron Smoothness for Layers in Deep Neural Networks
papers.abstract: In order to bound approximation errors for deep neural networks, we split the problem into two steps: First the selection of optimal infinite width limits for each layer and second an optimal discretization of all layers to obtain finite sized networks. We show that in expectation, the latter problem is equivalently characterized by a layer wise generalization of Barron norms. Moreover, we provide an analysis of the optimization landscape and show that local minima are characterized by an equidistribution principle akin to similar ideas in adaptive spline and finite element approximation.

papers.title: Norm of the Generalized Hilbert Matrix Operator Between Some Spaces of Analytic Functions
papers.abstract: We study the generalized Hilbert operator \[ \mathcal H_bf(z)=\int_0^1\frac{(1-t)^b}{(1-tz)^{b+1}}f(t)\,dt, \qquad b>0, \] on several spaces of analytic functions in the unit disk. For logarithmically weighted Korenblum spaces, we obtain an exact supremum representation and a lower estimate for the norm of the mapping from $H_{\alpha,\log}^{\infty}$ to $H_\alpha^\infty$. We then establish two-sided estimates and characterize the boundedness range of $\mathcal H_b$ on the $\alpha$-Bloch spaces $\mathcal B^\alpha$. We also derive norm bounds for the mapping from $H^\infty$ into the endpoint Zygmund-type space $\Lambda_1^{1,*}$. Furthermore, we give a norm representation for $\mathcal H_b:H_\alpha^\infty\to\mathcal B^{\alpha+1}$ and identify a norm-attaining function. In particular, for $0<\alpha\leq2/3$, the norm is expressed explicitly in terms of a Beta function. Finally, we obtain an exact supremum representation of the norm of $\mathcal H_b$ on $H_{\alpha,\log}^{\infty}$, together with explicit norm estimates. Our results extend those of Hao et al. [J. Geom. Anal. 35 (2025), Paper No. 184] for the classical Hilbert matrix operator ($b=0$) to the generalized case $b>0$.

papers.title: Interactive Proofs as a Unified Framework for Evaluating and Leveraging Verifiable Proof Generation by LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Recent advances in LLM-assisted theorem proving and program verification have attracted widespread attention. Beyond determining whether a proposition is true, LLM agents must produce evidence that can be independently checked by humans or formal verification tools. To evaluate the underlying, protocol-agnostic ability of LLM agents to construct verifiable proofs-rather than their proficiency with any particular proof language or verification tool, we introduce Merlin-Bench. Drawing on interactive proof systems from computational complexity theory, we cast an LLM agent as the prover: under a designated protocol, the agent interacts with a formal verifier to substantiate its claimed answer to a problem instance. We develop an automated framework for constructing test cases and use it to create 100 cases across 15 problem families, each formulated within this prover-verifier framework. Experiments with 10 frontier LLMs across multiple agent harnesses show that reliably producing verifiable proofs in accordance with specified protocols remains a substantial challenge. Our case studies further provide actionable insights into improving agents' ability to generate verifier-accepted proofs: tool use is essential for completing practical proof tasks; different forms of guidance, ranging from engineering instructions to problem-specific knowledge, substantially affect success rates on interactive-proof tasks; and proof-solving experience distilled from abstract tasks can transfer to concrete, real-world verification tasks.

authors.name: Yankai Shu
authors.institution: Hunan University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xingyu Zhao
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Chuan Mao
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Congchi Yin
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

papers.title: Manga Page Parser: Comprehensive Visual Parsing through Local Story Understanding
papers.abstract: Understanding manga requires connecting who appears and who speaks with the events, character states, and relationships that unfold across panels. We study manga visual parsing through local story understanding: analyzing each double-page spread independently to capture and organize its story information in a reusable structured representation. We propose MangaParser, an agentic reading framework that jointly performs character clustering, speaker diarization, and speaker-to-character binding within a shared multimodal conversation, without additional training or fine-tuning. The agent uses structured story memory to guide character and speaker identification, inspecting relevant image regions when uncertain and refining its predictions and story records together as evidence accumulates. Quantitative evaluations show that our parser substantially outperforms manga-specific models across multiple backbones. Parsing examples illustrate how a unified representation links the character and speaker predictions with narrative content and supporting evidence. We further test reusability through story question answering using outputs generated before the questions are provided. The results confirm output reusability, offering a foundation for manga translation, content retrieval, and question answering.

authors.name: Yingxuan Li
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A block coordinate descent method for nonconvex multiobjective optimization under H\"older continuity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a block coordinate descent method for unconstrained multiobjective optimization problems with possibly nonconvex objectives and H\"older continuous gradients, intended for large-scale instances, in which updating all the variables simultaneously is expensive. In each iteration, only one block is updated along a descent direction common to all objectives, obtained by minimizing the maximum of their regularized quadratic models. We show that, unlike the single-objective case, stationarity on each block does not imply Pareto stationarity, and that no method that updates only the blocks of a partition of the variables and is monotone in all the objectives reaches, in general, an $\epsilon$-Pareto stationary point. Therefore, when none of the blockwise stationarity measures exceeds the tolerance, the algorithm performs a joint step across all coordinates and terminates only at $\epsilon$-Pareto stationary points. We establish a complexity bound of $O(\epsilon^{-(\beta+1)/\beta})$ iterations, where $\beta$ is the smallest H\"older exponent, the same order as that of methods that update all the variables, as well as bounds on the numbers of function and gradient evaluations, which also hold with one regularization parameter per block.

authors.name: John Frank Matos Ascona
authors.institution: Universidade do Estado de Mato Grosso

authors.name: Danilo Rodrigues de Souza
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Oeste da Bahia

papers.title: Why $2$, $3$, and $5$? Lambert Series, Prime Logarithms, and a $48$-Step Octave for Musical Tuning
papers.abstract:
The primes $2$, $3$, and $5$ generate many familiar frequency ratios in musical tuning. We identify three mathematical properties that distinguish these primes in a construction based on modular transformations of Lambert series. We derive an exact identity for $\log p$ for every odd prime $p$, together with a separate identity for $\log2$. Within this construction, all transformed Lambert-series arguments can be chosen real precisely for $p=2,3,5$. In the identities obtained for these three primes, every series argument has magnitude at most $e^{-2\pi}$, whereas the identity for $\log7$ requires complex arguments and contains a more slowly converging series.
  The leading $\pi$-terms for $\log2$, $\log3$, and $\log5$ generate a $48$-step octave grid and recover its conventional prime mapping $(48,76,111)$ exactly, without rounding, while including the leading $\pi$-term for $\log7$ enlarges the grid to $1680$ steps. The identity for $\log7$ introduces no auxiliary logarithms of larger primes, whereas for every prime $11\le p<20000$, an exact computation identifies such logarithms in the construction.
  The Lambert-series remainders provide exact corrections for just intervals and musical commas. For a published theoretical model of $22$ Hindustani shrutis, the additive $48$-step mapping assigns all $22$ ratios to distinct positions, with corrections no greater than $15.3$ cents in magnitude. These results establish precise arithmetic distinctions that parallel the prominence of $5$-limit tuning, without implying that number theory determines musical practice.

papers.title: What Does RL Post-Training Teach Text-to-Image Models? A Skill-Wise Analysis of Flow-GRPO
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has become a standard way to improve text-to-image flow models: Flow-GRPO lifts the GenEval score of SD3.5-M from 0.63 to 0.95, a gain read as the model having learned compositional generation. We ask how much of that gain the base model's own samples already contained, by measuring pass@k over shared noise seeds, one skill at a time, before and after RL, on prompts never used in training. The answer differs by skill. On four of GenEval's six skills, where 32 base samples already solve almost every prompt, the gain is sharpening: one post-trained sample is worth 4 to 10 base samples, and pass@32 barely moves. On spatial relations it is unlocking: pass@32 rises from 0.69 to 1.00, 128 base samples do not match one post-trained sample, and prompts the base model never solved in 32 samples are solved 93% of the time, as often as those it solved. The benchmark average, 31 base samples per post-trained sample, describes no skill. Relations carry 35% of the gain; of the other 65%, selecting among 8 base samples with the judge behind the reward recovers nine tenths. We propose an account of when each occurs: within a prompt, a group-relative update re-weights only the outcomes its samples contain, and a flow policy cannot widen the noise that produces them; across prompts, shared parameters let successes on some prompts repair a deficit common to many. The same anatomy applies to a text-rendering checkpoint. The account's predictions are tested with a checkpoint trained without KL, within-prompt diversity, and controlled training that holds object classes out, where sharpening comes first and transfers, and unlocking follows, on practised objects before unseen ones.

papers.title: Ergodicity of the mapping class group action on components with small nonzero Euler number
papers.abstract: We study the action of the mapping class group on the $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ character variety of a closed oriented surface of genus $g$. On the components considered here, the infimum of the translation lengths of essential simple closed curves is zero almost everywhere for every invariant positive Radon measure. For Goldman measure we show that almost every character sends some such curve to a non-hyperbolic element. By the criterion of Marche and Wolff, this proves Goldman's ergodicity conjecture for $g\ge 3$ and Euler numbers $e$ with $0<|e|\leq g-1$.

papers.title: Deterministic Verification and Computation of Real Matrix Products Have the Same Arithmetic Exponent
papers.abstract: Given three $n\times n$ real matrices $A,B,C$, we ask whether $AB=C$. In an exact real arithmetic model that charges one step for each addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, comparison, or sign test, we prove that deterministic exact verification requires $\Omega(n^{\omega_{\mathbb{C}}})$ steps and has the same optimal arithmetic exponent $\omega_{\mathbb{C}}$ as matrix multiplication. Assuming the value $\omega_{\mathbb{C}}=9/4$ and the fixed-size border-rank lower bound stated in the OpenAI preprint of November 24, 2026, deterministic verification requires $\Omega(n^{9/4})$ steps, whereas Freivalds' randomized test uses $O(n^2)$ steps with one-sided error. More generally, if a tree of cost $s$ correctly decides $y=T(u,v)$ on all real inputs, the bilinear map $T$ is a coefficientwise limit of tensors of real rank $O(s)$.

papers.title: Invariance of log plurigenera in families of compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $(X_t,B_t)$ be a smooth proper family of pairs with K\"ahler fibres, where the boundary has relative simple normal crossings and real coefficients in $[0,1)$. We show that for every $m\ge1$, every section of $mK_{X_t}+\lfloor mB_t\rfloor$ extends locally over the base. In particular, the log plurigenera are locally constant, and for $B_t=0$ we obtain the deformation invariance of the plurigenera $P_m(X_t)$. Since the total space need not be K\"ahler, we run the minimal model program on the central fibre, using the work of Hacon-Wang and Hacon-Xie, and extend its steps over a disc. The obstruction to lifting a jet vanishes along the fixed part determined by the final model, and so it is square-integrable for the weight in the extension theorem of Cao-P\u{a}un. As an application, if the adjoint is pseudoeffective on one fibre, then the pair has a relative good minimal model near each point of the base and a relative canonical model over the whole base.

papers.title: Self-supervised Clipped-objective Reinforcement Leaning Framework for Risk-aware Portfolio Management
papers.abstract: Portfolio management involves balancing diverse financial assets, a critical yet challenging task in quantitative trading. Although deep reinforcement learning has emerged as an active research domain for solving complex sequential decision-making problems over the past decade, deploying reinforcement learning frameworks in non-stationary financial markets raises formidable difficulties. Most existing reinforcement learning-based portfolio management models fail to account for tick-level intraday market dynamics (e.g., order flow imbalances and liquidity fluctuations), which reflect rapid capital movements. Simultaneously, these models suffer from unstable learning processes due to reinforcement learning's inherent high variance. This paper presents a Self-supervised Clipped-objective Portfolio management framework (SCP), which addresses these limitations through a two-phase architecture. Market feature integration phase (application contribution) integrates micro-level market microstructure patterns with macro-level financial indicators to enhance sensitivity to intraday asset trend dynamics. Policy optimization Phase (AI contribution) employs intermediate asset state representations to derive optimal portfolio allocations via a self-supervised clipped-objective policy-learner, ensuring both effectiveness and computational efficiency. Extensive evaluations on three major index datasets from China's A-share market demonstrate that SCP's superior performance in balancing risk-return trade-offs compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Exploratory and ablation studies further validate the contributions of SCP's key components.

papers.title: The Brownian L\'evy transformation is exact
papers.abstract: We prove that the L\'evy transformation of Brownian motion is exact. This settles the long-standing question of whether the transformation is ergodic. The proof combines an interval cutting argument with an estimate for the first entrance of the iterated paths into a small neighborhood of zero at an independent exponential time.

authors.name: Zhi Ling
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University

papers.title: Multiwavelength Analysis of the Merging Cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8: A Three-way Merger in Disguise?
papers.abstract: We identify the galaxy cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8 as a candidate bimodal merging cluster due to its optical properties listed in the redMaPPer cluster catalog. To confirm the cluster's merging state and reveal its dark matter halo and intracluster medium (ICM) morphologies, we conducted a multiwavelength follow-up campaign encompassing HST/ACS optical observations, XMM-Newton X-ray imaging, and Keck/Deimos multislit spectroscopy. The weak lensing mass reconstruction performed with the HST images shows two resolved peaks whose positions coincide with the two brightest cluster galaxies. The ICM morphology is consistent with a post-pericenter merger, with significant asymmetry in X-ray flux between subclusters. Our Keck/Deimos redshift measurements reveal a relative velocity $\Delta v_{\mathrm{LOS}} = 480$ km s$^{-1}$ between eastern and western subclusters. The eastern, more massive subcluster, however, exhibits a highly elongated shape, suggesting either a dark matter halo of considerable eccentricity or the presence of a third, unresolved halo, eliciting the question of whether RMJ1219 is truly binary or a three-way merger. To investigate these hypotheses, we fit the weak lensing shear data using four different combinations of spherical and elliptical NFW halo models and provide an estimate of the mass and concentration of each subhalo. Although the best fit is achieved with a three-halo model, the data are insufficient to determine whether the introduction of extra parameters is statistically justified.

authors.name: Zhuoran Gao
authors.institution: First Hospital of China Medical University

papers.title: Uniqueness Sequences in the Bargmann-Fock Space
papers.abstract: We show that a locally finite sequence with prescribed multiplicities is a uniqueness sequence in the Bargmann-Fock space if and only if a variational supremum involving Jensen potentials and Gaussian relative entropy is infinite. The proof combines exact subharmonic duality with holomorphic realization at the original Gaussian weight. Restricting the supremum to radial tests yields a necessary and sufficient integral criterion for locally finite unions of pairwise disjoint regular rotation orbits satisfying a bounded-overlap condition. For a planar lattice containing the origin and having fundamental area $\pi$, changing only the arguments of its nonzero points yields a uniqueness sequence provided that the resulting points are pairwise distinct. In particular, independently and uniformly rotating the nonzero points of the critical square lattice yields an almost surely complete system of coherent states. Finally, we reduce the general criterion to countably many polynomial tests and give finite approximations to each test score with explicit error bounds.

papers.title: Inverse scattering transform for the $N$-component Gerdjikov-Ivanov equation with nonzero boundary conditions
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the inverse scattering theory of the $N$-component Gerdjikov-Ivanov equation with nonzero boundary conditions. The analyticity of the Jost eigenfunctions is analyzed, and auxiliary eigenfunctions are constructed using tensor products and generalized cross products, thereby yielding a set of analytic eigenfunctions required to formulate the inverse problem. Three fundamental symmetry relations satisfied by the eigenfunctions and scattering data are established, and the asymptotic behavior of both is examined. We provide a complete characterization of the discrete spectrum and derive the corresponding residue conditions by analyzing the ranks of the relevant matrices. The inverse problem is then formulated as a matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem whose solution is used to reconstruct the potential. In the reflectionless case, an explicit solution formula is obtained. Finally, taking the four-component case as an example, we illustrate the structural features of solitons, breathers, and their interactions.

papers.title: An offset--drift Kalman filter for continuous emotion recognition and annotation from sparse human reviews
papers.abstract: Continuous emotion recognition tracks how emotion changes over time, but its predictions often deviate from human ratings, and the traces it is trained on are rated in real time by several annotators, which is slow and costly. A few human reviews could help with both, but rejection only decides which predictions to hand over and adaptation adjusts the model or its outputs; neither uses reviews to correct unreviewed windows directly. We propose a Kalman-filter correction that models the predictor's error as a per-part offset plus a slow drift, estimates it from the reviewed windows and corrects every unreviewed window online, leaving the predictor unchanged. On MSP-Conversation, it beats four simpler corrections in all 48 paired comparisons, keeps correcting each part after reviewing stops and, for uncorrected predictions, tells a person which windows to take over. The same correction serves annotation: with 20% of windows reviewed, the completed trace comes closer to the raters.

authors.name: Jie Dong
authors.institution: North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: DocDUR-Net: Degradation-Aware Unified Document Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Captured document images often suffer from diverse degradations caused by uncontrolled imaging conditions, which reduce readability and obscure fine text structures. Single-degradation restoration methods are usually trained and deployed for individual degradation types, and therefore require model selection before restoration. Unified restoration models alleviate the need to maintain multiple restoration networks by sharing one network across tasks, but representative unified document image restoration methods still depend on external task selection. This dependency limits automatic document image restoration. We propose DocDUR-Net, a degradation-aware unified restoration network that derives restoration guidance directly from the input image. It introduces a Degradation Perception Module (DPM) to extract degradation representations and predict degradation weights, and Degradation Prior-guided Adaptive Feature Fusion (DP-AFF) to combine learnable degradation priors with degradation features extracted from the input. The resulting guidance is injected into a shared restoration backbone, enabling adaptive restoration without external task selection. DocDUR-Net also supports a manual mode with explicit task selection. Experiments on document image restoration benchmarks show that DocDUR-Net achieves the best average PSNR of 29.405 dB and SSIM of 0.960 among unified methods while remaining competitive with single-degradation methods.

authors.name: Xuhan Zheng
authors.institution: Qingdao University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Minkowski Problems for Mixed Centro-Section Integrals
papers.abstract: Recent studies in affine convex geometry have introduced two new families of geometric measures: affine dual curvature measures and centro-section measures. Motivated by these developments, we introduce mixed centro-section integrals and establish their variational formulas. Under the subspace concentration condition, we prove the existence of solutions to the corresponding Minkowski-type problems. We further introduce mixed bi-dual $m$-intersection bodies of index $q$ and establish the corresponding sharp affine isoperimetric inequalities. The resulting mixed centro-section measures include centro-section measures and affine dual curvature measures as special cases.

papers.title: On a Problem of Erd\H{o}s and Graham Related to Restricted Order
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a set of nonnegative integers. We prove that if $A\setminus F$ has a finite order for every finite subset $F\subseteq A$, then $A$ has finite restricted order. This resolves a problem posed by Erd\H{o}s and Graham in 1980. We also establish a local to global principle to characterize restricted asymptotic bases of finite order.

authors.name: Lilu Zhao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Spin superfluid transport of magnons in altermagnetic insulators
papers.abstract: We study the spin superfluidity for Lieb and inverse Lieb lattices in altermagnets, which enables coherent transport of spin angular momentum carried by the phase of an easy-plane N\'eel order. The easy-plane anisotropy supplies the $U(1)$ platform, while the nonrelativistic spin splitting generates sublattice-alternating exchange imbalance with $B_{1g}$ symmetry. Via a continuum theory and Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert simulations, we find that the Goldstone mode becomes quadratic at the critical stability boundary. An axial phase gradient transfers phase-channel spectral weight to the gapped mode, whereas a diagonal flow leaves these signatures absent. The spin superfluid exhibits momentum-space anisotropy due to the chiral-splitting magnon dispersion, while strong fields or elevated temperatures suppress phase coherence. Accounting for the contribution of thermal magnons at the interface, we present that the critical spin flow varies with the injection angle under the altermagnetic crystal-field effects. The spin-superfluid decay length scales with the interfacial spin-mixing conductance, which can be measured by the spin Hall magnetoresistance and spin Seebeck effect. Our findings establish altermagnetic insulators, particularly $\mathrm{La_2O_3FeMnSe_2}$, as promising platforms for low-dissipation spin transport.

authors.name: Dele Li
authors.institution: Fujian College of Water Conservancy and Electric Power

papers.title: TaCo: Rethinking Correlation for Visual Tracking on Edge Devices
papers.abstract: Lightweight trackers have replaced cross-correlation with attention, and on low-power edge hardware they pay for it, since memory-bound softmax, normalization and reshaping operators of attention cost far more time than their arithmetic suggests. Benchmarking efficient trackers on an edge Neural Processing Unit (NPU) and an Arm CPU under one numerically validated protocol, we find that correlation trackers are the fast ones, but they lag in accuracy unless they adopt a ViT backbone, which brings attention back. We revisit what correlation lacks. Template--search interaction serves two roles: conditioning the search features on the target and matching them against it spatially. Attention does both, whereas correlation only matches, and does so on features extracted without knowledge of the target. We present TaCo (Target-aligned Correlation), which supplies the missing conditioning without attention by letting the template enter the per-frame network only as operands computed once per video. A descriptor of the target scales and shifts the search features channel by channel inside the backbone, and kernels aligned with the target box, each with a weight predicted from the template, correlate with them in one matrix product. With the backbone fixed, our correlation remains essential while incurring negligible NPU overhead, offering a better speed-accuracy trade-off than the attention-based interactions we tested. TaCo-T achieves 62.3% LaSOT AUC at 184 FPS on the Rockchip RV1126B NPU and 96 FPS on a Raspberry Pi 5 CPU, 3.0x and 3.5x the NPU speed of HiT-Tiny and AsymTrack-T at higher accuracy. TaCo-B reaches 65.6% at 50 FPS on the NPU, more than twice the speed of HiT-Base, AsymTrack-B and LightFC-vit, again at higher accuracy. Code and models are available at https://github.com/TsingWei/TaCo-Tracker.

papers.title: Converse comparison of $g$-expectations and uniqueness of generators of BSDEs: a novel approach and some sharp results
papers.abstract: This paper investigates inverse problems for backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs), with a particular focus on the converse comparison theorem and the uniqueness of generators solely through the initial values of the corresponding solutions. To this end, we develop a forward-SDE representation approach that combines a contradiction argument with a representation of generators in terms of solutions to associated forward stochastic differential equations (SDEs). As one of the main consequences, we prove that an ordering between two $g$-expectations necessarily implies the pointwise comparability of their generators, without requiring any additional structural assumptions beyond the standard Lipschitz condition. This removes the continuity, $y$-independence, and deterministic assumptions required in previous works, thereby yielding a complete solution to the converse comparison problem for $g$-expectations under the standard Lipschitz framework and, at the same time, establishing a general uniqueness theorem for generators of BSDEs.

authors.name: Shengjun Fan
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology

papers.title: Do Language Models Mix? Experimental Evidence from Asymmetric Matching Pennies
papers.abstract: I test whether language models can select and implement mixed strategies using asymmetric matching pennies and a task with prescribed choice probabilities. Several models respond to their own payoffs, contrary to equilibrium and resembling human experimental subjects. Without randomization tools, no tested model reliably implements prescribed probabilities. Prompting models with their choice histories alone does not resolve this failure. While an external randomizer sharply improves implementation, I find most models remain exploitable by an opportunistic opponent. These results provide guidance on the delegation of strategic decisions to AI systems based on language models.

papers.title: Stochastic Optimization for Switch-System Identification under Errors-in-Variables
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address the identification of switched dynamical systems under errors-in-variables, where both input and output measurements are corrupted by noise, and the number of operating modes and subsystem orders are unknown. We propose a unified identification framework that simultaneously estimates the subsystem parameters, latent switching sequence, and model structure. The proposed formulation combines a variance-normalized data-fitting criterion with temporally regularized soft mode assignments and sparsity-inducing penalties for selecting the active modes and relevant input-output lags. To solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we develop an alternating algorithm that incorporates convex mode-assignment updates and proximal stochastic variance-reduced gradient optimization for parameter estimation. While the existing approaches in the literature require exhaustive searches over candidate structures, the proposed method performs structure selection within a single model. Numerical experiments demonstrate accurate recovery of the underlying system structure and favorable computational efficiency compared with a generalized total least squares and dynamic programming approach, particularly as the number of candidate structures increases.

authors.name: Mohammad Khosravi
authors.institution: Weifang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Gaussian Process Stochastic Frontiers with Two-Way Fixed Effects
papers.abstract: Parametric frontier restrictions and unobserved time heterogeneity can distort efficiency measurement in panel data. This paper develops a Bayesian stochastic frontier model with a Gaussian process prior and unrestricted individual and time effects that may be correlated with inputs. Conditional on inefficiency, orthogonal projection eliminates both sets of fixed effects, yielding a restricted likelihood that retains observation-specific inefficiency. Monte Carlo experiments show competitive performance under correct parametric specification and improved performance when benchmark models impose an incorrect frontier functional form or omit time effects. An application to Spanish dairy farms observed from 1999 to 2010 yields similar average technical efficiency across specifications, but a lower posterior mean of average returns to scale, with greater uncertainty, under the Gaussian process frontier. Models with year effects also yield more stable estimated efficiency profiles than the benchmark with a quadratic trend and time-input interactions. These findings show that conclusions about scale economies and efficiency dynamics depend on both frontier flexibility and the treatment of time heterogeneity.

papers.title: Stability of separable solutions to a fast diffusion system
papers.abstract: We study a Dirichlet fast diffusion system with symmetric linear cross-loss terms on a bounded smooth domain. A coupled Rayleigh quotient captures the variational structure of the coupling and is nonincreasing along sufficiently regular positive solution pairs. Under the common extinction and regularity hypotheses, this monotonicity and the energy identity yield upper and lower bounds \[ C^{-1}(T^*-t)^{1/(p-1)} \le \|(u(t),v(t))\|_{L^{p+1}(\Omega)} \le C(T^*-t)^{1/(p-1)}. \] In the Sobolev subcritical range, a Lyapunov functional for the rescaled system yields a sequence of times $t_j\uparrow T^*$ along which the rescaled pair converges strongly in $H_0^1(\Omega)\times H_0^1(\Omega)$ to a nonnegative classical stationary solution pair. The integral lower bound excludes the trivial limiting pair, while the coupling with $\alpha>0$ ensures that neither limiting component is identically zero. As a further property of the stationary system, we show that proportional components of a nontrivial nonnegative solution pair must coincide. We also construct a positive diagonal stationary solution pair by constrained minimization. Scalar upper comparison and a B\'enilan--Crandall-type estimate for smooth positive diagonal solutions provide complementary links with the scalar fast diffusion equation.

papers.title: Hetero-Associative Visuomotor Memory: Soft Recall as a Base for Learned Residuals in Few-Demonstration Imitation
papers.abstract:
Retrieve-and-correct policies typically refine the nearest retrieved demonstration chunk, the
  readout that works best when executed directly. We study what a demonstration memory should
  supply to the corrector instead and find that a smooth, softmax-weighted recall over the whole
  memory is a much better base. On ALOHA cube transfer (40 human demonstrations), soft recall is
  no better to execute alone than the nearest chunk; however, with keys, candidates, and training
  fixed, correcting it raises success by 22.4 points on fresh resets with new encoders and by 7.4
  against a closed-loop-tuned top-1 corrector. On robomimic Square, it leads by 7.9 points with
  the two better operators and by 6.7 on a label-free draw of equal size. This gain holds on
  sparse, varied demonstrations under an action-aware key and leave-one-demonstration-out
  training, and fades or slightly reverses on dense, scripted, or generated data. Building on this
  finding, our hetero-associative visuomotor memory (HAVM, 14M parameters) trains offline in about
  five minutes, including a learned retrieval temperature $\beta$, and runs in 1.1 ms. Across six
  fresh ALOHA encoders, it reaches 76.4% within 24 s, comparable to a 264M Diffusion Policy
  trained for 6.7 h (78.8%) and ahead of ACT (71.7%) and fine-tuned VLAs (65.2-75.2%), while
  leading every 40-demonstration baseline within the benchmark's 8 s limit (74.6%; +6.5 over
  Diffusion Policy, +15.1 over ACT). On LIBERO, one 40-task memory reaches 92.2% and loses far
  less than SmolVLA to rewording; on a real SO-101 arm, it sustains 30 Hz control without
  stalling. Unlike pretrained foundation policies aimed at zero-shot generalization to unseen
  tasks and workspaces, HAVM trades broad out-of-distribution generalization for rapid adaptation
  to the available demonstrations.

papers.title: An iterative procedure for statistical calibration
papers.abstract: We study the iterative proportional fitting procedure (IPFP) under multiple pushforward constraints, motivated by model calibration. The goal is to find a distribution on model parameters whose pushforward by models matches data distributions. The classic convergence result of IPFP under marginal constraints establish convergence of IPFP under suitable regularity conditions and develop a variant of sequential importance sampling to approximate the iterative procedure. We also propose a related procedure for constructing a high probability parameter region. Simulation studies illustrate the performance of these methods. Finally, we apply IPFP to COVID19 ensemble forecasting. Variation of Covid strains across regions can lead to variation in surge rates and thus affect forecasting accuracy. To capture the variation, we estimate a probability distribution of epidemiological model parameters using early stage surge data from an ensemble of regions. We then propagate the distribution through the model to forecast both the ensemble's overall trend and its variability.

papers.title: Halley's Comet Over New Zealand In 1910: An Overview Of A Spectacular Apparition
papers.abstract: Halley's Comet (1P/Halley) returns to the inner Solar System approximately every 76 years. In 1910, the comet put on a particularly wonderful display, whereby the comet attained an apparent magnitude of 1 or brighter, and had a tail of up to 120{\deg} in length. Many New Zealanders saw Comet 1P/Halley and submitted articles to newspapers across the land. Those articles were mostly from lay-people who reported their observations of this, the most famous of all comets. There were, however, numerous serious amateur and professional astronomers who made detailed observations and took world-class photographs of the comet. In this paper, we present the results of a thorough search through historical records and media publications in Aotearoa/New Zealand, to investigate how extensively Comet 1P/Halley was observed from this island nation. Where appropriate, we compare the observations described with international accounts, and find that those made from Aotearoa/New Zealand often echo what observers were witnessing around the world. We find that thousands of New Zealanders observed Comet 1P/Halley in 1910, and that the comet raised the interest in astronomy across the land resulting in the establishment of a number of astronomical societies that remain active to the current day.

authors.name: Wayne Orchiston
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Synchronizing Cameras via 3D Object Relationships
papers.abstract: In this paper, we synchronize multiple videos of the same dynamic event through object relationships. Driven by dynamic reconstruction and novel view synthesis, many recent synchronization methods rely on pixel-level evidence, such as point correspondences across views or the photometric losses of a reconstructed scene. In dynamic scenes, however, fast motion and occlusions make the moving regions that carry much of the timing information hard to match across views. We thus propose to bring back the traditional wisdom that objects are reliable cues for global reasoning about cameras. Measured in 3D, the relationships between objects, such as the distance between two people, are stable across all views up to scale; they can serve as cues for alignment. To compare these relationships across cameras, we only need the identity of each object in every view, as the cues are relational. We obtain these identities by giving a vision-language model a few frames of every camera and prompting it to identify the objects in the scene. We then segment and track each identified object through every video with an open-vocabulary segmentor. To obtain the 3D locations of objects, we use a pretrained depth estimator. Where depth or segmentation fails, we complement these 3D cues with 2D motion from point tracks. Finally, we synchronize the cameras by finding the temporal offsets at which the cues of different cameras agree best, first for each camera pair and then for all cameras jointly with robust optimization. We evaluate our method on four standard benchmarks, outperforming the state of the art.

papers.title: BreathSplat: Grounding One Smooth Motion in the Breathing Phase for 4D Cone-Beam CT
papers.abstract: Four-dimensional cone-beam computed tomography (4D-CBCT) images the anatomy of a breathing patient, but sees each breathing phase from only a few angles. Breathing, however, is a smooth motion that repeats; it has a phase. Existing methods exploit this either by reconstructing the anatomy as a function of the breathing phase, often through bins, or by estimating smooth dynamic motions in time. Yet none of these grounds one smooth motion in the phase. We thus propose to share projections across breathing phases with splines. Specifically, we represent the 4D volume with dynamic Gaussians whose motion uses B-splines in space and time. We ground the motion state in the respiratory phase, which we read from well-studied conventional surrogates. Projections at the same phase in different breathing cycles then constrain the same anatomy and motion. On simulated lung scans, our method, BreathSplat, outperforms recent dynamic methods in reconstruction and motion accuracy, including those given the ground-truth phase. We further show qualitatively, on two real patient scans, that our method provides clearer reconstructions than the state of the art.

papers.title: Exact high-order spectral moments and moment-based reconstruction of polaron spectra at finite temperature for arbitrary linear electron-phonon coupling
papers.abstract: We present a family of exact and efficient recurrence relations for the frequency moments of the single-electron addition spectral function of a generic single-band electron-phonon Hamiltonian with linear coupling to harmonic phonons. Working in the limit of zero carrier density, the formulation applies at zero and finite temperature and generalizes to arbitrary dimensions and lattice geometry. Using the Holstein and Peierls models coupled to Einstein and dispersive phonons as examples, we obtain closed-form expressions for moments of far higher order than those available in the literature, at modest computational cost. Beyond providing stringent benchmarks for numerical methods and experimental spectra, the high-order moments serve as input to approximate reconstructions of polaron spectra at weak-to-intermediate coupling and low temperature. The resulting spectral functions are exact in the weak-coupling and atomic limits, and respect rigorous bounds on the polaron energy and weight that we show the self-consistent Born approximation violates throughout the coupling-adiabaticity plane. The approach therefore offers an inexpensive yet accurate approximation, especially for unexplored or numerically intractable models, before computationally demanding exact methods are applied.

papers.title: Estimating subcritical multiplication from stochastic neutron noise: a branching Brownian motion model for leakage counts
papers.abstract: A neutron detector placed outside a subcritical system records fission chains as correlated bursts of counts. The time dependence of these correlations gives access to the $\alpha$ eigenvalues governing the decay of the system and, with additional physical information, to its effective multiplication factor $k_{\mathrm{eff}}$. The usual analysis relies on point kinetics, which ignores where chains are born and which neutrons escape. We examine this approximation in a model simple enough to be solved: branching Brownian motion, that is, one-group neutron diffusion with capture and fission, in a domain whose absorbing boundary plays the role of the detector. For a stationary Poisson source we derive the Feynman $Y$ function (the count variance-to-mean ratio minus one) by following pairs of neutrons from their common ancestor to their detection. In a homogeneous cube the result is an explicit sum over spatial modes whose weights are fixed by the geometry and the source. We compare it with direct branching simulations and with one-speed OpenMC transport calculations in which fission is sampled with analog reaction selection and FREYA multiplicities. At the longest simulated gate the model agrees with transport to about $1\%$ at $k=0.8$ and $0.9$, and to $10\%$ at $k=0.5$. The corresponding point-model discrepancies range from $25$ to $48\%$. When geometry, source and material parameters are known, retaining the spatial modes also reduces the bias on the inferred multiplication factor. Two extensions prepare the use of the model in inverse problems. Correlations between opposite faces distinguish systems that share the same fundamental decay rate but differ in leakage, and a hierarchy of three stationary problems links this spatial benchmark to multiplicity counting. Modal convergence, detector imbalance and spectral evolution remain limitations for quantitative inference.

papers.title: Faster and Better Query (FBQ): Learning Future-Position Probes from the First Generated Token
papers.abstract: When a large language model (LLM) evicts prompt keys and values at the end of prefill, it must decide what to keep before it sees the queries from subsequent decoding steps. Generating a draft continuation can approximate those queries at the cost of extra autoregressive steps. Can we use the embedding of the first output token, already available from the final prefill logits, to construct low-cost pseudo queries that approximate future decoding queries? We start with FTQ-8, which places eight copies of the first token ID at consecutive future positions and reads their attention to the prompt in one causal forward pass. Each copy sees a different prefix, but a generic opening such as the offers a poor literal guess for seven successive tokens. Faster and Better Query (FBQ) preserves the first embedding and learns an additive offset at each of the seven remaining positions. We train these offsets to predict the average prompt attention of a full-cache continuation. On LongBench, FBQ performs comparably to eight-step Lookahead Q-Cache at the same cache budget, using a single forward pass to compute all probe queries.

authors.name: Tongtong Yuan
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ShowNow: Fine-Grained Speculative Streaming for Responsive World Models
papers.abstract: Interactive world models must generate video continuously while responding promptly to user actions. Real-time throughput alone leaves input latency unresolved: coarse generation blocks delay action updates, and generation after input adds work to the response path. We introduce ShowNow, a fine-grained speculative streaming framework that uses computation available during playback to prepare action-conditioned futures before input arrives. Single-latent commitment enables frequent decisions, while configurable preparation covers one to eight actions. We construct a matched multi-future dataset to train alternative continuations from a common state; shared-history tree execution and fused commitment make their preparation efficient. On a single H100, our 5B model sustains 480p generation at 16 fps with eight prepared futures. In ViZDoom, the complete ShowNow deployment reduces median input-to-display latency from 620 to 208 ms relative to the native-block SolarWM-FT deployment. Matched-policy experiments reduce restart empty ticks from 1.56% to 0.09% (94%) and improve on-time responses to action changes. These results establish complementary roles for fine-grained commitment and advance preparation, with measured trade-offs in visual fidelity and long-horizon consistency. ShowNow turns playback-time computation into responsive visual interaction. Project: https://github.com/showlab/ShowNow.

authors.name: Mike Zheng Shou
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
