Averages hide a tail: under the actual timetables, 5.9% and 3.9% of residents are at stops whose expected wait rises by 10 minutes or more, against 0.5% and 0.3% in the alternatives, and capping the increase at 10 minutes at every served stop is feasible at the operator's sizes. If half the removed hours become paid hours saved, the labor saving of both reductions and their main alternatives fall short of the fare revenue on the removed trips.

papers.title: NEVA: Natural-Language Co-Evolution and Validation of Microarchitectures
papers.abstract: Recent large language model (LLM)-guided evolutionary approaches have demonstrated the potential to automate microarchitectural design exploration. However, existing approaches primarily evolve C++ simulator code rather than reasoning directly about the microarchitectural designs it represents. As C++ code embodies hardware designs with several layers of abstraction, evolving it directly forces LLMs to reason through implementation details rather than the actual architectural mechanisms, hardware state, and decision rules that define a microarchitectural design. To this end, we propose NEVA, an LLM-guided methodology that generates new microarchitectural policies by extracting, integrating and adapting architectural concepts from published research. NEVA extracts the underlying concepts from prior works into a structured knowledge library, which then guides the evolution of joint natural-language architectural specifications. This approach addresses three key challenges: architectural representation in natural language, validation of candidate designs under hardware constraints, and the coordination of microarchitecture components using diagnostic feedback through co-evolution. We evaluate NEVA across single-core and multicore configurations using SPEC CPU2017/2026, Google, GAP, and XSBench workloads, and compare specification-level evolution against code-level evolution across different search strategies. Under Claude Opus 5.5, NEVA discovers designs achieving up to 4.8% higher held-out single-core performance than the Pythia-Mockingjay baseline. A selected EvoX design achieves improvements of 3.4% and 1.5% under full and restricted memory bandwidth, respectively, although its multicore performance does not differ significantly from the baseline. The EvoX search evaluates 40 candidates over 2.2 days, with approximately $320 in LLM usage at API list prices.

papers.title: On infinite torsion of abelian varieties over large algebraic fields of positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a non-zero abelian variety defined over a finitely generated field $F$. A conjecture of Geyer and Jarden [GJ78] asserts that for every $\sigma\in \mathrm{Gal}(F^{sep}/F)$ outside a set of Haar measure zero, there exist infinitely many primes $\ell$ such that the $\ell$-torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(\sigma))$ is non-zero (or equivalently, the torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(\sigma))$ is infinite), where $F^{sep}(\sigma)$ denotes the subfield of $F^{sep}$ fixed by $\sigma$. While this conjecture remains open when $\mathrm{Char}(F)>0$, we establish a new case under the assumptions of $\mathrm{End}(A)=\mathbb{Z}$ and the connectedness of the algebraic monodromy groups attached to $A/F$.

papers.title: The involute function and its inverse in IEEE 754 double precision: measured and proved accuracy, and its effect on gear inspection
papers.abstract: Almost every spur and helical gear calculation uses the involute function inv(a) = tan(a) - a or its inverse. Near a = 0 the two terms almost cancel: at a = 10^-3 the textbook formula in binary64 keeps about 9 correct digits, and far fewer in binary32, binary16 or fixed point, and the result can depend on the platform's tan. We report the accuracy of a proprietary implementation that avoids these problems. On 50,000 committed test angles the forward function's largest error against an 80-digit reference is 0.4999681 ulp, so every tested result is correctly rounded (measured, not proved). The inverse is proved faithfully rounded, with error at most 0.6 ulp, for 10^-200 <= y < 2, using interval arithmetic and the SMT solvers z3 and cvc5 with a short, named list of trusted inputs; its largest measured error on 50,000 points is 0.5555115 ulp. A separate bracket around the root is proved to contain it for 0 < y <= 10^6, and did so at all 47,083 test points. Both functions return identical bits on x86-64 and aarch64 Linux, Apple-silicon macOS, AWS Lambda and an NVIDIA DGX Spark, in Python and Node.js, on every finite test input. Against public inverse methods on nine runtimes, our inverse returned the same bits on all of them and stayed within 0.54 ulp on 12,017 targets from 0.5 to 60 degrees, while textbook Newton iterations differed between runtimes on up to about 10% of inputs and kept only 12 correct digits. For external and internal spur gears with 5 to 500 teeth and pressure angles from 14.5 to 30 degrees, all inputs fall inside the tested and proved ranges. Against ISO 1328-1 tolerance classes, we give in micrometres the errors that shortcut inverses cause in pin measurement and centre distance, and how far circular-arc CAD teeth (SolidWorks Toolbox) depart from the involute. Drawing an involute is easy; accuracy matters in inspection.

papers.title: Planetary biotechnospheres, biotechnosignatures and the search for extraterrestrial intelligence
papers.abstract: The concept of planetary intelligence as collective intelligence is used to consider possible evolutionary paths of biotechnospheres that emerge on the intersection of the technosphere with the biosphere and support coupling of the technosphere with the biosphere, thus affecting planetary evolution. In mature biotechnospheres, the intelligence of technologies and the intelligence of life forms, including engineered life forms, could act in concert to perform various tasks (e.g. monitoring and restoring planetary environments and biodiversity; supporting space missions; terraforming cosmic objects). Space exploration can expand biotechnospheres beyond planets and create cosmic ecosystems. Humankind, other civilizations or their intelligent machines may produce biotechnosignatures (i.e. observables and artefacts of biotechnospheres) in the Solar System and beyond. I propose ten possible biotechnosignatures and strategies for the search for these biotechnosignatures in situ and over interstellar distances. For example, if a non-human advanced civilization existed and built biotechnospheres on Earth in the past, the descendants of its engineered bacteria could currently exist on Earth and have properties pertaining to the functions of the ancient bacteria in the biotechnospheres; intelligent technologies created by the ancient civilization could migrate to the Solar System's outer regions; these two scenarios are described as the Cosmic Descendants hypothesis. Interstellar asteroids, free-floating planets, spacecraft and objects gravitationally bound to flyby stars might carry extraterrestrial biotechnospheres and pass through the Solar System. In connection to the fate of post-main-sequence stars and their Oort clouds, the probability for interstellar asteroids to carry biotechnospheres or to be interstellar spacecraft is estimated as very low.

papers.title: Spectral stability and nonlinear asymptotics of radial steady states for the viscous vector Burgers equation in an exterior domain with negative far field
papers.abstract: We study radial stationary waves of the multidimensional viscous vector Burgers equation in the exterior of a ball, with strictly negative radial far-field data. For each fixed wave satisfying a strict modified-Bessel admissibility criterion, a positive-weight conjugation yields a self-adjoint linearized operator with a positive isolated lowest eigenvalue below its essential spectrum. We establish global nonlinear stability under general continuous vector perturbations that are small in a mixed weighted-$L^2$ and unweighted-$L^\infty$ norm, without requiring small initial gradients or compact support. The lowest-eigenvalue exponential decay rate is attained for a nonempty class of admissible data. We further identify the nonlinear lowest-mode amplitude and derive refined weighted-$L^2$ and physical-variable $L^\infty$ remainder estimates, including the possible resonant case, together with a quadratic expansion in the initial data with a uniform cubic remainder.

authors.name: Qingsong Zhao
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University

papers.title: Nonradial asymptotic stability of radial steady states for the viscous vector Burgers equation in an exterior domain with positive far field
papers.abstract: We study the viscous vector Burgers equation outside a ball in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, near a radial stationary state with positive far-field value. For every fixed $b,\mu,r_0>0$, we prove global existence and $L^\infty$ asymptotic stability for continuous, nonradial vector perturbations that vanish at infinity, satisfy the homogeneous boundary condition, and are small only in $L^\infty$. The perturbations need not be irrotational or integrable, and no initial-gradient assumption is imposed. A Bessel-weight conjugation and a divergence--curl identity yield weighted coercivity. A moving-front argument, a stopped stochastic estimate for angular momentum, and scalar Burgers comparison then recover convergence in the physical supremum norm. We also establish a quantitative Lyapunov estimate and, for perturbations compactly supported in the radial variable, an $O(t^{-1/4})$ decay bound. No additional restriction on the dimensionless parameter $br_0/\mu$ is required.

authors.name: Qingsong Zhao
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University

papers.title: SMOTE 25 Years of Magic: What Has Been Done, What the Evidence Shows, and Whom It Reached
papers.abstract: Background. SMOTE was published in this journal in 2002 and reviewed here at its fifteenth anniversary in 2018. At twenty-five it is cited by more than 34,000 indexed works, half of them outside computer science. Objectives. To establish what the methods built on SMOTE change, how strong the evidence for them is, and whom the technique has reached. Methods. We audited a curated corpus of 76 papers, 37 of which propose a SMOTE-family generator, and tested its coverage with a systematic search of 22,426 records in the PRISMA 2020 format. From the corpus we collected 1,756 dataset entries, 1,511 published comparisons with SMOTE and the evaluation design of 71 studies; from the search we drew 300 applications of SMOTE at random. We used an agentic AI approach to extract, screen and code under our written rules, and we report how each step was checked. Results. Every variant re-decides some of the six decisions of the SMOTE rule, and 24 of the 37 are only ever run on two classes. In their own papers, proposed methods beat SMOTE in 79.0% of the decided comparisons, but independent studies find that the gains shrink with strong learners and tuned thresholds, and that resampling damages calibration. The corpus holds 52 of the 3,097 records that pass the screen and covers the early years closely, the recent ones thinly. The reach is very wide, but a benefit at the level of outcomes is undemonstrated, four harms are documented, and an estimated 37% of applications resample the whole data set before splitting it. Conclusions. For tabular classification, a new SMOTE variant should no longer count as a contribution in itself: a new generator should be tested one decision at a time against class weighting and a tuned threshold with a strong learner, with calibration reported. We close with a selection guide, a reporting checklist of fifteen items and a research agenda.

papers.title: SprintGS: Eliminating Redundancy for Fast 3D Gaussian Splatting Training
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) renders photorealistic novel views in real time, but its per-scene training (optimization) remains slow. Recent fast training methods such as FastGS shorten training to a few minutes by reducing the number of Gaussians. Profiling FastGS, we find two costs that remain even in its compact model. First, rasterization is still the largest cost, and redundant work remains in it. Second, the loss computation does not shrink with the number of Gaussians, so its share of the training time grows as the model becomes compact. We present SprintGS, a training framework built on FastGS that keeps the model compact and reduces both costs. For rasterization, scheduled tile culling limits each Gaussian to the tiles where it matters, using a coarse footprint that is annealed to the exact one before training ends; convergence-aware pruning removes converged, nearly transparent Gaussians; and a shuffle-efficient backward pass reduces the data exchanged between GPU threads. For the loss, a fused loss computes the loss and its image gradient in the forward pass without a loss map, removing most of its cost. SprintGS trains 2.15x faster than FastGS at comparable quality, and 1.81x faster in its high-quality setting. It also accelerates other fast training methods and dynamic, sparse-view, and surface reconstruction.

papers.title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$
papers.abstract: The low-energy electronic structures of $\lambda$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ and $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$ were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs). For $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$, DFT-selected and directly XRD-refined structural models were compared before and after fixed-lattice relaxation. Their initially different near-Fermi-level electronic structures become similar after relaxation. Relative to BETS, relaxed STF has a narrower frontier bandwidth while retaining a substantial dimerization energy scale. Two MLWFs were constructed for each selected unrelaxed structure to represent the upper frontier bands, with total spreads of 36.708 \AA$^2$ for BETS and 37.578 \AA$^2$ for STF. The Wannier-derived transfer integrals show a pronounced reduction of $t_{d1}$ from 51 meV in BETS to 6.5 meV in STF, indicating selective modification of the low-energy electronic connectivity.

papers.title: Regularity Criteria for Ind-Sheaves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the Kashiwara-Schapira regularity conjecture [Conjecture 6.4, Masaki Kashiwara and Pierre Schapira, Microlocal study of ind-sheaves I: micro-support and regularity, 2003] in arbitrary dimension. For this purpose, we show that under suitable finiteness and isotropic micro-support conditions, ind-sheaves which are regular on the zero section come from $\mathbb{R}$-constructible sheaves. Furthermore, we characterize the essential image of constructible sheaves under the natural embedding functor, and relate them to regular holonomic $\mathcal{D}$-modules via the regular Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. Moreover, we present a non-characteristic deformation lemma and a microlocal Morse lemma for regular ind-sheaves as an application of the main theorem.

papers.title: ScaleCurve: From Constant Scale to Consistent Motion for World-Space Human Mesh Recovery
papers.abstract: World-space human mesh recovery can lose spatial consistency even when camera-space body estimates are accurate. A single sequence-wide scale resolves global scale ambiguity but cannot correct local scale distortion along a reconstructed camera path. We present ScaleCurve, a framework that estimates time-varying metric corrections from human-ground geometry. We construct scale observations by comparing predicted foot geometry with locally fitted ground planes. Joint temporal optimization downweights inconsistent observations and couples neighboring scale estimates, allowing calibration to adapt along the camera path without freely following measurement noise. We scale camera translation increments and integrate them into a calibrated trajectory. With this camera fixed, we refine the lifted body motion using 2D image evidence and pretrained 3D dynamics, while restricting global trajectory rescaling. ScaleCurve achieves state-of-the-art performance on most evaluated metrics on both EMDB-2 and SLOPER4D. Consistent gains across three HMR backbones demonstrate its compatibility with diverse body estimates without retraining. Code will be made publicly available.

papers.title: The Information Content of News Embeddings
papers.abstract: Does the predictive success of news embeddings reflect a better measure of news surprises or other sources of return predictability in text? We decompose news embeddings by content into event-category, firm-identity, and idiosyncratic components, and by timing into historical levels and current deviations. At short horizons, event categories account for most of the predictive power of embedding forecasts, and simple forecasts based on historical average returns after news in each event category outperform them. At longer horizons, firm information already present in earlier news coverage accounts for a substantial share of return predictability, even after residualization on firm characteristics. The dominance of event categories persists, and historical levels still contribute in the first months, when using a language model pretrained entirely before our sample period. For Llama-2, even embeddings constructed from news more than three years old predict returns at long horizons. However, its predictive advantage over RoBERTa is concentrated in firm identity and the historical level, and its advantage in these components largely disappears by its pretraining cutoff. A calibration shows that pretraining memory, a source of look-ahead bias, can account for this pattern. Describing news more fully is not the same as measuring news surprises, and persistent return predictability from news text does not by itself establish slow incorporation of news into prices.

papers.title: How Many Sources, Not Just How Many Problems: Planning the Precision of LLM Evaluations from Earlier Results
papers.abstract: When benchmark problems share sources, such as variants of one template or tasks from one repository, an evaluation budget must fix the number of sources as well as the number of problems. We ask whether pilot data or earlier evaluation results can predict, before an evaluation is run, how much the standard deviation (SD) of the score grows when the same budget is concentrated on fewer sources. We use the classical design effect with an intraclass correlation estimated on data disjoint from those used to check the prediction. On GSM-Symbolic, 100 problems drawn as 10 templates x 10 variants have an SD of 9.2 pp against 2.7 pp from 100 templates; pilot data on 15 other questions predict the ratio as 3.49 against 3.52 measured on held-out questions (medians over 20 splits; single splits err by -13% to +16%), once the actual sampling plan is included. On SWE-bench Verified, 10 randomly selected public submissions predict the median ratio for 119 other submissions within 3% for 2 or more repositories, and 3 submissions are nearly as good. Dropping the finite-population terms from the design prediction gives errors of 13-21% on GSM-Symbolic, where it reduces to the textbook formula, and 25-35% on SWE-bench. Widening iid intervals by the square root of the pilot design effect brings pass@1 coverage on concentrated designs to 0.93-0.98, but not pass@16 (0.85, 0.76). We also report two lessons for anyone validating such predictions: split pilot and held-out data by question source, not by difficulty version, and do not read a good fit of the formula as evidence of source clustering (MATH-500). The method is not new; we contribute a held-out test of its advance predictions and a recipe for using them. Code: https://github.com/Guang627/deff-eval

papers.title: Measuring the Value of One Shared Image at Robot Handoffs in Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: When the lead robot cannot continue, what should it send the teammate that must finish the route? We replay a frozen receiver at each contact under alternative messages. Across 3,920 autonomous departures in 106 environments, adding the view before the lead's last action block to its executed actions raised success by 7.51 percentage points (pp) per RxR handoff and 8.54 pp per SAGE handoff. Per departure the gains were 2.23 and 1.44 pp, respectively. The lead continuing in simulation defines the empirical full-history ceiling (Solo). At contact, the lead had accumulated a median of 41 frames. Sending one frame when available recovered 24% of the full-history advantage over actions alone in SAGE and 30% in RxR. Over an estimated progress cue in SAGE, the image rescued 100 routes and reversed 54 successes. Near-goal receivers finished outside less often (63.1% to 51.7%, post hoc). In secondary comparisons the earlier view outperformed the contact view by 6-7 pp per handoff. Exact-route specificity and image gains at controlled starts with mostly unknown progress or outside the goal region remained unresolved. Gains were detectable from about 7 kB per handoff. Random transmission matched within size bins nearly equaled the learned sender's team success. At a required handoff, a view of the approach to the last maneuver helps the receiver finish.

papers.title: Context Scaling: A New Frontier of AI Scaling
papers.abstract: Many failures of deployed AI arise not from weak inference but from a mismatch between the state a task depends on and the context available when the system acts. Relevant user state, repository revisions, tool traces, sensor readings, or environment changes may be unavailable, distorted, or poorly selected. We call the effort to reduce this bottleneck context scaling. We frame a model as $P_\theta(d\mid c)$ within a system governed by three budgets: training $B_\theta$, decision-time $B_d$, and context-infrastructure $B_c$. Pretraining scaling invests in $\theta$; decision-time scaling searches, refines, or verifies decisions under supplied context; context scaling improves the system's capacity to acquire, represent, deliver, evaluate, and persist deployment state for model use. The three programs interact, but only $B_c$ targets what the system can make available before a decision. This view makes the model-infrastructure pair the unit of analysis. We define effective-context value as a task- and intervention-dependent attribution, separate deployment state from model-visible context, and identify availability, fidelity, selection, and utilization failures. We then organize current mechanisms through a five-operation context lifecycle and propose controlled budget interventions and utility-cost curves for evaluation. The resulting agenda centers on grounded reporting, interaction-data and full-cost infrastructure, and safety and governance for persistent, adaptive systems.

papers.title: Quantization concealment of angular momentum: dynamic origin of spins
papers.abstract: Since their introduction, spins of elementary particles remain a phenomenological addition to modern quantum theories. While relatively recent studies on Dirac and other linearized equations of motion have revealed the spatial current nature of the spin magnetic moment (instead of the commonly pictured self-rotation), the dynamical origin of this circulating current remains unresolved. Here, we expose a long-overlooked generic shortcoming of wave mechanics ("quantization concealment of angular momentum") that undesirably reduces the canonical angular momentum of bound eigen-modes and renders incomplete the minimal coupling to magnetic fields. Recovering the kinetic orbital angular momentum resolves $1s$-orbital's counterintuitive "zero" angular momentum and reproduces all planar modes' anomalous Zeeman splitting. Regarding spins as effective remedy to the concealment offers natural explanations to their main puzzles: 1) dynamical origin of spin magnetic moment and 2) frame invariance of spin angular momentum. This implies absence of spin magnetic moment for free particles, a strong prediction verifiable through Stern-Gerlach experiments on electrons.

authors.name: Wenjie Long
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine

papers.title: The Exact Nef-Curve Cone Formula for dlt Pairs
papers.abstract: We prove an exact rational-curve formula for the nef-curve cone of every complex projective dlt pair with effective real boundary, answering the related question proposed by Cascini. Every $(K_X+\Delta)$-negative extremal ray is generated by a movable rational curve whose normalization is free in the smooth locus. We reduce the klt case to known results and treat the remaining limiting rays with a new argument based on an orthogonal movable divisor and induction on dimension.

authors.name: Jingcao Wu
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: A computer-assisted proof of one-cell snaking and lattice trapping for a nonlinear square lattice
papers.abstract: We establish a computer-assisted proof of lattice trapping in an infinite nonlinear square lattice with interaction potential $\phi(t)=(1-e^{-3t^2})/6$ and an antiplane crack far field $K\sqrt{r}\sin(\theta/2)$. We construct a connected branch of equilibria whose single-cell segment contains exactly two nondegenerate quadratic folds, with a stability sequence of stable, Morse index one, and stable in the full energy space. The fold loads satisfy $0.45897<K_-<0.45923$ and $0.46219<K_+<0.46242$, establishing a strictly positive lattice-trapping width $K_+-K_->0.00296$. A uniqueness argument establishes exact translation closure and smooth continuation across lattice cells. The proof combines renormalized energy, Schur complement estimates, analytic infinite-tail bounds, interval arithmetic, and exact integer positivity certificates. All finite input data, verification programs, and recorded certificate outputs are provided in the accompanying certificate archive.

authors.name: Jiangchao Qian
authors.institution: East China University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Code availability is not enough: schemas for documenting and extending data analysis
papers.abstract: A data analysis involves a sequence of decisions, from data cleaning to model specification, each of which can affect the reported result. Reproducing that result is not the same as understanding the sequence of decisions that produced it and the reasons for each: the code mixes those decisions with implementation details, while the manuscript states the major decisions and their rationale but scatters them across its sections and often leaves out the minor ones. A reader may then ask how the result would change under a different decision: the question itself is easy to pose, but implementing it is often non-trivial in practice. In this work, we propose a schema that represents a data analysis as a collection of decisions in natural language, from which large language models (LLMs) can generate and validate analysis scripts directly. This workflow can also expand a single analysis into a full multiverse of alternatives, specified in an alternative file, ready for comparison. We demonstrate the proposed workflow in two applications. In the first, we construct a schema for a published regression analysis of heaped smoking data and show that it reproduces the reported estimates, and that a reviewer-suggested alternative can be specified through the alternative file and turned into code automatically. In the second, where no schema is provided, we show how the workflow serves instead as a reproducibility check, applied to the many-analysts football study. As an intermediate representation between the manuscript and code scripts, our schema gives a self-contained account of an analysis and makes it extensible from a reader's perspective.

authors.name: H. Sherry Zhang
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.name: Roger D. Peng
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Impact of the Performance of Autonomy and Communication Subsystems on the Level-of-Safety of Partially Autonomous Machine Systems
papers.abstract: The level-of-safety of a partially autonomous machine system depends on two subsystems: the autonomy subsystem that manages the system between human interventions; and the communication subsystem that enables those interventions. These subsystems are typically evaluated independently. We model the level-of-safety analytically as a function of their joint performance. Three parameters characterize the autonomy subsystem: the Mean Time Between Interventions (MTBI); the urgency $\mathcal{U}$ or mean time within which an intervention must be completed to avoid failure; and the complexity $\mathcal{C}$ or mean time to understand, decide on and execute it. Two characterize the communication subsystem: its availability $P_A$ and its latency $\varepsilon$. A dimensionless criticality ratio $\rho=(\mathcal{C}+\varepsilon)/\mathcal{U}$ prescribes the shape of the Pareto tradeoff between the MTBI and $P_A$ at a constant level-of-safety. At $\rho=0.01$, a perfect link lowers the required MTBI by two orders of magnitude. At $\rho=1$, it only halves it. Under exponential timing assumptions the model is in closed form, and compliance with a safety budget can be stated at a chosen assurance level. We illustrate it for remotely piloted aircraft with assumed parameter values and propose a simulation procedure to estimate them.

authors.name: Yutian Pang
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.name: John-Paul Clarke
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Adaptive Blockwise Tensor Trains for Stochastic Finite-Volume Methods with Uncertain Geometry
papers.abstract: Stochastic finite-volume (SFV) methods extend conservative, shock-capturing discretizations to hyperbolic systems with uncertain inputs by partitioning the parameter domain into finite-volume cells. However, their memory and computational cost grow exponentially with the number of uncertain parameters. Tensor-train (TT) formats can remove this exponential dependence, provided the ranks of the discrete solution remain small throughout the simulation. This requirement is frequently violated when the uncertainty is geometric. Mapping each realization onto a common reference domain introduces parameter-dependent metric factors, so that shocks and contacts propagate at different reference speeds and come to occupy different cells across realizations. The resulting rank growth is spatially localized - a structure that neither a single global TT nor a separate TT for each physical cell is able to exploit. We propose an adaptive blockwise TT representation in which the SFV solution is partitioned along its physical mode into contiguous blocks, each stored as an independent TT for every conserved variable. Blocks are split near discontinuities and in regions of large variance or rank, and merged where the solution is smooth. The mesh itself is never changed; only the grouping of cells into trains adapts. We embed this representation in a TT-based SFV solver combining WENO3 reconstruction in the physical and stochastic directions, positivity-preserving limiters, and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta time integration, with nonlinear steps evaluated via cross approximation. A mean-conservative rounding that adds no rank, together with single-valued interface fluxes, conserves the parameter-mean mass and energy to round-off for any partition. The approach is demonstrated on a Sod shock-tube problem with uncertain wall positions.

papers.title: Supercritical Nodal Solutions on Annuli: Symmetry Breaking and Multiplicity
papers.abstract: We establish existence and multiplicity results for nonradial sign-changing solutions of the Dirichlet problem $-\Delta u=a(|x|)|u|^{p-2}u$ on annuli in $\mathbb R^N$, where $N\geq4$, $a$ is a positive radial coefficient, and $p$ may exceed the Sobolev critical exponent. For each decomposition $N=m+n$, with $m\geq n\geq2$, we minimize the energy on a nodal Nehari set within a signed cone of angularly nondecreasing, $O(m)\times O(n)$-invariant functions. Whenever $2<p<2(m+1)/(m-1)$, the minimum is attained, and every minimizer is a classical solution with exactly two nodal domains. A cone-preserving auxiliary Dirichlet operator and a two-parameter energy deformation recover the full equation from the constrained minimization. We prove that these minimizers are nonradial if $(p-2)\beta_\Omega>2N$, where $\beta_\Omega$ is the optimal Dirichlet Hardy constant associated with the weight $|x|^{-2}$. Under a common admissible exponent range satisfying this condition, different orthogonal decompositions yield distinct solution pairs $\{\pm u\}$. An explicit lower bound for $\beta_\Omega$ provides supercritical regimes on sufficiently thin annuli in which the nonradiality and multiplicity results apply.

papers.title: Geometry and Analysis of Spinor Valued Forms
papers.abstract: We study spinor valued differential forms, that is, sections of the bundles $\mathcal{S}_p=\mathcal{S}\otimes\Lambda_p\otimes L$ of spinor valued $p$-forms twisted by a $U(1)$ line bundle $L$, on compact even-dimensional Riemannian spin (or $\mathrm{Spin}^\mathbb{C}$) manifolds. We develop the algebra of spinor valued forms: the chirality, grading and duality involutions, the bilinear tensors built from spinor valued forms and the Fierz-type identities they satisfy, and the action of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ generated by Clifford multiplication and contraction, which we use to decompose the space of spinor valued forms into irreducible components and to construct an adapted orthonormal basis. We introduce the twisted exterior derivative and coderivative, the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators and, more generally, the natural first-order operators on spinor valued forms, as well as the twisted Hodge and signature operators, and derive their conformal transformation laws. We obtain the Weitzenb\"ock formulas for the twisted de Rham and Dirac Laplacians, express the curvature terms through the Weyl tensor, the Ricci tensor, the curvature of $L$ and the bilinear tensors of the spinor valued forms, and derive vanishing theorems, heat trace invariants and index formulas. Finally, in four dimensions we use these Weitzenb\"ock formulas to construct non-negative functionals whose absolute minima define two generalizations of the Seiberg--Witten monopole equations to right spinor valued $p$-forms, one based on the Dirac operator and one on the twisted de Rham Laplacian, and discuss the resulting integrability conditions.

authors.name: Ivan G. Avramidi
authors.institution: New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology

papers.title: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Information Hiding in Semantic Communication
papers.abstract: Semantic communication shifts the transmission goal from the accurate recovery of syntactic symbols to the reliable conveyance of semantic content, yet a systematic information-theoretic characterization of information hiding at the semantic layer is still missing. Building on the semantic information theory of Niu-Zhang and the classical information hiding theory of Moulin-O'Sullivan, this paper establishes an information-theoretic framework for information hiding under semantic communication. The classical hiding model is extended to a two-layer structure (semantic host, syntactic host, syntactic composite signal, syntactic received, semantic received) bridged by synonymous mappings f_s, f_x and the inverse mapping f_y^{-1}, subject to four distortion constraints: syntactic transparency, semantic fidelity, syntactic perturbation, and semantic destruction. The capacity is cast as a Stackelberg game with the hider moving first and the payoff J(Q,A) = I(U~; Y~ | K) - I(U~; S~ | K), yielding the single-letter maximin C^s = max_Q min_A J(Q,A), whose achievability and converse follow from random coding and joint typicality decoding. Relative to the classical capacity, comparison payoffs built from the up/down semantic mutual information give the endpoint sandwich C^s_end(0,1) <= C^s <= C^s_end(1,0) with the classical value C in the same interval, while closing semantic tolerance yields C^s_no-tol <= C_cl under a fair comparison. These results clarify that semantic hiding is not unconditionally superior to classical hiding. Binary, ternary, and Gaussian examples confirm the degeneration under one-to-one mappings and the capacity loss under coarsening.

papers.title: Carrying Feature Ablations Across Sparse Autoencoder Seeds
papers.abstract: A vision encoder turns an image into one vector per patch, refined layer by layer. A sparse autoencoder (SAE) writes each vector of one layer as a sum of learned directions, most with a coefficient of zero. Researchers call each direction a feature and edit the encoder by removing one feature. An SAE trained from another random seed learns different features. Earlier work matches the two SAEs' features one to one by how closely their directions agree. Matched features can point alike yet respond to different image parts, so removing them may change the encoder differently. We remove a feature and, separately, its match, then compare the changes in the encoder's output on the same held out images. When the second change nearly reproduces the first, we say the removal carries across seeds. A setting fixes a DINOv2 or SigLIP layer and its SAE feature count. At our tolerance, the removal carries for 12% to 70% of matched pairs across three settings. The share is 0% in two controls: an SAE whose directions stay random and, post hoc, matches shuffled among trained features. Post hoc, predicting which removals carry is more accurate with layer contributions than with directions. Some incorrect predictions remain. One persists on independent images. So pairs can be screened at the layer. Measuring the output detects errors this screen misses.

authors.name: Karl Li
authors.institution: The University of Texas at San Antonio Health Science Center

papers.title: A Hard Background Pairing Transfers across Classifiers and Images
papers.abstract: An image classifier names the object in an image, and its accuracy is the share of images named correctly. A classifier that names a car on a road may miss the same car pasted onto clouds. Composite benchmarks measure such failures by pasting objects cut from photographs onto backgrounds from other photographs. A pairing puts every object label on a different background label, such as truck on sea. The pairing on which some classifiers do worst, their hardest pairing, makes a strict test, but may be hard only for them or only on the photographs used to choose it. We show that the hardest pairing of some classifiers stays hard for others and on new photographs. We split 40 ImageNet classifiers into halves balanced by reported ImageNet accuracy. One half picks its hardest pairing of 8 object and 8 background labels from Common Objects in Context (COCO). The other half, held out of the choice, compares that pairing with random pairings of the same objects and backgrounds. For the 14 held-out classifiers with little net accuracy change after pasting objects back onto their own backgrounds, mean accuracy on composites from new photographs falls from 50.3% over random pairings to 43.7% on the hardest pairing, 6.6 percentage points lower. A benchmark using these composites can compare this pool's held-out classifiers on the fixed and random pairings.

authors.name: Karl Li
authors.institution: The University of Texas at San Antonio Health Science Center

papers.title: Distribution of the ratio of the two smallest eigenphases of the Jacobi unitary ensemble
papers.abstract: We compute the joint distribution of the two smallest eigenvalues of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and the distribution of their ratio. We use a framework for calculating Janossy densities based on the Tracy-Widom system of ordinary differential equations. For the cases studied here, the leading finite-N correction to the ratio distribution, relative to its universal Bessel-kernel limit, is O(N^{-4}). This behaviour reflects a nontrivial cancellation of lower-order corrections present in the Jacobi kernel. Eigenphase ratios may thus reveal subtle finite-size effects in quantum-chaotic systems with particle-hole or chiral symmetry. As an exploratory arithmetic application, we compare the ratio distribution for the two lowest zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with the hard-edge limit for Sp(N). The data indicate that the N_{eff}^{-1} term vanishes, leaving an O(N_{eff}^{-2}) correction.

papers.title: Nested Spherical Designs of Optimal Order
papers.abstract: Zheng and Zhuang [22] showed that a spherical $t_1$-design $Y$ with $|Y|=M\sim t_1^d$ points on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$ can be extended to a spherical $t$-design by adding points, with a total of order $t^{2d+1}$, and asked whether the optimal order $t^d$ is attainable. We keep their construction and improve the estimate of the pairing of the given points against polynomials of unit $L^1$-gradient norm. We prove that, if the given spherical $t_1$-design is upper regular at scale $t_1$ (in particular if it is well-separated; such a design exists by Bondarenko, Radchenko and Viazovska [6]), then for $d\ge2$, every $N\ge C(d,K)\,t^d$ suffices to admit a point set $X$ with $|X|=N$, for all $t_1<t$, such that the multiset union $X\uplus Y$ is a spherical $t$-design; in particular $|X\uplus Y|\le C(d,K)\,t^d$. The proof combines the design property, which removes the low frequencies exactly, with an $L^1$ Jackson-type estimate and a sampling inequality applied on dyadic frequency blocks. Upper regularity turns out to be automatic for nested spherical designs of optimal order; that is, every spherical $t_1$-design with $M\le C_M t_1^d$ points extends to a spherical $t$-design with $N+M\le C(d)\,C_M\,t^d$ (with $C_M\ge1$), uniformly in $t_1<t$, without any separation hypothesis. Some control of local multiplicity is necessary for an extension of optimal order. We also show that the estimate of the pairing functional cannot be improved within this method; that is, for every point set of at most $c\,t^d$ points it is at least of order $t^{d-1}$, and for upper regular designs it is of exactly this order. Finally, we treat finite chains of nested spherical designs, and on the circle we remove a logarithmic factor from the general estimate.

papers.title: Selecting $2 \times 2$ submatrices with optimally bounded inverses
papers.abstract: For a matrix $U \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ ($n \ge k$) with orthonormal columns, the Goreinov--Tyrtyshnikov--Zamarashkin (GTZ) conjecture asserts that there exists a $k \times k$ submatrix $U_I$ with $\|U_I^{-1}\|_2 \le \sqrt{n}$. The conjecture remains open for $3 \le k \le n - 3$. The existence of such a submatrix in the case $k = 2$ was proved for $n=4$ by Nesterenko (2023) and recently for general $n$ by Sengupta and Pautov (2026). In this paper, we give a short, elementary, constructive proof of a weighted strengthening of this result, which yields a single-pass streaming algorithm that selects a row pair satisfying the $\sqrt{n}$ bound in $\mathcal O(n)$ operations and $\mathcal O(1)$ auxiliary memory. We further give an explicit matrix representation of all equality cases for $k = 2$ characterized by Nesterenko (2026) and use it to construct a single matrix family on which standard selection strategies (including global and local maximum-volume selection, Bischof--Stewart pivoted QR, column-pivoted QR, and LU with partial pivoting) simultaneously fail to attain the $\sqrt{n}$ bound.

papers.title: Don't Waste the Population: Post-Anneal Refinement for Combinatorial Optimization
papers.abstract: Parallel annealers generate diverse candidate solutions; yet, conventional post-processing typically refines only the best, leaving much of the population's potential untapped. We introduce Iterative Path-Relinking Polish (I-PRP), a deterministic, training-free method that exploits this diversity to discover better solutions without modifying the underlying annealing process. I-PRP selects promising candidates, explores cost-guided paths between locally optimized solutions, and refines intermediate states to uncover better local minima. Newly discovered improvements are iteratively incorporated into the population, enabling further exploration. We theoretically guarantee that I-PRP never degrades solution quality relative to conventional single-candidate polishing on the same population and converges in finitely many iterations. Experiments across challenging combinatorial optimization benchmarks, including MaxCut, MaxClique, and graph coloring, demonstrate substantial improvements in several instances. Paired evaluations confirm non-degradation, while matched-runtime comparisons show that exploiting existing population diversity can outperform additional annealing. These results establish I-PRP as an effective and reliable refinement strategy for parallel annealing.

papers.title: JHealthBench-L: Clinician-Reviewed Localization of HealthBench for Rubric-Based Medical LLM Evaluation in Japan
papers.abstract: Rubric-based benchmarks such as HealthBench evaluate large language models (LLMs) on open-ended health consultations using case-specific physician criteria, many of which presuppose the healthcare institutions, medications, and care pathways of their source region. Under machine translation alone, these regional assumptions remain in the rubric, leaving responses appropriate in Japan uncredited or falsely penalized under foreign clinical rules. To adapt established clinical evaluation perspectives to Japan without authoring rubrics from scratch, we construct JHealthBench-L (79 patient-facing consultations, 1,022 criteria) through source-cited LLM drafting, single-specialist selection and revision, independent dual-physician review, and meta-review. Specialists rewrote only 4.4% of criteria from scratch, and independent reviewers approved 93.6% of Stage-2 criteria without issue. Comparing JHealthBench-L with a machine-translated baseline across 18 LLMs reveals that translation-only evaluation preserves coarse model rankings ($\tau = 0.817$, mean shift +0.027) yet flips verdicts on 17.7% of modified criteria (vs. 7.3% re-grading noise) and reduces false penalties on Japan-adapted negative criteria by 7.1 percentage points, masking item-level clinical mismeasurement behind stable leaderboards. Axis-level and paired analyses further show that context awareness and Japan-specific clinical criteria remain primary bottlenecks, whereas Japanese continual pretraining and reasoning post-training substantially improve locally grounded performance. Datasets, physician revision logs, and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/horshohei/JHealthBench-L.

papers.title: What Makes a Gavagai? Learning Visual Concepts from One Positive and Few Negatives
papers.abstract: Humans can recognize novel concepts from only a few observations by identifying defining visual attributes and eliminating alternative interpretations. However, a single observation is consistent with multiple possible concepts, and accurate visual perception alone is insufficient to determine the intended interpretation. Negative evidence can reduce this ambiguity by eliminating competing hypotheses. Inspired by Quine's gavagai problem, we introduce the Gavagai Benchmark to evaluate whether vision-language models can identify the attributes defining a novel concept from positive and negative examples. The benchmark consists of synthetic images depicting novel combinations of visual attributes and real images of newly described species. Using these datasets, we examine how models use negative examples to identify novel concepts and analyze the respective roles of visual perception and reasoning. Several models struggle even when correct attributes are provided, while others show large gaps when ground-truth attributes are replaced with model predictions. These diagnostic comparisons highlight challenges in both attribute perception and inference from limited evidence.

papers.title: Investigation of generalization to unseen audio generation models in audio--text semantic-alignment score prediction
papers.abstract: Text-to-audio generation (TTA) requires reliable evaluation of semantic alignment between generated audio and input text. Existing learning-based alignment-score prediction models have been evaluated only on audio generated by models included in the training data, leaving their generalization to unseen generation models unexplored. In this paper, we investigate the generalization of audio--text semantic-alignment score prediction models to unseen TTA models and introduce adversarial training using a generation-model classifier with a gradient reversal layer (GRL). Experimental results show that pretrained audio encoders capture generation-model-specific characteristics and that alignment-score prediction performance degrades on audio generated by unseen TTA models. Applying the GRL improves prediction performance in some settings, although its effectiveness in suppressing generation-model-specific information is limited.

papers.title: Quantum-centric assessment of saturated ferromagnetism beyond the flat-band limit
papers.abstract: Saturated ferromagnetism has been proven for every on-site repulsion $U > 0$ in Hubbard models with a flat lowest band, and the interaction required for it grows with the band width $W$ when the band becomes dispersive. We study the dispersive case at quarter filling by quantum-selected configuration interaction and sample-based quantum diagonalization with IBM Quantum's Heron processors, focusing on the quantized square of the total spin of the computed states. We treat a sawtooth chain of 16 unit cells on 64 qubits, whose full configuration space of $1.1\times 10^{14}$ determinants exceeds that of one of the largest full configuration interaction calculations, and obtain the stability diagram of saturated ferromagnetism on the decorated square lattice in the plane of $U$ and $W$. For the chain, a subspace of only $3\times 10^{-5}$ of the full configuration space gives a state with more than $97\%$ of its weight in the sector of maximal spin. For the decorated square lattice of $4\times 3$ unit cells on 48 qubits, the computed states in subspaces of less than $1\%$ of the full configuration space switch from low-spin states to nearly fully polarized states at $U \simeq 2W$. The calculations also give a rigorous lower bound of $1.9W$ on the critical interaction of the $4\times 3$ lattice.

papers.title: The positive-sphere variant of Tingley's problem for $C^1([0,1])$
papers.abstract: Let $C^1([0,1])$ be endowed with the norm $\|f\|=\|f\|_\infty+\|f'\|_\infty$, and let $S(C^1([0,1]))^+$ be the part of its unit sphere consisting of nonnegative, nondecreasing functions. We prove that every surjective isometry of $S(C^1([0,1]))^+$ is the identity and has a unique surjective real-linear isometric extension to $C^1([0,1])$.

papers.title: Geary-type expectation identities for Mardia's sample skewness and kurtosis
papers.abstract: Under multivariate normality, we establish exact Geary-type expectation identities for Mardia's sample skewness and kurtosis. A polar decomposition of the centered Gaussian data matrix shows that each of these statistics is independent of the sample covariance matrix. This independence allows the moments of each statistic to be expressed as ratios of expectations involving polynomial numerators and powers of the determinant of the sample covariance matrix. The identities hold in arbitrary dimension $p$. To illustrate their use, we give exact expressions for the variance of Mardia's sample skewness and the third central moment of Mardia's sample kurtosis for $p=2$ and $p=3$. As an application of the exact variance formulas, we construct a moment-matched chi-square approximation to the null distribution of Mardia's sample skewness and compare its performance with Mardia's classical and mean-corrected approximations.

papers.title: Proof of a cardinality conjecture for the correction terms in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture due to Kato and Sagaki (arXiv:2604.04476) concerning the cardinality of sets of directed paths in the quantum Bruhat graph that occur in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom for the full flag manifolds in the quasi-minuscule case. We prove that the cadinality is equal to one or even, and its signed sum vanishes in the latter case. Consequently, the cancellation-free divisor axiom obtained by Kato and Sagaki under this conjecture holds unconditionally. The proof uses Schremmer's results on affine Bruhat order and Demazure products, together with a theorem that we prove for arbitrary Coxeter groups.

papers.title: Tunable Terahertz Bandpass Filter based on the Photonic Emulation of a 2DEG Interferometer through the Geometric Phase of Light
papers.abstract: Terahertz frequencies are expected to become a key player in next-generation wireless communications. For this transition to occur seamlessly, tunable bandpass filters for channel selection are essential. However, conventional Fabry-P\'erot cavity-based bandpass filters face inherent limitations. Specifically, their tunability is restricted by physical constraints, such as the maximum achievable mirror separation. In this work, drawing inspiration from electronic interferometers, we demonstrate a continuously tunable bandpass filter operating near 0.3 THz by exploiting the geometric phase of light, the Pancharatnam-Berry phase. Our device incorporates intracavity waveplates for polarization control and is described by a mathematical expression analogous to that of the electronic interferometer governed by the Aharonov-Bohm phase, thereby realizing a photonic analogue. Using custom-designed subwavelength waveplates and cavity mirrors, we achieve a finesse of $\mathcal{F}\approx17$, a quality factor of $Q\approx1.5\times10^{3}$, and a resonance linewidth of $\Delta f_{\mathrm{FWHM}}\approx 200$ MHz. Beyond terahertz communication technology, this system is expected to find applications in fields requiring high frequency resolution, such as spectroscopy.

papers.title: BridgeSRDA: Efficient Probabilistic Super-Resolution Data Assimilation with Forecast-Informed Stochastic Interpolants
papers.abstract: High-resolution ensemble data assimilation is computationally demanding because it requires repeated forecasts and updates of many flow states. We introduce BridgeSRDA, a probabilistic super-resolution data assimilation framework that combines low-resolution numerical forecasts with sparse, noisy observations to generate high-resolution analysis windows. A neural network learns forecast-informed stochastic transport, which is sampled to produce an ensemble of reconstructions. Each current analysis initializes the next low-resolution forecast, while the same window provides retrospective reconstructions and short-range nowcasts. We evaluate BridgeSRDA over ten independently initialized trajectories of a three-dimensional quasi-geostrophic flow in a narrow-jet regime different from training. At the training observation spacing, BridgeSRDA approaches the mean and structural reconstruction accuracy of a high-resolution local ensemble transform Kalman filter and reduces the mean absolute error ratio by approximately 32.5% relative to deterministic four-dimensional SRDA. With 30 ensemble members, BridgeSRDA requires approximately 17 s per analysis, compared with 31 s for the filter under the recorded conditions. Ten members reduce the cost to approximately 6.6 s with little change in mean accuracy, though fine-scale accuracy and interval coverage are affected. BridgeSRDA achieves a competitive continuous ranked probability score, but its ensembles are underdispersed: nominal 90% intervals contain approximately 62% of reference values. Boundary spread artifacts and reduced skill under sparser observations also warrant attention. These results demonstrate the potential of forecast-informed stochastic transport for probabilistic data assimilation, while highlighting the need to improve uncertainty calibration and robustness to changing observation networks.

authors.name: Yuki Yasuda
authors.institution: Earthquake Research Institute, University of Tokyo

papers.title: Joint Estimation of Abilities and Item Parameters for Large Language Models Using Probability and Binary Responses: A Fractional-Response IRT Framework
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) evaluations provide two response types: probabilities assigned to correct answers and binary indicators of correctness. Restricting evaluation to one type narrows the range of available models or discards probability information. We propose a method to integrate both types through a common two-parameter logistic item response model and fractional-response quasi-maximum likelihood estimation. The framework includes binary-only models in common-scale evaluation without discarding available probabilityinformation; broader measurement coverage does not by itself ensure greater precision or measurement equivalence. Simulations evaluate statistical efficiency when both response types have the same expected value. Moreover, adding probability respondents improves item calibration more efficiently than adding binary respondents. However, adding noisier binary responses to an already precise probability sample can increase estimation error under equal observation weights. An application to Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) combines probability response data from the Open LLM Leaderboard with binary response data from Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM) and reveals model-family response patterns, differences in item characteristics, and systematic ability shifts between evaluation protocols. The proposed framework extends common-scale IRT evaluation to models with different response formats while highlighting the roles of observation variability and evaluation-protocol comparability in statistical efficiency and interpretation.

papers.title: Semiorthogonal decompositions of limit categories for symmetric stacks
papers.abstract:
In our earlier work with Tudor Padurariu, we introduced the notion of limit categories for derived stacks with self-dual cotangent complexes and used them to formulate the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture. In this paper, we generalize the notion of limit categories to a broader class of derived stacks, which we call symmetric stacks.
  One of the motivations for this generalization is to formulate Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type correspondences for a broader class of moduli stacks. We establish several fundamental properties of limit categories for symmetric stacks, including compact generation, the existence of semiorthogonal decompositions, functoriality, and a Kunneth formula.
  In a companion paper, we apply the results of this paper to formulate a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for moduli stacks of sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anticanonical divisors.

papers.title: The Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for smooth surfaces
papers.abstract:
Using a general theory of limit categories for symmetric stacks, we construct their semiorthogonal decompositions for moduli stacks of pure one-dimensional coherent sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anti-canonical divisors. The components of these semiorthogonal decompositions are quasi-BPS categories associated with the corresponding local Calabi--Yau threefolds.
  By comparing these semiorthogonal decompositions with those of dg-categories of coherent sheaves on moduli stacks of semistable sheaves, we propose a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for surfaces, generalizing the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture for $\GL_r$-Higgs bundles. Our conjecture includes a correspondence for Higgs bundles twisted by sufficiently ample line bundles on curves.
  We discuss examples and construct Hecke actions on limit categories and, under certain conditions, on quasi-BPS categories. For symplectic surfaces, these actions are expected to provide a categorical lift of the corresponding Hecke operators on BPS cohomology constructed by Davison--Hennecart--Kinjo--Schiffmann--Vasserot.

papers.title: ChemoMAE: Self-Supervised Spectral Representation Learning Reveals Chemical Heterogeneity in Historical Wood
papers.abstract: In historical timber buildings, multiple environmental factors act over centuries on wood whose chemical composition varies across anatomical regions, producing complex patterns of degradation. Understanding how timber members degrade is important for the effective conservation and restoration of historical buildings, yet the mechanisms underlying these patterns remain unclear. To investigate these mechanisms, we used self-supervised learning to establish a common basis for comparing specimens from timber members that differ in wood species and service history. We examined transverse sections of 49 wood specimens from several historical buildings in Japan using near-infrared hyperspectral imaging. ChemoMAE, a self-supervised Transformer, learns pixelwise spectral representations through masked denoising that exploits multicollinearity among spectral variables. Clustering these representations yields spatial maps without predefined chemical-state categories. Because anatomy and degradation can produce spatially continuous regions, we formulated Local Label Agreement (LLA) to quantify agreement among labels assigned to neighboring pixels. Using spectra alone, ChemoMAE yielded higher mean LLA than baseline methods on validation specimens. We then trained ChemoMAE anew and fitted cluster centers across all specimens. Spatial structures consistent with wood anatomy and the expected effects of surface exposure emerged in the resulting maps. By cross-referencing regional spectra and spatial distributions across specimens in light of wood anatomy, service histories, and prior studies, we proposed models of internal and surface degradation as mechanistic hypotheses. This exploratory AI for Science framework gives researchers a basis for linking latent patterns learned through self-supervision with domain knowledge when investigating how material states form.

papers.title: RecField: Embedding Recommendations into Spatial Movie Organization as Affordances for Serendipitous Encounters
papers.abstract: Research on serendipity-oriented recommender systems has focused on algorithms that recommend unexpected yet useful items. However, serendipity is increasingly viewed as a user experience shaped by both algorithmic outputs and system features. This study positions recommendations not as the primary goal users pursue but as an environmental affordance that creates opportunities for discovery during other activities. We propose RecField, a spatial movie organization interface where users freely arrange movies into collection zones. For each collection, RecField provides attribute-based recommendation lists labeled according to their recommendation perspectives. A between-subjects experiment ($N$ = 57) examined the effects of recommendations on discoveries made during a foreground task of creating and organizing personal movie profiles. Although recommendations did not significantly affect environment-level perceived serendipity, ratings of encounter-related aspects tended to be higher, with small effect sizes. At the individual-movie level, favorites in the recommendation condition received significantly higher ratings for stimulating the desire to watch and broadening preferences, but not for novelty or unexpectedness. Notably, only 14\% of evaluated favorites in the recommendation condition were added directly from recommendation lists. Differences in ratings showed similar effect sizes even when the analysis was restricted to favorites added through other routes. These findings suggest that embedded recommendations can contribute to serendipitous experiences both directly through item acceptance and indirectly by prompting users' own exploration and re-evaluation. They also highlight the value of evaluating serendipity at both the environment and item levels and the limitations of relying solely on direct recommendation acceptance rates.

papers.title: Integration of Vision-Language-Action Control for Autonomous Forklift Unloading with Limited Real-World Data
papers.abstract: Forklifts play a critical role in warehousing and distribution, but existing automation systems remain limited in handling complex tasks that require sequential decision-making. Recently, vision--language--action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising approach for multi-step decision-making by directly generating control actions from visual observations and language prompts. Although VLA-based control has been extensively researched for manipulators, to the best of our knowledge, its application to forklifts remains unexplored. Therefore, this study demonstrates the integration of VLA control for an autonomous forklift unloading task with limited real-world data. Moreover, training VLA models typically requires large-scale datasets. As there is currently no public dataset for forklift operations, we use a VLA model pretrained primarily on robotic manipulator data and construct a training dataset via simulation, which can be scaled up at low cost. We then adapt the pretrained VLA model to forklift control using 9.38 h of simulation data and 0.8 h of real-world demonstrations, with the latter accounting for approximately 8% of the collected forklift data by duration. The integrated system was validated through 72 real-world trials across four model variants. The results show that the proposed system can accomplish an unloading task even with limited real-world data.

authors.name: Koshi Oishi
authors.institution: Toyota Central Research and Development Laboratories (Japan)

papers.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of constructing knowledge bases for applications based on large language models, in which the structure of a knowledge base determines how an application can retrieve and connect the information needed to answer a question. We study Self-Structuring Learning, a setting in which questions and expected answers guide the construction of a persistent knowledge base whose editable structure can be a graph schema or the organization of linked knowledge documents. We propose Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent, which diagnoses discrepancies between expected answers and responses obtained through the current knowledge base. At each round, the method proposes a structural edit, rebuilds the knowledge base, and adopts the edit when the learning loss decreases. The retained structure is evaluated on other questions about the same sources. By randomizing over candidate edits, we express the loss change of an edit as a derivative with respect to the probability of selecting it, and we evaluate joint edits as single candidates because their changes interact. Schema Descent instantiates the method for graph schemas. In experiments on large documents, each a bundle of research papers, the updated knowledge cards and graph schemas obtain higher mean Answer F1 on held-out generated questions than their initial structures, with schema gains in every document. On human questions, mean F1 rises for schemas and falls for cards: the updated structures serve the kind of question they were learned from.

papers.title: On Zappa--Sz\'ep products of multiplicative racks
papers.abstract: We study Zappa--Sz\'ep products of multiplicative racks, namely monoids equipped with compatible rack operations. We characterize multiplicative rack structures on Zappa--Sz\'ep products of monoids and prove that every exact factorization of multiplicative racks induces a canonical exact factorization of their universal groups. We also establish exact factorizations of groups of units and cancellative quotients, show that reduction modulo units yields a direct product, and obtain consequences for Ore localization. We then generalize Bianchi's construction using augmentations from partially multiplicative racks into arbitrary multiplicative racks and establish a reconstruction theorem for multiplicative racks with suitable unital ideals. We investigate the interaction between unital ideals and exact factorizations, and characterize Zappa--Sz\'ep factorizations of generalized Bianchi-type multiplicative racks. Finally, we use a layered central-quotient construction to obtain finite and infinite non-cancellative multiplicative quandles with non-group factors and nontrivial Zappa--Sz\'ep actions, all directly indecomposable as monoids.

papers.title: Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings, with applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings and give applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers. We realize rational double points of ADE over $W(k)$ as invariant subrings $A^G$, where $A$ is a ramified two-dimensional complete regular local ring and $G$ is a finite linearly reductive subgroup scheme of $\mathrm{SL}_{2,W(k)}$. We also prove a general theorem on the existence of Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings: if a flat affine group scheme $G$ over $W(k)$ admits a functorial Reynolds operator and a relative Frobenius lift, then any formal power series ring equipped with a linear action of $G$ admits a Frobenius lift that restricts to a Frobenius lift on the invariant subring. Building on these results, we construct perfectoid towers arising from rational double points in mixed characteristic. We identify their tilts with the perfect towers arising from rational double points in positive characteristic of the same ADE type.

authors.name: Kazuki Hayashi
authors.institution: Nagoya City University East Medical Center

papers.title: Separation formulas for non-normalized generalized cluster algebras
papers.abstract: We study a class of not necessarily normalized generalized cluster patterns which are uniquely determined by the initial seed and mutations. For such generalized cluster patterns, we provide the separation formulas for cluster variables and coefficients.

affiliations.raw: Graduate School of Mathematics, Nagoya University, Chikusa-ku, Nagoya, 464-8604, Japan

papers.intro:
Cluster algebras are a class of algebras introduced by Fomin and Zelevinsky [FZ02]. Subsequently, Chekhov and Shapiro [CS14] introduced generalized cluster algebras, which are a natural generalization of ordinary cluster algebras, by extending the exchange relations from a binomial to a polynomial. Moreover, it is known that fundamental properties established in ordinary cluster algebras such as the Laurent phenomenon, the finite type classification [CS14], the separation formulas [Nak15, NR16], and the Laurent positivity [Mou24, BLM25a, BLM25b] hold in generalized cluster algebras. The greedy basis of a rank 2 cluster algebra is extended to a rank 2 generalized cluster algebra [Rup15]. The structure of generalized cluster algebras appears in various contexts, such as exact WKB analysis [IN16], the Drinfeld double of G​LnGL_{n} [GSV18, GSV22a, GSV22b], and the Badlands in (ordinary) cluster scattering diagrams of acyclic affine type [RS26a, RS26b]. More recently, Ramos and Whiting [RW25] showed that a generalized cluster algebra of geometric type is isomorphic to a subquotient of an ordinary cluster algebra, and Akagi and Nakanishi [AN26] extended this result to generalized cluster algebras with arbitrary coefficients.

The separation formulas introduced in [FZ07] are important for ordinary cluster algebras and their underlying ordinary cluster patterns. In particular, the CC-, GG-matrices, and the FF-polynomials appearing in these formulas are major objects for understanding the structure of cluster algebras. For instance, the periodicity of cluster variables coincides with that of GG-matrices [Nak21]. Nakanishi and Rupel established the separation formulas for generalized cluster patterns [Nak15, NR16]. However, the above separation formulas only hold for normalized (ordinary or generalized) cluster patterns, where the normalization condition is satisfied by their coefficients. On the other hand, non-normalized (ordinary or generalized) cluster algebras are also important objects to study (e.g., [FT18, MOT26] for ordinary cluster algebras, [GSV18, GSV22a, GSV22b] for generalized ones).

On the other hand, non-normalized (ordinary or generalized) cluster algebras are also important objects to study (e.g., [FT18, MOT26] for ordinary cluster algebras, [GSV18, GSV22a, GSV22b] for generalized ones).

In this paper, as the main results, we extend the separation formulas for normalized (ordinary or generalized) cluster patterns to non-normalized ones (Theorems 2.11 and 4.21). For this purpose, we need to introduce several new notions and formulations. Firstly, in contrast to the normalized (ordinary or generalized) cluster patterns, non-normalized (ordinary or generalized) cluster patterns are not uniquely determined by their initial seed and the mutations. Therefore, we first extend the usual normalization condition to the 𝒫\mathcal{P}-normalization condition (Definitions 2.6 and 3.5). Then, an (ordinary or generalized) cluster pattern satisfying this condition, which we call a 𝒫\mathcal{P}-normalized (ordinary or generalized) cluster pattern, is uniquely determined by their initial seed and the mutations and the separation formulations are available. Secondly, for generalized cluster patterns, we introduce yy-variables whose formulation is different from that in [Nak15, NR16]. This construction allows us to define yy-variables without assuming the existence of their roots in [Nak15, NR16], as detailed in Section 5.3. Finally, in the resulting separation formula of a cluster variable, the numerator is given by the FF-polynomials as usual, while the denominator is given by a new function (a JJ-function), which is no longer a polynomial.

Then, an (ordinary or generalized) cluster pattern satisfying this condition, which we call a 𝒫\mathcal{P}-normalized (ordinary or generalized) cluster pattern, is uniquely determined by their initial seed and the mutations and the separation formulations are available. Secondly, for generalized cluster patterns, we introduce yy-variables whose formulation is different from that in [Nak15, NR16]. This construction allows us to define yy-variables without assuming the existence of their roots in [Nak15, NR16], as detailed in Section 5.3. Finally, in the resulting separation formula of a cluster variable, the numerator is given by the FF-polynomials as usual, while the denominator is given by a new function (a JJ-function), which is no longer a polynomial.

Then, we present the separation formulas for 𝒫\mathcal{P}-normalized cluster patterns (Theorem 2.11), which generalize the formulas in [FZ07].

papers.title: On pseudo-null Iwasawa modules, restricted ramification, and Non-freeness Conjecture over a quartic CM-field
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a CM-field of degree greater than $2$, $p$ an odd prime number that splits completely in $k$, and $\Sigma$ a $p$-adic CM-type of $k$. In this setting, we show the non-triviality of the $\Sigma$-ramified Iwasawa module of the maximal multiple $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension $\widetilde{k}/k$. As a consequence, under a weak form of Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture, we see that the unramified Iwasawa module and the $\Sigma$-ramified Iwasawa module of $\widetilde{k}$ never coincide. In the case where $k$ is a quartic CM-field, under a certain assumption, we show that the non-coincidence condition is equivalent to Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture. We also study a relation of the non-coincidence condition with Non-freeness Conjecture, which is a conjecture studied in non-abelian Iwasawa theory.

papers.title: Learning a Whole-Body Pivot-Walking Gait for Heavy-Box Transport with a Humanoid
papers.abstract: Through pivot walking, humans can transport objects that are too heavy to lift. Previous humanoid studies have relied on planned sequences in which object manipulation and stepping are executed separately and the object is brought to rest between successive rotations. However, few studies have developed a single learned controller for humanoid pivot walking. In this paper, we propose a single reinforcement-learning policy that jointly coordinates stepping, balance control, and object manipulation. The policy is trained using rewards that promote alternating pivot motions and a phase reference that progresses according to the displacement of the object. In simulation, we confirmed that the humanoid can pivot a box. For deployment, we fine-tuned the policy into an object-blind version that follows a periodic clock instead of the progress reference. On the real robot, the deployed policy transported the box forward by more than 1 m in all five trials; each trial ended at a base-tilt safety stop. These results demonstrate that coordinated humanoid pivot walking can be learned with reinforcement learning and transferred to a physical humanoid robot without direct object-state sensing.

papers.title: Revisiting the Schottky-Mott Relation for Metal/ Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Interfaces: The Role of Interface Dipoles
papers.abstract: High contact resistance, predominantly stemming from Fermi-level pinning (FLP), becomes a critical bottleneck in the contact engineering of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) based two-dimensional field-effect transistors (2DFETs). Our study re-examines the inherent nature of FLP in 2D semiconductors, particularly focusing on regimes where the material thickness is commensurate with the interface thickness. Through the synergistic application of first-principles calculations and experimental validation via ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), we rigorously establish the metal effective work function (eWF) as the definitive figure of merit for substantiating the Schottky-Mott relation. Our findings indicate that FLP is intrinsically governed by both long-range dipole interactions and extended short-range Lennard-Jones potentials. This framework, in conjunction with the linear Schottky-Mott relation, improves predictive capabilities in contact engineering.
