papers.title: Sections and Constant Fields of Postcritically Finite Rational Maps
papers.abstract: We relate the constant fields of generic preimage towers to two invariants of geometric monodromy. Bounded section indices characterize branching of the closed action and imply a finite constant extension. Unbounded finite-level abelianization orders force an infinite cyclotomic subextension. For a quadratic rational map with hyperbolic orbifold, we compute the section indices and abelianizations at every sufficiently large level and obtain an infinite real cyclotomic subextension. We also give a branching criterion for quadratic maps with neither critical point periodic and formulate three conjectures about the discrete action, the constants, and the case of bounded abelianizations with unbounded section indices.

papers.title: Cross-Layer Characterization and AI-Assisted Diagnosis of C-to-Rust Performance
papers.abstract: Migrating C code to Rust can significantly improve software security, but understanding the performance implications of such migrations remains challenging. While Rust is often claimed to match C's performance, runtime safety checks, compiler optimizations, and hardware microarchitecture interact in ways that complicate performance diagnosis. We first conduct a systematic cross-layer characterization of 12 benchmarks comprising C implementations and their Rust counterparts. Our study reveals that runtime safety checks do not necessarily dominate performance overhead, as compiler and microarchitectural optimizations often mitigate their costs. Across 8 of the 12 benchmarks, at least one Rust implementation performs within 10% of its C counterpart or outperforms it. Motivated by these findings, we introduce FerroScope, an AI-assisted performance debugger that integrates source-level analysis, compiler optimization remarks, dynamic instruction traces, and hardware performance counters to diagnose performance differences between C and Rust. FerroScope reproduces our manual findings while providing more precise explanations in several cases, including identifying compiler optimizations inhibited by redundant bounds checks. Guided by these diagnoses, we develop an LLVM compiler pass that hoists redundant bounds checks through guarded loop versioning while preserving Rust's panic behavior. The pass enables downstream compiler optimizations, including loop unrolling and conditional-move conversion, reducing Selection Sort's overhead from 2.95x to 1.00x and improving Merge Sort from 1.43x to 0.91x relative to C. Together, our results demonstrate how cross-layer performance characterization and AI-assisted diagnosis can guide safety-preserving compiler optimizations for efficient C-to-Rust migration.

papers.title: Zero-cycles and holomorphic forms in families
papers.abstract: We establish parallel Chow and Hodge-theoretic rigidity theorems for dominant projective morphisms between smooth complex varieties. For instance, if the general fiber satisfies $CH_0(F) = \mathbb{Z}$, then the same is true of every fiber. Similarly, if the general fiber is connected with $H^0(F, \Omega_F^p) = 0$ for $p > 0$, then the same is true of every fiber. This extends the case of rationally connected fibrations from [Bur26]. We further introduce higher Chow-theoretic notions of singularities.

papers.title: Structural Anisotropy in Bi$_2$Se$_3$/$\lambda$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ Topological Insulator/Superconductor Bilayer
papers.abstract: We investigate the crystallographic-orientation dependence of the response of $\lambda$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ ($\lambda$-Ga) to Bi$_2$Se$_3$ deposition. Cross-sectional focused-ion-beam (FIB) imaging confirms formation of a deposited Bi$_2$Se$_3$-containing layer and a distinct interface with $\lambda$-Ga. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SC-XRD) shows that the coated $\lambda$-Ga crystal remains structurally intact but exhibits a strongly orientation-dependent, non-monotonic response, with the largest modification for the $ab$-plane after 4 min of deposition, whereas the $ac$-plane remains comparatively unchanged. This condition corresponds to the intermediate-deposition regime previously identified at a Bi$_2$Se$_3$ thickness of approximately 110 nm. First-principles calculations based on the refined structures show the largest orientation-dependent electronic modification under the same conditions. Complementary optical spectroscopy of Bi$_2$Se$_3$/SiO$_2$ films shows deposition-time-dependent evolution of the film response. These results establish a pronounced crystallographic anisotropy in the structural and calculated electronic response of $\lambda$-Ga to Bi$_2$Se$_3$ deposition.

papers.title: Remote and Noncontact Acceleration and Suppression of Heat Convection on Object Surfaces using Intensity-Adjusted Acoustic Streaming
papers.abstract: The temperature of objects in an environment is often controlled by accelerating or suppressing heat convection. Conventional methods generally involve insulation for heat retention and forced convection for cooling. However, there is no practical method for remotely and target-selectively controlling heat convection in objects in room environments. In this study, we demonstrated that intensity-adjusted acoustic streaming (ultrasound-driven airflow) can both suppress natural convection and induce forced convection on the surface of a heat source. The direct acceleration and deceleration of air over the object surface were induced by an ultrasonic beam with high temporal and spatial resolution. The experiment showed that it is possible to switch between insulating and cooling by adjusting the ultrasonic output intensity, and that it is essential for heat retention to prevent heat from escaping from the object surface by convection using acoustic streaming. We consider these results to lead to the realization of a situation where virtual heat-retaining blankets or cooling fans that are customized for specific objects in the environment can be ubiquitously attached to them, opening the door to applications such as temperature control of food and beverages and remote control of temperature profiles in manufacturing processes and laboratory settings.

papers.title: The role of hierarchy in Galactic molecular clouds
papers.abstract: To probe the role of hierarchical gas structures in massive star formation, we statistically analyzed 13 Galactic massive star-forming regions using FUGIN CO survey data. Applying a non-binary dendrogram to the position-position-velocity data, we classified the extracted structures into trunks, internal leaves (the densest substructures within trunks), and isolated structures, and compared their properties with an analysis of variance controlling for regional differences. In representative regions, the trunks correspond to morphologies such as filaments and hub-filament systems, or to kinematic signatures of structure-forming events such as cloud-cloud collisions. Across the sample, the trunks are extended, massive, and strongly bound reservoirs, while the leaves are significantly more massive, denser, and more tightly bound than isolated structures of similar spatial scale. Using YSOs and Hi-GAL clumps, we find that the leaves have a lower low-mass star formation efficiency than isolated structures, whereas their clump formation efficiency is comparable. At a fixed gas mass, the leaves show no higher low-mass star formation efficiency than isolated structures but convert a larger fraction of their gas into dense clumps. We interpret these contrasts, together with inward gas motions in the position-velocity diagrams, as indicating that the deep potential of the trunks sustains continuous accretion onto the leaves and promotes mutual interactions among them. These processes may raise the characteristic fragmentation mass, as theoretically expected for a dynamically accreting medium, so that a larger fraction of the gas forms massive clumps without a corresponding increase in low-mass star formation. Our single-epoch data constrain only these structural contrasts, but indicate that the gas available for massive star formation is organized on scales larger than a single core.

papers.title: Product-Linear POSIX Parsing
papers.abstract: POSIX regular-expression matching reports capture spans determined by the parse tree that its disambiguation rules select. Thompson's classical construction decides whether an expression $E$ matches a text $w$ in product-linear time, $O(|E|\,|w|)$. Whether the POSIX parse can also be computed in product-linear time has remained open since the rules were standardized in 1992. For instance, the algorithm of Okui and Suzuki takes $O(|E|^2|w|)$ time after precomputation. We give, to our knowledge, the first algorithm that computes the POSIX parse and all capture spans in product-linear total time, $O(|E|\,|w|)$. It uses $O(|E|+|w|)$ working space and supports full matching, longest-prefix matching, and leftmost-longest search. The algorithm scans the text backward and keeps one preferred continuation per traversal state. It implements POSIX selection with lists of end positions of the open subexpressions, which it compares and updates in constant time.

papers.title: Why $(4x(1-x))^{3/4}$ approximates the binary entropy so well: a proof of Tops{\o}e's convexity conjecture
papers.abstract: Write the binary entropy as $h(x) = u^{g(x)}$ with $u = 4x(1-x)$. Topsoe (2001) proved the sharp bounds $1/\ln 4 \le g \le 1$, i.e. $u \le h \le u^{1/\ln 4}$, and conjectured that the effective exponent $g$ is convex. We prove this conjecture. In the variable $s = (1-2x)^2$, $g$ extends to a Pick function on $\mathbb{C} \setminus [1,\infty)$ with an explicit positive density on the cut, so that $g(x) = \sum_n \gamma_n (1-2x)^{2n}$ with $\gamma_n > 0$ and $(\gamma_n)_{n \ge 1}$ a moment sequence. Pinelis's monotonicity theorem, Topsoe's power-type bounds and the optimality of their exponents follow as corollaries, together with a classification of all exponents $\alpha$ for which $u^\alpha$ bounds $h$. The proof is by hand except for one inequality in one real variable on a bounded interval, certified by interval arithmetic. As an application we give sharp, certified constants for the approximation $h \approx u^{3/4}$: $-0.0065493 \le u^{3/4} - h \le 0.0080004$ on $[0,1]$.

papers.title: Conditional Work Bounds and Timing Evidence for an Industrial NDT Scan Matcher: Cross-Language Work-Trace Conformance
papers.abstract: Normal Distributions Transform (NDT) scan matching has strongly input-dependent execution time on the localization critical path. We study the align kernel of Autoware's production matcher; map loading, preprocessing, and Robot Operating System scheduling are outside the timed scope. Our three-layer method enforces and property-tests a conditional structural work envelope, constructs stress witnesses with deterministic Rust counters, and measures frozen witnesses. It separates algorithmic work from platform time and does not claim a certified hard time bound. A domain-informed construction attains the configured ceiling for the language-common kernel-evaluation term; two archived candidates exercise higher Rust-specific kd-tree traversal at lower common work. Per-input traces define work-trace conformance over passes, processed points, neighbor counts, and leaf identities. Leaf payloads, implementation-specific traversal, total work, and latency remain outside that relation, so C++ results are observations over transferred fixtures rather than a C++ worst-case search. An auxiliary cropped-map, degraded-prior replay exposes the remaining conformance boundary, and a closed-loop replay with recovery shows both engines re-initializing at the same route sections with disjoint coverage bands. In a unified three-boot synthetic campaign, the largest observed values are 988.2 ms for C++ and 610.5 ms for Rust; Rust has the smaller maximum on all 10 paired fixtures. On neighbor-returning fixtures, C++ performs approximately 11 heap allocations per point per derivative pass, whereas the Rust align path allocates none within its reserved envelope. Rust narrows the safe-core verification surface but is not required for bounded execution; its unsafe code, foreign-function interface, and dependencies remain trusted.

papers.title: Understanding Failure Patterns in LLM-Based Mathematical Optimization Modeling
papers.abstract: Industrial optimization involves complex constraints, making optimization modeling difficult to automate. Large language models (LLMs) have been explored for generating optimization models from natural language, but their reliability in end-to-end settings remains limited, often producing non-executable, infeasible, or feasible but incorrect solutions. In this work, we study failure modes in LLM-based optimization modeling by decomposing the process into three components: mathematical reasoning, solver usage, and domain knowledge, and constructing datasets that target each aspect. Using these datasets, we analyze how different components relate to errors and find that they are associated with different types of failure, although these relationships are not always strong or consistent. Furthermore, while combining these components improves execution reliability, feasible but incorrect solutions remain the dominant failure mode, suggesting a remaining gap between executability and correctness. These findings highlight limitations of current dataset designs and suggest the importance of data that better capture constraint completeness and formulation accuracy to enhance reliability.

papers.title: Superconductivity from the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions: $U(1)$ gauge fluctuation, gauge invariance, and superconductivity
papers.abstract: The electromagnetic $U(1)$ gauge invariance and superconductivity are examined by employing the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions and the fluctuations of it that give rise to the probabilistic random transitions among quantum states. The gauge invariance in the classical electrodynamics is regarded as the requirement that extracts unaffected parts by the gauge fluctuation. In quantum mechanics, dissipation-free states from the gauge fluctuation exist, and we identify them as superconducting states. We explain the reversible superconducting-normal phase transition in a magnetic field including the force balance. The present superconductivity theory lifts two fundamental disagreements between theory and experiment existing in the current standard theory with keeping the major results by the BCS theory. Thus, it may be considered as a superconductivity theory encompassing the current standard one.

papers.title: Multimodal Safety Evaluation of Vision-Language Models in Japanese
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed in Japanese-language settings, yet multimodal safety evaluation has been largely English-centric. We extend the Multimodal Safety Test Suite (MSTS) of R\"ottger et al. (2025) to Japanese as the 12th language, contributing 320 machine-translated and post-edited cases with reference answers plus 82 culturally localized Japanese images. We introduce an evaluation framework that (i) extends MSTS's 3-class safety grouping with a 5-point scale that also rewards useful (not just safe) responses, and (ii) separates image recognition from safety judgment to isolate recognition errors. Using this framework, we evaluate five modern Japanese VLMs (Gemini-3-Flash, GPT-5, InternVL3, LLM-JP-4-VL, Qwen3-VL) against human evaluation, and find substantial variance in the safety readiness across the models. Finally, we evaluate two LLM-as-a-Judge models and find that providing a reference answer improves agreement with human safety judgments, though recall for detecting unsafe responses remains limited, underscoring the difficulty of automating multimodal safety evaluation. The dataset created for our study will be released upon publication.

papers.title: Monoidal analog of cluster-tilting theory and monoidal reachability of acyclic cluster algebras
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we prove that many analogous facts of cluster-tilting theory holds in monoidal categories from quantum affine algebras or quiver Hecke algebras. We show that a maximal commuting family of real prime modules, which is an analogous object of a cluster-tilting object, is always a laurent family introduced by Kashiwara-Kim-Oh-Park. By using $\widetilde{\Lambda}$-invariants, we construct an exchange matrix of each laurent family and show that a laurent family is always completely $\Lambda$-admissible monoidal seed. We obtain that a pair of real prime modules is an exchange pair if and only if $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is $1$.
  When the category is a monoidal categorification of a cluster algebra of acyclic type, we prove that $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is not less than generic Ext invariant by using tropical $F$-invariant introduced by Cao and Fei. Moreover, we show that, the conjecture asserting that real simple modules correspond exactly to cluster monomials holds in these cases.

papers.title: Post-Training Policy Replication for Strategy-Following Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning across Team Sizes
papers.abstract: Although multi-agent deep reinforcement learning enables coordinated behavior, aligning it with managerial intent remains difficult due to complex agent interactions. Although the strategy-following distributed attentional actor architecture (sfDA7-X) improves controllability via regional instructions, instruction combinations scale exponentially with team and instruction sizes, leading to prohibitive training costs and poor transferability. To reduce this computational cost, we introduce a team-size-independent observation architecture and reconstruct collective behavior by replicating a single trained policy across agents in teams of different sizes, thereby eliminating the need to train from scratch. Additionally, we evaluate warm-start retraining by initializing policy networks with a pre-trained policy to significantly lower computational overhead. In an object collection game, a policy trained in a four-agent team is deployed to teams of three to eight agents. Experiments demonstrate that training with the proposed aggregated observation matrix achieves performance comparable to that of the baseline method, sfDA7-X. Furthermore, policy replication preserves performance without substantial degradation in three- and five-agent teams, and warm-start retraining outperforms training from scratch while reducing required training episodes by up to 90%. Deployments to six- and eight-agent teams further confirm effective spatial region allocation following given instructions. These results demonstrate that the proposed method enables zero-shot collective behavior reconstruction via policy replication.

papers.title: Measuring a buried Bi$_2$Te$_3$ epitaxial film through a protective Te cap: an exact three-layer terahertz analysis
papers.abstract: Air-sensitive chalcogenide films are routinely protected by a capping layer, which must then be removed, or contacted through, before electronic transport can be measured, destroying the surface the cap was meant to preserve. Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy requires neither, but using it quantitatively demands a transmission model in which cap, film and substrate are treated on an equal footing. We formulate the cap/film/substrate problem exactly using a transfer matrix with a time-gated substrate, and show that the intuitive construction in which each thin layer contributes an independent Fabry--P\'erot factor fails for two adjacent thin films. In the thin-film limit we obtain a closed-form inversion together with a criterion for the error incurred by ignoring the cap. We apply the framework to Bi$_2$Te$_3$ films grown by molecular beam epitaxy on GaAs at three thicknesses, each prepared with and without a 25 nm Te cap. A Te-on-GaAs witness shows the cap to be optically indistinguishable from bare substrate, transmitting 1.00(4) of the substrate amplitude between 0.2 and 1.5 THz, which limits the error from neglecting it to 3.6 % for the 90 nm film, although the same estimate reaches 48 % at 25 nm. In this matched set, the capped films form an ordered series, monotonic in thickness in both conductance magnitude and lineshape, whereas the uncapped films do not. The capping layer therefore presents no obstacle to terahertz characterization, and in this set it coincides with a more reproducible film response.

papers.title: A Variability Metric Pipeline for AGN studies
papers.abstract: Variability in active galactic nuclei (AGNs) is remarkably diverse, spanning multiple timescales, wavelengths, and physical processes. Variability probes accretion physics and the interplay between supermassive black holes and their surroundings. Building on early case studies, the field has shifted toward population-level analyses of increasingly large datasets, making scalable techniques crucial for upcoming time-domain surveys. We developed a Python-based pipeline to analyze AGN light curves using variability metrics and applied it to 14,061 nearby AGNs ($z\lesssim 0.09$) observed with ZTF. We examined metric distributions and correlations. Amplitude-based metrics (e.g., $F_{\rm var}$) help identify major flares but are sensitive to single deviant epochs. Temporal metrics such as $\eta$ provide a complementary check. Comparison with WISE infrared photometry suggests that $\eta$ traces the strength of AGN activity. Most Type~I and Type~II AGNs in our sample exhibit similar variability patterns based on these metrics. This overlap may partly reflect misclassifications that targeted spectroscopic follow-up could help resolve. To identify subsets of AGNs with distinctive variability, we used UMAP to group sources with similar metric values. The resulting embedding shows a region enriched in high-amplitude variables, including a subset with long-term flux trends. We find evidence that extremely variable quasars and changing-look AGNs may populate this region, which can help prioritize sources for follow-up. Our pipeline offers a scalable, survey-agnostic framework suitable for application to Vera C. Rubin Observatory's LSST and other ongoing and upcoming photometric surveys.

papers.title: A Finite Automaton Translating Geometric Addresses into Dynamical Itineraries on the Basilica
papers.abstract: Fractals are generally known for their self-similarity and repeating patterns. One way to produce fractals is via the dynamics of functions from the extended complex plane to itself. These fractals are known as Julia sets. In this paper, we explore how methods from symbolic dynamics and computation theory can be used to describe where points on the basilica Julia set might be located depending on their dynamical orbit under the polynomial function $f(z)=z^2-1$.

papers.title: Community Notes Across Platforms: Evaluating the Feasibility of Re-using Crowd-sourced Context Notes
papers.abstract:
Crowdsourced fact-checking systems such as Community Notes can provide useful context for misleading content. Producing and rating new notes on such systems requires substantial contributor effort. However, the resulting context is typically confined to the post and platform for which it was created. We ask whether already-vetted notes can be reused when the same claims recur across posts and platforms.
  To investigate this question, we construct a human-labelled dataset using Community Notes attached to X posts created during a one-week period and candidate posts retrieved from Bluesky. Within our observation window, 140 of 340 claims had at least one confirmed recurrence on Bluesky, showing that cross-platform note reuse is a substantial opportunity. Recurrence alone, however, does not establish whether reuse would provide timely context. A timing analysis shows that many relevant notes were already Helpful when matching Bluesky posts appeared. Even when a Bluesky post appeared first, reuse could often still provide context sooner after publication than the original X post received its Helpful note. To automate the discovery of these opportunities, we evaluate a three-stage pipeline that searches the Bluesky stream for potential recurrences and determines whether an existing note applies. The pipeline achieves 72.6% precision in a held-out stream evaluation and 70.1% end-to-end recall on our known-positive set. We further characterize the pipeline's costs and principal failure modes. Crossnote, our prototype Bluesky labeler, implements this approach by applying existing Community Notes to matching posts.
  Our findings suggest that reusing vetted crowdsourced context is a compelling way to scale the reach and impact of Community Notes. Note reuse can complement the production of new notes by reducing duplicated effort and shortening time to context when misleading claims recur.

papers.title: Carrier relaxation confines the Bogdanov--Takens degeneracy of an optically injected semiconductor laser
papers.abstract: Optically injected semiconductor lasers are forced nonlinear oscillators whose locking boundaries are organized by codimension-two points. We ask which property of the carrier balance permits or forbids a Bogdanov--Takens (BT) point in the standard three-dimensional rate equations. Taking the carrier inversion $n$ as distinguished observable, the rate that enters the spectral conditions is the slope of the gain--loss balance, $\xi=\partial\dot n/\partial n=-2\Gamma/\kappa$, where $\Gamma$ is the damping of the relaxation oscillation and $\kappa=1+2Bn$ the normalized stimulated-emission factor. The two BT conditions become affine in $\xi$ and imply the exact sum rule $K^{2}=I[1-(1+\kappa)I]$ between injection amplitude $K$ and intracavity intensity $I$. The product of the two relaxation eigenvalues that survive at a saddle-node is bounded below by $1-16\Gamma^{2}$, so that no BT point exists for $\Gamma<1/4$, whatever $B$, the linewidth enhancement factor, the injection strength and the detuning; below this barrier every contact between Hopf and saddle-node curves is a fold--Hopf point. For $B=0$ the barrier is completed to an exact existence criterion. We prove that the unfolding of a BT point by injection strength and detuning is transversal if and only if two explicit curves cross transversally in the plane of locked states; for $B=0$ this is a simple root of an explicit function, and transversality fails exactly at the existence threshold. Two BT points at $\Gamma=1/2$, $\alpha=2$ are verified to be generic, and the contacts between Hopf and saddle-node curves are classified into fold--Hopf, BT and nilpotent triple-zero points.

papers.title: Singular rational S-functions of second-order ODEs: structure, degree bounds and a Kovacic-type search
papers.abstract: For a rational second-order ODE $y''=phi(x,y,y')$, the $S$-function method reduces the search for a first integral to finding a rational solution $S$ of the Riccati-type equation $X(S)=S^2+phi_z S-phi_y$ along the total-derivative field $X$. The standard ansatz $S=P/N^k$, with $N=den(phi)$, misses every $S$ with poles outside $N=0$. Such singular solutions cannot be avoided: for point transforms of linear equations without hyperexponential solutions we describe every quasi-regular $S$ explicitly, and for a generic transformation none exists. We then determine the structure of singular solutions. Outside $N$ every pole is simple, with residue $-1$, and is not a Darboux surface; along non-characteristic factors of $N$ the leading polar coefficient is free Cauchy data; and the only unknown denominator is a squarefree polynomial $D$, which enters a linear equation. A Newton-polygon analysis at infinity gives the polynomial part up to a correction of bounded weight. The weighted degree of $D$ is determined exactly when the excess is zero and the top Riccati equation has no algebraic solution, and is bounded by residues of the top field otherwise, conditionally on the vanishing of that correction. The dependence of $D$ on $x$ is obtained, without a degree bound, from the rational solutions of a linear differential system. These results give a certified search procedure, implemented twice, which finds the singular $S$ of nine non-Liouvillian pull-backs of the Airy and Bessel equations. In one regime it is a decision procedure; for instance, it proves that $y''=xy+1$ has no rational $S$.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi-UAV Data Harvesting Under Variable Team Sizes and Agent Loss
papers.abstract: Collecting data from wireless sensors can be challenging when limited communication infrastructure prevents them from offloading their measurements. In such settings, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can exploit their mobility to harvest data locally, while coordinated UAV teams can provide efficient and redundant coverage of remote areas. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables such teams to learn decentralized coordination policies. However, training separate policies for different team and sensor populations is costly, and fixed-population policies may be vulnerable to agent failures. This work proposes F-MADDPG, a flexible variant of Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) that supports data harvesting with varying numbers of wireless sensors and UAVs. The framework also accommodates unexpected catastrophic failures that permanently remove agents during a mission. We compare F-MADDPG with a MADDPG baseline that uses multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and evaluate training strategies based on team-size sampling and exposure to agent terminations. The results show that F-MADDPG learns across the evaluated population sizes, completes missions faster than the baseline on average, benefits from inverse-cardinality team-size sampling compared with uniform sampling, remains effective after permanent agent losses, and gains no consistent benefit from exposure to failures during training.

papers.title: On the Cluster Duration Distribution of the Markovian Hawkes Process
papers.abstract: The duration of a Hawkes process cluster, meaning the time from first point to last point in an entirely endogenously generated progeny stream, has been stubbornly resistant to analysis; even the mean has not been known in closed form. Recently, uniformly random parking functions have been found to be hidden spines of these history-driven clusters, offering a probabilistic combinatorial structure within self-excitement that has opened new avenues for analysis. Here, we leverage and refine this decomposition to provide a closed-form expression for the mean cluster duration in the case of an exponential excitation kernel. Specifically, we reduce from uniformly random parking functions to non-uniform preference counts. This change of probabilistic combinatorial structure in the decomposition leads us to both a Borel-based identity and an explicit integral-based expression for the mean duration.

papers.title: A proof of the Nevo-Peeva conjecture: Exact regularity and linear powers of gap-free edge ideals
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with at least one edge, and let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal over a field $K$. We prove that if $G$ is gap-free, then $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q=\max\{2q,\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)+q-1\}$ for all $q\geq 1$. This answers both open problems of Nevo and Peeva on ordinary powers: $I(G)^q$ has a linear resolution exactly when $q\geq \mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, and their proposed regularity recurrence holds with equality. As consequences, the upper bound $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q\leq 2q+\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-2$ conjectured by Alilooee, Banerjee, Beyarslan, H\`a, Jayanthan and Selvaraja holds for gap-free graphs; every power $I(G)^q$ with $q\geq 2$ has a linear resolution when $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)=3$; and the stabilization index equals $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, which is unbounded on this class. The proof rests on a combinatorial result of independent interest: a parity-sensitive homology vanishing theorem for a filtration of the independence complex by a weighted Hall defect. An internalization lemma and sublevel complexes of submodular functions control the local terms, and Hall's theorem together with an implication-digraph argument classifies the zero level. A capacitated form of the Tutte-Berge formula and Takayama's formula identify the filtration with the degree complexes of ordinary powers. The algebraic statements hold over every field, and the topological vanishing holds with arbitrary abelian coefficients.

papers.title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical Question Answering on ESC Cardiology Guidelines: Evaluation and Retrieval Optimization
papers.abstract: Background: Large language models produce hallucinations in medical question answering (QA). Verify-and-revise pipelines that check atomic claims against retrieved guideline evidence are a standard mitigation, but evaluations almost universally treat the verifier's output as ground truth, an assumption rarely tested. Objective: To measure, claim by claim against human judgement, how such a pipeline fails in a guideline-grounded clinical setting. Methods: We built a dataset of 160 questions (100 patient vignettes from 89 de-identified cases, 60 fact-based) over four recent ESC cardiology guidelines, all approved by a practising internist, and a retrieval corpus of 627 hand-verified guideline records at two chunk granularities. A five-stage pipeline was run under four retrieval configurations and three independent runs (1920 arm-runs); all 606 first-pass refuted claims were manually audited, an independent judge re-judged 906 decisions, and the expert blindly reviewed 100 accepted claims. Results: Only 44.7-50.6% of flagged claims were true hallucinations. Correction loops converged in 85.2-95.1% of cases, yet 35% of genuine final errors were introduced by correction. Single-run true-hallucination recall was 35.6-41.2%, the three-run union 71-80%; verifier agreement was moderate (kappa = 0.505). The blind probe estimated the accepted-claim miss rate at 3.2% (95% CI 0.7-6.7%). Final genuine-error rate: 1.7% of answers. Conclusion: Claim-level verification reduces hallucinated content by an order of magnitude, but verifier reliability, not generation, is the limiting factor and must be measured, not assumed.

papers.title: Escape Time with Quenched Extrinsic Fluctuations in Positive Feedback Systems
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks with positive feedback often exhibit multiple stable steady states representing distinct cellular phenotypes, allowing stochastic fluctuations to drive phenotypic switching between basins of attraction. Such transitions are commonly characterized by escape-time statistics. While previous studies have typically analyzed intrinsic fluctuation or dynamical environmental fluctuation separately, the combined effect of intrinsic biochemical fluctuation and quenched (slowly varying) extrinsic cell-to-cell parameter heterogeneity on population-level switching dynamics remains less understood. In this study, we formulate a theoretical framework to compute escape-time moments by combining the backward chemical Fokker--Planck equation with population averaging over a stationary distribution of kinetic parameters. We apply this approach to two paradigmatic bistable motifs---positive autoregulation and the genetic Toggle Switch---and quantify how quenched extrinsic heterogeneity modifies switching times across a population of autonomous cells. Our results show that extrinsic parameter variability can substantially alter the mean switching time and, more prominently, increase its dispersion, producing highly heterogeneous switching kinetics across genetically identical cells. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for cell-to-cell parameter heterogeneity when characterizing stochastic phenotypic switching in biological populations.

papers.title: The Traveling Salesman Problem with non-convex polygonal neighborhoods: A hybrid Iterated Local Search--Block Coordinate Descent approach
papers.abstract: The Traveling Salesman Problem with Neighborhoods (TSPN) generalizes the classical TSP by requiring a tour to visit a set of regions in the Euclidean plane rather than fixed point coordinates. It has applications in last-mile delivery, surveillance, and remote sensing in precision agriculture. In this paper, we address the Euclidean TSPN with arbitrary, non-convex polygonal neighborhoods---a highly complex setting due to the joint continuous and combinatorial optimization challenges. To solve the continuous subproblem of determining optimal visit points for a given visiting sequence, we propose a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) method based on solving fast one-dimensional geometric subproblems. Computational experiments demonstrate that BCD computes optimal visit points for a fixed sequence in almost all instances in which optimality is certified, more than six orders of magnitude faster than a commercial solver solving the equivalent Mixed-Integer Quadratically Constrained Programming (MIQCP) formulation. This efficiency enables an effective hybrid Iterated Local Search metaheuristic (ILS-BCD) that thoroughly explores the combinatorial search space at low computational cost. Extensive computational tests on 235 benchmark instances derived from the Generalized TSP (GTSP), with up to 100 neighborhoods, show that ILS-BCD matched or improved upon the best-known GTSP tours in all cases, obtaining strictly shorter tours in 234 instances. On the 80 instances for which optimality is proven, ILS-BCD attains the optimal tour length in all of them, within a relative difference below 0.001%. On 60 larger instances, with as many as 6,325 neighborhoods, ILS-BCD remains competitive up to about 220.

papers.title: Detecting Transmit Precoding in Commodity Wi-Fi Channel State Information and Its Effect on Measured Channel Statistics
papers.abstract: Channel state information (CSI) from commodity Wi-Fi receivers is increasingly used to estimate delay spread and fading. For multi-stream data frames, the access point may apply transmit beamforming, and the CSI then describes the precoded channel $\mathbf{HQ}$ instead of the propagation channel $\mathbf{H}$. This letter gives a blind test for eigen-beamforming based on the near-orthogonality and power ordering of the stream columns, evaluated at the receive-chain gain ratio that minimizes their coherence. The test needs no calibration or packet alignment, tolerates gain changes between sounding and data frames, and builds on the $\mathrm{Beta}(1,N_r-1)$ law of the squared column coherence under unprecoded Rayleigh fading. Simulations with compressed feedback, subcarrier grouping, feedback delay, antenna correlation, and SNRs of 10-30 dB give false-alarm rates of at most $2.9\times10^{-3}$ at the chosen thresholds and show precoding scales the per-entry RMS delay spread by factors of 0.3 to 5.7. The per-subcarrier Gram matrix $\hat{\mathbf{H}}\hat{\mathbf{H}}^{H}$ is preserved: the Frobenius norm is unchanged with two transmit antennas and within 1.7 dB (95th percentile) with four. With two generations of commercial access points at 5 and 6 GHz, 880 of the 896 two-stream data frames they sent to the client tested as precoded, including 601 of 605 IEEE 802.11be frames without a beamforming flag. A third access point gave 0 of 5221 in 802.11n mode and 4003 of 5225 flagged frames in 802.11ac mode, fewer in motion; a fourth gave 3283 of 3296 with beamforming on and 0 of 3223 with it off.

papers.title: Device-Referred Channel Sounding With Commodity Wi-Fi Receivers: Error Budget and Body-Worn Measurements at 5 and 6 GHz
papers.abstract: A wireless product experiences the channel through its own antennas and, when worn, its user's body. Commodity Wi-Fi receivers report channel state information (CSI) per frame and can serve as device-referred sounders if their impairments are corrected. Synthetic ground truth reproducing a commercial receiver's impairments shows that five corrections are needed: subcarrier mapping, receive-chain order, per-packet alignment, received-signal-strength referencing, and window-response removal. Without them, the RMS delay spread reads up to 191% high, the coherence bandwidth falls to about half, or the Rician $K$-factor and Doppler estimates lose their meaning; with all five, the median delay-spread bias is between $-6\%$ and $+14\%$. Applied to beacons from seven access points, including a body-worn receiver at six indoor sites at 5 and 6 GHz, the chain gives delay spreads of 24-96 ns; walking lowers the median correlation over one beacon interval from 0.85 to 0.15, near the estimator's floor. Unprecoded data frames gave 0.2-1.2 times the beacons' delay spread on the same channel, so the two should not be pooled.

papers.title: Improving the efficiency of the ratio-of-uniforms method
papers.abstract: In 1977, Kinderman and Monahan showed that under certain conditions, a random variable can be expressed as the ratio $V/U$, where $(U,V)$ is uniformly distributed over a bounded region $S\subset{\mathds R}^2$. Thus, by generating values of $(U,V)$ and computing the indicated ratio, samples from the random variable can be obtained. This procedure is now known as the ratio-of-uniforms method and relies heavily on our ability to produce uniform samples from $S$, for which an acceptance-rejection method is customarily used. In this paper, we propose three sampling schemes based on the polar representation of $S$. The first uses a covering consisting of triangles, the second uses a covering based on circular sectors, while the third employs rectangular coverings of an associated angular density. Numerical examples illustrate that these schemes can achieve acceptance rates close to $100\%$.

papers.title: Real-time Food Recipe Generation with Mobile Deep Learning and Large Language Model
papers.abstract: Finding recipes that match available kitchen ingredients can be cumbersome and inefficient. This paper addresses this challenge by developing a mobile application that generates tailored food recipes based on ingredients identified using a mobile camera. Leveraging deep learning and large language model (LLM), our system offers a seamless and efficient solution for real-time recipe generation. By integrating deep learning for accurate ingredient recognition with LLM for generating detailed and practical recipes, our approach ensures users receive precise cooking instructions based on actual ingredients on hand. Extensive dataset augmentation and model training have resulted in a robust system capable of high performance. Experimental results demonstrate that EfficientNet, used for food recognition, offers a balance of accuracy and computational efficiency, making it ideal for mobile applications. This dual-approach method enhances the cooking experience, reduces food waste, and provides a comprehensive, real-time tool for everyday cooking needs, bridging a significant gap in current food recommendation systems.

papers.intro:
In today’s fast-paced world, mobile devices have become an integral part of our daily lives, providing convenience and accessibility to a plethora of services and information. One common use case for mobile devices is searching for food recipes online. However, this process can often be cumbersome and inefficient. Many online recipes require ingredients that may not be readily available in our kitchens, necessitating a trip to the grocery store and adding an extra layer of complexity to meal preparation. This inconvenience is compounded when users face the challenge of navigating through a vast array of recipe websites, each with different media formats and varying levels of reliability. Moreover, the time spent searching for recipes that match the ingredients on hand can be frustrating, especially for individuals with busy schedules or limited culinary experience. Recent advancements in machine learning and artificial intelligence have highlighted the potential for more intuitive and personalized solutions, yet many current applications still fall short in addressing the practical needs of everyday users. Integrating seamless, intelligent recipe generation into a multimedia system for mobile devices represents a significant step forward in making cooking more accessible and enjoyable for everyone.

Moreover, the time spent searching for recipes that match the ingredients on hand can be frustrating, especially for individuals with busy schedules or limited culinary experience. Recent advancements in machine learning and artificial intelligence have highlighted the potential for more intuitive and personalized solutions, yet many current applications still fall short in addressing the practical needs of everyday users. Integrating seamless, intelligent recipe generation into a multimedia system for mobile devices represents a significant step forward in making cooking more accessible and enjoyable for everyone.

The motivation behind our paper is to simplify this process by developing a mobile application that generates food recipes based on the ingredients available in the user’s kitchen. This eliminates the need for extensive searches and makes cooking more accessible and convenient. While previous works [14, 1, 11] have made strides in ingredient recognition and recipe retrieval using deep learning models, our approach uniquely integrates deep learning for ingredient identification with large language model (LLM) for detailed recipe generation. This dual approach ensures that users receive accurate and practical cooking instructions based on the actual ingredients they have on hand, filling a critical gap in the existing literature on food recommendation systems.

By leveraging the ubiquitous nature of mobile devices, we aim to provide a seamless experience where users can simply take a photo of their ingredients using their mobile camera and receive tailored recipe suggestions. Our objective is to create an intelligent system that combines food recognition with deep learning and recipe generation with LLM. The deep learning model accurately identifies the ingredients from the captured image, while the LLM generates relevant recipes based on these recognized ingredients. To ensure the accuracy and relevance of the recipes, we provide the LLM with detailed information about the available ingredients and nutritional expectations, guiding it to produce practical and accurate cooking instructions. This dual approach is novel because it integrates real-time ingredient recognition with advanced recipe generation, a combination that has not been fully addressed by existing solutions. This innovative method addresses the practical challenge of utilizing available ingredients effectively, making cooking more accessible and reducing food waste, thus providing a significant improvement over current recipe search methods. We highlight our contributions as follows: • Dataset Augmentation: We augmented the GroceryStoreDataset by merging fine-grained categories into broader classes, such as grouping different apple varieties into a single “Apple” class. We further expanded the dataset with images scraped from Google and samples from Fruits-360, resulting in approximately 42,000 images split into training, validation, and test sets at a 70:15:15 ratio. • Integration of Deep Learning and LLM: Our system integrates deep learning-based food recognition with an LLM for recipe generation. papers.title: Massively multiplayer browser games on stateless pages and a relational database, a tutorial on their construction
papers.abstract: A massively multiplayer browser game is a persistent world that many players change through ordinary web pages, with no client to install. This work is a tutorial for a developer or developer who wants to structure such a game from the start, from the overall organisation into modules to the protocols between players. The running example is the open-source role-playing game Naruto! Nigeru, whose engine keeps the whole game state in a relational database and uses no third-party library. The tutorial presents the overall view of the game, how its code is separated into modules, which technologies it uses and which ones it avoids, and then each mechanism as a design decision with its alternatives, namely the request cycle, the data model, the identity of the player without sessions, the world map computed from a hash of the coordinates, the turn-based combat, the economy under simultaneous requests, the trade and duel protocols, the ways a page waits for another player, and the content and languages. It closes with a suggested order of construction and the lessons of the example. The example has 25,930 lines of code in 9 feature modules over a core of 2,364 lines.

papers.title: Incorporating the Knowledge Distillation to Improve the EfficientNet Transfer Learning Capability
papers.abstract:
Due to the Deep Learning requirement for a large training dataset, Transfer Learning has become a central method in the field of Computer Vision, which heavily used Deep Learning. Since the adoption of transfer learning in the field, the performance of the models in computer vision is significantly upgraded. The common transfer learning practice in computer vision research is to use state-of-the-art architectures in the ImageNet dataset as the backbone network. The best performing architecture in ImageNet is currently held by EfficientNet, which is a set of architectures that were progressively grown from a baseline architecture.
  By observing the EfficientNet development approach, it is natural to hypothesize that the smaller EfficientNet architecture is capable to contain the knowledge of the larger architecture. This hypothesis comes from the fact that the larger EfficientNet architecture was grown from the smaller architecture. Therefore, in this study, we experimented if it is beneficial to transfer the knowledge from the larger architecture to the smaller architecture of the EfficientNet. To achieve this goal, we proposed a transfer learning method that uses Knowledge Distillation as the knowledge transfer mechanism from the larger to smaller architecture. We found that the proposed method is able to upgrade the performance of each of the EfficientNet architecture. Several smaller architectures are even able to outperform the larger architecture that was trained using the standard transfer learning method.

papers.title: Extensions of congruent monotileable (and amenable) groups
papers.abstract:
A monotile of a countable group $G$ is a finite subset $F \subseteq G$ that tiles $G$, namely $G=\bigsqcup_{c\in C} c F$, for some set of centers $C\subseteq G$. The group $G$ is called congruent monotileable (CM) if it admits an exhaustive sequence of monotiles $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that each $F_{n+1}$ is teselated by $F_n$. If moreover $G$ is amenable and the sequence $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is Folner, we say $G$ is congruent monotileable amenable (CMA).
  In this work we observe that the classes of CM and CMA groups are stable under group extensions satisfying a certain technical condition, which we call $stepwise$ $monotileability$, and which is a weaker version of the notion of $X$-$monotileability$ introduced by Dikranjan $et al$. Our condition also includes central extensions previously considered by Gao, Jackson, Seward for CM groups, and by Cecchi Bernales, Cortez for CMA groups. We show that this condition is satisfied by semidirect products of the form $G\wr H$, provided $G$ and $H$ are CM/CMA groups, and also by extensions of locally finite groups by CM/CMA groups. This furnishes new examples of CM and CMA groups. In particular, we provide the first examples of finitely generated CMA groups which are neither solvable nor residually finite.

papers.title: Physical quasar pairs in DESI DR1 as tracers of protoclusters at $z\approx2$
papers.abstract: Close pairs of quasars at the same redshift are expected to mark overdense regions that will collapse into galaxy clusters. Earlier work with SDSS found about 2800 such pairs, too few to follow their environment with separation. We build the largest sample of physical quasar pairs to date from DESI DR1 and test whether pairs out to Mpc separations trace protoclusters. We select pairs with rest-frame velocity difference $|\Delta V|\leq900 km/s$ and projected separation $r_p\leq4$~Mpc at $1.2\leq z\leq2.8$, measure their purity and fibre completeness, and measure the clustering of pair members around all DESI quasars. We find 40\,626 physical pairs with projected separation $r_p\leq2.5$~Mpc, where their purity falls to 50\%, the effective radius of protoclusters at $z\approx2$. Pair members are $1.69\pm0.14$, $1.78\pm0.09$ and $2.01\pm0.06$ times more clustered than all quasars for projected separations $r_p\leq1$, 1--2.5 and 2.5--4~Mpc, while chance pairs show little excess ($1.08\pm0.05$). This corresponds to haloes of $\sim1.4$--$2.2\times10^{13}\,h^{-1}M_\odot$. Physical quasar pairs with projected separations up to 2.5~Mpc trace protocluster environments, at the level that AbacusSummit mocks predict in $\Lambda$CDM. The full DESI survey will turn them into a statistical census of protoclusters at cosmic noon.

papers.title: Teaching a Multilingual Translation Model Regional Varieties: Castilian and Latin American Spanish, Asturian, Aragonese and Aranese with MADLAD-400-3B-MT
papers.abstract: Massively multilingual translation models usually have one tag per language and no control over regional varieties, and they cover a region's smaller languages poorly or not at all. We report three fine-tunes of MADLAD-400-3B-MT, each adding target tags with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), back-translation of monolingual text and replay of the base model's own translations: <2es_ES> for Spanish as written in Spain, <2es_419> for Latin American Spanish, and one model for three Romance languages of the Iberian Peninsula, Asturian (<2ast>), Aragonese (<2an>) and Aranese (<2oc_aranes>). For the Spanish varieties we annotate the 250.9M documents of MADLAD-400's Spanish split with a domain-supervised Spain vs. Latin America classifier and select variety text with a rule that admitted no Latin American document in a 340-document reference set. The Castilian model chooses Spain's everyday vocabulary in 97% of a targeted test (base model 62%) and vosotros for informal plural address in 70% (10%), while improving chrF++ on human references. A first finding is tag collapse: with a new tag initialised from <2es>, the parent tag drifts to the new variety (84-87% identical outputs). In the Iberian model, contrastive pairs and a separate learning rate for the tag embeddings keep each tag in its own language. Trained only on publicly available data, mostly the TAN-IBE Wikipedia corpora, the Iberian model matches or beats the TAN-IBE Marian systems in four of six Spanish directions on FLORES+, is 1.9 BLEU behind in Spanish->Aranese, and is second only to SalamandraTA-7B in most directions. The exception, Spanish->Aragonese, reflects a difference of written variety between Aragonese Wikipedia and the FLORES+ reference, not model quality. All three fine-tunes lose 0.6-0.7 chrF++ on average in thirteen other FLORES-200 directions. We release the models, data and variety classifier under open licences

papers.title: Pettis integrability of $L^1$-functions in locally convex spaces
papers.abstract: In this article, for a Hausdorff locally convex space $E$, we investigate conditions under which every Lusin-measurable $L^1$-function $\gamma:[0,1]\to E$ is Pettis integrable. We show that this property on $E$ is local and equivalent to $E$ being absolutely summable and satisfying the metric convex compactness property. Via examples, we show that these two properties are independent. Moreover, we establish sufficient conditions, for a Lusin-measurable weakly integrable function with values in the topological dual $E'$, to be Gelfand integrable.

papers.title: Numerical analysis of a conservative Crank-Nicolson scheme for quasilinear Gross-Pitaevskii equations
papers.abstract:
We propose and analyze a fully discrete Crank-Nicolson finite-difference scheme for one-dimensional quasilinear Hamiltonian Gross-Pitaevskii equations with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. We establish the existence and uniqueness of numerical solutions and an $H^1$-stability estimate.
  For sufficiently regular exact solutions, we obtain second-order convergence in both time and space in the discrete $H^1$-norm. The analysis covers the focusing and defocusing cubic nonlinearities and both signs of the quasilinear coefficient $\kappa$, under a uniform discrete ellipticity condition when $\kappa<0$.
  The main difficulty in the error analysis comes from the derivatives introduced by the quasilinear interaction. To overcome this problem, we introduce a discrete action combining the discrete energy and mass, and establish a coercivity inequality in the discrete $H^1$-norm that allows us to control the numerical error. Together with consistency estimates and a discrete Gronwall inequality, this yields second-order convergence. Numerical experiments with bright solitons corroborate the predicted convergence rates.

papers.title: Sharp Query Bounds and Optimal Faithful Simulation under Smooth Changes of Variables
papers.abstract: We consider deterministic procedures that acquire information about an unknown real-valued function through scalar queries to its values and derivatives. We use two descriptions of computation, one in terms of states and transitions and another in terms of rules depending on the history of responses, allowing partially defined rules. We establish representations in both directions that exactly preserve the domains of valid computations within a finite budget, their outputs, records, and counts by derivative order. These representations make it possible to study the cost of reproducing derivative information under changes of variables. For a composite function $f\circ\chi$, with $\chi$ a known smooth diffeomorphism, we prove that the minimum number of queries to $f$ needed to reconstruct a derivative response equals the number of nonzero coefficients in the composition formula, even among adaptive procedures. We extend this characterization to faithful simulation of complete procedures and obtain the exact cost from the union of the active data in their records. For successive changes of variables, we determine the costs of reconstructing intermediate responses and of computing only the final derivative, and characterize the savings due to cancellation of data. Finally, upon composing a smooth change with its inverse, we prove that the direct cost is one, whereas the intermediate reconstruction cost remains equal to one if all higher derivatives of the change vanish at the point and tends to infinity with the order otherwise. In particular, affine changes are exactly those that admit a uniform bound on this cost over all points and orders.

papers.title: Scaled Coordinate Descent for Convex Quadratic Programs
papers.abstract: We study a modification of coordinate descent for unconstrained symmetric positive definite quadratic programs that combines a coordinate correction with an exact scaling of the current iterate. For a selected coordinate, the method minimizes the objective function over the two-dimensional subspace spanned by the current iterate and the corresponding standard basis vector. Closed-form expressions are obtained for the two update parameters and for the resulting objective decrease. The scaling produces a state-dependent effective curvature that is no larger than the diagonal curvature used by standard coordinate descent, so the exact scaled update makes at least as much progress for the same selected coordinate. We discuss initialization, numerical stability, randomized coordinate selection, experimental comparisons with ordinary two-coordinate descent, and a block coordinate extension. In the spirit of previous theoretical results, we give a probabilistic linear convergence result. Finally, we provide experimental results to show the effectiveness of the proposed method on synthetic data.

papers.title: New fast and accurate estimators of the five-parameter lambda distribution (FPLD) with practical applications
papers.abstract: When fitting parametric densities, simple distributions are often chosen because they are computationally efficient to estimate and easy to interpret. However, simplicity can result in important features of the data being missed. This paper introduces fast and reliable estimators of the five-parameter lambda distribution (FPLD). The FPLD is highly flexible, can take many different shapes, and provides greater control over skewness and tail behaviour than distributions with fewer parameters. Simulations are provided to demonstrate the excellent performance of the proposed estimators compared with existing methods, at a fraction of the computational cost. Applications in which speed and accuracy are important are also provided, with comparisons to commonly used but potentially overly simplistic approaches. Finally, an R package implementing the proposed estimators and a web application that allows users to determine the FPLD parameters required to approximate well-known distributions are provided.

papers.title: The $k$-disjoint paths problem for group-labelled graphs
papers.abstract: A $\Gamma$-labelled graph is an oriented graph with edge labels in a group $\Gamma$. Fix a finite abelian group $\Gamma$ and a positive integer $k$. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that finds $k$ vertex-disjoint paths joining prescribed pairs with a prescribed gain on each path, or determines that none exist. The result previously appeared only in the author's 2009 PhD thesis. This proof uses a reduction to unbreakable graphs and recent structure theorems for graphs drawn on a surface, and was found with the help of AI.

papers.title: Compressing probabilistic almost-linear recurrent networks without refitting
papers.abstract: Can a compressed recurrent network reuse its learned noise model? We applied finite-horizon balanced truncation to ten probabilistic almost-linear networks on delayed recall. Reducing 64 states to 32 without refitting met forecast tolerances for seven networks when balancing included rectifier inputs, compared with one using the readout alone. Including rectifier inputs improved agreement with the parent's mean-centred forecast distribution on all ten networks, with a median reduction in discrepancy of 65%. Compared with random directions, rectifier inputs reduced centred divergence on six networks and mean forecast error on all ten. Both full and reduced networks underestimated uncertainty on weak cues.

papers.title: Exact subtraction of electron self-interaction from the Kohn-Sham equations
papers.abstract: The self-interaction error (SIE) of Kohn-Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT) leads to a non-physical, non-linear dependence of an orbital's energy on its own fractional occupation [Dabo et al., Phys. Rev. B, 82:115121, 2010]. The generalized Koopmans condition (GKC) ensures an atomic orbital's eigenenergy is independent of its fractional occupation$-$ and is free of self-interaction. The constrained search of the Levy spin-density-functional theory yields orbital densities and delivers the ground-state energy to generalize the Hohenberg-Kohn theorems. In this work, the electron density of the Kohn-Sham equations is constrained to be orbital-density dependent, with a total energy functional linear with respect to variation of its orbital densities. That is, the KS multiplicative effective potential $v_{\text{s}}[{n}]$ for an orbital $\varphi_i[{n}]$ is constrained to a functional $v_{\text{eff}}[{n - n_i}]$. The result complies with the generalized Koopmans condition (GKC). This approach improves LDA and GGA mean absolute errors (MAEs) in fundamental band gaps by $\sim$ 1 eV, with respect to KS-DFT. Equations free of electron self-interaction provide the basis for improvements in the accuracy, efficiency, and simplicity of density functional theories.

papers.title: Fast Algorithms for Permanents of Permutationally-Dominant Matrices
papers.abstract: We establish a fast algorithm for approximating the permanent of permutationally-dominant matrices. In particular, we obtain a fully polynomial randomised approximation scheme whose runtime is quadratic in both the dimension of the matrix and the inverse of the approximation error. Our approach is based on a polymer model representation of the permanent and importance sampling of the logarithm of its partition function via the theory of heaps of pieces of Viennot.

papers.title: One Neural Operator for Re-planning Low-Thrust Cislunar Transfers after Thrust Outages, at the Original or a Later Arrival
papers.abstract: Safe-mode events causing thrust outages are common in missions with electric propulsion. To demonstrate mission feasibility in such an event, missed-thrust margin studies are performed where thousands of outage scenarios need an exact re-plan solved. We train a neural operator that maps a nominal trajectory with an outage profile to a re-planned trajectory and to the probability that the recovery exists, for 270 low-thrust near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO) to distant retrograde orbit (DRO) transfers, at an allowed slip of up to 10 days. On unseen transfers and zero slip, its median control error on the severe half of outages is 1.20% compared to 14.0% for the best cheap re-planner benchmark. With the arrival slip as an input, the error is 1.67% against 23.2%. It also predicts the recoverability of an outage for a given arrival slip with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.997, while the minimum recoverable slip prediction is optimistic by more than half a day on only 6 of the 84 checked outages needing slip. At the original arrival, the ensemble spread of an operator variant with solver inputs has a rank correlation of 0.91 with the actual error, and performing exact solves on the 31% most uncertain severe outages reduces the 90th-percentile error from 8.5% to 2.3%. A query takes milliseconds without a solver, making this a useful tool for large outage studies where the cost of thousands of exact solves outweighs the time to train the operator.
papers.intro:
Safe-mode events are common in deep-space missions, including missions that use electric propulsion. These events create outages in thrust, and then the transfer must recover with the remaining time and fuel. Flight records of about 240 safe-mode events give Weibull distribution fits for the duration and spacing of safe-mode events [1]. In April 2025, a single anomaly cost Psyche 76 days of thrusting [2, 3]. At the design stage of low-thrust missions, Δ​v\Delta v and arrival slip margins are set by sweeping outages along the nominal trajectory and re-optimising a recovery for each case [4], or by a Monte Carlo over flight statistics [5]. For example, the Dawn mission trajectory and margins were designed to tolerate a 28-day shutdown at any point [6]. Psyche, which uses Hall-effect thrusters in deep space, set explicit missed-thrust requirements stating that a 10-day outage at any time and a 22-day outage during solar conjunctions must be tolerable [7].

In these large outage studies, every sampled outage is a full re-optimisation. The Gateway insertion analysis re-optimised a recovery from three missed-thrust cases on each of 346 reference trajectories, over 1,000 solves, each with SNOPT inside a basin-hopping search [8]. Cislunar space is gaining traction with missions such as CAPSTONE, which entered a near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO) in November 2022 [9], Artemis I, whose Orion spacecraft flew a distant retrograde orbit (DRO) [10], and the Gateway, whose reference orbit was the 9:2 L2 southern NRHO [11], planned to be reached by an electric propulsion system [8] before NASA paused it in March 2026 [12]. Transfers between an NRHO and a DRO [13] are also a current research topic [14, 15, 16]. For the NRHO-to-DRO transfers in this study, the exact labelling procedure takes 14.5 s at the median and 71 s on average. A rapid tool that outputs a re-planned trajectory with accurate Δ​v\Delta v margins and closest lunar approach, together with an indication of whether a recovery exists at a given arrival slip, would accelerate outage studies.

Several methods build robustness to missed thrust into the nominal trajectory [14, 17]. In [14], a few branches of trajectories are optimised together with an NRHO-to-DRO reference, cutting the extra propellant needed after a 7-day outage by up to 90%. The authors of [17] apply a similar idea to interplanetary transfers, where they optimise the nominal trajectory together with a group of recovery trajectories. However, these studies add a set of chosen outages to one optimisation problem, so a new nominal trajectory would need a new solve. The authors of [18] bound the missed-thrust duration for which a first-order model of the recovery stays valid along the nominal trajectory. This results in a certificate that shows when the recovery problem is well behaved but does not fully determine if a recovery exists.

Learned methods compute optimal solutions in advance and train a network on them, so that each re-plan takes only one network evaluation. In [19], the authors train a network on optimal state–control pairs to fly as a feedback law, and the network repairs more than 75% of missed-thrust events. Similar networks can give real-time guidance for landing and for low-thrust transfers [20, 21]. However, these policies are generally compared to the exact solutions, not against cheap re-planners which also start from the nominal trajectory. Therefore, a network could appear accurate even when a cheap solver step from the nominal would do as well. In addition, these networks do not say whether a recovery exists, which is the critical information a margin study needs prior to using a re-planned trajectory. Thus, it is not clear if a learned re-planner performs better than a single convex or sequential quadratic programming (SQP) step from the nominal trajectory. Neural operators learn maps between functions [22, 23], which matches the form of this problem where the input is the thrust available over time and the nominal trajectory, and the output is a re-planned thrust history from the moment thrust recovers.

In this work, we train one neural operator for a transfer family consisting of 270 low-thrust NRHO-to-DRO transfers. The neural operator returns the re-planned trajectory and the probability that a recovery exists. The operator is an ensemble of Fourier neural operators [22] that are trained on exact trajectory re-plans. It is queried with the thrust available over time and the nominal trajectory. The controls flown until thrust returns are frozen, and later outages are unknown. Therefore, the re-plan is causal and targets the trajectory post thrust recovery. We compare the operator against cheap re-planners on transfers unseen in training, with the main comparisons fixed in advance.

papers.title: Can a Short Video Clip Verify a Model Fix?
papers.abstract: A developer who reproduces a video model's error on a short clip can replay that clip after an update. How often does a correct clip answer mean the original test now passes? On 960 prespecified CG-Bench questions, we updated from Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct to Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct. Accuracy on a 64-frame sample spanning the full video rose from 27.9% to 33.3%. Before scoring the newer model, we froze 388 clips on which the older model reproduced its exact reference error. The updated model passed the reference on 51 of 116 clip passes (44.0%, 95% Wilson interval 35.3-53.0%) and on 16 of 272 clip failures (5.9%). Closing cases on a clip pass would have declared 65 unresolved reference failures fixed. Requiring a clip pass would have missed 16 of the 67 reference fixes (23.9%). In a separate 1,028-video study with different checkpoints and direct option scoring, only 15 clips passed, and the 16-frame reference confirmed one. For the generated-answer update, the short replay identified cases worth checking, while the original input remained necessary to verify individual fixes.

papers.title: Dynamic Reasoning in Next-Gen Detection and Response: An Empirical Study of LLM Triage, Reinforcement Tuning, and Adversarial Evasion
papers.abstract: We present an end-to-end empirical study of dynamic reasoning in next-generation detection and response pipelines, evaluating how static classifiers, graph-based signal fusion, and large language model (LLM) triage agents perform under strict human-analyst attention budgets (Recall at B alerts/day). Across 56 reproducible experiments spanning a multi-layer enterprise-and-cloud simulator and four public datasets (SOREL-20M, BODMAS, LANL, and DARPA Transparent Computing), we test twelve architectural claims governing modern fleet-scale defense. First, we show that fleet growth halves recall at a fixed analyst budget even at negligible compute cost (<$0.0003 per million events), and that rarity-weighted graph risk propagation outperforms GraphSAGE without neural training. Second, evaluating frontier reasoning models (Gemini) and fine-tuned open-weight models (Qwen3-4B) for alert triage reveals that unconstrained LLM auto-closure eliminates 90% of false positives while silently discarding 31-44% of true attack cases. Third, post-training with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) causes severe reward hacking on unseen attack classes, suppressing up to 86% of novel attacks compared to two-epoch supervised fine-tuning. Finally, against an adaptive adversary generating plausible cover stories in benign telemetry fields, LLM triage evasion rises sharply unless gated by a deterministic policy harness prior to model invocation.

papers.title: Using AI to Simulate the Behaviour of European Populations
papers.abstract: Language models can stand in for survey respondents, but leading approaches build their simulated people from interviews or individual records. We show that a model can learn how European population groups respond from published statistics, without interviews and without training on individual records. We fine-tune an open-weight language model on more than 12 million published group-level answer distributions from about 40 European countries, setting it up to predict each group's departure from a reference distribution. On opinion surveys from its training families it calls the direction of group differences right 84% of the time, ahead of a demographic statistical model (77%, paired test) and level with Claude Opus 5 and 5.5, which it also ties on accuracy; the frontier models are more accurate on new questions. On 278 held-out questions, almost all from the survey families seen in training, its error is 12% lower than that statistical model. It runs on a single 32 GB GPU or a high-memory laptop, and in a test with an earlier model, an evidence gate calibrated on half of a survey's questions fell back to the reference where the model's adjustments did not help. Coupled to a transport simulation of a planned metro closure, with a conventional elasticity as the reference, it adds a testable age gradient to the response, which we freeze for later scoring.

Decisions about public services are made before anyone knows how people will respond. A transit authority closing a metro section, a city changing fares, or a ministry redesigning a benefit all need an estimate of how different groups will react. Language models offer a shortcut. Prompted with a description of a person, they produce answers that resemble those of real respondents [1]. Several lines of work have pushed this further: agents built from two-hour interviews with 1,052 people [10]; models fine-tuned on 2.9 million individual responses from social-science experiments [5]; and models fine-tuned on published opinion distributions of subpopulations [12, 11, 4]. Interview-based approaches depend on records of identifiable individuals, which in Europe are personal data and, when they touch health, politics or religion, special-category data. Most of this work is built on US populations, and in cross-national tests the respondent’s country acts as an assumption that further respondent detail does not revise [13].

papers.title: Deleted square of a cone over a graph
papers.abstract: The deleted square of a topological space is a subspace of the Cartesian product of this space with itself, obtained by removing the diagonal. Conjecturally, the deleted square of a cone over a graph has the homotopy type of a wedge sum of spheres of dimensions at most 3. We propose a geometric construction that is a key motivation for the conjecture and provides a major step towards its proof, while yielding direct results on deleted squares of certain families of graphs.
